case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Vada Samosas
case.setting: Saffron Valley College Canteen, near the main quadrangle
case.crime: 24 freshly made samosas went missing from the canteen counter during lunch break
case.victim: Raju Bhai, the beloved canteen owner known for his spicy potato samosas

suspects.name: Ananya Patel
suspects.personality: organized, ambitious, health-conscious, secretly loves junk food
suspects.motive: She was seen sneaking samosas into her eco-bag last week and warned by Raju Bhai
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying for her economics quiz
suspects.secret: She's been secretly blogging about college food under the pseudonym 'The Snack Spy'
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Nervously wiped her fingers on a napkin when questioned, even though she claimed not to have eaten anything

suspects.name: Karan Singh
suspects.personality: jokester, hungry always, likes pranks, loyal friend
suspects.motive: Publicly declared he would 'sacrifice his sandwich for a samosa' that morning
suspects.alibi: Says he was playing cricket on the back field
suspects.secret: He owes Raju Bhai ₹150 from last month and avoids him
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the canteen trash can tossing a paper plate with suspicious grease stains

suspects.name: Professor Mehta
suspects.motive: Known to eat at the canteen daily at 12:30 sharp; missed his routine today
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers in his office
suspects.secret: He’s been bringing home leftovers for his cat, Mr. Whiskers, who only eats spicy food
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His briefcase smelled faintly of cumin and fried dough when passing by

evidence.description: A half-eaten samosa found in the canteen trash can, still warm
evidence.location: Inside the canteen’s main waste bin
evidence.significance: Suggests the theft was recent and the thief didn’t leave the premises immediately

evidence.description: A blue eco-friendly cloth bag with a small grease stain and a crumpled 'Snack Spy' draft blog page
evidence.location: Under a bench near the library entrance
evidence.significance: Links Ananya to suspicious snack-related behavior

evidence.description: Rohan, a first-year student, saw Karan near the canteen at 12:45 PM, looking around 'suspiciously'
evidence.significance: Places Karan near the scene after the theft

evidence.description: Canteen CCTV shows Professor Mehta entering the canteen at 12:28 PM but not purchasing anything
evidence.significance: Suggests he might have taken the samosas without paying

evidence.description: A sticky label from a samosa tray with Raju Bhai's handwriting saying 'Batch #7 - 24 pcs'
evidence.location: Found in the pocket of a discarded jacket near the cricket field
evidence.significance: Direct link between the stolen batch and a location linked to Karan

timeline: 12:15 PM: Raju Bhai places a fresh tray of 24 samosas on the counter.
12:20 PM: Canteen CCTV shows Karan peering in through the window, then walking away.
12:25 PM: Ananya enters the library (confirmed by librarian).
12:28 PM: Professor Mehta enters canteen, looks at samosas, sighs, and leaves without buying.
12:30 PM: Raju Bhai steps into the kitchen to prepare chai.
12:31 PM: Samosas go missing. No one in canteen recorded on camera.
12:45 PM: Karan seen near canteen trash can by Rohan.
1:00 PM: Raju Bhai discovers the theft and raises alarm.
red_herrings: Ananya’s food blog and eco-bag suggest she might have stolen the samosas despite her alibi.
Professor Mehta’s unusual absence from his routine and the CCTV footage imply guilt.
Karan’s debt to Raju Bhai and his presence near the trash can make him look suspicious.

solution.method: While pretending to inspect the samosas, he secretly slipped the entire tray into his oversized briefcase when Raju Bhai turned away to make chai.
solution.motive: His cat Mr. Whiskers had been meowing for spicy food all morning, and the professor wanted to surprise him with a treat.
solution.proof: When questioned, he opened his briefcase to show his grading papers — a single crispy samosa corner poked out, still warm. The cat hair on the tray label matches fur from his coat.
solution.how_to_solve: The CCTV shows Mehta entering just before the theft and no one else approaching the counter. His briefcase was large enough to hold the tray. The cumin smell, combined with the timing, points to him. The other suspects have weak but explainable links: Ananya’s bag was lost earlier, Karan was tossing a sandwich wrapper. Only Mehta had access, opportunity, and a hidden reason to take the full tray.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Century Bat
case.setting: Delhi Public College of Arts and Science, Cricket Pavilion
case.crime: A prized cricket bat went missing just hours before the annual inter-college cricket final.
case.victim: Arjun Mehta, college cricket team captain

suspects.name: Rohan Patil
suspects.motive: Wanted to pressure Arjun into letting him open the batting
suspects.alibi: Claimed he was at the gym from 4 PM to 6 PM
suspects.secret: He secretly owes money to a local cricket bookie
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Acted unusually calm when the bat went missing and suggested Arjun 'calm down'

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Believed the bat was made from illegally sourced wood and wanted to 'rescue' it
suspects.alibi: Said she was in the library studying for her environmental science quiz
suspects.secret: She joined an underground eco-activist group last month
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen taking photos of the bat case earlier in the week

suspects.name: Professor Anand Joshi
suspects.motive: Disapproved of Arjun using a professional bat in college matches
suspects.alibi: Claimed he was grading papers in his office
suspects.secret: He misplaced the exam keys and was afraid of getting reported
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested the bat was 'probably cursed' and deserved to vanish

suspects.name: Chintu Sharma
suspects.motive: Wanted to borrow the bat to show his village friends 'college gear'
suspects.alibi: Said he was cleaning the auditorium till 5:30 PM
suspects.secret: He once accidentally broke a trophy and glued it back together
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Nervously laughed when the bat was mentioned and avoided eye contact

evidence.description: A single green thread found near the broken lock of the bat case
evidence.significance: Matches the fabric of the college’s eco-club T-shirts

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Chintu near the pavilion at 5:10 PM, but he’s seen cleaning with a mop
evidence.significance: Suggests opportunity but also supports his alibi

evidence.description: A note in Arjun's bag: 'If you don’t let me open, you won’t find your bat.' Handwriting unclear.
evidence.significance: Looks like a threat, but the paper is from a gym notepad

evidence.description: A student claims seeing Priya near the pavilion at 4:45 PM, taking photos
evidence.significance: Suggests opportunity, but photos were of the butterfly garden behind the pavilion

evidence.description: A small bat-shaped key hanging from Chintu’s cleaning trolley
evidence.significance: Turns out it’s a key to the pavilion storage room – not the bat case

evidence.description: The missing bat found wrapped in a gym towel under a bench in the pavilion changing room
evidence.significance: Not stolen—just hidden in plain sight

evidence.description: Professor Joshi’s office lights were on, but no one saw him leave or enter
evidence.significance: He never actually left his office, but has no proof of being there

timeline: 3:00 PM: Arjun locks his bat in the pavilion case after practice
3:30 PM: Chintu begins cleaning auditorium (witnessed by two students)
4:00 PM: Priya enters library (library sign-in sheet)
4:30 PM: Rohan arrives at gym (gym CCTV timestamp)
5:00 PM: Professor Joshi reportedly in office (no witnesses)
5:10 PM: Chintu passes pavilion while mopping (CCTV)
5:45 PM: Arjun returns to pavilion—bat gone
6:00 PM: College detective (player) begins investigation
red_herrings: The threatening note in Arjun’s bag pointing to Rohan
Green thread linking to Priya and the eco-club
Professor Joshi’s odd comments about the bat being cursed
Chintu being seen near the pavilion with a suspicious key

solution.method: Chintu borrowed the bat to show his visiting cousin from the village but panicked and hid it under a bench when he heard Arjun returning.
solution.motive: Wanted to impress his cousin with 'pro college gear' for a photo, not steal it
solution.proof: The gym towel the bat was wrapped in has Chintu’s name tag (used by staff) and a canteen food stain matching what he ate for lunch.
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects using alibis: Rohan (gym CCTV), Priya (library log), Professor Joshi (lights on but no movement — actually fell asleep). Chintu’s alibi is weak. The gym towel with his name tag directly links him to the bat. The threat note and green thread are unrelated. The bat was never stolen — just borrowed and poorly hidden.

case.title: The Case of the Chaotic Library
case.setting: Delhi Public College – Central Library, 3rd floor 'Silent Zone'
case.crime: All library books have been mysteriously rearranged overnight, completely mixed up by genre, author, and language.
case.victim: The college library system and students preparing for semester exams

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.personality: tech-obsessed, sarcastic, always late, hates physical books
suspects.motive: Wanted to prove the library should go fully digital
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at an all-night coding competition at another college
suspects.secret: He accidentally spilled chai on a rare philosophy book yesterday and didn’t report it
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was overheard saying, 'This library needs a hard reset'

suspects.name: Priya Desai
suspects.motive: Wanted to reorganize the library by her own 'efficient' system
suspects.alibi: Says she was studying in her hostel room from 8 PM to 2 AM
suspects.secret: She took home three library books to study but forgot to check them out
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen sketching a new library layout in her notebook

suspects.name: Rohan Khanna
suspects.personality: eccentric, strict, absent-minded, passionate about order
suspects.motive: Believes the Dewey Decimal System is outdated and wants to create his own
suspects.alibi: Claims he was home sick with a fever
suspects.secret: He's been writing a fantasy novel set in a magical library
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had a whiteboard in the staff room full of crazy color-coded charts for 'The New Order'

suspects.name: Zoya Mirza
suspects.motive: Wanted to create a real-life escape room challenge for her friends
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a midnight poetry slam on campus
suspects.secret: She painted graffiti art in the old library basement (not malicious, but unauthorized)
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was heard giggling and whispering, 'They’ll never find the clue I hid'

evidence.description: A crumpled sticky note found near the history section with doodles of books flying around and the words 'Chaos is the new order!'
evidence.location: Between pages of a misplaced 'World War II: A Military History' book
evidence.significance: Suggests someone planned the mix-up artistically

evidence.description: A receipt from a chai stall dated the previous night at 10:45 PM, with a smudged fingerprint and 'A.M.' written on it
evidence.location: Tucked inside a philosophy book on ethics
evidence.significance: Places Aarav on campus late, contradicting his alibi

evidence.description: Library security logs show no entry between 9 PM and 6 AM, but the admin override key was used at 11:03 PM
evidence.significance: Indicates insider access was used

evidence.description: A colorful origami raven made from a library checkout slip, found on the circulation desk
evidence.significance: Zoya is known for making origami animals; she left them as 'clues' for her prank

evidence.description: A night watchman reports seeing someone in a hoodie near the library door at 10:50 PM but couldn’t identify them
evidence.significance: Confirms someone was near the library, but no proof of entry

evidence.description: A pair of reading glasses with a 'No. 7 Dewey Rebellion' sticker on the case, found in the reference section
evidence.significance: Belongs to Rohan; suggests his involvement in a 'rebellion' against the current system

evidence.description: Zoya’s Instagram story from 11:15 PM showing her at the poetry slam, with timestamp and geotag
evidence.significance: Confirms her alibi is solid

timeline: 6:00 PM – Library closes normally, books in order
8:00 PM – Aarav leaves for coding competition (claims)
9:30 PM – Priya returns to hostel after dinner
10:00 PM – Poetry slam begins; Zoya performs
10:50 PM – Night watchman sees hoodie figure near library
11:03 PM – Admin override key used on library system (logged entry)
11:15 PM – Zoya posts Instagram story from poetry slam
6:00 AM – Librarian arrives, discovers chaos
8:30 AM – Students report missing and mixed-up books
red_herrings: The 'Chaos is the new order' note suggests a philosophical motive
Aarav’s chai receipt places him on campus late
Rohan’s 'Dewey Rebellion' glasses imply a planned takeover

solution.method: Used her knowledge of the librarian’s routine to sneak in during the 10-minute window when the back door was unlocked for trash pickup, then used the admin override key (which she copied earlier during a volunteer shift)
solution.motive: To create a fun mystery game for her friends to solve as a midnight challenge
solution.proof: The origami raven matches her unique folding style, and the security override log time (11:03 PM) conflicts with the poetry slam timing—she left briefly to pull the prank and returned
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-check alibis: Zoya’s Instagram proves she was at the event, but the admin log shows action at 11:03 PM—during a break in the slam. Only someone who left temporarily could have done it. The origami raven links her directly. Aarav and Rohan had motives but no access. Priya had no opportunity. The receipt and glasses are red herrings.

case.title: The Case of the Pink Pulsar
case.setting: Vivekananda Hostel, Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Technology, Mumbai
case.crime: A student's motorcycle was spray-painted bright pink overnight
case.victim: Arjun Mehta, a second-year mechanical engineering student

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.motive: She had publicly criticized Arjun for using his bike excessively and causing noise pollution in the quiet hours
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at an online climate activism meeting from 8 PM to 11 PM and then slept
suspects.secret: She secretly likes Arjun and was embarrassed after he rejected her group’s petition
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the bike parking lot late at night holding something wrapped in cloth

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Had lost a bet to Arjun and owed him 500 rupees, but joked about 'paying in style'
suspects.alibi: Says he was streaming a gaming session with friends until 2 AM
suspects.secret: He has a crush on Priya and was spying on her earlier that night
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to laugh about the pink bike and took multiple photos for meme content

suspects.name: Bunty Patel
suspects.motive: Disapproves of students owning bikes, calls them 'symbols of arrogance'
suspects.alibi: Claims he was doing rounds until 10 PM, then slept in his quarters
suspects.secret: He once accidentally scratched Arjun’s bike and never confessed
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was unusually silent in the morning and avoided looking at the bike

evidence.description: Pink spray paint can found near drainage pipe behind the parking lot, still slightly wet
evidence.location: Behind bike parking, near hostel wall
evidence.significance: Direct link to the vandalism

evidence.description: Rohan’s gaming livestream timestamp shows him online until 2 AM, with voice chat active
evidence.significance: Alibi confirmed for most of the night

evidence.description: First-year student saw someone in a hoodie near the bikes around 11:30 PM, but couldn't identify them
evidence.significance: Confirms late-night activity

evidence.description: Pink paint smudge on the sleeve of a sweater hanging in Priya’s room
evidence.significance: Appears incriminating

evidence.description: A receipt for three cans of pink spray paint from a local hardware store dated the previous day
evidence.significance: Suggests he bought the paint

evidence.description: Hostel security camera (partially working) shows a figure in a hoodie exiting parking area at 11:47 PM, holding something cylindrical
evidence.significance: Key visual clue

evidence.description: Tiny label on the spray can found behind parking lot with a sticker: 'For Diwali decorations – Store Room A'
evidence.location: On the discarded spray paint can
evidence.significance: Reveals the paint was taken from hostel property, not purchased

timeline: 6:00 PM: Arjun parks his black Bajaj Pulsar in the hostel bike zone.
8:00 PM - 11:00 PM: Priya attends online climate meeting (verified by logs).
9:30 PM: Bunty finishes hostel rounds, locks front gate.
10:15 PM: Rohan begins live gaming session streamed online.
11:30 PM: First-year student reports seeing a hoodie figure near bikes.
11:47 PM: Security camera captures hooded figure leaving bike area with cylindrical object.
7:00 AM: Arjun discovers his bike painted bright pink.
red_herrings: Priya seen near parking with cloth-wrapped object (later revealed to be a cake for a midnight snack club).
Pink paint on Priya's sweater (spill from hostel art workshop day earlier).
Bunty's receipt for pink paint (bought for hostel Diwali committee, not personal use).

solution.method: Used hostel’s own pink spray paint (meant for decorations) to paint the bike during a short break in his stream around 11:45 PM.
solution.motive: Wanted to pull a legendary prank to gain fame in the college meme group and avoid paying the 500-rupee bet with a 'creative' solution.
solution.proof: Security footage shows the hooded figure exiting at 11:47 PM. Rohan’s stream has a 12-minute unexplained audio loop at 11:40–11:52 PM, indicating he left the room. The spray can label proves it was hostel property, accessible only at night.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference the security footage time (11:47 PM) with digital alibis. Rohan’s stream shows a gap in live activity despite appearing active. The paint can's origin (hostel store) rules out Priya and Bunty as buyers. Combined with his prankster personality and motive to avoid paying the bet, the evidence points conclusively to Rohan.

case.title: The Case of the Chalk Dust Bandit
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts & Science, Classroom B24 (Botany Department)
case.crime: Mysterious accumulation of chalk dust on student desks every morning
case.victim: First-year B.Sc Botany students

suspects.name: Rahul Mehta
suspects.personality: Energetic, prankster, always cracking jokes, loves puzzles
suspects.motive: Wanted to create a mystery to make college life less boring
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at the college canteen finishing a late-night project
suspects.secret: Secretly writes anonymous campus humor blog
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen smirking near the classroom before the first incident

suspects.name: Dr. Anjali Nair
suspects.personality: Strict, punctual, detail-oriented, low tolerance for nonsense
suspects.motive: Believes students are too careless and wanted to teach them a lesson
suspects.alibi: Says she was grading papers at home
suspects.secret: Is secretly afraid of spiders and avoids the old classroom storage room
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Forced students to clean chalk dust themselves, claimed it was 'character-building'

suspects.name: Kabir Dalal
suspects.personality: Quiet, observant, proud of his cleaning skills, slightly grumpy
suspects.motive: Thinks students are messy and disrespect the classroom
suspects.alibi: Says he was cleaning the Chemistry lab on the second floor
suspects.secret: Wears noise-canceling earbuds while working and doesn’t hear people approaching
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen entering the classroom after hours with a janitorial cart

suspects.name: Priya Iyer
suspects.motive: Believes chalk dust wards off bad luck and placed it as a protective charm
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying for her microbiology quiz
suspects.secret: Leaves small 'good luck' items around campus for anonymous students
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen whispering to a friend about 'cleansing energy' before class

evidence.description: A thick layer of white chalk dust found neatly arranged on 8 student desks every morning, forming a small pyramid shape on each.
evidence.significance: Suggests intentional placement, not accidental

evidence.description: A single broken piece of pink chalk found near the window
evidence.significance: Unusual color — not used in this class; suggests prank

evidence.description: A student saw Kabir entering B24 late at night with a mop and bucket
evidence.significance: Points to janitorial access

evidence.description: Canteen CCTV footage shows Rahul typing on his laptop until 10:30 PM, but no footage of him returning to classrooms
evidence.significance: Supports his alibi

evidence.description: A tiny sticky note found stuck inside the chalk tray with the words 'Silence is golden' in messy handwriting
evidence.significance: Matches Rahul’s humor blog style

evidence.description: A pair of noise-canceling earbuds found in Kabir’s pocket during questioning
evidence.significance: Explains why he wouldn’t hear if someone saw him

evidence.description: Priya’s friend confirms Priya was at the library from 7–10 PM
evidence.significance: Alibi confirmed

timeline: Monday, 5:00 PM: Last class (Botany Lab) ends in B24
Monday, 5:15 PM: Classroom cleaned and locked by Kabir
Monday, 10:30 PM: Rahul leaves canteen (per CCTV)
Tuesday, 8:00 AM: Students enter B24 and find chalk dust pyramids on desks
Tuesday, 9:00 AM: Dr. Nair arrives, scolds students for 'messiness'
Tuesday, 1:00 PM: Investigation begins
Wednesday & Thursday: Chalk dust reappears each morning
Friday, 7:00 AM: Hidden camera placed by student council in ceiling fan
red_herrings: Pink chalk suggests a colorful prankster — not linked to any class materials
Kabir seen entering classroom at night — but he only checks locks after hours
Dr. Nair’s strict behavior makes her seem like she’s giving a lesson

solution.method: Used a remote-controlled mini drone (toy) to fly into the unlocked classroom window at night and drop chalk dust from a small compartment
solution.motive: Wanted to create a fun mystery to entertain students and gain attention for his humor blog
solution.proof: The hidden camera caught a small drone exiting through the window at 4:47 AM Friday with a white residue; drone found in Rahul’s dorm with chalk remnants
solution.how_to_solve: The consistent pyramid shape implies precision not possible by hand at night without being seen. The pink chalk is a red herring — Rahul planted it to mislead. The sticky note's phrase matches his blog. CCTV clears him of walking into B24, so method had to be indirect. Only Rahul had both motive (prankster) and tech knowledge. The drone explains how dust arrived without anyone entering.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Kulfi
case.setting: Jai Bharat Engineering College canteen, Mumbai
case.crime: A fresh batch of special mango kulfi mysteriously disappears from the canteen counter just before lunch break.
case.victim: Ramesh Bhai, the canteen owner who spent the morning preparing the kulfis for the annual 'Sweet Day' event.

suspects.name: Priya Mehta
suspects.motive: Wants to expose the canteen’s unhygienic practices after seeing Ramesh Bhai reuse containers.
suspects.alibi: Was in the library studying for her Chemistry quiz.
suspects.secret: She secretly skips lunch because of an eating disorder.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She was seen arguing with Ramesh Bhai yesterday about sugar content in sweets.

suspects.name: Rohan Patel
suspects.motive: Wanted to play a harmless prank on the canteen crowd by stealing the kulfis as a joke.
suspects.alibi: Says he was playing cricket on the back field.
suspects.secret: He owes Ramesh Bhai 300 rupees and avoids him.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the canteen 10 minutes before the disappearance with an oversized backpack.

suspects.name: Professor Kiran Desai
suspects.personality: strict, no-nonsense, loves sweets secretly, always late
suspects.motive: Has a secret sweet tooth and craved the mango kulfi after a stressful meeting.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers in her office.
suspects.secret: She hides her love for sweets because she lectures students about healthy eating.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen licking her fingers near the canteen trash can right after the disappearance.

suspects.name: Anand Kumar
suspects.personality: hardworking, quiet, loyal to Ramesh Bhai, poor eyesight
suspects.motive: None — genuinely wants to help solve the mystery.
suspects.alibi: Was cleaning the back storeroom.
suspects.secret: He borrowed Ramesh Bhai’s kulfi mold to make sweets for his sister’s birthday.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen handling the empty kulfi tray and didn’t report it immediately.

evidence.description: An empty kulfi tray found behind the canteen with traces of mango residue.
evidence.location: Behind the canteen near the dustbins
evidence.significance: Shows that the kulfis were removed from the mold after being stolen or taken.

evidence.description: A single green hairband found near the canteen counter.
evidence.location: On the floor near the sweet display
evidence.significance: Belongs to Priya, who wears green bands in her braid.

evidence.description: A first-year student says she saw someone in a cricket jersey sneaking around the canteen.
evidence.significance: Points toward Rohan, who wears a blue cricket jersey.

evidence.description: A sticky, sweet fingerprint on the canteen refrigerator handle.
evidence.location: On the handle of the canteen fridge
evidence.significance: Indicates someone opened the fridge recently with kulfi-covered fingers.

evidence.description: Canteen security camera footage (poor quality) showing a figure in a white shirt taking a tray at 11:48 AM.
evidence.significance: The figure resembles Professor Desai, but the resolution is too low to confirm.

timeline: 10:00 AM: Ramesh Bhai places 20 fresh mango kulfis in the canteen display fridge.
10:15 AM: Priya argues with Ramesh Bhai about sugar levels in sweets.
10:30 AM: Professor Desai passes by the canteen, glances at the kulfis wistfully.
11:00 AM: Rohan is seen heading toward the cricket field with his kit bag.
11:45 AM: Anand cleans the storeroom, borrows the kulfi tray to wash at home later.
11:48 AM: Security camera shows a figure in a white shirt removing the tray from the fridge.
12:00 PM: Students arrive for lunch — kulfis are gone. Chaos ensues.
red_herrings: The green hairband makes it seem like Priya took the kulfis.
The cricket jersey sighting falsely implicates Rohan.
Blurry camera footage suggests Professor Desai stole them.

solution.method: He accidentally took the kulfi tray home, thinking it was empty and needed washing, forgetting the kulfis were inside.
solution.motive: No ill intent — just an honest mistake due to poor eyesight and distraction.
solution.proof: The kulfi tray was found in his home sink, with melted mango kulfi residue and wrapper still intact.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-check alibis: Professor’s fingers were sticky from eating store-bought jalebi, not kulfis. Rohan’s jersey sighting was another student. Priya’s hairband was lost earlier. Anand’s secret about the tray, combined with the found tray at his house, confirms the accidental theft. The fridge handle fingerprint matches Anand, and his role as cleaner makes access logical.

case.title: The Case of the Missing Tiger Suit
case.setting: Surya Dev College of Technology, Delhi
case.crime: The college mascot costume – a full-body royal Bengal tiger suit – has gone missing the night before Founder's Day Parade
case.victim: The college mascot team and event organizers

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted to embarrass rival team by sabotaging their big moment
suspects.alibi: Claims he was rehearsing dance moves alone in the auditorium
suspects.secret: Failed his last Physics exam and is scared his parents will find out
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Actively suggests blaming the rival college, seems overly invested in solving the case

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Believes mascot is wasteful and promotes animal exploitation
suspects.alibi: Says she was at the campus organic garden, watering plants late at night
suspects.secret: Secretly dating the college principal's son, which could get her in trouble
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen sketching a protest sign saying 'Free the Tiger' earlier that week

suspects.name: Rajesh 'Raju' Patel
suspects.motive: None – but was seen near the costume room late
suspects.alibi: Says he was cleaning the canteen and then took a nap in the storage shed
suspects.secret: Collects random 'abandoned' items to sell at the Sunday flea market
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen carrying a large duffel bag toward the dorms at 10 PM

suspects.name: Dr. Meera Khanna
suspects.motive: Disapproves of distractions like mascot events affecting academics
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers at home; has no witnesses
suspects.secret: Once played the tiger in 1999 and still has a faded photo on her office wall
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was overheard telling a colleague the mascot was 'an embarrassment to academia'

evidence.description: A single yellow thread caught on the broken latch of the mascot storage room door
evidence.significance: Matches the material of the tiger suit

evidence.description: A muddy footprint near the storage room, size 10 sports shoe
evidence.significance: Matches Arjun's popular brand of sneakers

evidence.description: Canteen security camera footage shows Raju carrying a large black duffel bag at 10:05 PM
evidence.significance: Appears suspicious, but the bag contains old mops and a sleeping bag

evidence.description: A sketchbook with drawings of the tiger costume crossed out with red Xs and protest slogans
evidence.location: Under Priya’s desk in art class
evidence.significance: Suggests motive, but just part of her activist art project

evidence.description: A receipt from 3 days ago for '1 large waterproof storage bin' with Raju’s name on it
evidence.significance: He bought the bin to store his side-hustle collection – not related to the case

evidence.description: A first-year student reports seeing Dr. Khanna near campus at 9:45 PM, muttering about 'childish traditions'
evidence.significance: Supports her disapproval, but doesn't prove involvement

evidence.description: The tiger suit found stuffed inside a large green laundry bin marked 'Dorm 3 – Linens Only'
evidence.location: Laundry service pickup point near Dorm 3
evidence.significance: It was moved to avoid being used – but not stolen permanently

timeline: 6:00 PM – Mascot team confirms tiger suit is in storage room after rehearsal
7:30 PM – Lights go out briefly in admin block due to minor power fluctuation
8:45 PM – Raju seen cleaning canteen, then entering storage shed
9:20 PM – Priya seen watering plants in campus garden
9:45 PM – Student sees Dr. Khanna walking near admin block
10:05 PM – Security cam shows Raju with duffel bag leaving canteen
10:30 PM – Arjun alone in auditorium (no witnesses)
7:00 AM (next day) – Costume team discovers tiger suit missing
7:15 AM – Suit found in laundry bin at Dorm 3 pickup point
red_herrings: Raju’s duffel bag looks like he’s smuggling something
Priya’s protest sketches imply she sabotaged the costume
Dr. Khanna’s grudge against campus traditions makes her seem suspicious
Muddy footprint points to Arjun

solution.method: During rehearsal, he secretly unzipped the suit and loosened its lining. That night, he used a spare key (copied earlier) to enter the room, removed the suit, and hid it in the laundry bin so it would be taken off-campus temporarily.
solution.motive: His rival dance crew was scheduled to ride on the mascot float during the parade. Without the mascot, the float would be canceled, giving his team more spotlight.
solution.proof: The yellow thread on the door matches the inner seam of the suit — only someone who handled it roughly from the inside (like removing it hastily) would leave that trace. Arjun’s alibi falls apart when the auditorium’s motion sensor log shows no activity after 9 PM.
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects: Raju’s bag and receipt are harmless, Priya’s sketch is art, Dr. Khanna was seen on campus but no proof of entry. The footprint is misleading — many wear that shoe. The yellow thread indicates inside handling. Only someone with access and motive would move it temporarily. Arjun had opportunity, a weak alibi, and the most to gain.

case.title: The Case of the Swapped Hostel Keys
case.setting: Vasudev College of Arts and Science, Bangalore – Boys' Hostel Block A, Floor 3
case.crime: Room keys of two hostel roommates were mysteriously swapped, causing one to be locked out and the other to accidentally enter the wrong room
case.victim: Rohan Mehta and Arjun Patel – roommates in Room 304 who found their key assigned to Room 311 and vice versa

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Rohan accidentally spilled chai on her project notes last week
suspects.alibi: Was in the library studying for her Psychology quiz from 3 PM to 6 PM
suspects.secret: She secretly likes Arjun but is too shy to admit it
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She was seen near the key rack that morning, but only to return her own room key

suspects.name: Tanmay Joshi
suspects.motive: Loves pulling pranks and once swapped mess menu boards for fun
suspects.alibi: Claims he was playing FIFA in his room with Sid at the time
suspects.secret: He borrowed a senior's motorbike without permission and parked it behind the generator shed
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed when he heard about the mix-up and said, 'Classic move!'

suspects.name: Babu Anna
suspects.motive: Rohan was late returning twice this week – Babu Anna threatened to report him
suspects.alibi: Doing rounds on Floor 2 between 4:30 PM and 5:30 PM
suspects.secret: He drinks herbal 'medicinal' toddy every evening and hides the bottle in the mop closet
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refused to help at first, muttering about 'bad omens' and 'key karma'

suspects.name: Dr. Shilpa Reddy
suspects.motive: None – but was seen near the hostel that evening
suspects.alibi: Conducted a lab session until 5 PM, then walked to hostel to meet a student
suspects.secret: She secretly runs a popular cooking TikTok under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She picked up a misplaced key from the rack and handed it to the warden – but it wasn’t logged

evidence.description: Two identical-looking brass keys swapped on the hostel key rack – labeled '304' now opens 311, and '311' opens 304
evidence.location: Main key rack in hostel reception
evidence.significance: Keys were physically moved; no signs of forced removal

evidence.description: A sticky note with '304 → 311?' written in messy handwriting, found crumpled near the rack
evidence.significance: Suggests someone planned the swap

evidence.description: Hostel security camera footage (blurry) shows a person in a green hoodie adjusting the key rack at 4:15 PM
evidence.significance: Tanmay owns a green hoodie, but frame is too low-res to confirm identity

evidence.description: Sid, Tanmay’s friend, confirms they were playing FIFA together from 4 PM to 5:30 PM, but admits Tanmay left for '2 minutes' to 'use the loo'
evidence.significance: Small window of opportunity for Tanmay

evidence.description: Tiny smudge of blue paint on the '311' key tag
evidence.location: Back of key tag for Room 311
evidence.significance: Matches paint from Tanmay’s DIY Rubik’s Cube he was modifying that day

timeline: 3:00 PM – Rohan and Arjun leave Room 304 for a lecture
3:15 PM – Priya returns her key after class and sees the rack undisturbed
4:15 PM – Security camera shows figure in green hoodie near key rack (blurry)
4:20 PM – Dr. Reddy arrives at hostel, speaks to warden, picks up a fallen key
4:45 PM – Babu Anna begins rounds on Floor 2
5:45 PM – Rohan returns, tries key in Room 304 – opens Room 311 instead
6:00 PM – Chaos ensues; complaint filed
red_herrings: The sticky note suggesting a planned swap – actually written by a confused first-year who misread the board
Dr. Reddy handling a key – she simply returned a found key, not involved in swap

solution.method: Used his brief bathroom break to quickly swap the keys on the rack, using knowledge of their size and shape
solution.motive: Wanted to play a harmless prank after Rohan complained about his loud music last night
solution.proof: Blue paint on the '311' key tag matches Tanmay’s Rubik’s Cube project; only he was near the rack during the narrow time window
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects: Babu Anna was on Floor 2, Priya in library, Dr. Reddy picked up a fallen key but didn’t touch the rack. Tanmay had both motive and opportunity. The paint smudge links him directly to the key. The green hoodie in footage is a red herring, but the paint is irrefutable.

case.title: The Case of the Flat-Footed Final
case.setting: Vikram University, Ujjain – Men's Hostel Common Room & Football Field
case.crime: The official match football was found completely deflated 2 hours before the inter-college football finals.
case.victim: The Vikram University Falcon Strikers football team

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.motive: Worried the team would lose and disgrace him; wanted to delay the match to let injured players recover
suspects.alibi: Says he was reviewing tactics in his room alone
suspects.secret: Failed his midterms and is hiding it from his parents
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Seemed unusually calm about the deflated ball, almost relieved

suspects.name: Priya Deshpande
suspects.motive: Opposes sports events for using excessive plastic and energy; wanted to 'cancel' the match symbolically
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at the college radio station recording a podcast
suspects.secret: She skipped her sociology exam to do the podcast
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen sketching a cartoon of a popped football earlier that day

suspects.name: Arvind Patel
suspects.motive: Accidentally sat on the ball while moving equipment and panicked
suspects.alibi: Says he was setting up speakers near the field
suspects.secret: He has a crush on the team manager and doesn’t want to disappoint her
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Jumped when the ball was mentioned and spilled his chai

suspects.name: Coach Balwant Singh
suspects.motive: Believes the team plays better under pressure; wanted to 'toughen them up' by creating a crisis
suspects.alibi: Says he was at the gym doing his routine
suspects.secret: He secretly bets on college matches (small amounts with friends)
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested using a different, older ball that he 'just happened' to have

evidence.description: Deflated football with a tiny pinprick near the valve. No tool found nearby.
evidence.location: Football equipment bag in the hostel common room
evidence.significance: Ball was deliberately punctured, not just leaked air

evidence.description: A cartoon sketch of a popped football with 'Game Over' written in Hindi.
evidence.location: Found in the trash near the art block
evidence.significance: Suggests a sabotage motive

evidence.description: Timestamped audio log from college radio showing Priya’s podcast aired live from 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM.
evidence.significance: Provides alibi for Priya during the critical window

evidence.description: A bent safety pin found under the equipment table near the field.
evidence.location: Underneath the table where balls are stored
evidence.significance: Likely tool used to puncture the ball

evidence.description: A first-year student saw someone crouching near the equipment bag around 4:15 PM.
evidence.significance: Places suspect near scene at critical time

evidence.description: A crumpled exam schedule with 'SOCIOLOGY – MISSED' scribbled on the back, in Priya’s handwriting.
evidence.location: In the radio station trash can
evidence.significance: Confirms Priya was hiding skipping class

evidence.description: Arvind was seen carrying a stack of speaker boxes from the storage room to the field between 3:45 PM and 4:20 PM.
evidence.significance: He passed near the common room but has no clear alibi for the exact time

timeline: 3:30 PM – Team captain Rohan locks the football in the equipment bag in the hostel common room.
3:45 PM – Arvind begins moving speaker boxes toward the field, passing the common room.
4:00 PM – Priya starts her live podcast at the radio station.
4:15 PM – First-year student sees someone crouching near the equipment bag.
4:30 PM – Coach Balwant finishes gym session, confirmed by gym log.
5:00 PM – Team discovers the deflated football.
5:15 PM – College detective (you) arrives to investigate.
red_herrings: Priya’s cartoon suggests she planned to sabotage the ball.
Her missed exam makes her seem dishonest and evasive.
Coach Balwant’s old spare ball makes him seem suspiciously prepared.

solution.method: While setting up speakers, he briefly stopped to borrow tape from the equipment bag. He accidentally dropped a safety pin into the bag, which later rolled and punctured the ball when the bag was moved.
solution.motive: No malicious intent — it was a complete accident, but he panicked and stayed silent.
solution.proof: The bent safety pin found under the table matches the puncture hole, and witness confirms Arvind was last seen near the bag. No one else had access during the window.
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects with solid alibis: Priya (radio log) and Coach (gym log). Rohan had no reason to help his own team. The pinprick suggests accident, not intent. Arvind’s nervousness wasn’t guilt — it was fear of embarrassment. The safety pin links directly to him as he used it to fix a speaker wire earlier.

case.title: The Case of the Pilfered Bookmarks
case.setting: Central Library, Anand Vihar College, Delhi
case.crime: A rare collection of handcrafted bookmarks, created by students for a cultural fest exhibit, was stolen from the library display cabinet.
case.victim: The College Book Club, especially its president, who curated the collection

suspects.name: Priya Mehta
suspects.personality: Organized, meticulous, passionate about literature, slightly anxious
suspects.motive: She was in charge of the collection and fears being blamed for the theft.
suspects.alibi: Says she was attending a poetry reading in the auditorium from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM.
suspects.secret: She accidentally broke the display lock earlier that day while adjusting the exhibit and didn’t report it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She seems overly defensive and keeps insisting the thief must be an outsider.

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: Charming, lazy, always cracking jokes, obsessed with short-cuts
suspects.motive: Was mocked during the fest for his own bookmark, which he didn’t finish on time.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was napping in the library lounge after skipping his evening class.
suspects.secret: He copied a friend’s bookmark design and passed it off as his own in the contest.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the display case just before closing time, 'adjusting' the bookmarks.

suspects.name: Dr. Arvind Patel
suspects.personality: Strict, traditional, nostalgic, passionate about old things
suspects.motive: Publicly praised the bookmarks as 'reminders of a more thoughtful age.'
suspects.alibi: Was grading papers in his office from 4:30 PM to 7:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He collects vintage stationery and hides it from colleagues, fearing they’d think it unprofessional.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen sketching a bookmark design in his notebook the day before the theft.

suspects.name: Meera Khan
suspects.motive: Her bookmark didn’t make it into the final display due to a judging error, which upset her.
suspects.alibi: Was studying alone at her favorite window table in the library from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM.
suspects.secret: She secretly took a photo of the display every day to remember what could have been.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen staring intently at the empty display case the morning after the theft, looking emotional.

evidence.description: A small, broken silver clasp found near the display cabinet.
evidence.location: Floor beside the Cultural Exhibit case
evidence.significance: Matches the type used on vintage stationery cases—links to someone who collects old items.

evidence.description: A torn corner of a bookmark with a doodle of a sloth wearing sunglasses.
evidence.location: In the library lounge trash can
evidence.significance: Matches Rohan’s unique art style—he often draws the same sloth in class notes.

evidence.description: A librarian reports seeing someone in a beige trench coat near the cabinet around 5:45 PM.
evidence.significance: Dr. Patel often wears a beige trench coat; places him at the scene.

evidence.description: Library security footage shows the cabinet being opened at 5:50 PM by someone using a bent paperclip.
evidence.significance: Shows the lock was picked, not broken—consistent with a nimble, careful attempt.

evidence.description: A sticky note with 'Need more thread – blue and gold' in neat handwriting.
evidence.significance: Matches the colors of Priya’s bookmark; suggests the thief left a note about materials used in the bookmarks.

timeline: 4:00 PM – Meera arrives at the library and sits by the window.
4:30 PM – Dr. Patel enters his office; claims to be grading.
5:00 PM – Priya attends poetry reading in the auditorium.
5:15 PM – Rohan enters the library lounge and lies on the sofa.
5:45 PM – Librarian sees someone in a beige coat near the display.
5:50 PM – Security camera shows figure picking the display lock with a paperclip.
6:00 PM – Meera leaves the library.
6:30 PM – Priya returns to check the display and discovers theft.
7:00 PM – College security is alerted.
red_herrings: The broken silver clasp suggests Dr. Patel stole the bookmarks for his collection.
Rohan’s sloth doodle implies he took the bookmarks out of jealousy.
The trench coat sighting falsely implicates Dr. Patel.

solution.method: She used a bent paperclip to unlock the cabinet (after previously breaking the lock) and took the bookmarks to hide them in her dorm, fearing the broken lock would get her removed as Book Club president.
solution.motive: She panicked about being blamed for the damaged lock and thought removing the bookmarks temporarily would buy time to fix it.
solution.proof: The sticky note with 'Need more thread – blue and gold' matches the unique thread she used in her own bookmark—she wrote it absentmindedly while planning to repair the display later.
solution.how_to_solve: The thief had to know the lock was already damaged. Only Priya knew that. The sticky note has her handwriting and references her materials. The security footage shows a small hand using a paperclip—consistent with her—while Rohan was asleep, Dr. Patel was in his office, and Meera was too far away to have reached the cabinet unnoticed.

case.title: The Case of the Stolen Chai Recipe
case.setting: Canteen at Delhi Shiksha Vihar College
case.crime: The secret recipe for 'Super Masala Chai', a college canteen specialty, was leaked online, causing a rival canteen to copy it.
case.victim: Rajesh Bhai, the canteen owner whose chai recipe was stolen

suspects.name: Priya Mehta
suspects.motive: She runs a popular food blog and wanted viral content.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying for her economics midterm.
suspects.secret: She secretly submitted a food review about the chai last week.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen scribbling notes near the canteen counter during chai preparation.

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: laid-back, prankster, tech-savvy, always on his phone
suspects.motive: He made a bet with friends that he could hack the canteen's 'secret' recipe.
suspects.alibi: Says he was napping in the hostel after a late-night gaming session.
suspects.secret: He has a side hustle creating fake memes about professors.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen taking photos of the canteen spice jars last week.

suspects.name: Mrs. Lata Iyer
suspects.personality: strict, traditional, health-conscious, dislikes overly sweet drinks
suspects.motive: Believes the chai is too sugary and wanted to discourage students from drinking it.
suspects.alibi: Was scanning books in the library between 10 AM and 1 PM.
suspects.secret: She's secretly writing a self-help book titled 'Detox Your Campus Life'.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly criticized Rajesh Bhai’s chai as 'unhealthy' during parent-teacher meeting.

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.personality: quiet, observant, loyal, part-time canteen helper
suspects.motive: No clear motive, but had access to the recipe
suspects.alibi: Was helping Rajesh Bhai prepare samosas in the kitchen that morning.
suspects.secret: He's secretly in love with Priya and copied her chai notes to impress her.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the canteen's private shelf where the recipe was kept.

evidence.description: A crumpled piece of paper with 'Sugar: 3tsp, Ginger: 1cm, Cardamom: 2 pods' written in neat handwriting.
evidence.location: Waste bin near the canteen counter
evidence.significance: Partial recipe — matches the stolen version posted online.

evidence.description: A post on a food blog titled 'The Secret Behind DSVC’s Famous Chai — EXPOSED!' with full recipe.
evidence.significance: Confirms the leak and timing. Blog shows 'Priya Mehta' as author.

evidence.description: A student reported seeing Rohan taking pictures of the canteen spice rack two days prior.
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation to steal the recipe.

evidence.description: A sticky note with 'Do NOT share!' stuck to a locked cupboard in the canteen kitchen.
evidence.significance: Shows recipe was meant to be confidential.

evidence.description: A draft blog post on Priya’s laptop titled 'My Chai Investigation — DON’T PUBLISH'.
evidence.significance: Proves she was researching but had no intent to leak.

evidence.description: Rajesh Bhai confirms Vikram helped prepare samosas and handed him a spice mix at 10:30 AM.
evidence.significance: Vikram had access and opportunity.

evidence.description: A WhatsApp message from Vikram to a friend saying, 'Got the full recipe lol, gonna show Priya I’m cool.'
evidence.significance: Proof he took the recipe and shared it informally.

timeline: 9:00 AM – Canteen opens, Rajesh Bhai begins chai prep.
9:15 AM – Vikram arrives to help with kitchen duties.
10:00 AM – Priya enters canteen, buys chai, takes notes at a table.
10:30 AM – Vikram prepares spice mix under Rajesh’s supervision.
11:00 AM – Rohan seen walking near canteen, yawning (possibly from nap).
11:45 AM – Recipe appears on food blog.
12:00 PM – Rajesh discovers leak, alerts college authorities.
red_herrings: The blog post is under Priya’s name, suggesting she leaked it.
Rohan was photographing spices, making him look like a suspect.

solution.method: Vikram memorized the recipe while helping Rajesh Bhai and texted it to a friend, who then posted it online without telling him.
solution.motive: He wanted to impress Priya by showing he knew the secret recipe.
solution.proof: His WhatsApp message reveals he shared the recipe, and the timeline shows he was the only one with both access and opportunity during prep time.
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects: Priya’s draft shows she didn’t publish intentionally; Rohan’s photos were for memes; Mrs. Iyer was in the library. Vikram had access, was near the recipe, and his message proves he shared it. The actual leak came from his friend’s account, but Vikram is responsible for the initial breach.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Whiteboard Markers
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts & Science, Classroom F3 — a second-floor humanities classroom known for its squeaky chalkboard and AC that never works
case.crime: Someone has been secretly hoarding all the whiteboard markers before lectures, causing chaos during morning classes
case.victim: Dr. Meera Patel, professor of Political Science, and the general sanity of faculty and students

suspects.name: Aryan Malhotra
suspects.personality: organized, ambitious, overly punctual, slightly anxious
suspects.motive: Wants to appear more prepared than others by bringing his own markers; may have taken extra to build a stockpile
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for Economics until class started
suspects.secret: He has a secret fanfiction blog where he writes about college professors
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Always carries a large, overstuffed pencil case with brand-new markers

suspects.name: Professor Nandini Iyer
suspects.personality: eccentric, eco-conscious, absent-minded, passionate about sustainability
suspects.motive: Believes whiteboard markers are wasteful and toxic; may be hiding them to push digital note-taking
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her office grading papers and had no reason to enter F3
suspects.secret: She composts used dry-erase sheets in her office potted plants
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen muttering about 'chemical pollution' near the classroom last week

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: class clown, tech geek, prankster, loyal friend
suspects.motive: Plays harmless pranks; thought disappearing markers would be funny
suspects.alibi: Says he was at the canteen buying samosas before class
suspects.secret: He rigged the classroom bell to play 'Never Gonna Give You Up' last Monday
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed loudly when Dr. Patel couldn’t write on the board

suspects.name: Priya Venkat
suspects.motive: Responsible for classroom supplies; might be hoarding markers to impress the department head
suspects.alibi: Says she was setting up the projector in F3 10 minutes before class
suspects.secret: She collects colored pens and has a shelf at home with over 200 markers
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen taking uncapped markers from the tray and inspecting them

evidence.description: A nearly empty marker tray in Classroom F3 with only two dried-up markers left
evidence.significance: Confirms markers were present but deliberately removed

evidence.description: A blue cap from a whiteboard marker found near the window sill, partially stuck with chewed gum
evidence.significance: Suggests a marker was tampered with or discarded carelessly

evidence.description: Arya, a first-year student, saw Professor Iyer near F3 at 8:45 AM, frowning at the marker tray
evidence.significance: Seems to place Professor Iyer at the scene

evidence.description: Canteen security camera shows Rohan buying samosas at 9:05 AM, two minutes before class
evidence.significance: Supports Rohan’s alibi

evidence.description: A small notebook labeled 'Supply Log' with entries showing Priya signed out 12 markers last week but only returned 2
evidence.significance: Suggests Priya has unaccounted markers

evidence.description: A hidden drawer in the teacher’s desk in F3 containing 8 unused black markers and 3 blue ones
evidence.location: Classroom F3, under false bottom in desk drawer
evidence.significance: The hoard — but who put it there?

evidence.description: Janitor Ramu says he saw Aryan entering F3 at 8:40 AM, looking nervous, and leaving without teaching materials
evidence.significance: Places Aryan in the classroom before anyone else

timeline: 8:30 AM: Classroom F3 is empty; markers are present (per cleaning staff log)
8:40 AM: Janitor sees Aryan near F3, briefly entering and exiting
8:45 AM: Arya sees Professor Iyer standing outside F3, looking at the marker tray
8:50 AM: Priya enters F3 to set up projector
8:55 AM: Rohan buys samosas at canteen (per camera footage)
9:00 AM: Dr. Patel arrives, discovers missing markers, class delayed by 10 minutes
9:15 AM: Student reports mystery to college WhatsApp group, titled 'Marker Mafia Alert'
red_herrings: Professor Iyer’s anti-marker rant during faculty meeting last week
Priya’s unreturned markers in the supply log
Blue marker cap found near window (Rohan’s prank residue)

solution.method: Used her access as TA to stash markers in a secret compartment in the teacher’s desk before class
solution.motive: Wanted to create a 'backup supply' for emergencies but forgot to return them, causing panic
solution.proof: The hidden drawer in the desk contained the exact number of missing markers, and only TAs and faculty had keys to the desk — camera shows no one but Priya opened it that morning
solution.how_to_solve: Eliminate suspects using alibis and evidence: Rohan has solid camera proof; Professor Iyer was only observing; Aryan was seen entering but no proof he took anything. Priya had access, a motive involving responsibility, and the supply log shows a discrepancy. The hidden markers in a desk she accessed confirm it — not malicious, just poorly executed planning.

case.title: The Case of the Missing Meow-tector
case.setting: Delhi Shakti College of Arts and Sciences, near the canteen and library courtyard
case.crime: The campus cat, Whiskers, has gone missing just before the annual fest 'Shakti Utsav'.
case.victim: Whiskers, the beloved campus cat who naps on philosophy books and steals samosas.

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.motive: He once joked about turning Whiskers into a 'spy drone mascot' for the fest.
suspects.alibi: Was in the computer lab uploading drone footage at 5:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He accidentally broke the canteen’s chai kettle and hasn’t confessed.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the library with a net and a shoebox earlier that day.

suspects.name: Dr. Anita Rao
suspects.motive: Publicly complained about Whiskers sneezing on her lecture notes.
suspects.alibi: Was grading papers in her office from 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM.
suspects.secret: She secretly feeds Whiskers plain bread when no one is looking.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen carrying a large air purifier toward her office.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.personality: kind, animal lover, eco-warrior, runs the campus 'Save the Strays' club
suspects.motive: Wanted to have Whiskers vaccinated and microchipped.
suspects.alibi: Was at a club meeting in the auditorium from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM.
suspects.secret: She named Whiskers 'Lord Fluffington' in her diary.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen with a pet carrier near the biology lab.

suspects.name: Bunty Patel
suspects.personality: grumpy, lazy, hates cats, loves order
suspects.motive: Caught Whiskers stealing three samosas last week and swore revenge.
suspects.alibi: Claimed to be cleaning the canteen storeroom from 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM.
suspects.secret: He hides expired snacks in the same storeroom to avoid getting scolded.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refused to answer questions at first and mumbled about 'feline freeloaders'.

evidence.description: A small blue pet carrier found behind the biology lab with cat hair and a chewed samosa wrapper.
evidence.location: Behind the biology lab near the drainage pipe
evidence.significance: Suggests someone tried to transport Whiskers.

evidence.description: A drone with a tiny camera and a note: 'Operation Flufflift – Phase 1'.
evidence.location: On the rooftop, near the engineering department
evidence.significance: Looks like a plan to kidnap Whiskers for fun.

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Priya entering the canteen with the pet carrier at 4:45 PM.
evidence.significance: Places a suspect near Whiskers’ usual snack spot.

evidence.description: A student saw Dr. Rao sneezing violently near the library garden at 4:15 PM.
evidence.significance: Suggests she might’ve wanted Whiskers gone due to allergies.

evidence.description: A torn piece of canteen apron with 'Bunty' stitched on it, found near the pet carrier.
evidence.significance: Links Bunty to the carrier.

evidence.description: A milk bowl with Whiskers’ paw print, still fresh, found under a bench in the library garden.
evidence.significance: Shows Whiskers was there recently and wasn't stressed.

evidence.description: Drone footage from Rohan’s device shows Whiskers napping peacefully at 4:55 PM.
evidence.significance: Confirms Whiskers was safe after most suspects were last seen.

timeline: 4:00 PM – Whiskers seen stealing samosas from canteen counter.
4:15 PM – Dr. Rao sneezes near library garden after Whiskers walks by.
4:45 PM – Priya enters canteen with pet carrier (security footage).
5:00 PM – Rohan in computer lab uploading drone videos.
5:10 PM – Whiskers last seen napping under philosophy stack in library (confirmed by drone footage).
6:00 PM – Students report Whiskers missing; fest mascot costume left unused.
6:30 PM – Search begins across campus.
red_herrings: The drone and 'Operation Flufflift' note make Rohan look guilty.
Bunty’s torn apron near the carrier suggests he trapped Whiskers.
Priya entering canteen with a carrier seems suspicious.

solution.method: She gently placed Whiskers in the carrier to take him to the vet for vaccination, as part of her 'Save the Strays' duty.
solution.motive: She wanted to get Whiskers vaccinated before the fest crowds arrived.
solution.proof: The pet carrier has her 'Save the Strays' club sticker inside, and the vet clinic confirms she brought Whiskers in at 5:45 PM.
solution.how_to_solve: The drone footage proves Whiskers was safe after 5:10 PM, eliminating early suspects. Priya’s alibi is weak because her club meeting started at 5:00 PM, but she wasn’t seen until 5:30 PM. The carrier has her club’s sticker, and the chewed samosa shows Whiskers wasn’t distressed—just full. The torn apron was caught when Bunty tripped near the lab earlier and has no connection. Priya didn’t announce her plan to avoid drawing attention and causing a scene.

case.title: The Case of the Mysterious Marked Underwear
case.setting: Hostel Block C, Shri Ram College of Arts and Science, Mumbai
case.crime: A conspiracy to swap and mark laundry items across hostel rooms to frame someone for prank vandalism
case.victim: Rohan Mehta, a second-year economics student

suspects.name: Ananya Patel
suspects.personality: Organized, competitive, quietly mischievous, loves pranks
suspects.motive: Wanted to prank Rohan for winning the inter-hostel quiz she lost
suspects.alibi: Claimed she was in the library studying for her political science midterm
suspects.secret: She secretly runs a meme page mocking college faculty
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the laundry room late at night with a marker pen

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.motive: No real motive, but has a history of mixing up laundry accidentally
suspects.alibi: Was binge-watching a web series in his room with roommates
suspects.secret: He owes the canteen owner 800 rupees and is avoiding him
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Admitted to borrowing Rohan’s blue sweater once by mistake

suspects.name: Dr. Meenakshi Iyer
suspects.motive: Believes in discipline and wanted to teach pranksters a lesson
suspects.alibi: Was in her office drafting hostel conduct guidelines
suspects.secret: She writes anonymous motivational notes left in laundry baskets
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Has master key access and was seen collecting laundry logs

evidence.description: A pair of Rohan’s boxers with 'Quiz Loser' written in black marker
evidence.significance: Proof of targeted prank; handwriting matches Ananya’s

evidence.description: Blue sweater with 'Property of Vikram' safety-pinned to pocket
evidence.location: Lost & Found bin near laundry room
evidence.significance: Suggests Vikram marks his clothes, but he claims he never does

evidence.description: Laundry room security camera log showing timestamped entry
evidence.significance: Shows Ananya entered the laundry room at 10:47 PM the night before

evidence.description: A pink gel pen with 'Ananya' engraved on it, found near detergent shelf
evidence.significance: Same brand as the marker used on the boxers

evidence.description: A first-year student saw someone wearing a yellow hoodie near the laundry late at night
evidence.significance: Ananya owns a yellow hoodie; Vikram does not

timeline: 6:00 PM – Rohan drops off laundry in common basket
8:30 PM – Vikram watches web series in room with friends
10:00 PM – Dr. Iyer returns to office after dinner
10:47 PM – Security log shows Ananya enters laundry room
10:52 PM – First-year witness sees yellow hoodie figure near laundry
11:15 PM – Vikram orders late-night poha from canteen
7:30 AM – Rohan finds marked underwear in his basket
red_herrings: The labeled blue sweater implies Vikram marks clothes, suggesting he might tamper with laundry
Vikram’s past laundry mix-ups make him seem careless or possibly vindictive

solution.method: She entered the laundry room after hours, took Rohan’s clothes, wrote 'Quiz Loser' on his boxers using her marker, and returned the basket
solution.motive: To play a light-hearted revenge prank after losing the quiz competition to Rohan
solution.proof: Security log timestamp + witness sighting of yellow hoodie + her pen found at scene + handwriting match on the boxers
solution.how_to_solve: Compare the timeline: Vikram has an alibi with friends and ordered food at 11:15 PM, making a late-night laundry trip impossible. Dr. Iyer was in her office. Only Ananya has no solid alibi, appears on camera, matches the witness description, and left behind personal belongings linked to the prank

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Shuttlecocks
case.setting: Indira Gandhi College of Physical Education, Pune
case.crime: All 48 official tournament-grade badminton shuttlecocks disappeared from the sports storeroom the night before the inter-college championship
case.victim: College badminton team and tournament organizers

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.motive: Wants to delay the tournament so he can recover from a minor ankle injury
suspects.alibi: Claims he was meditating in the yoga shed from 7 PM to 9 PM
suspects.secret: Borrowed his roommate's lucky sweatband without permission
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Actively suggested rescheduling the tournament during the team meeting

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Wanted to prank the team for forgetting her birthday
suspects.alibi: Says she was editing a video in the computer lab until 8:30 PM
suspects.secret: Accidentally deleted the team's practice footage and hasn’t told anyone
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the storeroom with a large bag after dinner

suspects.name: Coach Dilip Rao
suspects.motive: Worried the expensive shuttlecocks would be wasted if players didn’t take the match seriously
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home grading player performance sheets
suspects.secret: Bought cheaper shuttlecocks online last week to replace worn ones
suspects.suspicious_behavior: First person to suggest the shuttlecocks were 'misplaced' not stolen

suspects.name: Arvind Patel
suspects.motive: No direct motive
suspects.alibi: Says he was cleaning the gymnasium until 7:30 PM, then went home
suspects.secret: Has been feeding a family of street dogs behind the storeroom and hides food there
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen unlocking the storeroom after hours with a spare key

evidence.description: A torn piece of green cloth caught on the storeroom window latch
evidence.location: Inside storeroom, near the back window
evidence.significance: Suggests someone entered through the window

evidence.description: A receipt for 50 budget shuttlecocks from an online store, dated 3 days ago
evidence.location: In Coach Rao's office trash bin
evidence.significance: Suggests the coach might have replaced the shuttlecocks

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Priya walking toward the storeroom at 7:45 PM with a large backpack
evidence.significance: Makes Priya look suspicious

evidence.description: A nest made of goose feathers and string behind a loose brick near the storeroom
evidence.significance: Reveals the shuttlecocks were dismantled for nesting material

evidence.description: A student reports seeing Arvind feeding pigeons near the storeroom every evening
evidence.significance: Connects Arvind to bird activity near the storeroom

evidence.description: Goose feathers and cork scraps found hidden behind a ventilation panel
evidence.significance: Indicates shuttlecocks were taken apart on-site

evidence.description: Coach Rao mentions that goose feathers have been disappearing from old shuttlecocks all week
evidence.significance: Points to animal involvement

timeline: 5:00 PM – Storeroom last used; 48 shuttlecocks accounted for
5:30 PM – Arvind cleans gym and storeroom area, seen by two students
6:00 PM – Team practice ends; storeroom locked by Coach Rao
7:00 PM – Rohan at yoga shed (witnessed by instructor)
7:45 PM – Priya seen on camera near storeroom with backpack
8:00 PM – Arvind goes home (confirmed by neighbor)
9:30 PM – Coach Rao calls campus security to report missing shuttlecocks
red_herrings: The torn green cloth (actually from a gardener’s jacket caught while pruning near the window)
Priya’s late visit to the storeroom (she was retrieving her drone used to film the prank video)
Coach Rao’s receipt for cheap shuttlecocks (he bought them for the junior team, not to replace the stolen ones)

solution.culprit: A pair of love-struck jungle mynas (birds)
solution.method: Birds pried loose a ventilation panel, entered the storeroom over several days, dismantled shuttlecocks, and took the feathers to build a nest behind the outer wall
solution.motive: Natural nesting instinct – goose feathers are ideal for nest-building
solution.proof: The nest made of shuttlecock feathers found behind the storeroom, along with cork bits and the open ventilation panel showing claw marks
solution.how_to_solve: Combine the witness report about birds, the feathers in the nest, the attic debris, and the coach’s comment about missing feathers. Realize the theft was gradual, not one-night. The torn cloth, receipt, and Priya’s visit are distractions. The ventilation panel is too small for a human, but perfect for birds.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Table Reserver
case.setting: Central Library at Indraprastha College of Technology
case.crime: Chaotic and fake study table reservations disrupting students during exam season
case.victim: Second-year engineering students preparing for midterms

suspects.name: Riya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted to secure the best table for her study group and may have overstepped
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library’s group study room reviewing physics notes from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM
suspects.secret: She accidentally erased someone else’s reservation while trying to book her own
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the reservation board erasing a name quickly

suspects.name: Amit Patel
suspects.motive: Likes causing harmless chaos for fun, especially during stressful times
suspects.alibi: Says he was at the college canteen eating samosas with friends from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM
suspects.secret: Created a fake app mockup that looks like the library reservation system
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was heard boasting, 'I’ve reserved Table 7 for the next week — no one can touch it!'

suspects.name: Prof. Nandini Iyer
suspects.motive: Disapproves of reservation misuse and might have taken action to discourage it
suspects.alibi: Was teaching a class from 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM, then in her office until 6:30 PM
suspects.secret: Her nephew is failing her class and she’s been giving him extra help at Table 6
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen writing on the reservation board with a bold red marker

suspects.name: Chandan Kumar
suspects.motive: Wants to prove students can't be trusted with self-reservation
suspects.alibi: Claims he was restocking shelves in the reference section from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM
suspects.secret: He’s been secretly applying to be the new library manager and wants to show initiative
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen collecting reservation slips from the board and shredding them

evidence.description: A crumpled reservation slip with 'Table 7 - Amit Patel - 4:00 PM' written in bold, found in the library trash can.
evidence.significance: Suggests Amit reserved Table 7, but the time doesn’t match when tables are cleared.

evidence.description: Library security camera still shows Riya erasing a name from the board at 4:10 PM, then writing her group's name.
evidence.significance: She tampered with the board, but only corrected her own mistake.

evidence.description: A sticky note with a hand-drawn 'Reservation App v1.0' interface sketch, labeled 'Just for fun.'
evidence.location: Inside Amit’s notebook, left on a canteen table
evidence.significance: Shows he enjoys joking about reservations but didn’t actually create a real system.

evidence.description: A red marker found in Prof. Iyer’s coat pocket, matching the one used to write 'Reserved - Faculty Use Only' on Table 6.
evidence.significance: She marked a table, but had proper authority and reason.

evidence.description: A shredded pile of reservation slips in the library’s disposal bin, including some with correct times.
evidence.significance: Someone destroyed valid reservations—points to Chandan, who had access.

evidence.description: Time-stamped log from the library printer showing 12 fake reservation slips printed at 3:45 AM, all from a staff account.
evidence.significance: Proves fake slips were printed early morning using staff credentials.

evidence.description: A student reports seeing Chandan near the board at 7:00 AM placing new 'reserved' slips before anyone arrived.
evidence.significance: Confirms he planted fake reservations to discourage misuse.

timeline: 3:45 AM - Library printer logs staff account printing 12 fake reservation slips
4:00 PM - Library opens; students arrive to find tables 'reserved' with suspicious slips
4:10 PM - Security still shows Riya erasing and rewriting on board
4:30 PM - Amit seen at canteen, joking about his 'unbreakable reservation'
5:00 PM - Prof. Iyer marks Table 6 with red 'Faculty Use' tag
5:30 PM - Chandan collects old slips from board, some still valid
6:00 PM - Students file complaint to library manager about reservation chaos
red_herrings: Amit’s fake app sketch makes him seem like a tech-based prankster
Riya’s erasing looks like sabotage, but was just a correction
Prof. Iyer’s red marker seems suspicious, but she used it properly

solution.method: Used his staff access to print fake reservation slips at 3:45 AM and placed them on tables to make students think spots were taken, hoping they’d stop reserving early
solution.motive: Believes students abuse the reservation system and wanted to teach them a lesson while proving his worth for a promotion
solution.proof: Printer log shows staff account used at 3:45 AM, and witness saw him placing slips early; shredding valid slips shows pattern of interference
solution.how_to_solve: The key is the printer log: only staff have access. The fake slips couldn’t have been made by students. Combined with the early timing and witness account, only Chandan fits. His shredding of valid slips shows he’s been taking unilateral action against reservations all along.

case.title: The Case of the Switched Lunch Boxes
case.setting: St. Clara's College for Arts and Science, Chennai – Central Canteen
case.crime: Mysterious switching of lunch box labels in the canteen storage shelf, causing students to eat each other's meals
case.victim: Multiple students, primarily Ravi, who received a spice-heavy lunch not meant for him

suspects.name: Priya Menon
suspects.motive: Wanted to prank Ravi for copying her assignment without asking
suspects.alibi: Was in the library studying for her sociology quiz
suspects.secret: She has been secretly dating the canteen manager’s son
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the storage shelf just before lunch, adjusting her lunch box

suspects.name: Ravi Iyer
suspects.personality: Lazy, humorous, forgetful, loves spicy food
suspects.motive: To create chaos and get a spicier meal than his mother packed
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the restroom during the switch
suspects.secret: He once accidentally broke the canteen’s microwave and never told anyone
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed unusually hard when he found someone else’s spicy lunch in his box

suspects.name: Professor Arvind Patel
suspects.personality: Eccentric, forgetful, kind-hearted, obsessed with order
suspects.motive: Believes students should learn responsibility; wanted to teach a lesson about labeling
suspects.alibi: Was grading papers in his office
suspects.secret: He mislabels his own coffee mugs all the time
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen muttering about 'chaotic labeling systems' near the shelf

suspects.name: Babloo Sharma
suspects.personality: Goofy, clumsy, helpful, talks to himself
suspects.motive: Accidentally mixed up the labels while cleaning the shelf
suspects.alibi: Was wiping tables during lunch prep
suspects.secret: Can't read English well—he only understands Hindi labels
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen peeling off and re-sticking labels while cleaning

evidence.description: A lunch box with a sticker that reads 'Ravi - No Spice' now contains a very spicy curry dish.
evidence.significance: Proof that labels were switched

evidence.description: Small pile of removed label stickers found near the dustbin.
evidence.significance: Someone deliberately removed and reapplied labels

evidence.description: A first-year student saw Professor Patel near the shelf muttering, 'Labels must be orderly!'
evidence.significance: Makes the professor look suspicious

evidence.description: Canteen security camera footage (low quality) shows Babloo bending near the shelf with a cloth and peeling something.
evidence.significance: Suggests Babloo tampered with the labels

evidence.description: A Hindi-labeled lunch box with 'Babloo - Homemade' is missing its sticker, now found stuck on Ravi’s box.
evidence.significance: Babloo’s sticker was mistakenly placed on Ravi’s box

timeline: 11:45 AM: Students place labeled lunch boxes on the canteen storage shelf.
12:00 PM: Babloo begins cleaning the canteen area, including around the shelf.
12:10 PM: Professor Patel walks by, complains about messy labels, does not touch shelf.
12:15 PM: Priya adjusts her lunch box but doesn’t remove the label.
12:20 PM: Lunch distribution begins; confusion erupts when Ravi gets a spicy meal.
12:25 PM: Investigation starts; students gather around the shelf.
red_herrings: Professor Patel’s outburst about labeling makes him seem like a strict prankster.
Priya’s tension with Ravi suggests a targeted prank.

solution.method: While cleaning, Babloo peeled off wrinkled labels to wipe the shelf and stuck them back incorrectly, not realizing some were in English. He mistook 'Ravi - No Spice' for an empty label and placed his own Hindi sticker on it.
