solution.motive: Accidental mix-up due to poor English literacy and desire to keep the area clean.
solution.proof: Ravi’s box has Babloo’s Hindi label, and the security footage shows him reapplying stickers haphazardly.
solution.how_to_solve: Realize that the switch wasn’t intentional—no one would label a box in Hindi if pranking Ravi. Babloo’s secret (illiteracy in English) explains why he didn’t understand the labels. The misplaced Hindi sticker is the key clue.

case.title: The Case of the Missing Sapphire Pen
case.setting: St. Aravind College of Arts and Science, Chennai - Room 204, Economics Department
case.crime: Professor Mehta's favorite sapphire-blue fountain pen has gone missing from his desk during class.
case.victim: Professor Rajan Mehta, a beloved economics lecturer known for his old-school charm and signature pen.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: She admires the pen and wanted to borrow it to take notes in another class but was too shy to ask.
suspects.alibi: Was sitting in the front row the entire lecture, taking notes.
suspects.secret: She has a crush on Professor Mehta’s teaching assistant and was doodling his initials in her notebook.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Acted flustered when the pen was mentioned and quickly closed her notebook.

suspects.name: Arjun Patel
suspects.motive: Once joked about 'borrowing' the pen to replace it with a cheap replica as a gag.
suspects.alibi: Was filming a TikTok-style video on his phone during the break before class.
suspects.secret: He accidentally spilled coffee on his own notebook and was trying to hide it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed too loudly when the professor announced the pen was missing.

suspects.name: Sneha Desai
suspects.motive: She thought the pen looked like one her little brother lost and wanted to check if it was his.
suspects.alibi: Was sketching in her drawing pad during the lecture, sitting near the window.
suspects.secret: She drew a detailed caricature of Professor Mehta with a giant pen, which she doesn’t want him to see.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Hid her sketchpad under her bag when the professor approached.

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: Feels overshadowed by the professor’s theatrical style and resents being overlooked.
suspects.alibi: Was grading papers in the department office during the lecture.
suspects.secret: He applied for the professor’s upcoming sabbatical replacement position and is anxious about it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested the professor might have just misplaced it, which seemed dismissive.

evidence.description: A single blue ink stain on Arjun’s sleeve, still slightly wet.
evidence.significance: Suggests recent contact with a blue pen.

evidence.description: A photo on Priya’s desk of her holding a similar-looking pen at a college fair.
evidence.significance: Implies she owns a similar pen, possibly hinting at a motive to steal an identical one.

evidence.description: A crumpled note in the classroom trash can with 'I must find the pen before he notices' scribbled in blue ink.
evidence.location: At the bottom of the classroom’s waste bin.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone knew it was missing early and panicked.

evidence.description: Arjun’s phone shows a video timestamped five minutes before class started, showing him filming near the professor’s desk.
evidence.significance: Places him near the desk right before class with a device that could record theft.

evidence.description: The missing sapphire pen is found tucked inside a hollowed-out copy of 'Principles of Economics' on the bookshelf, still capped.
evidence.location: Inside a hollowed book on the shelf behind the professor’s desk.
evidence.significance: The pen was never taken from the classroom—just hidden.

timeline: 10:00 AM: Professor Mehta places his sapphire pen on his desk before writing on the board.
10:05 AM: Students settle into seats; lecture begins.
10:15 AM: Professor turns around to write on board; pen is still on desk.
10:18 AM: Sneha drops her pencil; bends down to pick it up—briefly out of sight.
10:20 AM: Professor reaches for pen—it’s gone.
10:21 AM: Professor announces the pen missing; class murmurs.
red_herrings: The ink stain on Arjun's sleeve (he spilled ink while fixing a leaky pen earlier).
The crumpled note in the trash (written by Priya, who panicked after realizing she mistakenly took the pen briefly).
Priya’s photo with a similar pen (it's a promotional pen from an event, not the same model).

solution.method: When she dropped her pencil and bent down, she saw the pen near the edge of the desk and impulsively picked it up, thinking it had fallen. Fearing blame, she hid it in the hollowed book on the shelf.
solution.motive: She panicked after accidentally picking it up, thinking she’d be accused of stealing.
solution.proof: During inspection, a tiny sketch of the pen is found in Sneha’s drawing pad with the note: 'Hid it in the book, hope no one finds it.'
solution.how_to_solve: The timeline shows the pen disappeared between 10:15 and 10:20. Only Sneha was out of sight during that window (when she dropped her pencil). The hidden pen was never removed from the room, and the sketchpad confession confirms her guilt. Other evidence is misleading but can be logically dismissed: Arjun’s ink stain is from another pen, Priya’s note was guilt over briefly holding it, and Vikram was in another room.

case.title: The Case of the Vandalized Fest Poster
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College - Main Campus Notice Board near Cafeteria
case.crime: The official poster for the upcoming 'Rang-E-Josh Cultural Fest' was found defaced with scribbles and a cartoonish doodle of a dancing goat wearing glasses
case.victim: Student Council and Cultural Committee

suspects.name: Aryan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted to prank the council after being rejected as event host
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the cafeteria eating samosas at the time
suspects.secret: Secretly has a crush on the council president
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed when seeing the defaced poster and said, 'Now it actually looks fun!'

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Angry about last-minute changes to fest schedule affecting her debate event
suspects.alibi: Says she was studying in the library’s silent zone
suspects.secret: Copied parts of her sociology assignment from a senior
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen glaring at the poster the previous day, muttering about 'amateur design'

suspects.name: Rahul Patil
suspects.motive: Believes the fest lacks creativity and wanted to 'improve' the poster
suspects.alibi: Claims he was sketching in his notebook near the amphitheater
suspects.secret: Runs an anonymous college meme page
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His sketchbook has doodles of goats with glasses; he can't explain why

suspects.name: Professor Meenakshi Iyer
suspects.motive: Disapproves of student-led cultural events distracting from academics
suspects.alibi: Was in a department meeting from 10 AM to 12 PM
suspects.secret: Secretly submits poetry to a literary magazine under a pen name
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen frowning at the fest posters every morning

evidence.description: A thick black marker pen found near the notice board, partially hidden under a bench
evidence.location: Under the bench near the cafeteria notice board
evidence.significance: Same marker used to deface the poster, brand is 'InkBold Max'

evidence.description: A torn corner of a sketch paper with a doodle of a goat in glasses, matching the poster vandalism
evidence.location: Behind Rahul's usual bench in the amphitheater
evidence.significance: Matches the style on the poster; links to Rahul

evidence.description: Photo posted on anonymous campus meme page at 1:15 PM showing defaced poster with caption: 'Finally got the vibes right!'
evidence.significance: Suggests insider involvement; page run by Rahul

evidence.description: Cafeteria vendor states Aryan bought two samosas at 12:45 PM and left at 1:05 PM
evidence.significance: Supports Aryan's alibi

evidence.description: A sticky note with 'Fix poster design – too boring' in messy handwriting, found crumpled in library bin
evidence.significance: Matches Priya's handwriting sample; shows frustration

evidence.description: Meeting minutes from faculty meeting listing Prof. Iyer present from 10 AM to 12 PM
evidence.significance: Solid alibi for Prof. Iyer

evidence.description: A photo in the student council’s printer tray showing a test print of the original poster, with the goat doodle faintly visible under a Post-it
evidence.significance: Proves doodle was made before the defacement, using council materials

timeline: 10:00 AM - Professor Iyer attends department meeting
11:30 AM - Priya seen in library, appears upset
11:45 AM - Rahul seen sketching near amphitheater
12:30 PM - Aryan enters cafeteria, orders samosas
1:00 PM - Poster observed intact by passing student
1:10 PM - Defaced poster discovered by council volunteer
1:15 PM - Meme posted online showing vandalized poster
red_herrings: Rahul's goat doodles and meme page activity suggest he defaced the poster
Priya's angry note and critique of the poster design imply motive
Aryan's public joke about the poster makes him seem guilty despite alibi

solution.method: Used council printer to add the goat doodle to a test print, then snuck back at 12:55 PM to replace the original poster with the fake one
solution.motive: Wanted revenge for being rejected as host and to make the poster 'funny' like his humor
solution.proof: Test print with doodle under Post-it matches defaced poster exactly; only someone with council access could do this, and Aryan volunteered there last week
solution.how_to_solve: Check evidence chain: the defacement was too clean for marker vandalism; the real clue is the test print with the hidden doodle. Only someone with printer access could do this. Aryan had access and motive. His alibi is solid for after 12:45 PM, but the switch happened before 1:00 PM. Timeline shows he could have slipped out earlier.

case.title: The Case of the Midnight Drummer
case.setting: Lakshmi Narayan Engineering College Hostel Block B, Girls' Wing
case.crime: Repeated loud drumming noises heard every night at 12:15 AM, disturbing residents
case.victim: Hostel residents of Block B who are sleep-deprived and annoyed

suspects.name: Aanya Patel
suspects.motive: Practices tabla at odd hours for upcoming cultural fest performance
suspects.alibi: Claims she was asleep by 11:30 PM in her room with her roommate
suspects.secret: She secretly entered a music competition she didn’t tell anyone about
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen carrying a duffel bag late at night; denies knowing anything about drumming

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.motive: Likes to pull harmless pranks using tech gadgets
suspects.alibi: Says he was video gaming in his room on Discord with friends
suspects.secret: Built a remote-controlled prank machine that plays random sounds
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughs nervously when drumming is mentioned; owns a speaker system

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: None — actually filed the first noise complaint
suspects.alibi: Claims she was studying in the library until 12:30 AM
suspects.secret: Is scared of the dark and sleeps with a nightlight and white noise app
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Tried to inspect everyone’s rooms aggressively, making her seem over-involved

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: Disapproves of late-night activities and suspects students are partying
suspects.alibi: Says he was in his ground-floor office, awake and on duty
suspects.secret: Sleeps with a loud snore recording to help him sleep — plays it from his phone
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly eager to punish someone; was seen near the staircase at 12:15 AM

evidence.description: A small drumstick wrapped in green tape found near the staircase exit
evidence.location: Bottom of the emergency staircase, Block B
evidence.significance: Matches the description of Aanya’s tabla sticks

evidence.description: Sound recording from a student’s phone that captures drumming at exactly 12:15 AM
evidence.significance: Confirms timing and nature of noise; reveals it's not live drumming but a looped audio track

evidence.description: A first-year student saw someone in a hoodie leaving the common room around 12:20 AM
evidence.significance: Suggests someone was present there late

evidence.description: A Bluetooth speaker hidden inside a hollowed-out textbook on a shelf in the common room
evidence.significance: Was programmed to play drum loop every night at 12:15 AM

evidence.description: Rohan’s Discord log shows he was online playing games from 11 PM to 1:30 AM on the nights in question
evidence.location: Verified by friend and server timestamp
evidence.significance: Supports his alibi

evidence.description: Warden Vikram was seen checking doors with a flashlight at 12:15 AM
evidence.significance: Looks suspicious but was part of routine patrol

evidence.description: Priya’s library login card shows she checked in at 8 PM and out at 12:25 AM
evidence.significance: Confirms her alibi

timeline: 11:00 PM: Hostel gates locked, lights out rule begins
11:30 PM: Aanya retires to room, roommate confirms she's there
11:45 PM: Rohan logs into Discord game server
12:00 AM: Priya leaves library, walks back to hostel
12:15 AM: Loud drumming noise echoes through Block B (every night for 5 nights)
12:20 AM: First-year student sees hooded figure leaving common room
12:25 AM: Priya enters hostel, scans card
12:30 AM: Drumming stops, speaker turns off automatically
red_herrings: Green-taped drumstick found near staircase
Hooded figure seen near common room
Warden patrolling at midnight

solution.method: Used a Bluetooth speaker hidden in a book and programmed it to play a 5-minute loop of drumming sounds at 12:15 AM daily
solution.motive: Wanted to prank students and see how long it would take someone to find the 'ghost drummer'
solution.proof: Speaker found with Rohan’s fingerprint; programmed via his phone (metadata shows creation of audio file)
solution.how_to_solve: Player must notice the drumming is too consistent to be live (digital evidence). Library log and Discord confirm alibis. Drumstick is a red herring. Speaker hidden in common room with tech-savvy culprit fits. Rohan’s prankster personality and secret tech interest point to him.

case.title: The Case of the Cracked Campus Wi-Fi
case.setting: Vidya Sagar College of Engineering, Mumbai – Central Computer Lab & Student Hub
case.crime: College Wi-Fi password was hacked and changed, locking out 2000+ students and staff during mid-semester exams week
case.victim: The college administration and student body, especially final-year students preparing for project submissions

suspects.name: Arjun Mehta
suspects.motive: Believes college restricts internet access unfairly; wants to expose weak security
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library studying for Operating Systems exam from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM
suspects.secret: He runs an anonymous blog criticizing college policies
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the admin server room earlier in the week asking about network protocols

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.motive: Her project submission was due online the next morning; she didn’t finish and may have wanted to delay the deadline by causing chaos
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her hostel room editing her thesis alone from 7:30 PM to 10:00 PM
suspects.secret: She plagiarized part of her project and fears detection
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Asked a friend how to change router settings 'for a prank' two days prior

suspects.name: Prof. Rajiv Nair
suspects.motive: Recently denied a promotion; suspects the head of department of sabotaging his career
suspects.alibi: Reports he was at home grading papers from 6:30 PM onward; no witnesses
suspects.secret: He has been using college servers to mine cryptocurrency on the side
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was last known person to log into the network admin panel before the hack

evidence.description: Login logs show network admin panel accessed at 7:47 PM from IP address 192.168.1.15 (student lab computer #7)
evidence.significance: Pinpoints time and device used to change password

evidence.description: A sticky note with the new Wi-Fi password 'V!dya#FREEnet' found crumpled in a bin near Arjun’s usual seat in the library
evidence.significance: Suggests Arjun knew the new password

evidence.description: Cryptocurrency mining software detected on Prof. Nair’s registered device via college network scan
evidence.significance: Shows misuse of college resources, but unrelated to the hack

evidence.description: Hostel warden reports seeing Priya leave her room at 7:15 PM and return at 8:05 PM, contradicting her alibi
evidence.location: Hostel gate logbook and witness statement
evidence.significance: Breaks her alibi

evidence.description: USB drive labeled 'OS Notes' found in lab computer #7; contains a script named 'pw_reset_v1.py'
evidence.significance: Direct link to method of hack

evidence.description: Lab assistant recalls seeing Arjun in the lab at 7:30 PM but leaving before 7:45 PM
evidence.significance: Placed suspect near crime scene

evidence.description: Printout of network architecture diagram with admin path highlighted, found in trash near professor's office
evidence.significance: Suggests inside knowledge, points to faculty

timeline: 6:00 PM – College Wi-Fi operational normally
6:45 PM – Arjun Mehta seen entering library, according to security log
7:00 PM – Priya Deshmukh texts friend: 'Need to go offline. Too much pressure.'
7:15 PM – Hostel warden sees Priya leave her room
7:30 PM – Arjun briefly enters computer lab to 'retrieve a forgotten notebook' (per lab assistant)
7:47 PM – Admin panel accessed from IP 192.168.1.15 (lab computer #7)
7:50 PM – Wi-Fi goes down across campus
8:00 PM – Prof. Nair remotely logs into college server from home IP for grading
8:05 PM – Priya returns to hostel, seen by warden
9:00 PM – College IT team confirms password changed; no backdoor access available
red_herrings: Arjun’s blog criticizing the college’s tech policies makes him seem ideologically motivated
Prof. Nair’s cryptocurrency mining suggests he has hacking skills and motive for retaliation
The network diagram near the professor's office implies faculty involvement
The sticky note with the password near Arjun’s seat suggests prior knowledge

solution.method: Used lab computer #7 to run a Python script she copied from an online forum to reset the Wi-Fi password, hoping to delay project deadlines due to technical issues
solution.motive: Panicked about incomplete project and fear of plagiarism exposure; wanted system failure as an excuse for delay
solution.proof: USB drive with her name on it (from file metadata) found in lab computer #7, containing the script and a text file titled 'Project_Delay_Idea.txt'
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference the timeline: Priya broke her alibi by leaving her room during the critical window. The USB drive in computer #7 was used at the exact time of the hack. Though Arjun was near the scene, the lab assistant confirms he left before the access time. Prof. Nair accessed the system after the hack. The script on the USB has user-specific metadata linking to Priya’s college login. The sticky note and crypto mining are distractions.

case.title: The Case of the Shattered Stage
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, Arts Block A, Cultural Fest Stage
case.crime: Sabotage of the main stage decorations two hours before the inauguration of the annual cultural fest
case.victim: Cultural fest committee and its organizing team

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wants to take over as fest director after disliking current design theme led by senior panel
suspects.alibi: Claims he was rehearsing for his band performance in basement music room
suspects.secret: Secretly dating the fest director's ex-girlfriend
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Insisted on being first to inspect the damage and offered to 'fix' it quickly

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Her elaborate rangoli-based stage design was rejected in favor of a more 'urban' theme
suspects.alibi: Says she was sketching ideas in the rooftop garden
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing scathing satirical cartoons about the fest committee online
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near stage storage closet the previous night, acting furtive

suspects.name: Professor Vinod Rao
suspects.personality: Traditional, stern, values discipline, resentful of 'excessive festivity'
suspects.motive: Believes the fest distracts from academics; wanted to delay it due to midterms
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers in his office until 8:00 PM
suspects.secret: Submitted a formal complaint to the dean about fest scheduling, fearing low academic performance
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made a public comment earlier that 'this fest will collapse under its own glitter'

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: Jovial prankster, tech-savvy, impulsive, loyal to friends
suspects.motive: Best friend was disqualified from stand-up comedy finals over controversial joke
suspects.alibi: Says he was live-streaming gaming with friends online
suspects.secret: Built a prank drone with friends meant to drop fake confetti at inauguration
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughs nervously when asked about drones; mentions 'accidents happen' too casually

evidence.description: A shattered fiberglass peacock statue — centerpiece of the stage — covered in black spray paint with 'GARBAGE' tagged on it
evidence.significance: Main decorative element destroyed; vandalism suggests personal anger

evidence.description: A single blue thread caught on a broken bolt near the storage cabinet
evidence.significance: Matches the uniform of stage crew, but Arjun wore blue jeans that evening — misdirection

evidence.description: Timestamped security camera footage shows a shadowy figure near the storage room at 6:42 PM, wearing a hoodie — face not visible
evidence.significance: Confirms sabotage occurred before 7:00 PM; time-critical evidence

evidence.description: A small drone with a broken propeller, recovered from behind stage curtains
evidence.significance: Looks like sabotage tool — but has no paint or debris; actually a failed prank device

evidence.description: Rohan’s live-stream footage shows him online at 6:30–7:15 PM, but the stream can be looped
evidence.significance: Alibi appears solid, but tech-savvy users could fake it

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing Professor Rao near the Arts Block at 6:50 PM, muttering about 'waste of time'
evidence.significance: Places professor near crime scene; aligns with motive

evidence.description: A sketchbook found in rooftop garden with violent scribbles over fest logo and the words 'burn it all' — dated today
evidence.significance: Looks like Priya's rage — but she denies ownership; planted as red herring

timeline: 5:30 PM – Stage crew leaves after final setup check
6:00 PM – Students begin gathering for 8:00 PM inauguration
6:30 PM – Rohan starts online gaming stream
6:42 PM – Shadowy figure seen entering storage room on CCTV
6:50 PM – Janitor sees Professor Rao near Arts Block
7:00 PM – Priya seen entering library via main gate (access card log)
7:15 PM – Fest committee discovers vandalism
7:20 PM – College security alerted; investigation begins
red_herrings: The drone found backstage suggests a tech-based sabotage, but it was a failed prank
The sketchbook with violent notes appears to implicate Priya but was planted
Security footage of hoodie figure leads to assumption of sneak attack, but hooded figures common in college
Professor Rao’s public criticism and sighting near scene, but he was only walking to his car

solution.method: Used a hidden set of master keys (copied from faculty) to enter storage room, brought a spray can and sledgehammer to destroy decorations, then staged drone as distraction
solution.motive: Resentful over being passed for fest leadership; wanted chaos so he could 'rescue' the event and gain credit
solution.proof: CCTV footage shows the hooded figure has a distinctive limp — Arjun injured his ankle during morning band practice, visible in rehearsal footage; confirmed by video
solution.how_to_solve: By cross-checking the CCTV time (6:42 PM) with Arjun’s alibi: his band rehearsal ended at 6:15 PM, giving him time. His 'rehearsal' alibi is unsupported by anyone else. The blue thread is a red herring — but his limp in the grainy footage matches his known injury. His motive, opportunity, and attempt to control the narrative after the sabotage reveal his guilt.

crime_type: stolen answer key from professor's office

case.title: The Case of the Missing Midterm Key
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts and Science, Chennai – Professor Meenakshi Iyer's office in the Department of Mathematics
case.crime: The answer key to the upcoming Calculus-II midterm exam was stolen from the locked drawer of Professor Meenakshi Iyer's office two days before the exam.
case.victim: Professor Meenakshi Iyer, who spent weeks preparing the exam and now fears academic misconduct or sabotage.

suspects.name: Arjun Patel
suspects.motive: He's on academic probation and needs a near-perfect score to avoid suspension.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a minor assignment last semester and fears exposure if he fails again.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the professor's office building after hours, though he claims he was returning a book.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: She believed the exam was unfairly difficult and wanted to expose what she saw as poor teaching methods by leaking the key anonymously.
suspects.alibi: Says she was grading papers at her apartment with her roommate as a witness.
suspects.secret: She has been applying for a graduate position at a rival college and submitted the professor's negative evaluation without her knowledge.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted her browser history the morning after the theft, raising IT's suspicion.

suspects.name: Rahul Desai
suspects.motive: He resents Professor Iyer for blocking his promotion and wanted to create chaos to undermine her reputation.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a pub with friends until midnight.
suspects.secret: He submitted a research paper with falsified data and fears Professor Iyer, a reviewer, will discover it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Asked a student if the professor had 'lost anything important' the day after the theft.

evidence.description: A bent paperclip found in the trash can inside Professor Iyer's office. The lock on her drawer shows slight scratch marks.
evidence.significance: Suggests the drawer was picked. A simple tool like a paperclip could have been used.

evidence.description: A failed login attempt to the department's internal server from Priya Nair's ID at 8:47 PM on the night of the theft.
evidence.significance: Appears to place Priya trying to access restricted files remotely.

evidence.description: A sticky note with the words 'Check drawer after 7?' written in pencil, partially erased.
evidence.location: Back of a textbook on Professor Iyer's shelf
evidence.significance: Suggests someone planned to return to the office after a certain time. Handwriting is smudged but resembles Arjun's.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing someone in a blue hoodie entering the math wing at 6:45 PM. Arjun was wearing a blue hoodie that day.
evidence.significance: Places a suspect near the office around the time of the theft.

evidence.description: A printed sheet with partial solutions to the exam problems, found crumpled in a toilet in the men's restroom near the math department. The paper has Rahul Desai's fingerprints.
evidence.significance: Suggests Rahul had access to the exam content and tried to destroy evidence.

evidence.description: A spare key to Professor Iyer's office, labeled 'MATH 204 Backup', found hidden inside a potted plant in the department lounge.
evidence.significance: Explains how someone could enter the office without breaking in. Only staff knew about this key.

evidence.description: A student reports Rahul laughing and saying, 'Iyer's going to have a meltdown soon,' at the pub that night.
evidence.significance: Suggests prior knowledge of the theft.

timeline: 5:30 PM – Professor Iyer locks her office and leaves after a meeting.
6:15 PM – Arjun visits the library, confirmed by entry log.
6:45 PM – Janitor sees a person in a blue hoodie entering the math wing.
7:00 PM – Priya logs into the department server from her apartment (routine check).
7:30 PM – The failed login from Priya’s ID occurs (later revealed to be spoofed).
8:00 PM – Rahul checks in at 'The Study Break' pub via social media.
8:47 PM – Suspicious server login attempt using Priya’s credentials.
9:15 PM – Campus security patrol checks offices; Iyer’s office door is locked, but the spare key is missing from the plant.
10:00 AM (next day) – Professor discovers the answer key is missing.
red_herrings: The partial exam sheet in the restroom points to Rahul, but he only found it and panicked, trying to destroy it.
Priya’s deleted browser history was to hide her job applications, not the theft.
The blue hoodie sighting misleads toward Arjun, but the janitor misidentified the person’s build.
The sticky note was actually a reminder Professor Iyer wrote to herself but forgot to erase.

solution.method: Rahul used the spare key hidden in the department lounge—known only to faculty and TA’s—to enter Professor Iyer's office between 6:30 PM and 7:00 PM after sneaking out of the pub early. He copied the answer key, then returned the key. Later, he accessed the server using a spoofed proxy to make it look like Priya attempted a breach.
solution.motive: To sabotage Professor Iyer’s reputation and create grounds for her to be removed from the promotion committee, improving his chances for advancement.
solution.proof: Security camera footage (recovered later) shows Rahul leaving the pub at 6:20 PM and returning at 7:45 PM. His fingerprint on the spare key (after forensic dusting) matches, and the ISP log proves the spoofed login originated from his laptop’s MAC address.
solution.how_to_solve: The key insight is that only a staff member would know about the spare key. Arjun and Priya lacked access to it. The spoofed login is digital misdirection—too obvious for a real thief. Rahul’s fingerprint on the partial exam paper shows he handled it, but it was already printed, meaning he didn’t create it. His alibi is weak due to early departure. Combining the timeline, knowledge of the spare key, and technical capability to spoof the login proves his guilt.

case.title: The Case of the Fake Influencer
case.setting: St. Xavier's College, Mumbai - Department of Mass Media
case.crime: A fake Instagram account falsely portraying a student as a party-loving, rule-breaking influencer was created, leading to public humiliation, disciplinary action, and social isolation.
case.victim: Aarav Mehta, a quiet second-year Mass Media student known for academic excellence and reserved nature

suspects.name: Kiara Reddy
suspects.motive: Aarav recently won the 'Best Campus Journalist' award, which Kiara believed she deserved. She resents his low-key success.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at a dance rehearsal at the college auditorium from 6–9 PM on the night the account was created.
suspects.secret: She plagiarized a major assignment and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Aarav the day before the account appeared. Also, her real Instagram analytics dropped after the fake account gained traction.

suspects.name: Dev Patel
suspects.motive: Known for running anonymous meme pages. Believes Aarav is 'too serious' and needed to be 'taken down a peg'.
suspects.alibi: Says he was binge-watching a series at home and shows chat logs with a friend from 8 PM onward.
suspects.secret: He was suspended last semester for hacking into the college Wi-Fi to change grades (never proven).
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Laughed openly when the fake posts went viral. Was seen accessing Aarav’s public profile repeatedly.

suspects.name: Professor Neha Iyer
suspects.motive: Aarav reported her for favoritism after she gave Kiara higher marks despite poor performance. She may want to discredit Aarav’s credibility.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers at home alone.
suspects.secret: She has a chronic anxiety disorder and takes medication she doesn’t want known.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Initiated the disciplinary probe against Aarav after the fake posts surfaced, even before investigation.

evidence.description: The fake Instagram account (@AaravUnleashed) was created using a burner email (aaravinaction2002@gmail.com) registered at 8:47 PM on Monday. First post uploaded at 9:03 PM.
evidence.significance: Narrows down time of creation. Burner email suggests premeditation.

evidence.description: A screenshot shows Kiara’s phone with the fake account open during rehearsal, timestamped 8:50 PM. However, the screenshot lacks metadata and was sent via WhatsApp.
evidence.location: Forwarded in a group chat by an anonymous sender
evidence.significance: Seems to place Kiara accessing the account during her alibi.

evidence.description: A sticky note found in the college computer lab with the burner email and password scribbled on it. Handwriting analysis suggests a rushed, left-handed writer.
evidence.significance: Suggests the account was created on campus. Dev is left-handed; Kiara is right-handed.

evidence.description: Rohan, a junior student, says he saw Professor Iyer in the computer lab at around 8:30 PM, looking nervous and carrying a USB drive.
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi of being at home.

evidence.description: IP address used to create the account traced to the college network, specifically Lab 3, from 8:45 PM to 8:52 PM.
evidence.significance: Confirms account was created on campus in a public lab.

evidence.description: The fake account used a photo-editing app to superimpose Aarav’s face onto stock images of parties. The app leaves a digital watermark detectable in metadata.
evidence.significance: The watermark shows the edits were made using 'FaceSwap Pro'—a premium app Dev has installed on his device.

evidence.description: A library sign-in sheet shows Dev signed in at 7:45 PM and checked out a book on 'Digital Identity and Ethics'—but no checkout record exists in the system.
evidence.significance: Suggests Dev may have forged the log to fake an alibi.

timeline: Monday, 6:00–9:00 PM: College dance rehearsal (Kiara's alibi)
Monday, 7:45 PM: Dev signs into library (per log)
Monday, 8:30 PM: Rohan claims to see Professor Iyer in computer lab
Monday, 8:45–8:52 PM: IP log shows activity from Lab 3 computer creating burner email
Monday, 8:47 PM: Burner email registered
Monday, 8:50 PM: Anonymous screenshot of Kiara’s phone with fake account circulates
Monday, 9:03 PM: First fake post uploaded
Tuesday, 10:00 AM: Fake post goes viral on campus
Tuesday, 1:00 PM: Professor Iyer initiates disciplinary meeting
red_herrings: The forwarded screenshot of Kiara’s phone accessing the fake account
Professor Iyer being seen in the computer lab
The FaceSwap Pro watermark linking to Dev’s device
Kiara’s public argument with Aarav

solution.method: Used the college computer lab to create a burner email and fake Instagram account, edited images using FaceSwap Pro on his phone, and scheduled the first post. Later, he forged a library log to appear alibied.
solution.motive: He resented Aarav’s serious demeanor and popularity among professors, viewing him as a 'holier-than-thou' student. The prank was meant to 'expose the boring kid' but spiraled out of control.
solution.proof: Lab 3 IP log matches the creation time; sticky note with login details matches Dev’s left-handed handwriting; library sign-in log has a mismatched timestamp with the digital checkout system—proving forgery.
solution.how_to_solve: The witness sighting of Professor Iyer is unverified and contradicted by security cam data (not provided). Kiara’s screenshot is anonymous and unverifiable. The FaceSwap app clue is misleading—many students use it. The key is the IP log + left-handed note + forged library log: only Dev had both access to Lab 3 and motive to fake an alibi. His 'binge-watching alibi' relies on unverifiable chat logs, while physical evidence places him on campus.

case.title: The Case of the Stolen Thesis
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts and Sciences, Kolkata – Department of English Literature
case.crime: A final-year honors student is publicly accused of plagiarizing her entire thesis after a faculty review. Digital timestamps and source comparisons suggest the work was copied from an obscure online journal. However, she insists she wrote it herself. An investigation reveals the plagiarism report was tampered with, and someone deliberately framed her.
case.victim: Priya Menon, a 21-year-old English Honors student with a spotless academic record

suspects.name: Arjun Patel
suspects.role: senior research assistant and former teaching assistant for English
suspects.personality: intelligent, meticulous, socially awkward, jealous of top performers
suspects.motive: Priya was selected for a prestigious research fellowship he had applied for; he resented her selection
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the college library from 6 PM to 9 PM reviewing journals
suspects.secret: He failed his own thesis defense last year and had to re-submit anonymously
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to run the plagiarism check on Priya’s thesis and was the first to report the issue

suspects.name: Professor Ruma Das
suspects.personality: strict, ambitious, image-conscious, fair but intimidating
suspects.motive: Priya's thesis critically analyzed Professor Das’s published work, calling it 'derivative' — Das risks professional embarrassment if published
suspects.alibi: Was at a faculty meeting from 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM, then claims to have gone straight home
suspects.secret: She submitted a paper to a journal last year that was rejected for similarity to another scholar’s work — a fact she concealed
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for immediate disciplinary action and blocked Priya from defending her thesis

suspects.name: Naina Reddy
suspects.role: Priya’s roommate and fellow English student
suspects.motive: Wanted Priya to be disqualified so she could take her place in the university’s publication journal and gain academic prestige
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a theater rehearsal from 5:30 PM to 8:30 PM
suspects.secret: She had plagiarized parts of her own midterm essay and was terrified of exposure if a full audit began
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Priya two days before the accusation and deleted her browser history the day after

evidence.description: Plagiarism report generated by Turnitin-style software showing 87% match to a Lithuanian literary journal article titled 'Postcolonial Echoes in Modern Indian Fiction'
evidence.location: Department server, flagged by Arjun Patel
evidence.significance: Formal basis for accusation; however, the Lithuanian article was published two months *after* Priya submitted her draft — impossible if genuine

evidence.description: Priya’s cloud backup folder showing 17 revisions of her thesis over 4 months, with time-stamped auto-saves from her laptop
evidence.location: Her personal Google Drive, accessed with permission
evidence.significance: Proves she wrote the thesis incrementally; timestamps confirm early drafts predate the alleged source

evidence.description: Printed copy of the plagiarism report with handwritten notes in the margin: 'Make sure this sticks.' in Marathi script
evidence.location: Found crumpled in a bin outside Professor Das’s office
evidence.significance: Suggests Das wanted the accusation to succeed — but handwriting analysis later shows it’s a poor imitation

evidence.description: Librarian confirms Arjun was in the library but says he left at 6:45 PM and came back at 8:15 PM, using his ID to re-enter
evidence.location: Library log and security camera notes
evidence.significance: Contradicts his alibi of continuous stay; creates opportunity to tamper with digital files remotely

evidence.description: IP log from college server showing a login from the department printer room at 7:12 PM on the night before the accusation — used to generate and email the fake plagiarism report
evidence.significance: Links the tampering to a physical location on campus; IP traced to a printer with scanning and email function

evidence.description: A sticky note with a Lithuanian website URL and login credentials written in blue ink, tucked inside Naina’s drama notebook
evidence.location: Found during a search of her bag after she left it in the common room
evidence.significance: Suggests she accessed the fake source — but she claims she was researching 'international theatre journals' and the note was unrelated

evidence.description: Metadata from the fake plagiarism report shows it was created using a spoofed version of the college’s Turnitin plugin, modified with a script that falsified the source article’s publication date
evidence.location: Digital forensics report from college IT
evidence.significance: Proves deliberate forgery; the script used matches one previously accessed by Arjun in a computer science elective

timeline: April 10, 3:00 PM: Priya submits final thesis to department portal
April 10, 5:30 PM: Faculty meeting ends; Professor Das leaves campus
April 10, 6:00 PM: Naina attends theater rehearsal in auditorium
April 10, 6:30 PM: Arjun enters library; logs show he accesses department server remotely at 7:12 PM from printer room IP
April 10, 7:15 PM: Fake plagiarism report generated and emailed to Professor Das
April 10, 8:15 PM: Arjun returns to library, logs seen entering with ID
April 11, 9:00 AM: Professor Das announces plagiarism findings; Priya is suspended pending review
red_herrings: Handwritten note in Marathi near Das’s office — designed to implicate her
Naina’s Lithuanian URL note — coincidental but suspicious
Priya’s thesis criticizing Professor Das — strong apparent motive
Arjun’s jealousy of Priya’s fellowship — emotional motive but not proof

solution.method: Arjun used his technical knowledge to create a fake plagiarism report by spoofing the college’s academic software. He falsified the publication date of a real but obscure Lithuanian article to make it appear Priya had copied from it. He remotely accessed the department printer room computer to generate and send the report, timing it to arrive after hours.
solution.motive: Jealousy over losing the research fellowship to Priya, combined with embarrassment over his own past academic failure, drove him to sabotage her.
solution.proof: The metadata of the fake report contains a unique script signature that matches a file Arjun downloaded in a CS elective. The IP log places him at the printer room during the tampering window, and the cloud backups prove Priya’s work predates the source.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must recognize that the plagiarism source postdates Priya’s draft, proving the report is fake. Then, cross-reference the IP log with Arjun’s alibi to expose the gap. Finally, match the technical signature in the report’s metadata to Arjun’s digital footprint. The red herrings (Das’s grudge, Naina’s note) distract but collapse under scrutiny of timestamps and digital evidence.

case.title: The Case of the Silent Stage
case.setting: Siddhartha Institute of Technology, Pune — Annual Cultural Fest 'ZestFest' at the open-air amphitheater
case.crime: The main sound system was sabotaged minutes before the finals of the inter-college band competition, rendering all amplifiers and microphones completely inoperative.
case.victim: The college’s reputation and the organizing committee; the headlining band 'Electric Raaga' could not perform, causing massive audience dissatisfaction.

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: His rival band 'Electric Raaga' was the favorite to win; his own band 'No Signal' was eliminated in the semifinals under controversial judging.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the green room reviewing notes for his next day’s quiz competition.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his elimination round performance from a foreign indie band and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly calm after the sabotage, even suggesting the fest continue with acoustic sets—convenient for his unplugged-style band.

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Deshpande
suspects.role: professor and faculty in-charge of the fest
suspects.personality: strict, detail-oriented, socially awkward, deeply protective of college's reputation
suspects.motive: She strongly opposed the inclusion of rock bands, fearing noise complaints from neighboring hostels. Wanted the fest to focus on classical arts.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her office, finalizing the award certificates.
suspects.secret: She submitted a fake expense report for festival funds to cover her son’s medical bills.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the sound engineer two days prior about 'excessive volume levels'.

suspects.name: Karan Patel
suspects.role: student technician and sound crew lead
suspects.personality: quiet, technically brilliant, socially withdrawn, easily flustered under pressure
suspects.motive: He was publicly reprimanded by Arjun during a soundcheck for 'ruining' No Signal’s mix, and was overheard muttering threats.
suspects.alibi: Claims he went to the restroom five minutes before the sabotage and returned to find the system dead.
suspects.secret: He has a crush on the lead singer of Electric Raaga and secretly recorded their rehearsals.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person seen adjusting the main mixer rack before the failure, and hesitated when questioned.

suspects.name: Neha Reddy
suspects.role: student fest coordinator and president of the cultural committee
suspects.motive: The sabotage could void insurance coverage if sabotage is proven; she cut corners in equipment rental to stay under budget, using a dubious vendor.
suspects.alibi: Was on stage introducing the next act when the system failed.
suspects.secret: She used substandard backup cables purchased from a local flea market to save money.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Immediately blamed 'technical glitches' and tried to downplay the incident, discouraging investigation.

evidence.description: A small, custom USB device plugged into the primary audio interface, labeled 'DSP-Boost v3'—a known signal jammer that forces audio drivers into an unrecoverable crash loop.
evidence.location: Found inside the main mixer rack, hidden behind cables.
evidence.significance: Proves intentional sabotage, not an accident.

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Arjun entering the green room at 6:48 PM but no clear footage of him leaving or returning during the critical 7:02–7:08 PM window.
evidence.location: Campus security server, camera near green room corridor.
evidence.significance: Suggests Arjun could have slipped out unnoticed.

evidence.description: A crumpled note in Dr. Deshpande’s office trash can reading: 'No more noise. Fest must end loud phase.'
evidence.location: Recovered during search of professor’s office.
evidence.significance: Appears to be a motive confession, but handwriting analysis shows it was written by a student imitating her style.

evidence.description: A crew member recalls seeing Karan arguing with Arjun during soundcheck and hearing Karan say, 'You’ll regret messing with me.'
evidence.location: Overheard near stage left during rehearsal.
evidence.significance: Suggests personal vendetta.

evidence.description: A personalized USB drive with Karan’s nickname 'K-Sound' engraved, found near the mixer—containing only audio calibration files.
evidence.location: On the floor beside the mixer rack.
evidence.significance: Looks incriminating, but the jammer device isn’t his and isn’t on the drive.

evidence.description: Log file from the audio interface shows the jammer was activated remotely via a Bluetooth connection from a phone logged as 'FestBackupAdmin'—a credential issued only to Neha and Dr. Deshpande.
evidence.location: Recovered from the interface’s internal memory.
evidence.significance: Narrows down access to two people.

evidence.description: A damaged backup cable with visible frayed wires and a distinctive red stripe—identical to the ones Neha purchased from the flea market.
evidence.location: Found coiled beneath the stage, plugged into an emergency power outlet.
evidence.significance: The cable was used to restore partial power too late, but its poor quality may have contributed to suspicion of general technical failure.

timeline: 5:30 PM — Final soundcheck completed; all systems functional.
6:15 PM — Arjun’s band eliminated; he confronts Karan about sound mix.
6:40 PM — Dr. Deshpande argues with the sound team about volume control policy.
6:58 PM — Neha gives final stage clearance; Karan last seen adjusting EQ settings.
7:00 PM — Performance is about to start; lights dim, band takes stage.
7:02 PM — Sound system fails entirely; no feedback or static, just silence.
7:05 PM — Karan discovered near mixer; claims he just returned from restroom.
7:08 PM — Security called; investigation begins.
red_herrings: Arjun’s plagiarism secret makes him seem desperate to eliminate competition.
Karan’s angry remark and misplaced USB drive point to personal revenge.
Dr. Deshpande’s note and opposition to rock music suggest ideological sabotage.
Neha’s faulty cables imply negligence causing failure, masking intentional act.

solution.method: Used her 'FestBackupAdmin' phone to remotely activate a pre-planted Bluetooth jammer inside the audio interface during her introduction speech.
solution.motive: If sabotage was proven, the college wouldn’t reimburse rental losses, exposing her budget fraud. But if it looked like an accident, insurance would cover costs.
solution.proof: Bluetooth log shows activation from 'FestBackupAdmin' at 7:02 PM—simultaneous with Neha’s on-stage speech. Her phone was not in airplane mode, and a timestamped selfie she posted at 7:01 PM proves she had phone access.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is the digital log: only Neha and Dr. Deshpande had admin access. Dr. Deshpande’s phone was off (verified by IT), but Neha’s was active. Cross-reference the activation timestamp with her onstage presence—she could have triggered it during her speech. The public blame on 'technical issues' and her rush to hide the faulty cables reveal her desire to disguise sabotage as failure. The other suspects’ motives and behaviors are suspicious but lack access to the admin system.

case.title: The Case of the Leaked Confessions
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, South Campus - Department of Social Sciences
case.crime: An anonymous confession page on Instagram, 'DMC_Secrets', was compromised and used to post deeply personal, damaging confessions falsely attributed to students, leading to public shaming and emotional distress.
case.victim: Multiple students, particularly Priya Malhotra, whose fake confession about cheating on exams went viral within the campus, causing her to withdraw from midterms.

suspects.name: Aryan Kapoor
suspects.motive: Wanted to eliminate competition for student council president; Priya was a strong rival.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a debate club meeting from 6:00 PM to 8:30 PM on the night of the leak.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his major research paper and is terrified of exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was unusually interested in the confession page and was seen arguing with Priya a week before the leak.

suspects.name: Meera Desai
suspects.motive: Was publicly humiliated when an anonymous post on the same page revealed she had a panic disorder, which she never confessed; suspects Priya was behind it.
suspects.alibi: Says she was alone in her hostel room studying from 5:30 PM onward.
suspects.secret: She has been secretly running a blog criticizing campus mental health policies under a pseudonym.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Downloaded a hacking tutorial app two days before the breach and visited the confession page admin panel link found in browser history.

suspects.name: Professor Nitin Rao
suspects.motive: The confession page mocked his outdated teaching methods and rumored affair with a staff member; wanted to discredit it entirely.
suspects.alibi: Attended a faculty dinner from 7:00 PM to 9:30 PM; several witnesses confirm.
suspects.secret: He did have an affair with an administrative assistant, which the page hinted at.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Called the confession page 'cyber vandalism' in a public lecture and suggested the college should shut it down.

evidence.description: Login IP address to the 'DMC_Secrets' admin panel traced to a campus Wi-Fi node near the library server room at 7:48 PM on the night of the leak.
evidence.location: Instagram backend logs (obtained via college IT cooperation)
evidence.significance: The breach occurred when the page was accessed to alter its bio and post the fake confessions.

evidence.description: Search history on Meera Desai's laptop shows visits to 'how to hack Instagram accounts' and 'bypass two-factor authentication'.
evidence.significance: Suggests technical intent to compromise accounts.

evidence.description: A library security guard recalls seeing Aryan Kapoor near the server room corridor at 7:40 PM, though he wasn’t supposed to be there.
evidence.location: Library surveillance log and guard testimony
evidence.significance: Places Aryan near the IP source close to the time of the hack.

evidence.description: A sticky note with the confession page’s backup password written in shorthand was found in Professor Rao’s office trash bin.
evidence.location: Office waste bin, collected by janitor who alerted authorities
evidence.significance: Suggests he had access to sensitive information about the page.

evidence.description: Server logs show the admin session from the library IP used a college-issued faculty login token to bypass security.
evidence.significance: Indicates the attacker had access to a staff-level authentication token, not just Wi-Fi.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Aryan Kapoor attends debate club meeting (confirmed by 8 members).
6:15 PM: Meera Desai checks into the library using her student ID.
7:00 PM: Professor Rao arrives at faculty dinner (confirmed by roll call and photos).
7:38 PM: Security camera shows Aryan leaving debate room hallway (not returning).
7:40 PM: Security guard sees someone resembling Aryan near server room (low-light footage).
7:48 PM: Admin login to 'DMC_Secrets' from library Wi-Fi node.
7:50 PM: Three fake confessions posted, including one about Priya cheating.
8:15 PM: Meera Desai checks out of library (camera timestamp).
9:30 PM: Professor Rao leaves faculty dinner.
red_herrings: Meera’s hacking-related searches, which were for a psychology research project on cyberbullying trends.
Aryan seen near server room, but footage is too grainy for positive ID.
Professor Rao’s password note — he found it in a shared printer tray and wrote it down to report it, then forgot.
Rumors that Priya was actually running the page, which were false and planted by Aryan.

solution.method: Used a stolen faculty RFID tag to access the server room corridor and borrowed a professor’s laptop (left unattended during dinner) to authenticate via the college’s single-sign-on system, then accessed the Instagram page through a saved session.
solution.motive: To sabotage Priya Malhotra’s reputation and clear his path to student council president.
solution.proof: Server logs show the admin login used a faculty authentication token; cross-referencing RFID swipes revealed Aryan’s ID was never used, but Professor Banerjee’s was at 7:42 PM — Banerjee confirmed his laptop was taken by a ‘student helping him carry books’ around 6:50 PM, matching Aryan’s alibi gap.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the IP location with the authentication method: Wi-Fi near the server room is accessible to students, but a faculty token is required for backend access. Only someone with physical access to a professor’s device during dinner could have done it. Aryan’s alibi breaks at 7:38 PM, and his encounter with Professor Banerjee (who mistook him for a volunteer) places him with the device. The guard’s sighting and stolen RFID (from a lost-and-found tag he never returned) allowed corridor access. Meera’s searches and Rao’s password note are distractions.

case.title: The Case of the Switched Schedules
case.setting: Rashtriya Engineering College, Chennai - Department of Computer Science
case.crime: The final exam schedule for B.Tech Computer Science students was altered without authorization, swapping the dates of two major papers and causing chaos during exam week.
case.victim: Students and faculty of the Computer Science department, particularly those preparing for Theory of Computation and Data Structures exams

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.motive: Aarav excels in Data Structures but struggles with Theory of Computation. The schedule change gave him extra prep time for the latter.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying until midnight the night before the change went live.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a minor assignment earlier in the semester and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the professor over grading two weeks prior; also accessed the department server under a false login (later revealed to be a red herring).

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Dr. Nair teaches Theory of Computation. She believed students were unprepared and wanted more lecture time before the exam.
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a virtual conference call with a colleague in Germany the evening the change occurred.
suspects.secret: She delayed submitting her research grant report and used college server logs to backdate a file.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed hard in faculty meetings to 'adjust exam dates for pedagogical reasons'—recorded in meeting minutes.

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.role: junior lab assistant and part-time student
suspects.motive: Rohan had agreed to tutor five students for Theory of Computation—for a fee—but the original date conflicted with a family emergency. The reschedule aligned with his availability, letting him fulfill the commitments and collect money.
suspects.alibi: Says he was attending his sister’s wedding in Kolhapur that weekend.
suspects.secret: He’s running an unofficial tutoring side business not approved by the college.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the admin portal on a lab computer the night before—though he claims it was to fix a printer issue.

evidence.description: Log entry from the college portal showing the schedule edit made at 10:17 PM on June 4th from IP address 192.168.10.54, assigned to Lab 3.
evidence.significance: Pinpoints time and location of the change; Lab 3 is under Rohan’s maintenance.

evidence.description: Fake login attempt from 'admin_aarav' seen in logs two minutes after the change, quickly deleted.
evidence.significance: Looks like Aarav tried to cover his tracks, but the IP traces to a public proxy.

evidence.description: A handwritten note found in the admin office trash with 'Swap CoA and DS' scribbled, with coffee stains and a fingerprint smudge.
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation; fingerprint matches Dr. Nair.

evidence.description: A student reports seeing Rohan in the campus cybercafe on June 4th around 9:30 PM, but he was supposedly in Kolhapur.
evidence.significance: Contradicts his alibi.

evidence.description: Dr. Nair’s conference call had no video, and the German colleague confirms it lasted only 20 minutes, not the claimed two hours.
evidence.significance: Her alibi is weak, but no direct link to the server.

evidence.description: USB drive labeled 'Backup - DO NOT OPEN' found plugged into Lab 3’s admin computer. Contains a script that auto-uploads schedule changes to the portal.
evidence.location: Under keyboard of Lab 3 admin PC
evidence.significance: Reveals technical method used; script created using Rohan’s personal coding style.

evidence.description: Night watchman recalls seeing a student wearing a red hoodie entering Lab 3 around 10:00 PM—matches Rohan’s usual attire.
evidence.significance: Supports presence at scene.

timeline: June 1st: Original exam schedule posted—Data Structures on June 6th, Theory of Computation on June 8th.
June 3rd: Dr. Nair complains in faculty meeting about low quiz scores in Theory of Computation, suggests delaying exam.
June 4th, 6:00 PM: Rohan boards a train to Kolhapur (per ticket records).
June 4th, 9:15 PM: Rohan arrives at Kolhapur station (CCTV footage).
June 4th, 9:30 PM: Student claims to see Rohan in campus cybercafe.
June 4th, 10:00 PM: Security guard sees someone in red hoodie enter Lab 3.
June 4th, 10:17 PM: Schedule change logged from Lab 3 computer.
June 5th, 8:00 AM: Students discover new schedule—exams swapped to June 8th and June 6th respectively.
June 5th, 10:00 AM: College IT begins forensic investigation.
red_herrings: Aarav's fake login attempt suggests guilt but was planted by someone else.
Dr. Nair’s fingerprint on the note—she wrote it during a meeting but discarded it; someone stole it and used it to frame her.
Her weak conference call alibi distracts from the real timeline.
The handwriting on the note appears rushed and matches no suspect exactly, causing confusion.

solution.method: Rohan used a pre-written script on a USB drive to alter the exam schedule. He exploited a flaw in the lab’s auto-login system for admin tasks. Though he was in Kolhapur, he returned secretly by catching an early return train, arriving around 9:15 PM, and used the lab computer before 10:30 PM.
solution.motive: He had accepted payments from five students to tutor them for Theory of Computation. The original exam date conflicted with his sister’s wedding. By delaying it, he could tutor them and collect fees without defaulting.
solution.proof: The USB drive with his custom-coded script, witness sighting at cybercafe (which contradicts his alibi), security footage of red hoodie, and the IP log from Lab 3—all converging at the critical time.
solution.how_to_solve: Compare alibis with physical sightings: Rohan's train ticket shows return journey was possible. The cybercafe sighting and red hoodie place him on campus. The fake 'admin_aarav' login is a proxy—too sophisticated for Aarav. Dr. Nair’s fingerprint on the note is incidental. The script on the USB matches Rohan’s coding patterns (verified by IT). Only Rohan had both technical access and a motive tied directly to the rescheduling.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Beats
case.setting: Jaydev Hostel, Room 204, Shanti Vidyalaya College, Pune
case.crime: Expensive wireless headphones (Beats Studio Pro) belonging to a student go missing from his hostel room
case.victim: Arjun Mehta, 21, second-year engineering student

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.personality: Charismatic, tech-savvy, always broke, social media obsessed
suspects.motive: Rohan had previously expressed envy for Arjun's headphones and asked to borrow them multiple times, which Arjun refused
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a late-night coding session in the college computer lab from 8 PM to 11 PM
suspects.secret: He secretly sold his laptop to pay off a gambling debt and doesn’t want anyone to know he’s broke
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly curious about the investigation and keeps suggesting that someone from outside broke in

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Quiet, studious, socially awkward, environmentally conscious
suspects.motive: Arjun had accidentally spilled chai on her handmade notebook two days ago, and she was visibly upset
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the library studying for her environmental science mid-term from 6:30 PM to 10 PM
suspects.secret: She has a crush on Arjun but is too shy to express it and writes poems about him in secret
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen loitering near Arjun’s room door earlier that day, though she claims she was just returning a misplaced book

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.personality: Strict, by-the-book, dislikes noise, holds grudges
suspects.motive: Arjun had been reported twice for playing loud music past curfew; Vikram warned him he’d 'deal with it personally'
suspects.alibi: Says he was in his office reviewing attendance logs until midnight
suspects.secret: He’s been accepting bribes from students to alter curfew records but fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to close the case quickly, suggesting the headphones were probably sold off-campus

evidence.description: A single smudged fingerprint on Arjun’s windowsill, partially wiped
evidence.location: Inside Room 204, near the open window
evidence.significance: Suggests possible entry from outside, but window is on the second floor with no drop marks below

evidence.description: Security camera footage from hostel gate shows Rohan entering the hostel at 7:45 PM and not leaving until 11:15 PM
evidence.significance: Confirms he was inside during the time of disappearance but does not prove he didn’t go to Room 204

evidence.description: A crumpled receipt for a second-hand electronics store dated the next morning, found in the hostel trash near Room 204
evidence.significance: Suggests someone tried to sell the headphones early morning; receipt has no name

evidence.description: A student from Room 206 claims to have heard arguing in Room 204 around 8:20 PM, sounding like Arjun and another male voice
evidence.significance: Timeline places a suspect in the room around the time the headphones went missing

evidence.description: A small tuft of dark blue thread caught on the edge of Arjun’s broken drawer lock
evidence.significance: Matches the fabric of the warden’s official uniform jacket

evidence.description: Arjun’s roommate mentions that the headphones were last seen charging on his desk at 7:30 PM
evidence.significance: Establishes timeline; headphones were present before 7:30 PM

evidence.description: The librarian confirms Priya was in the library from 6:45 PM to 10:05 PM and signed the logbook
evidence.significance: Strong alibi for Priya

timeline: 6:30 PM: Arjun returns to Room 204 with headphones, seen plugging them into charger by roommate
6:45 PM: Priya enters library (confirmed by log)
7:30 PM: Roommate leaves for dinner, headphones still on desk
7:45 PM: Rohan enters hostel (CCTV confirmed)
8:20 PM: Neighbor hears argument in Room 204
8:30 PM: Warden seen entering his office via security log
9:15 PM: Lights in Room 204 turn off
10:05 PM: Priya leaves library
10:30 PM: Arjun returns, discovers headphones missing
11:15 PM: Rohan leaves hostel
red_herrings: The fingerprints on the windowsill imply a break-in, but window was unlocked and often used by students to sneak back in
The crumpled receipt suggests a quick sale, but it's from a store that doesn’t open until 7 AM, making it impossible for theft to be reported so soon
Rohan’s financial troubles and obsession with gadgets make him seem guilty, but he has a solid alibi and no physical evidence links him
Arjun’s loud music complaints point to warden’s motive, but the argument may have seemed louder than it was due to thin walls

solution.method: Vikram used his master key to enter Room 204 at 8:25 PM after seeing Arjun leave. He broke the drawer lock with a screwdriver to make it look like a forced entry, took the headphones, and later planted the fake receipt to mislead the investigation.
solution.motive: He wanted to teach Arjun a lesson about noise discipline and believed confiscating the headphones without reporting it would serve as silent punishment. Later decided to keep them for his son.
solution.proof: The blue thread from his uniform caught on the drawer lock, and security log shows he left his office at 8:23 PM and returned at 8:32 PM — matching the time of the alleged argument. No one else had access to that floor during that window.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-referencing the warden’s office log with the witness testimony of the argument places him at the scene. The thread matches his uniform, and the broken lock shows tool marks consistent with a screwdriver (found in his office). The receipt is a red herring — timing proves it couldn’t be linked to the theft. Priya and Rohan have verified alibis. The argument heard was likely Vikram moving furniture while searching the room.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Fest Fund
case.setting: Vidya Vihar Institute of Technology, Pune – Cultural Fest Main Tent
case.crime: The ₹50,000 prize money for the annual cultural fest's flagship event disappeared from a locked wooden chest during the final performance.
case.victim: The Cultural Committee of Vidya Vihar Institute of Technology

suspects.name: Arnav Mehta
suspects.motive: He lost the final round of the solo singing competition, which he heavily invested in winning. Rumor says he needed the prize money to pay off a gaming app loan.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was backstage helping with stage lights after his performance.
suspects.secret: He was secretly dating the event judge, which could bias scoring.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the event coordinator 30 minutes before the prize was to be announced.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: As treasurer of the Cultural Committee, she was responsible for securing the cash. If it went missing, she could be expelled or barred from future leadership roles.
suspects.alibi: Says she handed the money chest to the coordinator before the final act and then went to the registration desk.
suspects.secret: She mistakenly left the chest unlocked earlier in the day but fixed it before anyone noticed.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the chest 10 minutes before the announcement, adjusting the lock.

suspects.name: Rahul Deshpande
suspects.personality: strict, rule-following, grumpy, bitter about fest chaos
suspects.motive: He opposed the use of cash prizes, calling it 'archaic and risky.' Wanted the committee to fail to prove his point.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was filing paperwork in the admin cabin from 8:00 PM onward.
suspects.secret: He took home a sound system cable last year and never returned it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen walking toward the admin building but a witness saw him near the tent exit at 8:15 PM.

evidence.description: A half-burned festival ticket with 'Seat B12' written in red ink, partially charred and found under a trash can near the tent's back exit.
evidence.location: Behind the main tent, near firecracker disposal bin
evidence.significance: Suggests someone tried to destroy evidence of attendance. B12 was Arnav’s seat.

evidence.description: A small key with 'VVI Admin – 3B' engraved, found in a potted plant near the registration desk.
evidence.significance: Matches the master key for event storage rooms. Could imply Priya had access to duplicate keys.

evidence.description: Security camera footage (low-res) shows a figure in a black hoodie placing something into a backpack behind the chest at 8:10 PM. Face not visible.
evidence.location: CCTV from south side of tent
evidence.significance: Timing matches the window of opportunity. Hoodie resembles ones sold at fest merch stall.

evidence.description: Faint greasy fingerprint smudge on the chest lock, tested later as machine grease, not common on human skin.
evidence.location: On the lock of the prize chest
evidence.significance: Indicates someone with mechanical work recently handled the lock – possibly Rahul, who maintains campus equipment.

evidence.description: A volunteer reports seeing Rahul arguing with the event coordinator about 'security breaches' at 7:50 PM, near the chest.
evidence.significance: Places him near crime scene with motive and tension.

evidence.description: A torn corner of a ₹500 note stuck in the chest's false bottom, accessible only by lifting the wooden panel.
evidence.significance: Proves the chest was opened not by force, but by someone who knew its trick – only staff and committee heads knew.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Final performance begins. Chest with ₹50,000 placed center stage, locked.
6:45 PM – Arnav performs, finishes to mixed applause, exits stage looking upset.
7:20 PM – Priya reports handing chest to coordinator for safekeeping near stage.
7:45 PM – Coordinator locks chest and places it behind stage curtain.
8:10 PM – Security cam captures figure in black hoodie near chest.
8:12 PM – Lights briefly flicker; power glitch reported by stage crew.
8:15 PM – Chest found empty during winner announcement.
8:20 PM – Campus security called, area sealed.
red_herrings: The burned ticket suggests Arnav tried to destroy evidence.
The master key implies Priya had a duplicate and stole the money to cover her earlier mistake.
Rahul’s argument with coordinator suggests premeditated sabotage.
Hoodie in footage matches one sold at fest stall, linking to Arnav who wore one earlier.

solution.method: Used his knowledge of the chest's false bottom (from previous years’ maintenance) and a duplicate master key to access the chest during the power flicker at 8:12 PM. He wore a borrowed hoodie from the lost-and-found to avoid recognition.
solution.motive: To sabotage the fest's prize system and prove his long-standing argument that cash prizes invite theft and mismanagement.
solution.proof: The greasy fingerprint matches oil from the wrench in Rahul’s office tool kit. Also, the false-bottom access method was known only to staff who maintained the chest – confirmed by past committee records.
solution.how_to_solve: The key lies in the grease on the lock and the false bottom. Only someone with mechanical tools and institutional knowledge could access it cleanly. The hoodie and ticket were red herrings. Arnav’s argument and Priya’s key find were distractions. The witness placing Rahul near the tent at 8:15 PM, plus the power flicker giving cover, completes the timeline. The greasy mark ties him definitively to the chest.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Data
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, Vidyasagar Institute of Technology, Pune
case.crime: Critical research data for a national-level AI research paper was maliciously deleted from a secure lab server
case.victim: Dr. Anjali Mehra, Associate Professor and lead researcher on the AI fairness algorithm project

suspects.name: Rohan Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Brilliant but arrogant, competitive, socially aloof
suspects.motive: Wanted sole credit on the paper; he believed Dr. Mehra was downplaying his contributions
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for his Operating Systems exam from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a small section of a previous assignment and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Dr. Mehra two days before the deletion about authorship order

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Believes she did most of the groundwork on the project and was overlooked for a co-lead position given to Rohan
suspects.alibi: Says she was at her cousin’s engagement party in Lonavala from 5:00 PM onward, with photos as proof
suspects.secret: She applied for a research grant using preliminary data without permission
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person logged into the lab server before the deletion, according to logs

suspects.name: Prof. Arvind Kelkar
suspects.personality: Traditional, skeptical of new methods, authority-driven, cautious
suspects.motive: Disagreed with Dr. Mehra’s AI fairness approach; feared it would bring discredit to the department if flawed
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home grading papers; no witnesses
suspects.secret: He invested personal money in a competing AI startup that specializes in algorithmic bias detection
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly criticized Dr. Mehra’s research direction in a staff meeting the week before

evidence.description: Server log showing a login from Priya Malhotra’s credentials at 8:47 PM on the night of the deletion
evidence.significance: Places Priya as the last user on the system before the data wipe

evidence.description: USB drive found in a trash can near the server room, labeled 'Backup_Important'
evidence.location: Behind recycling bin outside server room
evidence.significance: Contains partial corrupted data; appears to be failed backup attempt

evidence.description: Deleted file recovery reveals the data was wiped using a script called 'clean_research_v3.py'
evidence.significance: Script matches Rohan’s coding style and naming convention from past submissions

evidence.description: Night security guard reports seeing Prof. Kelkar entering the department building at 8:20 PM
evidence.location: Campus security log and witness interview
evidence.significance: Contradicts Kelkar’s alibi of being at home

evidence.description: IP address 10.12.4.21 accessed the server remotely at 8:45 PM, traced to the library Wi-Fi
evidence.significance: Matches Rohan’s known device MAC address

evidence.description: Fingerprint on the server room door handle matches Prof. Kelkar
evidence.location: Door handle swabbed by campus security
evidence.significance: Kelkar had physical access to the server room that night

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Priya’s cousin waving at the camera at 8:30 PM at the engagement party; Priya is not in frame
evidence.location: Private party video shared by cousin
evidence.significance: Suggests Priya may have left the party early

timeline: 4:30 PM – Dr. Mehra leaves campus, last to access data normally
5:00 PM – Priya leaves for cousin’s engagement party in Lonavala (claims)
6:00 PM – Rohan arrives at library (claimed alibi start)
7:15 PM – Prof. Kelkar recorded entering department building by security camera
8:20 PM – Security guard sees Prof. Kelkar near server room corridor
8:45 PM – Remote login from library IP, server accessed
8:47 PM – Login recorded under Priya’s credentials
8:49 PM – 'clean_research_v3.py' executed; 3.2 GB of research data deleted
9:15 PM – Rohan leaves library (library swipe record)
10:00 PM – Priya messages group chat from party location
red_herrings: Priya’s login timestamp makes her look guilty, but her credentials were stolen
Rohan’s device connected to the server, but someone used the library public terminal under his saved profile
The labeled USB suggests a panicked cover-up, but it was planted to mislead
Party footage shows Priya may have left early, but she never returned to campus

solution.method: Used a keycard to enter the server room, physically accessed the terminal, used stolen credentials (obtained via phishing email) for Priya and Rohan to mask his involvement, ran the deletion script written in Rohan’s style to frame him
solution.motive: Feared Dr. Mehra’s controversial research would harm the department’s reputation and his own financial stake in a competing startup
