solution.proof: Security footage places him in the building; his fingerprint on the door; IP from library was a red herring—actual deletion occurred from the internal server terminal (verified by local access log not synced to main server); script used custom admin privileges only Kelkar possessed
solution.how_to_solve: Compare server access logs: the deletion command originated from the local terminal (not remote). The remote login at 8:45 was a distraction. The script required elevated privileges only Kelkar had. His presence on camera, fingerprint, and financial conflict confirm motive and opportunity. The phishing email to steal credentials was found in Priya’s deleted mail folder.

case.title: The Case of the False Profile
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, South Campus
case.crime: A student created a fake dating app profile using another student's photos and personal details to catfish multiple peers, leading to emotional distress and public humiliation.
case.victim: Ananya Patel, a 21-year-old third-year psychology student

suspects.name: Rohan Mehra
suspects.personality: Charismatic, tech-savvy, insecure about rejection, popular
suspects.motive: Had a crush on Ananya, but she rejected him. Created the fake profile to discredit her after she publicly embarrassed him at a college fest.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a coding hackathon in Mumbai during the week the fake profile became active.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his major project and fears expulsion if it's discovered.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to help the investigation, offers technical insights about dating apps.

suspects.name: Priya Desai
suspects.personality: Ambitious, competitive, socially strategic, outwardly supportive
suspects.motive: Jealous of Ananya's leadership role in the student council. Wanted to tarnish her reputation to take her place.
suspects.alibi: Says she was volunteering at a women’s shelter every evening when the catfish messages were sent.
suspects.secret: She’s secretly dating a professor, which violates college ethics policy.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Tried to convince others that Ananya might have created the profile herself for attention.

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: Had unrequited feelings for Ananya and created the fake profile to 'test' who truly liked her—eventually spiraling into sending manipulative messages.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was home alone, grading assignments during the key nights.
suspects.secret: He has a history of obsessive behavior and was once counseled for stalking a previous classmate.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen searching Ananya’s name online during a lab session and quickly minimized the window.

evidence.description: The fake profile on 'ChingariChat' used Ananya’s Instagram photos and a bio mentioning her favorite book: 'The Alchemist'. Messages were sent between 8 PM and 10 PM from March 12 to March 18.
evidence.significance: Proves the catfish had access to Ananya’s private Instagram and knowledge of niche details about her.

evidence.description: IP logs show the fake profile was accessed from two locations: off-campus (public Wi-Fi at 'Cuppa Joe' cafe) and the college computer lab.
evidence.location: ChingariChat server logs (provided after college admin request)
evidence.significance: Indicates the catfish visited campus or had access to the lab during restricted hours.

evidence.description: A sticky note with a partial password ('AnanyaP@') and the name 'Chingari' was found in a trash can near the computer lab.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone was attempting to access an account related to Ananya.

evidence.description: A first-year student claims to have seen Priya arguing with Ananya near the library on March 11, the day before the fake profile appeared.
evidence.significance: Strengthens Priya’s motive, but later revealed to be a discussion about a missed council meeting.

evidence.description: A deleted draft message in Arjun’s personal email reads: 'I just wanted to see if someone could love her for her mind, not her face.'
evidence.location: Cloud backup of Arjun’s email (recovered by college IT during investigation)
evidence.significance: Reveals emotional obsession and planning related to the catfish profile.

evidence.description: The cafe manager at Cuppa Joe confirms a man matching Rohan’s description used the Wi-Fi frequently between March 12–18, but lacks CCTV footage.
evidence.location: Cafe Wi-Fi logs and verbal testimony
evidence.significance: Supports Rohan’s alibi partially—he was in Mumbai, but could have visited earlier.

evidence.description: A printed copy of Ananya’s Instagram profile was found in the recycling bin of the Computer Science department lounge.
evidence.significance: Links the suspect to both access to Ananya’s photos and the department where Arjun works.

timeline: March 10, 4:30 PM: Ananya posts a selfie on Instagram tagged at Delhi Metropolitan College South Campus.
March 11, 7:00 PM: Priya and Ananya are seen near the library (witness account).
March 12, 8:15 PM: First message sent from the fake profile to a male student.
March 13, 9:30 PM: Fake profile messages a second student, using intimate details about Ananya’s interests.
March 14, 1:00 PM: Rohan boards a train to Mumbai for a hackathon (ticket confirmed).
March 15, 8:45 PM: Profile active from college computer lab IP (logged by IT).
March 17, 7:20 PM: Arjun checks out a lab key from the CS department after hours.
March 18, 6:00 PM: Ananya discovers the fake profile and reports it to college admin.
March 19, 10:00 AM: Investigation begins; IT retrieves server logs.
red_herrings: The sticky note with the partial password implies someone was hacking Ananya’s account directly.
Rohan’s technical expertise and past rejection make him a prime suspect despite his alibi.
Priya’s argument with Ananya and secret relationship suggest ulterior motives.
Cafe Wi-Fi logs place someone resembling Rohan at Cuppa Joe, conflicting with his Mumbai trip.

solution.method: Used his access to the college computer lab to create the fake ChingariChat profile using Ananya’s public Instagram photos and information from her student council bio. Sent messages during lab hours and after using the department’s Wi-Fi.
solution.motive: Was emotionally obsessed with Ananya and wanted to 'test' if people admired her intellect or just her looks. When the messages turned manipulative, he couldn’t stop.
solution.proof: The deleted email draft expressing his motive, combined with the lab key checkout log and the printed Instagram page found in the CS lounge, confirms his involvement. IP logs tie activity to the lab during his access window.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is to cross-reference IP logs with physical access records. Though Rohan and Priya have motives, their alibis hold. Arjun’s alibi is unverified (home alone), and the digital footprint—especially the email draft—combined with access to lab resources and the printed photo—directly implicates him. The red herrings distract with emotional motives, but the physical and digital trails point to Arjun.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Vengeance Jersey
case.setting: St. Arvind College of Arts and Sports, Pune – Men's Cricket Team Locker Room, Hostel Common Room, and College Grounds
case.crime: The official match jersey of the college cricket team, 'Vengeance,' was stolen the night before the inter-collegiate Zonal Finals tournament.
case.victim: The St. Arvind Vengeance Cricket Team – the jersey is symbolic and essential for official tournament participation.

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.personality: Competitive, hot-tempered, ambitious, resentful of seniors
suspects.motive: Was benched for the finals despite better stats; suspects favoritism in team selection.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for his Economics exam until 10 PM.
suspects.secret: Failed a course last semester and is on academic probation.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the captain the previous evening; showed no concern about the jersey loss.

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Calm, observant, socially conscious, fiercely loyal to friends
suspects.motive: Best friend is on the rival college team; accusations of leaking team strategies have circulated.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her hostel room streaming a movie with roommates from 8 PM to midnight.
suspects.secret: She runs an anonymous college gossip blog criticizing the sports culture.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted her social media post praising the team hours before the match; found near locker room at 7:30 AM.

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Charismatic, popular, flippant, hides insecurity with humor
suspects.motive: Team captain; the jersey has his name stitched first; fears humiliation if team loses with him leading.
suspects.alibi: Says he left the jersey in the locker room after practice at 6:30 PM and went to dinner with friends at the canteen until 8:30 PM.
suspects.secret: Borrowed money from a local bookie to fund a failed startup idea.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly insistent that the jersey was definitely in the locker after practice; pressured coach to delay reporting the theft.

suspects.name: Professor Anika Roy
suspects.personality: Strict, principled, no-nonsense, deeply invested in college reputation
suspects.motive: Wants the team disqualified for bringing negative attention; believes sports distract from academics.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in her office until 7 PM, then went home and watched a webinar online.
suspects.secret: Submitted a research grant proposal tied to reducing student sports funding.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to suggest the jersey might have been 'misplaced due to carelessness' and discouraged a formal investigation.

evidence.description: A single blue thread caught on the edge of the broken locker padlock.
evidence.location: Locker room, Team Vengeance’s main equipment locker
evidence.significance: Matches fabric from a specific college-issued sports hoodie.

evidence.description: Security camera footage (partial) showing a figure in a blue hoodie entering the locker room at 7:15 PM. Face not visible.
evidence.location: Campus security office, footage from east wing corridor
evidence.significance: Suggests someone returned after practice.

evidence.description: A crumpled note in the trash bin of the hostel common room: 'If they can’t win fair, they don’t deserve to play.'
evidence.location: Hostel common room bin, near Rohan’s floor
evidence.significance: Appears to be a threat, linking to Rohan’s resentment.

evidence.description: A first-year student reports seeing Vikram toss a red duffel bag into a storage cupboard in the gym basement late at night.
evidence.significance: The official jersey is red and black; bag wasn’t seen earlier.

evidence.description: A red fabric swatch found inside the duffel bag in the gym basement, matching the official jersey material.
evidence.location: Inside a dusty duffel bag in gym basement storage cupboard
evidence.significance: Confirms the jersey was moved, not destroyed.

evidence.description: Wi-Fi logs show Priya’s phone connected to the campus network near the locker room at 6:45 PM, not her hostel.
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi of being in her room.

evidence.description: The night watchman recalls seeing Professor Roy’s car leave campus at 7:20 PM, not earlier as she claimed.
evidence.significance: Undermines her alibi.

timeline: 4:00 PM – Team practice ends; Vikram confirms jersey is in locker.
4:30 PM – Vikram and others leave; Vikram heads to canteen with friends.
5:00 PM – Professor Roy leaves her office (per security swipe), but says she went home.
6:45 PM – Wi-Fi logs show Priya’s phone active near locker room.
7:15 PM – Security camera shows hooded figure in blue entering locker room area.
7:20 PM – Professor Roy’s car exits campus (per guard log).
8:00 PM – Rohan seen entering library.
10:00 PM – Rohan leaves library.
11:30 PM – Student sees Vikram near gym basement with duffel bag.
7:30 AM (next day) – Priya spotted near locker room, agitated.
8:00 AM – Theft discovered by team manager.
red_herrings: Blue hoodie thread and footage – suggests an outsider or revenge motive, but hoodie is common college attire.
Priya’s phone near locker room – she was retrieving a lost earbud, not stealing the jersey.
Professor Roy’s late departure – she stayed to meet a confidential student counselor, unrelated to sports.
Rohan’s threatening note – written in anger after being benched, but never acted upon.

solution.method: After dinner, Vikram returned to the locker room around 9:30 PM using his captain’s key, took the jersey, and hid it in an old duffel bag in the gym basement to create a crisis and delay the match, hoping the team could regroup and prepare better.
solution.motive: He feared the team was unprepared and would embarrass the college – and himself – in the finals. He believed stalling the tournament would allow for extra practice.
solution.proof: The witness who saw him with the duffel bag; the red fabric matching the jersey found inside; and his unnecessary access to the locker (only captain and coach have keys).
solution.how_to_solve: The key is to eliminate red herrings: the blue hoodie is worn by hundreds, Priya’s phone location has a plausible explanation, Professor Roy’s alibi lapse is unrelated. Rohan’s anger is evident but he was in the library. Vikram’s alibi ends at 8:30 PM, but he was seen at 11:30 PM near the gym. Only he had the key to the locker. The jersey wasn’t destroyed – it was hidden. His motive wasn’t malice, but misguided leadership. The duffel bag sighting and fabric evidence point conclusively to him.

case.title: The Case of the Sabotaged Scholarship
case.setting: Kalinga Institute of Technology, Bhubaneswar - Department of Computer Science
case.crime: A top student's national merit scholarship application was altered to contain false academic misconduct allegations, leading to its rejection.
case.victim: Arjun Mehta, 21, final-year Computer Science student with a 9.7 CGPA

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.motive: She was the second-ranked student and stood to gain the scholarship if Arjun was disqualified.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying for her Machine Learning quiz from 6 PM to 9 PM.
suspects.secret: She plagiarized a minor assignment last semester and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to review Arjun’s application draft and had access to his shared Google Drive folder.

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.motive: He applied for the same scholarship and needs the money to avoid dropping out.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at his cousin’s wedding in Cuttack that evening.
suspects.secret: He accessed the department server last month to fix a grading glitch for a friend—unauthorized but well-intentioned.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the department computer lab after hours the night before the sabotage.

suspects.name: Dr. Nandini Rao
suspects.motive: Publicly criticized Arjun for his 'arrogant attitude' after he questioned her grading in class.
suspects.alibi: Was at a faculty dinner at the college guesthouse from 7 PM to 10 PM; confirmed by three colleagues.
suspects.secret: She is the anonymous donor of a smaller scholarship and wanted Arjun to fail so he'd accept hers instead.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person to access the scholarship portal before the deadline via admin credentials.

evidence.description: Edited Google Doc of Arjun’s scholarship essay, showing a revision history where a paragraph accusing him of cheating in 'CS302' was added from an IP address linked to the college Wi-Fi.
evidence.significance: Proves intentional sabotage; timestamped at 8:47 PM on submission day.

evidence.description: Security log showing Dr. Rao’s admin login to the scholarship portal at 8:45 PM on submission day.
evidence.significance: Suggests she could have submitted the fake misconduct report.

evidence.description: Rohan’s college ID card found near the computer lab trash bin, with smudged ink as if hastily discarded.
evidence.significance: Suggests he was on campus despite claiming to be at a wedding.

evidence.description: Google Drive access log showing Priya opened Arjun’s document at 8:30 PM on submission day and stayed active for 18 minutes.
evidence.significance: She had opportunity and access.

evidence.description: Library security guard confirms Priya was present from 6:10 PM onward but left briefly at 8:15 PM for ‘fresh air’ and returned at 8:50 PM.
evidence.significance: Her alibi has a 35-minute gap matching the sabotage window.

evidence.description: A cached browser snapshot from the lab computer showing the fake misconduct form draft, auto-saved under a guest profile.
evidence.significance: Proves physical use of lab computer for sabotage.

evidence.description: Cafeteria staff remembers seeing Rohan on campus that night, but can’t confirm time.
evidence.significance: Contradicts his wedding alibi.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Arjun submits his final scholarship application draft to Professor Rao.
6:10 PM: Priya enters the library; Rohan’s ID is swiped at campus gate (outbound).
7:00 PM: Faculty dinner begins; Dr. Rao seen there by multiple staff.
8:15 PM: Priya leaves library briefly; security camera shows her heading toward admin block.
8:30 PM: Google Drive log shows Priya accessing Arjun’s document.
8:45 PM: Dr. Rao logs into scholarship portal (routine check, per her statement).
8:47 PM: Malicious paragraph added to Arjun’s essay via Google Docs.
8:50 PM: Priya returns to library, seen by guard.
9:00 PM: Rohan’s cousin texts him a wedding photo; Rohan replies instantly (proving remote presence).
10:00 PM: Scholarship portal locks; changes can no longer be made.
red_herrings: Dr. Rao’s late login suggests tampering, but she only reviewed submissions.
Rohan’s lost ID and canteen sighting imply he was on campus, but he was at the wedding.
The lab computer draft was planted; auto-save doesn’t match final altered version.
Priya’s plagiarism secret distracts from her motive but isn’t directly related.

solution.method: Used her access to Arjun’s shared Google Drive folder to edit his essay directly, adding the false misconduct claim from a lab computer she accessed during her library break.
solution.motive: Desperate to secure the scholarship for herself, knowing Arjun was her only competition.
solution.proof: The Google Drive revision history shows her account made the edit, and the library guard confirms her unaccounted absence exactly during the sabotage window.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference the Google Drive access log with the library security timeline. The only person with motive, opportunity, and access during the 8:30–8:50 PM window is Priya. Rohan’s wedding alibi is verified by message timestamp, and Dr. Rao’s portal access was read-only. The lab computer cache is a red herring—Priya used it to mislead but saved the edit from her account, which can’t be faked.

case.title: The Case of the Sabotaged Stage
case.setting: Sri Ramachandra College of Arts & Science, Chennai – Main Auditorium and adjacent backstage storage room
case.crime: All key stage props for the inter-college drama fest finals were deliberately damaged overnight
case.victim: The college drama club and its reputation; also affects the upcoming finale performance of 'Midnight Masquerade'

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.motive: His rival team won the judges' preference vote; he stood to gain if their performance was ruined
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at an all-night coding hackathon in the computer lab
suspects.secret: He plagiarized part of his own team's script and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Seemed unusually calm about the sabotage, almost pleased

suspects.name: Professor Nalini Iyer
suspects.motive: Strongly opposed the theme of 'Midnight Masquerade,' calling it 'morally questionable' due to its themes of deception and rebellion
suspects.alibi: Says she was at home grading papers and was alone
suspects.secret: She secretly applied for early retirement and was rejected, making her resentful of college activities
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the auditorium late at night arguing with students days before

suspects.name: Priya Venkatesh
suspects.personality: quiet, brilliant, socially awkward, intensely loyal
suspects.motive: Was fired as the lead prop designer a week ago due to 'creative differences'; held a grudge
suspects.alibi: Claims she was working on a research paper in her dorm room
suspects.secret: She still has a duplicate key to the storage room
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her sketchbook contains detailed, angry scribbles of broken props

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.motive: Was reprimanded by the drama club president for 'poor maintenance' of storage locks
suspects.alibi: Says he was asleep in the staff quarters
suspects.secret: He’s been borrowing props to run a side business renting them for weddings
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Nervous when questioned; over-explains trivial details

evidence.description: Torn piece of blue fabric caught in the jagged edge of a broken masquerade throne
evidence.location: On the damaged throne in the storage room
evidence.significance: Matches the uniform of stagehands, but also similar to janitor uniforms

evidence.description: A single unused prop key with 'P.V.' scratched faintly on the handle
evidence.location: Under a stack of tarps in storage
evidence.significance: Suggests Priya still had access, but could have been planted

evidence.description: Timestamped campus security log showing access to auditorium side door at 2:17 AM by ID card 4821 (Aarav Mehta)
evidence.significance: Places Aarav at the scene, but he claims his card was stolen

evidence.description: Night canteen staff recalls seeing Professor Iyer near the auditorium around 11:30 PM with a large folder
evidence.significance: Timeline places her nearby, but doesn’t confirm entry

evidence.description: A heavy-duty bolt cutter with fresh sawdust and paint flakes matching the props
evidence.location: Hidden behind the furnace in the basement near staff quarters
evidence.significance: Tool used to cut locks and destroy props; linked to staff access

evidence.description: A receipt for industrial-strength cleaning solvent dated the previous evening, signed by Rohan Deshpande
evidence.location: In the janitor’s office trash bin
evidence.significance: Solvent could have been used to weaken wood props beforehand

evidence.description: Priya’s laptop shows a draft email to the drama club president titled 'You ruined my design' sent at 1:45 AM but never delivered
evidence.location: Recovered from Priya’s cloud drafts by consent
evidence.significance: Shows emotional distress but no proof of action

timeline: 7:00 PM – Drama club secures the auditorium after final rehearsal
9:30 PM – Professor Iyer seen near auditorium with folder by canteen staff
10:15 PM – Aarav clocks into computer lab for hackathon (verified by sign-in)
11:00 PM – Rohan logs off security monitor system for 'scheduled reboot' (unauthorized)
2:17 AM – ID card 4821 (Aarav) used at auditorium side door (camera shows figure in hoodie)
6:00 AM – Stage manager discovers destruction of props: throne smashed, masks slashed, backdrop torn
6:30 AM – College admin notified; campus police and faculty form investigation team
red_herrings: The 'P.V.' key suggests Priya broke in
Professor Iyer's late-night presence implies involvement
Aarav's ID card at the scene seems incriminating
Priya's angry draft email looks like a confession

solution.method: Used his staff access to disable cameras, used bolt cutters to destroy props, weakened key wooden structures with solvent beforehand to make destruction easier and quieter
solution.motive: Revenge for being blamed for poor security; wanted to prove the drama club should take responsibility for their own props
solution.proof: The bolt cutter found behind the furnace has his fingerprints and fibers from his uniform; the solvent receipt ties him to the weakening of props
solution.how_to_solve: The timeline shows Rohan disabled the security system at 11:00 PM, creating a blind window. Aarav’s ID card was stolen during the hackathon (confirmed by witness). The bolt cutter and solvent receipt place Rohan at the scene with means and opportunity. The destruction required tools and knowledge of building access—only staff had all three. Priya’s key and email, while suspicious, lack physical corroboration. Professor Iyer had no access method. Rohan’s over-nervousness under questioning reinforces guilt. Solving requires connecting the unauthorized system reboot, tool location, and receipt.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Laptop
case.setting: Nehru College of Technology, Pune - Saraswati Hostel, Room 307
case.crime: An expensive MacBook Pro worth ₹2.3 lakh vanished from a locked hostel room during a 90-minute gap between classes.
case.victim: Rohan Mehta, a final-year Computer Science student and coding competition finalist

suspects.name: Kavya Deshpande
suspects.motive: Rohan beat her in a national coding hackathon last month, humiliating her publicly
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the student council meeting in the admin block from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM
suspects.secret: She’s secretly dating the hostel warden’s son, which violates hostel rules
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Rohan two days before the theft and avoided eye contact during questioning

suspects.name: Vikram Patel
suspects.motive: Owes ₹40,000 in overdue fees and has been researching MacBook resale value online
suspects.alibi: Says he was in the college library studying for a thermodynamics test
suspects.secret: Buys and resells used electronics online to support his family
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was spotted near Room 307 15 minutes before the theft and deleted his browser history after the incident

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.personality: charming, irresponsible, spends beyond means, habitual gambler
suspects.motive: Recently lost ₹50,000 in an online poker game and owes money to a shady peer
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a bar off-campus for a 'quick drink' during the gap period
suspects.secret: Has been placing illegal bets through a Telegram group
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His phone GPS shows he never left campus during the theft window

evidence.description: A single partial fingerprint on the windowsill of Room 307, smudged by rainwater
evidence.significance: Suggests possible entry via window, though the room is on the third floor

evidence.description: Rohan’s MacBook was last connected to the college Wi-Fi at 10:42 AM, logged in under the guest network
evidence.significance: Indicates the laptop was powered on and connected during the theft window

evidence.description: A torn Rs. 500 note found under Rohan’s bed with 'AP' scribbled on it in blue ink
evidence.significance: Matches Arjun’s initials; he was seen with similar marked notes at poker games

evidence.description: A first-year student, Neha, claims she saw Vikram near Room 307 at 9:45 AM wearing a hoodie, though it was warm
evidence.significance: Places Vikram near the crime scene before class

evidence.description: Vikram’s laptop search history (recovered) includes: 'how to factory reset MacBook Pro' and 'buy used MacBook Pune'
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation

evidence.description: A bent brass key scraper mark on the outside of Room 307’s door lock
evidence.significance: Indicates lock-picking attempt

evidence.description: Hostel CCTV shows Arjun entering the building at 10:15 AM through the fire escape, not the main gate
evidence.significance: Contradicts alibi; shows presence during theft window

timeline: 9:00 AM: Rohan leaves Room 307 for class, locks door with key
9:10 AM: Vikram seen in library (confirmed by librarian)
9:45 AM: Neha claims to see Vikram near Room 307 (later proven misidentification)
10:00 AM: Kavya enters admin block for student council meeting (verified by sign-in sheet)
10:15 AM: Arjun enters Saraswati Hostel via fire escape (CCTV footage)
10:18 AM: College Wi-Fi logs show Rohan’s MacBook connected via guest network
10:20 AM: Arjun’s phone GPS pings near hostel Wi-Fi router
11:15 AM: Rohan returns to Room 307, discovers laptop missing
11:25 AM: Complaint filed with hostel warden
red_herrings: Partial fingerprint on windowsill (left by a cleaning staff member during routine window cleaning two days prior)
Vikram’s search history (research for his side hustle, not theft prep)
Torn Rs. 500 note with 'AP' (Arjun had borrowed Rohan’s notebook earlier; it fell from the desk)
Hooded figure seen by Neha (later identified as a visiting cousin of another student)

solution.method: Used a forged master key (copied from the warden’s son, whom he knows through Kavya) to unlock Room 307, powered on the laptop briefly to disable tracking, then took it out through the fire escape
solution.motive: Desperate for cash to repay gambling debt and avoid threats from loan sharks
solution.proof: CCTV footage placing him in the hostel at 10:15 AM, Wi-Fi login from Rohan’s laptop at 10:18 AM (requires physical access), and his phone GPS confirming presence. The master key was later found hidden in his shoe
solution.how_to_solve: The key is the Wi-Fi log: the laptop connected at 10:18 AM, meaning someone had physical access to it after 10:00 AM. Kavya was in a verified meeting. Vikram was in the library. Only Arjun, despite his off-campus alibi, was on campus. His GPS and CCTV confirm this. The lock scratch matches a master key, not picking. The red herrings distract from the digital timestamp, which is the linchpin.

case.title: The Case of the Missing Admin
case.setting: Delhi Public College of Arts and Science, North Campus
case.crime: The anonymous removal of the official WhatsApp group admin from the 'DPC Final Year B.A. 2024' group, causing chaos in exam coordination and assignment distribution
case.victim: The student community of the Final Year B.A. batch, particularly those dependent on the group for academic updates

suspects.name: Riya Mehra
suspects.motive: She believed the admin was mismanaging the group and spreading misinformation about exam dates
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying alone from 6 PM to 9 PM on Tuesday
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously running a study motivation Instagram page that plagiarizes content
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She was seen arguing with the admin two days before the incident and had recently posted about 'clean leadership'

suspects.name: Arjun Patel
suspects.motive: He was removed as a co-admin earlier for posting memes during exam week and wanted revenge
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a cricket match at the college grounds with friends from 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM
suspects.secret: He’s secretly retaking his third year due to failed exams and is hiding it from everyone
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen smirking when the admin lost access and later joked, 'Group needed a reset'

suspects.name: Professor Anita Desai
suspects.motive: She disapproves of student-run WhatsApp groups and believes they spread rumors and reduce classroom authority
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers at home and was on a Zoom call with a colleague from 7 PM to 8:15 PM
suspects.secret: She has been using a fake account to report student groups to the college IT department
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly criticized the WhatsApp group in class last week, calling it 'a breeding ground for anarchy'

evidence.description: Log from WhatsApp showing the admin was removed at 7:42 PM on Tuesday by someone with admin rights who then immediately left the group
evidence.location: Admin access log (retrieved via group member with backup)
evidence.significance: Only current admins can remove another admin — the culprit must have been an admin before the incident

evidence.description: A deleted message in the group from Arjun saying, 'This admin is clueless. Time for a coup soon.'
evidence.location: Recovered from a student's notification log
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation by Arjun

evidence.description: A sticky note found in the library trash bin with WhatsApp group settings scribbled on it, including the word 'revoke'
evidence.significance: Could link to someone planning to remove the admin

evidence.description: A student claims they saw Riya near the computer lab at 7:30 PM, though she said she was in the library
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi

evidence.description: Professor Desai’s IP address accessed the college’s Wi-Fi network at 7:38 PM on Tuesday, but from the main building — the same building as the admin's dorm
evidence.significance: Places her on campus, contradicting her alibi of being at home

evidence.description: The admin rights were transferred to a new account named 'B.A._Guardian' at 7:43 PM, which was created that same day
evidence.significance: The new admin must be the culprit or their accomplice

evidence.description: A club member confirms Arjun helped them access a ‘ghost admin’ trick in another group last semester using a temporary re-add loophole
evidence.significance: Shows Arjun has technical knowledge of exploiting admin transfer weaknesses

timeline: 6:00 PM, Tuesday: Group admin posts updated exam schedule
6:15 PM: Arjun comments sarcastically, 'Hope this one is accurate unlike last time'
6:30 PM: Cricket match begins; Arjun seen there by 4 friends
7:00 PM: Professor Desai joins Zoom call with colleague (claims she's at home)
7:10 PM: Riya seen entering library by security cam
7:38 PM: Professor Desai’s IP logs into college Wi-Fi
7:42 PM: Admin removed from WhatsApp group
7:43 PM: 'B.A._Guardian' added as new admin
8:15 PM: Professor ends Zoom call
8:30 PM: Cricket match ends; Arjun leaves campus
9:00 PM: Riya leaves library; confirmed by exit cam
red_herrings: The sticky note in the library implies Riya was planning the removal
The witness sighting of Riya near the computer lab contradicts her alibi
Professor Desai’s IP being on campus suggests she lied about being home
Arjun’s deleted threat message makes him look like the planner

solution.method: He used a known WhatsApp loophole: when an admin is removed, if the group is set to 'All Participants Can Add,' the person who removed the admin can temporarily re-add them and instantly reassign rights to a new account. He used a burner number to create 'B.A._Guardian' and executed it remotely during the cricket match by stepping out for 5 minutes.
solution.motive: He was humiliated after being demoted from co-admin and wanted to prove he was smarter and in control.
solution.proof: The witness from the debate club confirms Arjun taught this trick before, and the timing of the admin change (7:42–7:43 PM) coincides with a 7-minute gap when Arjun left the match saying he 'forgot his water bottle' — long enough to perform the exploit on his phone.
solution.how_to_solve: Deduction path: (1) Only an admin could remove the admin. (2) The new admin 'B.A._Guardian' was created right after, suggesting the remover planned to take over. (3) Arjun had both motive and technical knowledge. (4) His alibi has a gap during the crime window. (5) The other evidence (IP, sticky note, sighting) can be explained innocently — Desai’s IP was from a remote login, the sticky note was from a confused student, the sighting was a case of mistaken identity. Only Arjun had means, motive, and opportunity.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Fines
case.setting: Sri Ramachandra College of Science and Arts, Chennai – Central Library & Computer Lab
case.crime: The college library's automated fine payment system was hacked, resulting in the deletion of all pending fine records for over 300 students and a forged transaction log showing $0 collected. The hack occurred during finals week, exploiting a backdoor in the outdated system.
case.victim: The college library’s financial integrity and the trust in the academic honor system

suspects.name: Ananya Patel
suspects.personality: Brilliant, socially anxious, environmentally conscious, fiercely protective of fairness
suspects.motive: Believes the fine system exploits poor students and wanted to expose its flaws
suspects.alibi: Was in the library reading room from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM, studying for Environmental Science
suspects.secret: She’s been secretly organizing a student campaign against administrative overreach
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen typing rapidly in the computer lab the day before the hack and deleted her browser history

suspects.name: Professor Karthik Menon
suspects.personality: Strict, image-conscious, rule-abiding, protective of department reputation
suspects.motive: Wanted to cover up the fact that the department failed to update the library system despite repeated warnings, which could cost him his promotion
suspects.alibi: Attended a faculty meeting from 5:00 PM to 7:30 PM, then returned home
suspects.secret: Submitted a falsified 'system maintenance' report last month
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Urged the library to delay reporting the hack and claimed it was a 'server glitch'

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Owed ₹2,800 in fines and faced library suspension before a major project deadline
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a friend's off-campus apartment watching movies from 7:00 PM onward
suspects.secret: Has a side hustle selling pirated software to other students
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was caught trying to access the admin panel of the library website two weeks prior

evidence.description: Log file showing a login from IP 192.168.3.15 at 8:47 PM the night before finals began. The session deleted all fine records and uploaded a script named 'clean_fines_v2.py'.
evidence.significance: Pinpoints time and method of hack. IP 192.168.3.15 belongs to a workstation in the Computer Lab.

evidence.description: A sticky note with the library admin password 'LibAdmin@SRCSA2023' written in blue ink, found crumpled under a desk in the computer lab.
evidence.location: Under workstation #7 in the computer lab
evidence.significance: Suggests password theft. Workstation #7 was logged in at the time of the hack.

evidence.description: A draft blog post on Ananya Patel's cloud account titled 'How the Library’s Fine System Perpetuates Inequality' with code snippets resembling SQL injection commands.
evidence.location: Google Docs accessed via library Wi-Fi
evidence.significance: Seems to show intent and technical knowledge, but was written weeks prior and never executed.

evidence.description: Library assistant Priya Nair recalls seeing Professor Menon accessing a terminal in the computer lab at 8:15 PM, though he was supposedly at home.
evidence.significance: Contradicts his alibi, but Priya admits lighting was poor and she may have mistaken someone else.

evidence.description: A cryptocurrency transaction log from Rohan’s phone (retrieved via college network audit) showing a $50 payment to a hacker forum three days before the breach.
evidence.location: Phone metadata synced to college Wi-Fi
evidence.significance: Suggests he hired someone, but the forum was for learning, not hiring.

evidence.description: Keystroke logs from workstation #7 reveal the hacker used Tab completion and a custom Python alias 'pyrun' – a setting only configured on Ananya’s personal profile.
evidence.significance: Links the machine to Ananya's account preferences

evidence.description: A timestamped security camera still showing someone wearing a green hoodie at workstation #7 at 8:42 PM. The person matches Ananya’s height and posture.
evidence.significance: Visual confirmation of presence during hack window

timeline: 5:00 PM – Faculty meeting begins (Professor Menon in attendance)
6:00 PM – Ananya checked into library reading room via ID swipe
7:00 PM – Rohan claims to have left for friend’s apartment
8:15 PM – Library assistant possibly sees Professor Menon in computer lab (unconfirmed)
8:42 PM – Security camera shows figure in green hoodie at workstation #7
8:47 PM – Hack initiated from IP 192.168.3.15 (workstation #7)
9:00 PM – System alert triggered but auto-dismissed by值班 staff
9:30 PM – Ananya swipes out of the library
10:00 AM (next day) – Library staff discovers all fines are zeroed
red_herrings: The sticky note with the password suggests an amateur hack, pointing to Rohan
Ananya's blog draft makes her appear ideologically motivated and technically capable
Professor Menon’s falsified report and contradictory sighting make him look guilty of a cover-up
Rohan’s crypto payment implies he hired a hacker

solution.method: Used her deep knowledge of the library system to exploit a known SQL vulnerability. She logged in using a shared workstation, bypassed authentication using a session hijack technique she researched, then executed a script to delete fine records and alter logs.
solution.motive: She believed the fine system unfairly punished underprivileged students and wanted to force systemic change by exposing its fragility.
solution.proof: The keystroke logs showing her unique 'pyrun' alias and Tab completion behavior, combined with the timestamped camera footage, place her at the machine during the hack. Her alibi is weakened by the 30-minute gap between her library entry and the hack – enough time to move to the computer lab unseen.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must discount the red herrings by noting: the password note was too obvious (likely planted), Rohan’s payment was to a learning forum, Menon’s sighting was unverified. The real clue is the 'pyrun' alias—unique to Ananya—embedded in system logs. Combined with her ideological motive and presence in the building, this establishes guilt through digital footprint matching.

case.title: The Case of the Leaked Celebrity Invite
case.setting: Vishwakarma Institute of Technology, Pune – during its annual cultural fest 'Vishwa Utsav'
case.crime: The exclusive invitation to surprise celebrity guest Aryan Malhotra, a rising Bollywood star, was leaked to a fan forum 48 hours before the event, causing chaos and media attention.
case.victim: The Fest Organizing Committee and the college's reputation

suspects.name: Kavya Mehta
suspects.motive: Wanted to increase fest visibility and footfall; believed a controlled leak would generate buzz without blame
suspects.alibi: Was reviewing stage decorations at the main auditorium from 6 PM to 9 PM on the day of the leak
suspects.secret: She's running for student council president and fears a low-profile fest will hurt her chances
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen hastily deleting messages on her phone when approached by committee members the next day

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.motive: Is a huge fan of Aryan Malhotra and wanted to gain clout by being the 'first' to post the news online
suspects.alibi: Claims he was gaming with friends online from 7 PM to 11 PM
suspects.secret: Runs an anonymous fan blog with 50k followers under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Posted a cryptic story on Instagram: 'Big things coming. #StarPower' minutes after the leak

suspects.name: Dr. Anil Patil
suspects.personality: Traditional, strict, skeptical of celebrity culture, deeply image-conscious
suspects.motive: Opposed the celebrity invite from the start, believing it was 'frivolous'; may have leaked it to sabotage the event
suspects.alibi: Was grading papers in his office until 8:30 PM
suspects.secret: Submitted a conservative proposal for the fest that was rejected in favor of a 'glamorous' theme
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made a public comment in a meeting: 'If the invite gets out, it’s on them, not me'

evidence.description: A post on the 'BollywoodFanatics_IN' forum with the subject 'Aryan Malhotra coming to VIT Pune!' posted at 8:12 PM. Attached is a blurred but recognizable screenshot of the official invite email.
evidence.significance: Proves the leak occurred after 7 PM, when the final invite email was sent

evidence.description: Metadata from the leaked image shows it was captured on a OnePlus 9 smartphone.
evidence.location: Server logs of the fan forum
evidence.significance: Rohan owns a OnePlus 9; Kavya and Dr. Patil use different devices

evidence.description: A torn piece of paper found in the department office bin with the words '...not appropriate for academics...' and 'Malhotra' partially visible.
evidence.location: Waste bin outside Dr. Patil's office
evidence.significance: Suggests Dr. Patil was angry about the celebrity invite

evidence.description: A junior student reports seeing Kavya arguing with Dr. Patil near the admin block at 6:45 PM about 'publicity strategies'.
evidence.significance: Shows tension between two key figures

evidence.description: Kavya’s phone backup log shows she deleted a 2-minute voice note from Rohan at 7:58 PM.
evidence.significance: Suggests collaboration or guilt; voice note could contain incriminating content

evidence.description: The official invite email was accessed from the college’s guest Wi-Fi network at 7:56 PM, originating from IP address 192.168.10.42.
evidence.significance: Only someone on campus with access could have done this at that time

evidence.description: The security guard at the admin gate confirms a student matching Rohan’s description entered the admin block at 7:40 PM using a staff ID card borrowed from a friend.
evidence.significance: Places Rohan in a restricted area at the time of the leak

timeline: 6:00 PM – Final invite email sent to core committee members
6:45 PM – Kavya and Dr. Patil seen arguing near admin block
7:40 PM – Rohan enters admin block using borrowed staff ID
7:56 PM – Invite email accessed via guest Wi-Fi (IP 192.168.10.42)
8:12 PM – Post appears on BollywoodFanatics_IN forum
8:30 PM – Dr. Patil leaves office
9:00 PM – Kavya finishes auditorium inspection
red_herrings: The torn note in Dr. Patil's bin suggesting sabotage
Kavya deleting the voice note from Rohan
Rohan owning the same phone model as the leak
Kavya’s secretive behavior with her phone

solution.method: Used a borrowed staff ID to enter the admin block, logged into a staff computer via guest Wi-Fi, accessed the invite email forwarded to a committee member, and uploaded the screenshot to the fan forum.
solution.motive: Wanted fame and recognition on his fan blog; believed being first to break the news would boost his online influence.
solution.proof: Security footage timestamped 7:42 PM shows Rohan at the staff computer terminal; matched with server log of email access and forum post time. His borrowed ID was logged at entry.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is the access time (7:56 PM) and IP address. Only someone physically in the admin block could use that terminal. Rohan was seen entering at 7:40 PM. The OnePlus 9 metadata is a red herring—many students own that model. The real proof is the combination of physical access, Wi-Fi log, and security entry. Kavya's deleted voice note was just her warning Rohan not to leak it, which he ignored.

case.title: The Case of the Shattered Weights
case.setting: Vasudev College of Arts, Science & Sports, Pune – Central Gymnasium
case.crime: Multiple gym machines sabotaged overnight: resistance cables cut, barbell collars filed down, and protein shaker bottles filled with sand
case.victim: College gym and athletes preparing for inter-university sports meet

suspects.name: Aryan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wants to eliminate top competitors in weightlifting and sprinting to secure his spot on the team
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at an all-night study session in the library with friends
suspects.secret: He cheated on his last semester exams and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to volunteer for equipment inspection; acts overly shocked

suspects.name: Priya Deshpande
suspects.motive: Her artwork was rejected from the college fest; blames athletics for overshadowing arts
suspects.alibi: Says she was sketching at the rooftop garden alone
suspects.secret: She’s been skipping classes and hiding poor grades
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the gym late at night with a backpack, denies entering

suspects.name: Professor Nikhil Rao
suspects.motive: Wants to push for gym renovation and believes sabotage will force administration to act
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers at home; no witnesses
suspects.secret: He’s secretly applying for a job at a rival college
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested 'mysterious external sabotage' too quickly

evidence.description: Frayed resistance cable with fine, clean cut—consistent with a precision wire cutter
evidence.location: Torn cable on leg extension machine
evidence.significance: Suggests deliberate sabotage with proper tools

evidence.description: Three protein shakers filled with fine beach sand; one has a painted chipped corner with peacock design
evidence.location: Locker of team captain, found in changing room
evidence.significance: Targeted prank or sabotage; the peacock matches Priya’s art style

evidence.description: CCTV footage shows blurred figure in grey hoodie entering gym at 1:17 AM, exiting at 1:48 AM
evidence.significance: Confirms intrusion during night; no clear face

evidence.description: Small metal file covered in rust and rubber residue found behind storage cabinet
evidence.significance: Matches tool used to file barbell collars; rubber residue matches gym mat

evidence.description: Rohit, night watchman, says he saw someone resembling Aryan near gym at 1:00 AM but wasn’t sure
evidence.significance: Weakly points to Aryan

evidence.description: Torn sketch of the gym with red X over machines; found in trash bin outside art studio
evidence.significance: Suggests planning; drawing style matches Priya’s

evidence.description: Email draft on Professor Rao’s college account titled 'Urgent Safety Report' describing gym hazards, never sent
evidence.location: Recovered from professor’s computer via tech admin
evidence.significance: Shows intent to highlight gym issues, possibly justify sabotage

timeline: 6:00 PM: Gym closes after evening session.
6:15 PM: Aryan seen arguing with team coach about selection trials.
7:30 PM: Priya collects sketchpad from art studio, walks toward dorms.
8:00 PM: Professor Rao attends faculty meeting, leaves at 9:30 PM.
1:17 AM: Blurry figure in grey hoodie enters gym via side door.
1:48 AM: Figure exits, hood pulled low.
6:00 AM: Janitor discovers damage while cleaning.
7:00 AM: College security alerted; investigation begins.
red_herrings: Peacock-painted shaker links to Priya’s artwork
Torn sketch with red X suggests Priya planned sabotage
Rohit’s uncertain ID of Aryan near gym at night
Professor Rao’s unsent email about gym dangers

solution.method: Used wire cutters and file from his engineering project kit to damage equipment; wore hoodie to avoid cameras
solution.motive: To disable top athletes’ training, increasing his chances of selection for the inter-university meet
solution.proof: The file found behind storage has Aryan’s fingerprints; matches one missing from his project toolbox in engineering lab
solution.how_to_solve: Though evidence points to multiple suspects, only Aryan had both motive tied to competition and access to precision tools. The fingerprint on the file is definitive. Priya’s sketch and shaker were planted red herrings—she often draws the gym. Rao’s email was never sent. The hooded figure’s build matches Aryan’s frame. Corroborate with library friends—none confirm seeing him all night.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Research Notes
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Science and Technology, Mumbai - Department of Biotechnology
case.crime: Professor Anika Mehta's encrypted USB drive containing five years of unpublished cancer research was stolen from her locked office drawer during a faculty meeting.
case.victim: Professor Anika Mehta – a respected 42-year-old biotech researcher on the verge of a major breakthrough in targeted gene therapy.

suspects.name: Rohan Patel
suspects.personality: Intense, ambitious, socially awkward, highly intelligent
suspects.motive: He was recently rejected as lead author on Professor Mehta's upcoming paper, despite believing his contributions deserved it.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for his comprehensive exams from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He has been secretly applying to rival labs in the US without Mehta’s knowledge.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Professor Mehta the day before the theft. Also seems unusually calm about the situation.

suspects.name: Dr. Farhan Siddiqui
suspects.motive: His own research grant proposal on a similar topic was rejected last month; Mehta’s breakthrough could overshadow his career.
suspects.alibi: Attended the full faculty meeting from 2:30 PM to 4:00 PM in Room B203.
suspects.secret: He has been plagiarizing small sections of another scholar’s work in a side publication.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Asked unusually detailed questions about the security of Mehta’s files during the meeting, just before the theft was discovered.

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.personality: Eager to please, observant, anxious, diligent
suspects.motive: Fears being blamed since she was the last person seen in the lab before the theft. May have taken the notes to prove herself.
suspects.alibi: Says she left the lab at 2:15 PM and went straight to a student council meeting in the arts building.
suspects.secret: She accidentally spilled a reagent on Mehta’s secondary notes the previous week and never reported it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Hesitates when questioned, avoids eye contact, and initially lied about whether she touched the drawer.

evidence.description: A single partial fingerprint on the outside of the locked drawer – smudged but partially visible.
evidence.location: On the metal handle of Professor Mehta’s office drawer.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone tried to open it without a key. Matches no one in the department database.

evidence.description: A failed login attempt on Professor Mehta’s university cloud storage at 2:47 PM, traced to a terminal in the main computer lab.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone tried to access her files remotely during the faculty meeting.

evidence.description: A torn corner of a lab notebook with chemical calculations in Mehta’s handwriting found crumpled behind a bookshelf near the lab entrance.
evidence.location: Behind a bookshelf in the Biotech lab corridor.
evidence.significance: Indicates possible struggle or hurried disposal. Later confirmed to be from a discarded draft.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing someone in a lab coat leaving Mehta’s office around 2:20 PM, but couldn't identify the person.
evidence.significance: Suggests the theft occurred before the faculty meeting when the office should have been empty.

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Dr. Siddiqui entering Mehta’s office at 2:22 PM, staying for 3 minutes, then leaving. He is not on the official meeting attendance list until 2:30 PM.
evidence.location: Campus surveillance system (corridor outside Mehta’s office).
evidence.significance: Places a suspect alone in the office minutes before the janitor’s sighting.

evidence.description: A spare key to Mehta’s office found hidden inside a potted plant in the department lounge.
evidence.location: Behind a ficus plant in the staff lounge.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone had access to a copy. Mehta didn’t know a spare existed.

evidence.description: A timestamped draft email in Professor Mehta’s outbox from 2:25 PM, addressed to her colleague, stating 'I’ve backed up the research data to my cloud. Key is in the drawer. – Anika'.
evidence.location: Email server logs and Mehta’s computer.
evidence.significance: Proves the notes were still in the drawer at 2:25 PM and suggests a motive for theft – someone saw the email and knew where the key was.

timeline: 2:00 PM: Priya Malhotra finishes her lab work and leaves the department.
2:15 PM: Rohan Patel arrives at the library.
2:20 PM: Janitor sees someone in a lab coat exiting Mehta’s office.
2:22 PM: Security camera shows Dr. Siddiqui entering Mehta’s office.
2:25 PM: Timestamped draft email from Mehta’s computer indicates backup complete and key location.
2:30 PM: Faculty meeting begins. Dr. Siddiqui arrives and is marked present.
2:47 PM: Failed login attempt on Mehta’s cloud storage from computer lab.
4:00 PM: Meeting ends. Theft discovered when Mehta returns to office.
red_herrings: The partial fingerprint – actually from a technician who tried the drawer earlier in the week.
The failed login attempt – a student later confesses to trying to access Mehta’s public syllabus for exam tips.
The torn notebook – discarded by Mehta herself days earlier.
Rohan’s US applications – unrelated to the theft, though they make him seem secretive.

solution.method: He used a spare key copied weeks earlier to enter Mehta’s office at 2:22 PM, stole the USB drive from the drawer after reading her email draft, and left before the faculty meeting. He then pretended to arrive at 2:30 PM.
solution.motive: Professional jealousy and fear that Mehta’s breakthrough would secure funding and recognition he desperately needed.
solution.proof: Security footage shows him entering the office at 2:22 PM. The timestamped email confirms the drive was still present at 2:25 PM. The spare key hidden in the lounge links to him, as only faculty had access to the key cabinet.
solution.how_to_solve: The key deduction is the email timestamp: if the drive was still in the drawer at 2:25 PM, the thief must have taken it after that moment. Only Dr. Siddiqui was seen near the office (via camera) during that window. His alibi is broken by the footage. The spare key confirms premeditation. The other evidence leads can be explained by coincidence or unrelated actions.

case.title: The Case of the Viral Revenge Post
case.setting: Vidyarthi Mahavidyalaya, a bustling college campus in Jaipur, Rajasthan, known for its social activism and tight-knit student community
case.crime: A damaging social media post falsely accuses the college's beloved student council president of cheating in exams and physically threatening a peer. The post goes viral within hours, sparking protests and online harassment.
case.victim: Aarav Malhotra, 21, Student Council President — emotionally distressed, suspended temporarily pending investigation, reputation in ruins

suspects.name: Kriti Sharma
suspects.motive: She lost the student council election to Aarav by a narrow margin and resents his popularity despite what she sees as poor academic performance.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying for a chemistry exam from 6 PM to 9 PM.
suspects.secret: She plagiarized her debate competition entry last semester and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Aarav two days before the post went up, and deleted her browser history the morning after.

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: He was rejected by Aarav’s sister, who he was dating briefly. He posted online before about 'getting even' with people who 'screwed him over'.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night movie with friends at the mall.
suspects.secret: He used a fake ID to buy alcohol and was caught by campus security, which could get him expelled.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Liked the revenge post anonymously under a burner account and was seen laughing about 'watching the chaos' the next day.

suspects.name: Prof. Nandini Rao
suspects.motive: Aarav accused her of bias in grading last semester and filed a formal complaint, which embarrassed her department.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers at home alone.
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously mentoring a student in a romantic correspondence, blurring professional boundaries.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was unusually eager to support the investigation and suggested Aarav 'might not be as innocent as he looks'.

evidence.description: The revenge post was made on an anonymous Instagram account '@JaipurExposed' at 8:17 PM. It includes photoshopped exam answer sheets and a fake threat message allegedly sent by Aarav.
evidence.significance: The post caused immediate backlash. Metadata shows it was uploaded via a college Wi-Fi network.

evidence.description: Kriti’s laptop was found to have visited the '@JaipurExposed' account twice the day before the post, but no login or upload activity.
evidence.significance: Suggests she was stalking the account, but not proof of creation.

evidence.description: A security guard reports seeing Rohan near campus Wi-Fi hub at 8:10 PM, claiming he 'forgot something' in the computer lab.
evidence.significance: Places him near the upload location minutes before the post.

evidence.description: A sticky note with the password 'Exposed@JM2024' was found crumpled in a bin outside the faculty lounge.
evidence.significance: Matches the password to '@JaipurExposed' recovered via digital forensics.

evidence.description: Rohan’s phone shows a timestamped selfie from the mall cinema at 8:20 PM — supposedly proving his alibi.
evidence.significance: Appears to confirm he wasn’t on campus when the post went live.

evidence.description: A student saw Prof. Rao entering the admin building around 7:45 PM, though she claimed to be at home.
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi and places her on campus.

evidence.description: The '@JaipurExposed' account used a unique font style (‘Bebas Neue’) also found in a deleted draft email from Prof. Rao’s registered college email.
evidence.significance: Links her digital footprint to the post’s design — the smoking gun.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Aarav leaves the student council office after a long meeting.
6:30 PM: Kriti enters the library — confirmed by entry logs.
7:15 PM: Rohan arrives at the cinema mall with friends.
7:45 PM: Prof. Rao is spotted entering the admin building by a student.
8:10 PM: Security guard sees Rohan near Computer Lab B.
8:17 PM: '@JaipurExposed' posts the revenge message via college Wi-Fi.
8:20 PM: Rohan’s selfie timestamped at the cinema appears online.
9:00 PM: Viral backlash begins; Aarav receives first threatening DM.
10:30 PM: College IT logs show a device linked to faculty credentials accessed the network near the admin server room.
red_herrings: Kriti’s visits to the anonymous account suggest involvement, but she was only researching rumors.
Rohan’s presence near the lab and love for drama make him look guilty, but he was set up.
Prof. Rao’s presence on campus contradicts her alibi, but initially seems unrelated.
Rohan’s selfie appears to confirm alibi, but was pre-scheduled to post automatically.

solution.method: She created the '@JaipurExposed' account using a faculty guest login in the admin building, uploaded the post via college Wi-Fi at 8:17 PM, and wiped her device traces. Used design tools matching her previous academic presentations.
solution.motive: She felt humiliated by Aarav’s formal complaint and wanted to discredit him publicly, believing he was undeserving of his influence.
solution.proof: The unique font 'Bebas Neue' in the post matches a deleted draft email from her college account. IT logs show faculty-level access from the admin server room at the time of the post.
solution.how_to_solve: Analyzing the digital design fingerprint links the post to Prof. Rao. The sticky note password near her office, her false alibi, and the server log access confirm her presence and technical capability. Rohan’s selfie was auto-posted, and Kriti’s browsing was curiosity, not guilt.

case.title: The Case of the Spoiled Sambar
case.setting: Hostel 3, Kaveri Mess, Ananda College of Engineering, Tamil Nadu
case.crime: Systematic sabotage of mess food quality leading to health complaints and mass protests
case.victim: Mess committee and student body (collective health and trust)

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.role: final-year student and ex-mess committee member
suspects.personality: intense, organized, socially awkward, holds grudges
suspects.motive: Was removed from the mess committee after a dispute over food budgets
suspects.alibi: Claims to be in the library studying for competitive exams from 6 PM to 10 PM on all sabotage nights
suspects.secret: Secretly dating the current mess committee head, which he hides to appear unbiased
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly defensive when questioned and tries to redirect blame to the cook

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.role: second-year student and influencer on campus food review page
suspects.motive: Wants to expose the mess to boost her social media following and attract brand sponsorships
suspects.alibi: Says she was streaming live on Instagram during the incidents
suspects.secret: Running an off-campus food delivery side hustle that competes with the mess
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Coached some students to exaggerate symptoms for dramatic effect

suspects.name: Kamala Das
suspects.motive: Angered by recent pay cut blamed on student mismanagement
suspects.alibi: Says she went home by 8 PM each night after handing over kitchen duties
suspects.secret: Hides her son’s gambling debts, fearing it could cost her job
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the mess storage room late one night with a key she shouldn’t have had

evidence.description: A half-empty bottle of industrial-grade cleaning solution found behind spice racks with traces in a sambar pot
evidence.location: Kaveri Mess kitchen, behind turmeric containers
evidence.significance: The substance explains the bitter taste and gastrointestinal symptoms

evidence.description: Instagram live stream showing Priya Nair talking about exam stress on the night of the first incident
evidence.significance: Appears to confirm alibi

evidence.description: A key to the mess storage room found under Rohan’s mattress during a dorm check
evidence.significance: Suggests unauthorized access to kitchen area

evidence.description: A receipt for bulk purchase of low-quality lentils from a shady vendor dated two days before sabotage
evidence.significance: Suggests she tried to save money by cutting corners

evidence.description: A first-year student recalls seeing someone in a hoodie tampering with pots around 8:30 PM
evidence.significance: Places an unknown person at the scene

evidence.description: Security camera footage (fuzzy) showing someone unlocking the back door of the mess kitchen at 8:15 PM
evidence.location: Campus security office, camera facing rear exit
evidence.significance: Proves unauthorized late-night access; figure matches Priya’s build

evidence.description: Another student confirms Priya’s livestream was prerecorded — seen editing it earlier
evidence.significance: Breaks her alibi

timeline: Day 1: Mess food receives multiple complaints — sambar unusually bitter, rice undercooked.
Day 3: 7 students report nausea and dizziness after dinner; campus health center involved.
Day 4: Protest held demanding mess overhaul; Principal orders investigation.
Day 5: First evidence (cleaning bottle) found; security cameras reviewed.
Day 6: Receipt found in Kamala’s apron; Rohan’s key discovered.
Day 7: Live stream alibi challenged by peer; security footage analyzed further.
Night of Day 7: Camera shows figure entering kitchen at 8:15 PM, exiting at 8:40 PM.
red_herrings: Kamala’s receipt suggests cost-cutting sabotage.
Rohan’s hidden key implies he accessed the kitchen.
Priya’s fake livestream makes her seem guilty of hiding evidence.
Kamala seen near storage room with a key, reinforcing suspicion.

solution.method: Used a duplicated kitchen key to enter at night; added diluted cleaning solution to sambar and stirred contaminated lentils into rice
solution.motive: Wanted a viral scandal to grow her social media brand and undermine the mess as competition to her food delivery service
solution.proof: Security footage shows her build and gait entering the kitchen; second witness confirms her livestream was prerecorded; her fingerprints on the cleaning bottle cap
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference alibis with digital proof. The livestream appears solid but is debunked by a peer. Rohan’s key and Kamala’s receipt are red herrings — both explain access or motive but lack direct evidence. Only Priya has broken alibi, opportunity, and physical proof (footage + fingerprints). The method required stealth and timing, fitting her influencer mindset.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Internship
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Technology and Management (DTM), Department of Computer Science, New Delhi
case.crime: A prestigious Google-sponsored AI internship opportunity was announced internally but hidden from the class group chat and noticeboard, affecting all final-year students
case.victim: Final-year Computer Science students who missed the 24-hour application window

suspects.name: Aarav Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted exclusive access to the internship to boost his placement chances in a saturated job market
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM
suspects.secret: He applied for the internship but was rejected in the first round last year and is terrified of failing again
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the department's admin portal on a lab computer the morning of the announcement

suspects.name: Professor Nandini Rao
suspects.personality: Strict, traditional, skeptical of corporate internships, values academic research
suspects.motive: Believes corporate internships distract students from pursuing research and PhD programs
suspects.alibi: Was conducting a class from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM, confirmed by attendance sheet
suspects.secret: She is applying for a sabbatical and feared department budget cuts if students leave for internships
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was overheard saying, 'This internship will only benefit a few and ruin the cohort’s academic focus.'

suspects.name: Tanya Verma
suspects.personality: Charismatic, influential in student council, strategic, empathetic
suspects.motive: Wanted to delay the internship announcement to help her cousin, who was traveling and couldn't apply on time
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a student council meeting in Room 204 from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM
suspects.secret: She helped her cousin cheat in an internal exam last semester and owes them a favor
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted a message thread with the department’s admin assistant the night before

evidence.description: Log entry showing someone accessed the internal department portal from Lab 3, PC-12 at 9:47 AM and deleted the internship announcement scheduled for 10:00 AM
evidence.significance: Proves the announcement was deliberately removed before broadcast

evidence.description: A screenshot from a student’s phone showing a message from Tanya to the admin assistant: 'Can you hold off on the post? Just for a few hours?'
evidence.location: Forwarded to detective by an anonymous student
evidence.significance: Suggests Tanya tried to delay the announcement

evidence.description: A sticky note found in the admin office trash with a handwritten reminder: 'Rao - meeting re: internship concerns - 10:15 AM'
evidence.significance: Suggests Professor Rao planned to oppose the announcement

evidence.description: Lab assistant reports seeing Aarav logging into a faculty account using a sticky note under PC-12
evidence.significance: Suggests Aarav used unauthorized access to delete the announcement

evidence.description: Tanya’s deleted message restored via backup: 'Ignore my earlier text. Proceed with the post. Family drama sorted.' Sent at 9:30 AM
evidence.significance: Shows Tanya withdrew her request to delay the announcement before it was deleted

evidence.description: Three students confirm Professor Rao was lecturing during the deletion window (9:47 AM)
evidence.significance: Supports her alibi

evidence.description: A coffee-stained copy of a rejection letter addressed to Aarav from 'Google AI Internship – Round 1 Fail' found crumpled in a bin near Lab 3
evidence.significance: Reveals Aarav’s past failure and possible motive for sabotage to ensure no one else gets the chance

timeline: 8:45 AM – Internship announcement scheduled to publish via department portal and group chat
9:30 AM – Tanya texts admin assistant asking to delay, then retracts request
9:47 AM – Unauthorized login from Lab 3, PC-12; announcement deleted from draft queue
10:00 AM – Announcement fails to appear; students begin inquiring
10:15 AM – Professor Rao meets admin to express concerns (as per sticky note), but after deletion
10:00–11:30 AM – Professor Rao teaches class (confirmed by attendance and students)
12:00 PM – Student discovers deletion in system logs; report filed
red_herrings: Tanya’s initial request to delay the post
Professor Rao’s vocal opposition to corporate internships
The sticky note suggesting a meeting to block the announcement
Tanya’s deleted message appearing suspicious before context restored

solution.method: Used a sticky note with a temporary faculty login (left by a careless professor) under PC-12 in Lab 3 to access the department portal and delete the internship announcement before it went live
solution.motive: Afraid that others would succeed where he had failed, and wanted to level the playing field by eliminating the opportunity altogether
solution.proof: Lab assistant’s testimony, server logs showing login from PC-12, and the crumpled rejection letter near Lab 3 link Aarav to both motive and action
solution.how_to_solve: Compare alibis: Professor Rao was teaching, Tanya retracted her delay request before the deletion. The login time (9:47 AM) and location (Lab 3) match Aarav’s known presence. The rejection letter confirms motive. Only Aarav had both access (via sticky note) and reason to sabotage the announcement.

case.title: The Case of the Rigged Rhythm
case.setting: Kalinga Institute of Technology, Bhubaneswar - Main Auditorium during Antaragni Fest
case.crime: The dance competition finals were rigged; scores were altered after judging to favor a single team.
case.victim: Praja Dance Crew and the integrity of the Antaragni Cultural Fest

suspects.name: Riya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Her team, Elite Pulse, narrowly won after suspicious score changes; she would lose her scholarship if they didn't win
suspects.alibi: Claimed to be in the green room reviewing performance footage with her team
suspects.secret: She plagiarized part of the choreography from a viral Korean dance video
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to give interviews after winning; avoided discussing the scoring process

suspects.name: Professor Arvind Nair
suspects.motive: Strongly opposed the inclusion of hip-hop in the fest; wanted to discredit dance events
suspects.alibi: Said he was in his office grading papers during score consolidation
suspects.secret: He submitted a false expense claim for last year’s fest and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly criticized the final results at the prize ceremony

suspects.name: Dev Talwar
suspects.motive: His childhood friend leads Elite Pulse; he has access to the scoring software
suspects.alibi: Claimed to be rebooting the projector system in the auditorium basement
suspects.secret: He skipped three mandatory committee meetings to play online tournaments
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the judges’ tablet station 10 minutes before results were announced

evidence.description: Log file from the scoring server shows a last-minute override of the final scores at 8:42 PM, initiated from a backend admin account.
evidence.significance: Proves scores were manually changed after judging ended.

evidence.description: A torn piece of notepad with scribbled calculations and 'EP +15?' written in blue ink.
evidence.location: Found near the judges’ table under a chair
evidence.significance: Suggests someone was altering scores manually; matches Riya’s handwriting.

evidence.description: A junior crew member saw Dev entering the judges’ booth with a tablet under his arm just after performances ended.
evidence.location: Testimony from Ananya, first-year event volunteer
evidence.significance: Places Dev near the scoring system during a critical window.

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Professor Nair walking toward the admin block at 8:38 PM, not his department.
evidence.location: CCTV footage from admin wing corridor
evidence.significance: Contradicts his alibi of being in his office; raises suspicion.

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'Backup Scores' found in a trash can outside the IT room. Contains unaltered original scores.
evidence.significance: Proves original scores were discarded; tampering occurred after judging.

timeline: 17:00 – Dance finals begin; 5 teams perform live.
18:30 – Judging concludes; scores entered into tablets.
18:40 – Scores sent to central server for consolidation.
18:42 – Server log shows admin override altering scores (Elite Pulse gains 18 points).
18:45 – Original score file deleted; USB drive with backup discarded.
18:50 – Dev seen near judges’ booth by volunteer.
18:55 – Professor Nair seen on CCTV near admin block.
19:00 – Official results announced; Elite Pulse declared winners.
19:15 – Riya gives celebratory interview; avoids question about scoring delay.
red_herrings: The torn notepad with 'EP +15?' – planted by Riya to frame suspicion on score manipulation but not linked to her actual method.
Professor Nair’s presence near admin block – he was secretly meeting a colleague to discuss fest budget cover-up.
Riya’s plagiarized choreography – a moral flaw but unrelated to score rigging.
Dev’s absence from committee meetings – creates doubt about his reliability but irrelevant to the crime.

solution.method: Used his admin access to the fest scoring software to override the final scores after they were submitted, inflating Elite Pulse’s score by 18 points.
solution.motive: Loyalty to his childhood friend, the captain of Elite Pulse, who promised him a spot in a Mumbai dance academy connection if they won.
solution.proof: Server logs show the override came from Dev’s authorized admin account; his access token was active at 18:42. The USB drive was wiped after copying, but forensic recovery reveals he accessed the original scores minutes before deletion.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is cross-referencing the server log (digital evidence) with witness testimony. Dev was the only one with both access and opportunity. The override required admin rights, which only Dev and two staff members had. The staff were accounted for. Riya’s notepad is a red herring—handwritten changes wouldn’t affect digital scores. Professor Nair lacked technical access. Dev’s presence near the booth and the discarded USB (which he failed to fully erase) seals his guilt.

case.title: The Case of the Hacked Confession Page
case.setting: Vidyalaya Institute of Technology, Mumbai — a bustling urban engineering college with a vibrant student culture
case.crime: The official college Instagram 'confession' page, @VITConfessions, was hacked and began posting deeply personal, humiliating confessions allegedly from students, including false claims of cheating, theft, and romantic betrayals. Over 12 posts went up in one night, causing widespread panic and social chaos.
