case.victim: The college student body, particularly those falsely implicated in the fake posts; the reputation of the college and the integrity of student-run digital platforms

suspects.name: Aryan Mehta
suspects.motive: Wanted to discredit the page after a real confession exposed his secret relationship with a professor’s daughter, which he denied.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at an all-night coding hackathon in the computer lab with teammates.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his final year project and is terrified of exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the page admin a week before the hack and later searched 'how to trace Instagram logins' on the college Wi-Fi.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Believes the confession page promotes toxic anonymity and cyberbullying; wanted to shut it down permanently to make a statement.
suspects.alibi: Says she was volunteering at a late-night mental health helpline on campus.
suspects.secret: She posted an anonymous confession herself six months ago about self-harm, which no one knows was hers.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed the college server logs two days before the hack under a 'research project' pretext.

suspects.name: Professor Rajan Malhotra
suspects.personality: strict, traditional, disdainful of social media, controlling
suspects.motive: Disapproves of the confession culture; his daughter was falsely accused in one of the fake posts, but he blames the platform, not the hacker.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers at home; no witnesses.
suspects.secret: He has been secretly monitoring student social media for 'disciplinary insights'.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen meeting with the IT head the day before the breach and requested expanded server access.

evidence.description: Login logs show that the @VITConfessions account was accessed from a college server IP at 11:47 PM, using a proxy to mask location.
evidence.significance: The hack originated inside the college network, suggesting insider involvement.

evidence.description: A draft post in Aryan’s personal cloud notes titled 'How to Ruin a Confession Page' with technical details on phishing attacks.
evidence.location: Aryan's Google Drive, synced to college network
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation and technical knowledge.

evidence.description: A night security guard reports seeing Professor Malhotra entering the admin building at 10:30 PM on the night of the hack.
evidence.significance: Places the professor on campus during the breach window.

evidence.description: A crumpled sticky note found in a campus trash bin with the Instagram password for @VITConfessions written on it.
evidence.significance: Suggests the password was physically exposed — possibly a leak.

evidence.description: Metadata from the first hacked post shows it was uploaded using a college-issued tablet registered to the Computer Science department.
evidence.location: Instagram server logs (obtained via IT cooperation)
evidence.significance: Device was assigned to faculty but often used by students under supervision.

evidence.description: Priya’s login history shows she accessed the college server’s API gateway at 11:40 PM using admin-level permissions she shouldn’t have had.
evidence.significance: Direct evidence of unauthorized access minutes before the hack.

evidence.description: Two students recall Priya loudly criticizing the confession page in class, saying, 'Someone should just take it down for good.'
evidence.location: Classroom, two days before the hack
evidence.significance: Demonstrates motive and intent.

timeline: 6:00 PM – @VITConfessions last normal post goes live.
8:30 PM – Aryan attends the official start of the coding hackathon in Lab 3.
9:15 PM – Priya checks in at the campus mental health helpline.
10:30 PM – Security guard sees Professor Malhotra enter the admin block.
11:40 PM – Priya’s ID logs into the college API gateway.
11:47 PM – @VITConfessions accessed from internal IP.
11:50 PM – First fake post appears. Over 12 posts follow over the next two hours.
1:00 AM – Aryan leaves the hackathon with teammates.
2:30 AM – Priya logs out of the helpline system.
8:00 AM – Panic erupts as students see the posts; IT reports breach.
red_herrings: Aryan’s draft in Google Drive makes him look like a calculated hacker.
The sticky note with the password suggests a careless admin leak.
Professor Malhotra being on campus implies guilt, but he was retrieving graded papers.
Aryan searched for Instagram tracing tools — but it was to check if his ex tracked him.

solution.method: Used her research project credentials to gain temporary admin access to the server API, then exploited a weak OAuth configuration to hijack the Instagram account linked to the confession page. She used a college tablet to post, wiping it afterward.
solution.motive: She wanted to destroy the platform she saw as harmful, especially after her own traumatic confession was ignored. She believed mass disruption would force the college to shut it down.
solution.proof: The server logs show her credentials were used at 11:40 PM to access the API gateway — the only access point that could route to external social media accounts. The tablet’s sync history confirms it was used from that session.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is cross-referencing the API access logs with the Instagram login timestamp. Only someone with server API access could initiate the proxy login. Aryan was at the hackathon with verified attendance. Professor Malhotra’s presence was coincidental. Priya’s alibi is weak — the helpline doesn’t monitor real-time activity. Her credentials are the only ones logged during the critical window, and her motive aligns with her activist personality. The misleading evidence (Aryan’s draft, sticky note) distracts from the technical sophistication of the real method.

case.title: The Case of the Sabotaged Project Server
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, Indraprastha Institute of Technology, Delhi
case.crime: A final-year group project was sabotaged 12 hours before the submission deadline: the central code repository was corrupted, and a fake commit message falsely accused one team member of the act.
case.victim: Team Navaidar, a final-year B.Tech student group working on an AI-based campus navigation app

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.motive: Believed his teammates were dragging the project down; wanted sole credit for a high-scoring project
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for his Algorithms retake exam from 8 PM to 11 PM
suspects.secret: He had secretly rewritten half the codebase without telling the team, fearing last-minute changes would ruin it
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the team leader two days before; acted unusually calm after the sabotage

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.motive: Felt overlooked and uncredited for her work; feared failing the project would delay her scholarship renewal
suspects.alibi: Says she was video-calling her sister in Mumbai from 8:30 PM to 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: She had applied to transfer to another college and didn’t want academic strikes on her record
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her GitHub account was active during the sabotage window, but she claims she was only reviewing code

suspects.name: Professor Arvind Malhotra
suspects.motive: Disapproved of the team's use of open-source AI models, believing it was academic dishonesty
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers at home and was logged into the university LMS portal from 7 PM to 11 PM
suspects.secret: He had been warned by the dean for leaking exam questions last semester
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Visited the computer lab the morning after the sabotage and demanded the team use 'original algorithms only'

evidence.description: A corrupted Git commit with the message: 'Final push — deleting this junk. -PriyaD' timestamped at 9:47 PM
evidence.significance: Implicates Priya directly, but the syntax used doesn’t match her usual commit style

evidence.description: Rohan’s laptop was found to have a local backup of the full project with a timestamp of 9:15 PM — 32 minutes before the sabotage
evidence.location: Confiscated from his dorm during investigation
evidence.significance: Suggests he anticipated the sabotage or intended to work independently

evidence.description: Priya’s GitHub login was active at 9:40 PM, and she viewed the repository’s admin settings
evidence.significance: Looks incriminating, but does not prove malicious action

evidence.description: A sticky note in Rohan’s room with the handwritten phrase: 'They’ll fail without me'
evidence.significance: Suggests arrogance or intent, but could be a venting note

evidence.description: Professor Malhotra accessed the university’s server admin panel at 9:42 PM using elevated credentials
evidence.significance: He had the technical ability and timing, but no direct link to the sabotage

evidence.description: An automated script was run from an admin account that overwrote the repo with corrupted data and forged the commit using Priya’s username
evidence.significance: Reveals technical sophistication and access beyond a regular student

evidence.description: The night watchman recalls seeing a tall figure in a hoodie entering the server closet at 9:40 PM but couldn't identify them
evidence.significance: Confirms physical access, though not conclusive

timeline: 6:00 PM: Team Navaidar holds final group meeting in Lab 3; tensions rise over code integration
7:30 PM: Priya logs into GitHub to review backend modules
8:00 PM: Rohan arrives at the library; library CCTV confirms his presence until 10:50 PM
8:30 PM: Priya starts video call with her sister (verified by call metadata)
9:40 PM: Server room door accessed via keycard (logged to faculty account); GitHub admin panel accessed remotely
9:42 PM: Corrupted script initiated from admin terminal
9:47 PM: Fake commit appears on GitHub with Priya’s name
10:00 PM: Night watchman sees hooded figure leaving server closet
10:30 PM: Priya ends call; attempts to access GitHub and discovers the corruption
red_herrings: The fake commit message directly naming Priya
Priya’s GitHub activity during the sabotage window
Rohan’s backup and angry note suggesting premeditation
Professor Malhotra’s server access and known disapproval of the project

solution.method: He used stolen faculty credentials (copied from Professor Malhotra’s unattended laptop during class) to access the server remotely. He ran a script from the admin terminal that corrupted the repository and forged a commit under Priya’s name to frame her.
solution.motive: He wanted the project to fail publicly so he could submit a solo version later and claim full credit, believing his backup was superior.
solution.proof: The script execution timestamp (9:42 PM) coincides with the admin login, but Rohan’s library CCTV shows him present until 10:50 PM — however, IT logs reveal the remote session originated from a MAC address registered to his personal router, not the faculty terminal’s local network.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the admin login with the actual device used. Despite the login appearing to come from campus, the MAC address in the server logs reveals it was a remote session. Combined with the fact that Rohan had both motive, technical skill, a complete backup, and prior access to the professor’s laptop, the digital trail points to him despite his alibi. The other suspects’ actions, while suspicious, lack the technical means or opportunity to execute the sabotage remotely.

crime_type: common room TV remote programmed weirdly

case.title: The Case of the Possessed Remote
case.setting: Jai Bharat Engineering College, Girls' Hostel Common Room, New Delhi
case.crime: The hostel common room TV remote has been reprogrammed to respond only to absurd commands like 'sing a lullaby' or 'turn into a toad', rendering it nearly useless. Attempts to reset fail, and the TV behaves erratically—switching channels randomly and once playing only Shakespearean quotes for two hours.
case.victim: All hostel residents who rely on the common room for evening entertainment and relaxation

suspects.name: Ananya Mehta
suspects.personality: brilliant coder, introverted, sarcastic, socially awkward
suspects.motive: Frustrated with loud common room noise every night; wanted to disable the TV subtly
suspects.alibi: Was in her room coding a hackathon project until 2 a.m., according to her laptop logs
suspects.secret: She has a secret blog where she writes satirical tech parodies
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen giggling while muttering 'turn into a toad' under her breath days before the incident

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.role: hostel maintenance staff and part-time electrician
suspects.motive: Wanted to create a 'fault' so he could get paid extra for fixing the TV under a new repair contract
suspects.alibi: Claims he was visiting his brother in Noida and has a train ticket stub as proof
suspects.secret: He’s been siphoning old electronics to sell on the black market
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Offered to 'fix' the remote immediately for ₹500, even before diagnosing it

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.role: second-year Electronics student and hostel council representative
suspects.motive: Wanted to ban TV usage after 9 PM; may have sabotaged it to prove her point about misuse
suspects.alibi: Was in the library studying for finals, confirmed by sign-in sheet
suspects.secret: She borrowed the remote to practice voice commands for her robotics project and never returned it
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Acted overly concerned about the 'mystery', urging others to file a formal complaint

evidence.description: Log file from smart TV shows unusual voice command history: 'activate party mode', 'reverse polarity', 'emit dolphin sounds'. Last authenticated user was 'admin' with IP 192.168.1.34.
evidence.location: Internal memory of the TV, accessed through service menu
evidence.significance: Indicates remote was paired via voice-enabled app or smart device. Only someone with admin access could reprogram it this way.

evidence.description: A crumpled note found in common room trash bin with scribbled phrases: 'chicken soup = off', 'lion roar = volume up', 'moonwalk = channel down'.
evidence.significance: Looks like programming notes, but handwriting doesn’t match any suspect. In reality, it's a prank by first-years trying to prank someone else.

evidence.description: A GitHub repository under the name 'CodeWitch94' with a published script called 'VoiceToad', which hacks smart remotes to interpret fantasy-style commands.
evidence.location: Online, discovered via search on tech forums
evidence.significance: Link to Ananya’s secret blog username. Script matches the behavior of the TV. But the repo was uploaded *after* the incident.

evidence.description: A spare universal remote found in the maintenance closet with visible wiring tampering and custom voice module attached.
evidence.location: Locked storage cupboard in hostel basement, unlocked at the time
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan was experimenting with remotes. But it's unrelated—he was fixing a resident’s personal device.

evidence.description: Wi-Fi access logs show a voice command was sent to the TV at 9:47 PM from a device registered as 'PriyaNair_Phone'.
evidence.significance: Direct link to Priya sending the command. But she claims her phone was stolen that evening.

evidence.description: A first-year student reports seeing Priya near the common room at 9:40 PM, whispering into her phone while glancing around nervously.
evidence.significance: Corroborates timing of command. Priya said she was only retrieving a notebook.

evidence.description: A sticky note behind the TV listing voice commands and labeled 'Project Hydra – DO NOT ERASE'.
evidence.significance: Handwriting matches Priya’s. 'Project Hydra' is the name of her robotics entry for a college competition requiring voice control prototypes.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Common room TV used normally during dinner
7:30 PM – Priya checks out library book, signs out at front desk
8:15 PM – Priya seen entering hostel by gate guard
9:00 PM – Common room students gather, TV works fine
9:45 PM – TV suddenly stops responding to normal buttons, activates via voice with strange commands
9:47 PM – Network log records voice command from 'PriyaNair_Phone'
9:50 PM – Priya seen exiting common room area by first-year student
10:00 PM – Complain filed with warden
10:30 PM – Rohan offers to fix the remote for cash
11:00 PM – Ananya seen laughing while typing about 'magic remotes' on her blog
red_herrings: The crumpled note with fake command codes
Ananya’s GitHub script published after the event
Rohan’s tampered spare remote in the maintenance room
Ananya muttering 'turn into a toad'—a quote from her favorite fantasy web series

solution.method: She used her own phone to reprogram the TV remote via the smart home app during her robotics project testing. She intended to test only one command but accidentally activated full admin mode and forgot to revert it before leaving the room.
solution.motive: She was testing voice commands for her 'Project Hydra' robotics submission and needed real-world calibration. She didn’t intend to break it but panicked and hid her involvement.
solution.proof: Wi-Fi log linking her phone to the command at 9:47 PM, the sticky note behind the TV with her handwriting and project name, and the witness placing her at the scene moments before.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is cross-referencing the network logs with the physical sticky note. The command originated from Priya’s device, and the note proves she had technical intent and access. Her alibi fails because the library sign-out doesn’t account for return. The GitHub repo and spare remote are distractions. Ananya’s blog and script came too late. Rohan’s offer was opportunistic. The witness account confirms presence. Priya’s motive wasn’t malice, but negligence combined with cover-up made her seem suspicious.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Visa Funds
case.setting: Kala Sangam, a cultural fest at Vikram University, Ujjain
case.crime: ₹500,000 in sponsorship money from a major bank (Visa India) went missing before the college fest concluded
case.victim: Vikram University Student Council – the funds were meant to cover artist performances and logistics

suspects.name: Aarav Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted to cover massive personal debt from online gambling; feared expulsion if exposed
suspects.alibi: Claimed he was meeting the sound engineer backstage from 6 PM to 8 PM to fix speaker issues
suspects.secret: Has a secret gambling addiction and borrowed money from a local loan shark
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to blame the treasurer; tried to access the sponsorship ledger multiple times post-theft

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.motive: As Fest Treasurer, she mishandled initial allocations and panicked; thought she could 'borrow' temporarily and repay quietly
suspects.alibi: Says she was coordinating with caterers in the mess hall between 5:30 PM and 7:30 PM
suspects.secret: Authorized an unauthorized advance to a friend’s band without council approval
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overexplained her alibi and refused to let anyone audit her personal notebook

suspects.name: Prof. Rajiv Nair
suspects.motive: Believes fest culture is wasteful; wanted to sabotage the event to make a statement
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers alone in his office from 5 PM to 9 PM
suspects.secret: Wrote an anonymous letter to the dean complaining about the fest’s budget a week prior
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the admin block late at night the day after the theft, 'checking lights'

evidence.description: Bank transaction log showing two transfers: one official ₹500,000 to the university account, and a second identical one flagged 'VOID' 20 minutes later
evidence.location: Printed from the online banking portal by the finance office
evidence.significance: Suggests the money was reversed before being fully settled, possibly by someone with login access

evidence.description: A crumpled betting slip found near the generator shed with Aarav’s student ID faintly visible in the corner
evidence.location: Behind the temporary power unit near Stage 2
evidence.significance: Ties Aarav to gambling, implying motive

evidence.description: A blue notebook with scribbled expense adjustments and an entry reading 'Adv. Band: ₹70k approved?' with no signature
evidence.location: Inside Priya’s backpack, confiscated during routine locker check
evidence.significance: Suggests financial overreach and possible embezzlement

evidence.description: Security camera timestamp shows Priya accessing the admin office at 4:47 PM, before the money disappeared
evidence.significance: Appears to place her at the scene before the transfer was voided

evidence.description: Rohan, the sophomore intern, says he saw Prof. Nair arguing with the bank representative during the sponsorship handover
evidence.significance: Creates suspicion of animosity toward the sponsor

evidence.description: Auto-save draft in the Treasurer’s Google Drive titled 'Confession Draft - Do Not Send', explaining panic over a mistaken reversal
evidence.significance: Indicates emotional distress but not guilt

evidence.description: A sticky note with a password written as 'Visa2024!Kala' taped under the keyboard of the admin computer used for transactions
evidence.significance: Reveals weak security; the password matches the one used to reverse the transaction

timeline: 3:00 PM: Visa India representative hands over sponsorship confirmation and first payment proof to Student Council in Admin Block
3:30 PM: Bank confirms ₹500,000 credited to university account via email
4:00 PM: Aarav and Priya log into finance portal to verify funds; system shows 'Payment Received'
4:47 PM: Priya accesses admin office (CCTV) to print vendor contracts
5:15 PM: Transaction log shows reversal of ₹500,000 with note: 'Duplicate transaction – voided'
5:20 PM: Bank sends automated alert to finance office about reversal
5:30 PM: Priya and Aarav argue in corridor over missing funds
6:00 PM: Prof. Nair seen walking near admin block, says he was 'checking lights'
6:00 PM – 8:00 PM: Aarav claims he was backstage fixing sound issues
7:00 PM: Caterers complain to Priya about delayed payments
9:00 PM: Theft officially reported to campus security
red_herrings: The betting slip with Aarav’s ID – planted by someone else to mislead
Priya’s unauthorized advance to the band – unrelated misuse but suggests financial recklessness
Prof. Nair’s argument with the bank rep – he was just confirming tax documentation
The CCTV footage showing Priya early – she was only printing documents, not accessing the system

solution.method: Used the sticky-note password under the admin computer to log in after 5:00 PM, reversed the transaction by marking it 'duplicate', then planned to redirect funds to a dummy account he created
solution.motive: Desperate to repay ₹480,000 in gambling debt to a loan shark threatening to expose him
solution.proof: IP log from university network shows login from admin computer at 5:12 PM linked to Aarav’s biometric ID (he used the machine for printing earlier, so his profile was cached); combined with reversed transaction timestamp and the sticky note password
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the transaction reversal time (5:15 PM) with access. Priya was in the mess hall, Prof. Nair was grading. Only Aarav had both opportunity (was free before 6 PM) and motive. The betting slip is a red herring, but the network log proves he accessed the machine. The reversal required insider knowledge of the weak password – which only someone familiar with the office (like a council member) would know.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Viva Grades
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, Vidya Bharati Institute of Technology, Pune
case.crime: Online submission portal for final viva reports was hacked; 28 out of 30 student assignments were deleted minutes before the deadline.
case.victim: Students submitting final viva reports and Professor Meera Desai, the course in-charge

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted to reset submission deadline to buy time—he hadn't finished his report.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was debugging code in the lab from 8:30 PM to 10:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized parts of his earlier assignment and fears exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Professor Desai earlier that day about extension requests.

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Believes the grading system is unfair; wanted to force a re-evaluation for all students.
suspects.alibi: Says she was meditating in her hostel room from 8:00 PM to 9:30 PM.
suspects.secret: She suffers from anxiety and recently missed a therapy session.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her login was active on the portal at 8:58 PM—two minutes before deletion.

suspects.name: Dr. Arvind Rao
suspects.motive: Wants to undermine Professor Desai's credibility—believes she got the department head position he deserved.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers at home; no one saw him.
suspects.secret: He accessed the server logs from his home IP late at night—trying to cover his resentment, not the crime.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made a cryptic comment in faculty meeting: 'Some systems need a crash to be fixed.'

suspects.name: Kabir Sheikh
suspects.motive: Accidentally left a server backup incomplete and panicked the system might crash—he wanted to delay submissions.
suspects.alibi: Says he was watching a live cricket match with friends online from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
suspects.secret: He skipped weekly server maintenance to go to a concert.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had admin-level access to the portal and was the last person to perform maintenance.

evidence.description: Log file shows deletion command executed at 8:58 PM from IP address ending in 142.
evidence.location: Server logs accessed by college IT
evidence.significance: Timestamps match the crime; IP belongs to the student lab.

evidence.description: Login record shows Priya Nair's account was active at 8:58 PM during deletion.
evidence.significance: Suggests she might have committed the act.

evidence.description: Rohan's laptop shows a script for bulk file deletion, labeled 'test_project'.
evidence.significance: Appears to be a tool for the crime.

evidence.description: A sticky note with server credentials written in haste, found crumpled near Kabir’s workstation.
evidence.significance: Suggests poor security practices and possible access misuse.

evidence.description: A student saw Dr. Rao entering the admin block at 8:45 PM alone.
evidence.location: Campus gate security camera & student testimony
evidence.significance: Contradicts his alibi; places him near server room.

evidence.description: Kabir’s admin access was used to disable backup sync 12 hours before the incident.
evidence.significance: Indicates negligence or intentional weakening of system.

evidence.description: Deleted files were purged from trash bin—requires admin override.
evidence.significance: Only someone with elevated privileges could have erased them permanently.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Submissions begin pouring into viva portal.
7:30 PM – Kabir skips scheduled server backup to attend concert.
8:00 PM – Students report minor lag on portal; Kabir dismisses alerts.
8:45 PM – Dr. Rao seen entering admin block (security cam).
8:58 PM – Deletion command executed from lab IP; 28 reports erased.
8:58 PM – Priya Nair's account logs in briefly (auto-save sync).
9:00 PM – Portal crashes; panic ensues among students.
9:15 PM – Kabir returns and checks system; discovers damage.
9:30 PM – Professor Desai alerted; incident reported to IT head.
red_herrings: Priya Nair's login during the attack (coincidental auto-sync)
Rohan's deletion script (part of a cybersecurity project)
Dr. Rao’s presence on campus (visiting the library, not server room)
Rohan’s argument with professor (about extensions, not sabotage)

solution.method: Used his admin access to remotely trigger a script that deleted submissions, then cleared the trash bin to prevent recovery—done in panic after realizing the server was unstable due to skipped backup.
solution.motive: He panicked over potential blame for system failure and tried to delay submissions by sabotaging the portal temporarily, but went too far.
solution.proof: Server logs show admin override used in deletion—only Kabir and two senior staff had that access, and their IPs don’t match. His sticky note with credentials confirms carelessness.
solution.how_to_solve: The deletion required admin override (not available to students). Priya’s login was passive. Rohan’s script was non-functional. Dr. Rao’s IP doesn’t match. Only Kabir had both motive (fear of blame), access, and physical evidence (credentials note). His alibi is weak—friends confirm he joined match late.

case.title: The Case of the Poisoned Dal
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Technology, North Campus Mess Hall
case.crime: Mysterious food poisoning outbreak after lunch in the college mess
case.victim: 42 students hospitalized with acute gastrointestinal symptoms; no fatalities

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.personality: Intense, brilliant but socially awkward, environmentally conscious, obsessive about food safety
suspects.motive: Wants to expose the mess's use of banned preservatives and substandard ingredients; believes poisoning will force an investigation
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for an exam from 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM
suspects.secret: He has been secretly collecting food samples from the mess for weeks to build a case for the student council
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the mess manager two days prior; has access to lab-grade chemicals through his department

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Her rival for the student body presidency, Arjun Malhotra, was among those poisoned and had to withdraw from campaigning
suspects.alibi: Says she was attending a meditation session in the yoga hall from 12:00 PM to 1:30 PM
suspects.secret: She has been forging attendance records for a scholarship that requires perfect attendance
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Texted a cryptic message before lunch: 'One meal, and the field clears.'

suspects.name: Rajiv Chaudhary
suspects.personality: Gruff, defensive, financially stressed, deeply loyal to his staff
suspects.motive: Facing termination due to repeated hygiene violations; might have poisoned the food to fake a crisis and delay inspection
suspects.alibi: Claims he left for a doctor’s appointment at 10:30 AM and returned at 2:15 PM
suspects.secret: He has been skimming funds from the mess budget to support his ailing wife's medical treatment
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refused to let the health inspector collect the main spice container, claiming it was 'personal property'

suspects.name: Ananya Desai
suspects.role: Final-year Food Technology student and part-time mess inspector
suspects.personality: Idealistic, meticulous, quietly rebellious, deeply ethical
suspects.motive: Discovered that the mess was using expired lentils; planned to report it but feared retaliation
suspects.alibi: States she was in her dorm room writing a thesis from 12:00 PM to 1:45 PM
suspects.secret: She is anonymously running a viral blog criticizing institutional corruption in college hostels
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the only person who didn't eat lunch that day and warned a friend: 'Don’t eat the dal today'

evidence.description: Traces of sodium azide found in a leftover portion of dal from the main pot. The chemical is used in labs and airbags, not in cooking.
evidence.location: Leftover food sample collected by college nurse
evidence.significance: Points to a perpetrator with access to chemistry labs or technical knowledge

evidence.description: Security camera footage shows Rohan Mehta entering the chemistry lab at 10:15 AM and leaving at 10:48 AM with a small vial.
evidence.significance: Suggests he had means and opportunity to obtain poison

evidence.description: A torn label from a spice jar found near the mess dumpster, showing the name 'R. Chaudhary' handwritten on it.
evidence.significance: Implicates the mess manager in tampering

evidence.description: A first-year student claims to have seen Priya Nair near the mess kitchen door at 11:45 AM, looking nervous.
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi and suggests intent

evidence.description: Text message from Priya to an unknown contact: 'After today, it’s just me and the ballot box.'
evidence.location: Recovered from a deleted messages app on a friend’s phone
evidence.significance: Suggests a political motive

evidence.description: A receipts log from the mess kitchen showing purchase of lentils dated three weeks prior, but with a handwritten correction to 'fresh delivery, 2 days ago'. The ink is different.
evidence.significance: Shows possible fraud, but not directly tied to poisoning

evidence.description: A lab notebook belonging to Rohan Mehta with detailed notes on food preservatives and toxicity levels of sodium azide, but with a page torn out dated the day before the incident.
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation

timeline: 10:15 AM: Rohan Mehta enters chemistry lab (per security cam)
10:30 AM: Rajiv Chaudhary leaves campus on a motorbike (per gate log)
10:48 AM: Rohan leaves chemistry lab with a vial
11:30 AM: Lunch service begins in mess
11:45 AM: Witness claims to see Priya near kitchen
11:50 AM: Ananya Desai enters mess, observes food, leaves without eating
12:00 PM: Majority of students begin eating
12:30 PM: First reports of nausea and vomiting
1:15 PM: College infirmary overwhelmed; ambulance called
2:00 PM: Health department arrives; mess sealed
2:15 PM: Rajiv returns to mess
red_herrings: Rohan's access to sodium azide and lab notes suggest premeditated poisoning
Priya's text messages and sighting near kitchen imply political sabotage
Torn label with Rajiv's name suggests he tampered with spices
Ananya’s warning to her friend makes her seem like an accomplice or insider

solution.method: She laced the pre-cooked dal with sodium azide, which she obtained by impersonating a lab assistant and using forged authorization from a professor’s template she found online. She added the chemical during the 10-minute window when the kitchen staff were on break and the dal was left unattended before final seasoning.
solution.motive: She discovered the mess was using dangerously expired lentils that could cause natural food poisoning. She believed causing a severe but non-lethal incident would force the college to permanently shut down the corrupt mess operation and initiate reform.
solution.proof: CCTV footage from a hidden camera in the food storage corridor (installed after prior thefts) shows Ananya entering the kitchen at 11:42 AM and handling the main dal pot. Her fingerprint was found on the inside lid of the pot. Additionally, the vial used matched residue found in the food, and a search of her room revealed a forged lab access document with her handwriting.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is recognizing that the sodium azide could not have been added before cooking without degrading—it must have been added post-cooking. Rohan’s lab visit was to collect a safe preservative for his samples, not poison. Priya’s message was about competition, not poisoning. Rajiv’s missing label was from a personal spice he brought in, unrelated. Ananya’s warning to her friend was genuine concern, but her refusal to eat contradicts her stated thesis-writing alibi. The final proof lies in cross-referencing her presence with the kitchen surveillance blind spot and the undetectable method of poison delivery she knew from her Food Tech training.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Marks
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Engineering, Mumbai – Department of Computer Science
case.crime: Grades of six students in the 'Advanced Algorithms' course were altered in the digital academic portal three days before result declaration, resulting in wrongful academic probation and scholarship revocations.
case.victim: Six high-performing students (including a national olympiad winner), the integrity of the academic evaluation system, and the reputation of the department

suspects.name: Arjun Mehta
suspects.personality: Intense, perfectionist, socially isolated, highly competitive
suspects.motive: Desperately needed top rank to secure a scholarship abroad; feared being outranked by the victims
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying from 7 PM to 1 AM on the night of the breach
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a major project earlier in the semester and is terrified of exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Frequently accessed the department server via remote login in the past month; known to have advanced coding and network penetration skills

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Strict, principled, respected but feared, emotionally reserved
suspects.motive: Believes some students cheated in the final exam and wanted to 'correct' the results without formal investigation to avoid departmental scandal
suspects.alibi: Claims she was attending an online conference call with a university in Germany from 8 PM to 10:30 PM; conference logs confirm partial attendance
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously reporting grade discrepancies for years, suspecting systemic corruption
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the only faculty with full admin access to the grading portal; altered access logs the day after the breach

suspects.name: Kavita Reddy
suspects.role: second year student and teaching assistant (TA) for the course
suspects.personality: Ambitious, charismatic, manipulative, eager to impress faculty
suspects.motive: Wanted to discredit the top students to increase her chances of becoming a research assistant under Dr. Deshmukh
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a college drama rehearsal from 6:30 PM to 9:30 PM
suspects.secret: She falsified her TA application by inflating her GPA
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the department server room during lunch break two days before the breach; has a personal grudge against one of the victims

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Holds a grudge against Dr. Deshmukh for denying his promotion; wanted to undermine her authority
suspects.alibi: Claims he was home streaming a football match; no one can confirm
suspects.secret: He runs an underground side business helping students bypass college firewalls
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Disabled the server room surveillance cameras during 'maintenance' on the night of the breach; logs show his admin credentials were used briefly at 10:47 PM

evidence.description: Server access log showing Rohan Malhotra's admin ID used to enter the grading system at 10:47 PM on May 14th, lasting 6 minutes.
evidence.significance: Suggests direct IT staff involvement

evidence.description: A handwritten note found crumpled in a bin near the server room with a partial SQL command for editing grade tables and the words 'Make sure Arjun is safe.'
evidence.significance: Appears to implicate Arjun Mehta and someone trying to protect him

evidence.description: A spoofed login from Arjun Mehta's registered device at 10:42 PM on May 14th, originating from the college library Wi-Fi.
evidence.significance: Suggests Arjun attempted entry just before the breach

evidence.description: A junior student reports seeing Kavita Reddy arguing with one of the victims, Riya Shah, in the lab two days before the incident, shouting, 'You don’t deserve any of this!'
evidence.significance: Suggests personal animosity

evidence.description: Hidden backup log from a secondary server shows a script was executed at 10:45 PM on May 14th that altered grades and then deleted primary logs. The script was uploaded from a guest Wi-Fi session linked to a burner laptop.
evidence.location: Secondary network monitoring system (old, rarely checked)
evidence.significance: Proves a sophisticated, pre-planned attack from outside the main system

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'Backup - Deshmukh' found in Dr. Deshmukh’s office drawer, containing a script identical to the one used in the breach.
evidence.significance: Appears to be irrefutable proof of her involvement

evidence.description: Metadata analysis of the grade alteration script shows it was written in an IDE using a regional language keyboard layout (Telugu), which only Kavita Reddy uses in the department.
evidence.location: Forensic analysis of script file (recovered from secondary log)
evidence.significance: Links the script directly to Kavita

timeline: May 14, 6:30 PM: Kavita attends drama rehearsal (confirmed by 8 witnesses).
May 14, 7:00 PM: Arjun logs into the university portal from the library; activity shows standard browsing.
May 14, 8:00 PM: Dr. Deshmukh joins online conference; verified by IP and login duration (8:00–10:30 PM).
May 14, 9:00 PM: Rohan Malhotra clocks out of IT office; claims to go home.
May 14, 9:30 PM: Drama rehearsal ends; Kavita leaves the auditorium.
May 14, 10:00 PM: Surveillance cameras in server room disabled (logged as 'scheduled maintenance' by Rohan).
May 14, 10:42 PM: Spoofed login from Arjun’s device recorded.
May 14, 10:45 PM: Hidden network log captures execution of malicious script from guest Wi-Fi.
May 14, 10:47 PM: Admin credentials (Rohan’s) used briefly – likely to cover traces.
May 15, 8:00 AM: Students discover altered grades on portal.
May 15, 10:00 AM: Dr. Deshmukh finds USB in her drawer; denies planting it.
red_herrings: The USB drive in Dr. Deshmukh’s drawer, planted to frame her.
Rohan’s admin credentials being used – he was spoofed via a credential-harvesting link sent by the real culprit.
The note mentioning 'Arjun' – written by Kavita to shift suspicion toward him.
Kavita’s argument with the victim – emotionally charged but not proof of criminal action.
Arjun’s advanced hacking skills – real, but he did not act on them this time.

solution.method: Kavita used her TA access to obtain server IPs and exploit a weak guest Wi-Fi authentication. She used a burner laptop with a Telugu keyboard to write and execute a Python script that altered grades and deleted logs. She spoofed Rohan’s credentials using a phishing email and planted the USB in Dr. Deshmukh’s office during lab cleaning hours.
solution.motive: She believed the top students were blocking her path to elite research opportunities; altering grades would remove competition and make her appear more exceptional by comparison.
solution.proof: Metadata of the malicious script shows Telugu keyboard layout usage, which matches only Kavita’s registered device settings. Additionally, the guest Wi-Fi connection was traced to a MAC address cloned from a college lab machine, which Kavita had access to.
solution.how_to_solve: The detective must ignore the planted physical evidence (USB, note) and focus on the digital forensics. The script’s metadata is the key. Cross-referencing keyboard layout data with student device registrations reveals Kavita’s involvement. The spoofed logins and altered access logs were misdirections, but the secondary server’s untouched log provides the real timestamp and source. Kavita’s alibi fails when theater staff recall she left early to 'fetch forgotten notes' – unverified. Her opportunity, means, and digital fingerprint converge irrefutably.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Fest Fund
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay
case.crime: Embezzlement of ₹8.7 lakh from the annual tech-fest budget through forged vendor payments and shell invoices
case.victim: Technectrix, the official annual tech-fest of the college, losing critical funding days before the event

suspects.name: Aanya Mehta
suspects.motive: Needed money to cover personal losses from a failed cryptocurrency investment that she misrepresented as profits to her family
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been working on the fest mobile app in the CS lab from 6 PM to midnight on the night the payments were processed
suspects.secret: She used fest funds to pay off part of her crypto debt two months prior in a smaller, undetected transaction
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Aggressively opposed audit suggestions and tried to classify vendor data as 'confidential' to prevent scrutiny

suspects.name: Professor Arvind Khatri
suspects.motive: Believes student festivals are wasteful; wanted to sabotage the fest to prove a point about fiscal responsibility
suspects.alibi: Says he was at home grading papers; wife partially corroborates but was asleep by 9 PM
suspects.secret: He approved a personal research grant using overlapping budget codes, creating a loophole others could exploit
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed hard for manual, non-digital approvals, then claimed 'technical errors' when questioned about missing signatures

suspects.name: Rohan Deshmukh
suspects.motive: Running an off-campus event management startup that was under financial strain; saw fest funds as a 'temporary loan'
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a client meeting in Vashi; no verifiable attendees or receipts
suspects.secret: Had previously inflated quotes from real vendors and pocketed the difference in prior fests, but nothing over ₹50k
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Submitted multiple last-minute vendor changes with hastily prepared documentation

suspects.name: Nalini Patil
suspects.motive: None financial; but resents student organizers for bypassing proper channels and disrespects protocol
suspects.alibi: Clock-out record shows she left office at 5:15 PM; insists she didn't return
suspects.secret: She disabled a server alert for after-hours access because it kept triggering false alarms, leaving a security blind spot
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Initially denied server access logs could be tampered with, then backtracked when confronted with evidence

evidence.description: Transaction log showing two vendor payments of ₹4.2 lakh and ₹4.5 lakh approved via the internal fest portal at 10:47 PM and 11:03 PM on March 12. Both vendors (‘Innovatech AV’ and ‘Campus Buzz Media’) have generic email IDs and no GST registration.
evidence.location: Finance department server, extracted by IT audit team
evidence.significance: These payments were unauthorized and sent to shell companies. Timestamps are critical.

evidence.description: A printed copy of a bank transfer receipt for ₹4.5 lakh to ‘Campus Buzz Media’ found crumpled in a bin outside the CS lab. Has a coffee stain obscuring part of the timestamp.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone printed the receipt locally; coffee stain matches mugs in the CS lab.

evidence.description: Git commit log from the fest app repository showing Aanya Mehta pushed code at 10:55 PM on March 12 that modified API endpoints related to payment confirmations.
evidence.location: Private GitHub repo for fest app
evidence.significance: Appears to show Aanya altering systems during the theft window.

evidence.description: Rahul, a night security guard, recalls seeing Rohan near the admin block at 9:40 PM arguing on the phone. Says he didn’t enter but couldn't confirm.
evidence.location: Admin block security log and interview
evidence.significance: Places Rohan near the scene, but doesn’t confirm entry.

evidence.description: IP log from the finance server showing login from terminal #7 in the admin office at 10:40 PM on March 12. Login used Nalini’s credentials but originated from an IP not assigned to her workstation.
evidence.significance: Indicates credentials were either stolen or used remotely. Terminal #7 is near Nalini’s desk.

evidence.description: A sticky note in Rohan’s desk drawer listing ‘Innovatech AV’ with a fake GSTIN and bank details. Smudged handwriting, partially erased.
evidence.location: Rohan’s dorm room during room check (with consent)
evidence.significance: Appears to link Rohan directly to the fake vendor.

evidence.description: Hidden script discovered in the fest portal’s backup: a cron job set to auto-approve payments with vendor names containing ‘Buzz’ or ‘Tech’ if initiated after 8 PM and under ₹5 lakh. Created using elevated admin privileges.
evidence.significance: Proves premeditated sabotage. Could not have been set by student accounts.

timeline: March 10, 4:30 PM: Final budget approval meeting. All suspects present.
March 10, 6:00 PM: Professor Khatri submits revised approval protocol requiring dual verification for payments over ₹2 lakh—implemented weakly in the system.
March 11, 11:00 AM: Rohan submits three new vendor proposals, including ‘Innovatech AV’.
March 11, 3:15 PM: Nalini processes vendor onboarding; adds new vendors to system but skips background checks due to ‘time constraints’.
March 12, 5:15 PM: Nalini clocks out. Security logs show no re-entry.
March 12, 9:40 PM: Security guard sees Rohan near admin block.
March 12, 10:40 PM: Suspicious login from terminal #7 using Nalini’s credentials.
March 12, 10:47 PM: First fraudulent payment initiated and auto-approved.
March 12, 10:55 PM: Aanya pushes code to fest app (legitimate bug fix).
March 12, 11:03 PM: Second fraudulent payment sent.
March 13, 9:00 AM: Finance clerk discovers missing funds during reconciliation.
red_herrings: Aanya’s late-night coding activity suggests system manipulation.
Rohan’s presence near admin block and fake GSTIN note imply direct involvement.
Printed receipt in CS lab bin implicates someone from the student team.
Professor Khatri’s vocal opposition to the fest paints him as a moral saboteur.

solution.method: Abused his elevated admin privileges two weeks prior to plant a hidden cron script in the fest payment system that auto-approved transactions for vendors with certain keywords if initiated after 8 PM. Used knowledge of Nalini’s weak password (from a sticky note he saw) to remotely log in via a spoofed IP and trigger two payments to shell vendors Rohan had unknowingly introduced. Leveraged the fact that Nalini had disabled server alerts.
solution.motive: To sabotage the fest and force administrative reform by demonstrating student-led events are financially reckless. Wanted to justify cutting student budgets and restoring faculty control.
solution.proof: The cron script found in the server backup was timestamped March 1 and linked to a system admin account only Khatri possessed. Network logs show the login on March 12 originated from the faculty lounge router, where Khatri had access. His personal laptop’s browser history (recovered from cloud sync) had a search: 'how to schedule automated tasks on Linux cron'.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Eliminate Aanya: her code push was unrelated and occurred after the first payment. 2. Eliminate Rohan: the sticky note was a draft he abandoned; no digital trail links him to payment initiation. 3. Eliminate Nalini: no physical or digital evidence places her at the office post-5:15 PM; her credentials were spoofed. 4. Focus on who had admin access and motive to sabotage: only Khatri. 5. The cron script’s creation date predates the theft, indicating premeditation. 6. Terminal login via spoofed IP required internal network knowledge only a faculty member would have. 7. Final proof: browser history confirming research on cron automation.

case.title: The Case of the Rigged Ballot
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, Arts Building and Student Union Office
case.crime: Accusation of election rigging in the Student Union President election, involving fabricated proxy votes and tampering with digital tally
case.victim: Fair democratic process and reputation of the Student Union Election Commission

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.role: final-year Political Science student, Elected Union President (by narrow margin)
suspects.motive: Desperate to win after losing previous election; has political ambitions beyond college
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a debate club meeting from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM on election day
suspects.secret: Received unauthorized funding from an off-campus political group to run his campaign
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Immediately celebrated victory before official results were announced; pressured election officer to fast-track count

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.role: third-year Computer Science student, Election Commission Tech Coordinator
suspects.motive: Felt overlooked and disrespected by the Commission chair; wanted to prove she could control the system
suspects.alibi: Says she was working alone in the server room from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM to 'optimize vote tally software'
suspects.secret: She was romantically involved with the runner-up candidate
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refuses to provide log files from election server; unusually nervous during investigation

suspects.name: Rohan Deshmukh
suspects.role: fourth-year Economics student, Runner-up in election, anti-corruption activist
suspects.motive: Publicly accused the election of being rigged; may have fabricated evidence to discredit the process and force a re-vote
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been live-streaming a protest outside the Arts Building from 6:30 PM onward
suspects.secret: Hacked into the college forum months ago to leak admin emails, which he later deleted
suspects.suspicious_behavior: First to raise alarm about rigging; produced 'proof' of duplicate votes within minutes of results

suspects.name: Dr. Kavita Reddy
suspects.role: Professor of Sociology, Faculty Advisor to Student Union
suspects.motive: Wanted Aarav to win to strengthen her influence over student politics and secure future support for her research grants
suspects.alibi: States she was in a faculty meeting from 5:00 PM to 7:15 PM
suspects.secret: She bypassed protocol to approve proxy votes for students 'on medical leave' without verification
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed administration to dismiss allegations quickly; deleted text messages during inquiry

evidence.description: Vote tally log showing 47 additional proxy votes added to Aarav's count after the official closure time (5:00 PM). All from students listed as 'medically absent'.
evidence.location: Backup server logs accessed via admin override
evidence.significance: Suggests post-deadline vote manipulation.

evidence.description: Anonymous GitHub commit log showing a script pushed at 4:45 PM on election day that altered vote validation logic to accept duplicate ballot IDs.
evidence.location: Public GitHub repository under a pseudonymous account
evidence.significance: Appears to show premeditated digital tampering.

evidence.description: A crumpled sticky note found in the server room trash with a handwritten list of student IDs and vote assignments, including duplicates.
evidence.significance: Suggests manual orchestration of vote fraud.

evidence.description: Timestamped security footage showing Dr. Reddy using a master key to enter the administrative office at 4:50 PM on election day, exiting at 5:05 PM.
evidence.significance: Places her near election materials during vulnerable window.

evidence.description: Testimony from a janitor that he saw Rohan Deshmukh entering the server room at 6:10 PM despite no access privileges.
evidence.location: Interview conducted by internal inquiry panel
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan may have planted digital evidence or altered logs.

evidence.description: A printed list of proxy forms with forged signatures from absent students, discovered in a locked drawer in Dr. Reddy's office.
evidence.significance: Direct physical evidence of fabricated votes.

evidence.description: Metadata from the election software showing that the vote validation override was activated via an administrative account, not the student tech account.
evidence.significance: Proves tampering required faculty-level access.

timeline: 3:00 PM: Voting ends. Ballot boxes sealed and stored in administrative office.
4:45 PM: GitHub commit logs show malicious script uploaded (later revealed to be a decoy).
4:50 PM: Dr. Reddy enters administrative office with master key (CCTV footage).
5:00 PM: Official vote count window closes; proxy submissions no longer allowed.
5:05 PM: Dr. Reddy exits office.
5:30 PM: Priya Nair enters server room for 'system optimization'.
6:00 PM: Aarav Mehta attends debate club (witnesses confirm presence, but he leaves briefly at 6:18 PM).
6:10 PM: Janitor claims to see Rohan Deshmukh near server room (no CCTV coverage in that hall).
6:30 PM: Rohan begins live-stream protest outside Arts Building.
7:00 PM: Initial results leaked online showing Aarav's narrow win.
7:30 PM: Priya exits server room.
8:00 PM: Official results announced; accusations of rigging begin.
red_herrings: The GitHub script suggests a tech-savvy student (Priya) rigged the system.
The sticky note in the server room implies Priya orchestrated the fraud.
Rohan's unauthorized server room access suggests he planted evidence to frame others.
Aarav's early celebration implies prior knowledge of rigged results.

solution.method: Used her administrative access to forge proxy vote forms and manually input 47 fake votes into the system before the count began. She exploited her authority to bypass verification and used the master key to access physical ballot records.
solution.motive: To ensure Aarav Mehta won, thereby gaining political leverage and securing support for her upcoming research grant tied to student engagement initiatives.
solution.proof: The forged proxy forms found in her office match the irregular votes in the tally log. CCTV shows her accessing the office during the critical window. Server metadata confirms the override was executed from her administrative account, not student accounts.
solution.how_to_solve: Investigators must cross-reference the forged proxy forms with the digital logs and CCTV footage. The GitHub script and sticky note are decoys — their language doesn't match the actual system code. The janitor's sighting of Rohan is uncorroborated and contradicted by his live-stream. The key realization is that student accounts couldn't authorize the vote override — only a faculty admin could. This, combined with Dr. Reddy's access and the physical evidence in her drawer, confirms her guilt. Priya’s nervousness stems from hiding her relationship, not guilt. Aarav's win was illegitimate, but he was unaware of the fraud.

case.title: The Case of the Forged Doctorate
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Advanced Learning, Department of Computational Sciences
case.crime: A tenured professor's academic credentials are discovered to be falsified, threatening the legitimacy of the department's research grants and accreditation.
case.victim: Dr. Arvind Malhotra, Professor and Head of the Department of Computational Sciences

suspects.name: Isha Mehta
suspects.motive: Wanted Dr. Malhotra removed to increase her chances of promotion to department head.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at home grading papers on the night the anonymous complaint was filed.
suspects.secret: She plagiarized part of her own PhD thesis from an obscure Japanese journal.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the university’s records portal late at night two days before the complaint surfaced.

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Discovered Malhotra’s plagiarism in a published paper and believed exposing credentials was the only way to stop academic corruption.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night coding meet-up at a café in Hauz Khas.
suspects.secret: He illegally accessed Malhotra’s university email using a phishing script.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly criticized Malhotra in a department seminar a week before the scandal.

suspects.name: Prof. Nalini Reddy
suspects.personality: Sharp, politically astute, reserved, morally ambiguous
suspects.motive: Long-standing professional rivalry; a scandal would shift research funding to her department.
suspects.alibi: Attended a closed-door academic review meeting on campus during the filing period.
suspects.secret: She has been falsifying grant utilization reports for years.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to suggest a formal investigation and pressured the dean aggressively.

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: None directly, but he discovered the truth accidentally and feared losing his job if he reported it.
suspects.alibi: Was on night shift logging documents in the admin office.
suspects.secret: He delayed processing Malhotra’s credential verification during hiring due to a bribe from a third party (now deceased).
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Erased a log entry related to credential file access the day before the scandal broke.

evidence.description: Anonymous complaint filed through a university ethics portal using campus Wi-Fi at 2:17 AM on March 12. IP traced to a library computer.
evidence.significance: Triggered the formal investigation into Malhotra’s PhD from a now-defunct university in Kazakhstan.

evidence.description: A printed copy of Malhotra’s PhD diploma with irregular formatting and a missing accreditation seal, found crumpled in a bin near the admin office.
evidence.location: Waste bin outside Administrative Block, Room 104
evidence.significance: Suggests someone had physical access and was suspicious of authenticity.

evidence.description: Login record showing Isha Mehta accessed the HR database at 1:45 AM on March 12, two hours before the complaint.
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation and motive.

evidence.description: A security guard reported seeing Rohan Desai exiting the library at 2:30 AM on March 12, claiming he was working on his thesis.
evidence.significance: Places Rohan near the IP source of the complaint.

evidence.description: Email draft on Rohan’s cloud account titled 'Exposing the Fraud' dated March 10, never sent.
evidence.significance: Indicates intent to expose Malhotra, but no action taken.

evidence.description: A sticky note in Vikram Joshi’s drawer with a handwritten password labeled 'HR Backup Access'.
evidence.significance: Suggests ability to manipulate records.

evidence.description: Metadata from the anonymous complaint shows it was drafted using a template previously accessed by Prof. Nalini Reddy during a workshop on ethics reporting.
evidence.location: Document metadata analysis from ethics portal submission
evidence.significance: Links the complaint’s structure to Nalini, though not the sender.

timeline: March 5, 10:00 AM: Rohan Desai submits internal review noting anomalies in Malhotra’s cited sources.
March 8, 3:00 PM: Prof. Nalini Reddy meets privately with the Dean about 'departmental integrity concerns'.
March 10, 9:20 PM: Rohan accesses Malhotra’s email via phishing (detected by IT, but not reported).
March 11, 11:30 PM: Vikram Joshi logs into HR system to correct a payroll error, accesses credential files.
March 12, 1:45 AM: Isha Mehta logs into HR database (viewing promotion eligibility criteria).
March 12, 2:17 AM: Anonymous complaint filed from library computer.
March 12, 2:30 AM: Security guard sees Rohan leaving library.
March 12, 9:00 AM: Dean announces investigation into Malhotra’s credentials.
red_herrings: Rohan’s phishing incident suggests he had motive and means to expose Malhotra.
Isha’s late-night HR access implies she was checking Malhotra’s status for personal gain.
The diploma found in the bin appears to be evidence of tampering, but it's a photocopy made by Vikram for personal record-keeping.
Nalini’s use of the ethics template creates false suspicion of authorship.

solution.method: Used his administrative access to anonymously file the complaint from a library computer during his night shift, using a guest login to mask his identity.
solution.motive: Guilt over having overlooked Malhotra’s fake credentials during the hiring process years earlier due to a bribe; feared exposure would ruin his career and implicate him.
solution.proof: Security camera footage (recovered from backup) shows Vikram entering the library at 2:10 AM and leaving at 2:20 AM — matching the complaint timestamp. His fingerprint was found on the guest login terminal.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the timeline and access: only Vikram had both motive related to past complicity and uninterrupted movement across campus at night. Rohan’s presence was coincidental. Isha’s access was unrelated. Nalini’s template was standard. The physical diploma was a red herring. The clincher is that the complaint used a guest account, which only staff could authorize — and Vikram was logged into the system minutes before. Combined with the fingerprint and footage, guilt is irrefutable.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Merit Fund
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts and Science, Chennai
case.crime: INR 22 lakh diverted from the Rajiv Gandhi Merit Scholarship Fund meant for economically disadvantaged students
case.victim: The scholarship fund and 44 deserving students whose awards were halted mid-semester

suspects.name: Arun Mehta
suspects.role: final-year BCom student and student representative on the scholarship committee
suspects.motive: Wants to fund his startup idea and gain favor with corporate sponsors by showing 'financial acumen'
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at an off-campus startup pitch event in T. Nagar on the night of the transfer
suspects.secret: He has secretly taken a private loan from a family friend to cover his own tuition, which he hasn't repaid
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was unusually anxious during the audit meeting and tried to redirect blame to staff inefficiency

suspects.name: Dr. Leela Nair
suspects.role: Associate Professor of Accounting and fund overseer
suspects.motive: Her younger brother is in deep debt with loan sharks; she was blackmailed into diverting the funds
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at home grading papers; no direct eyewitness
suspects.secret: Her brother was arrested last month for gambling; she paid bail but now owes 15 lakh
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed the fund’s digital ledger three times late at night in the week before the theft but logged out before completing transactions

suspects.name: Vijay Raman
suspects.role: second-year Computer Science student and college IT intern
suspects.motive: Wanted to expose the college’s lax cybersecurity by staging a 'proof-of-concept' breach, but lost control of the funds when a real hacker piggybacked on his exploit
suspects.alibi: Says he was in his dorm room coding a personal project; no alibi witness
suspects.secret: Developed a backdoor script to test the finance server vulnerabilities without authorization
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted browser history and reformatted his SSD after the theft was discovered

suspects.name: Prakash D’Souza
suspects.role: College Bursar and chief financial officer
suspects.personality: bureaucratic, rigid, status-conscious, deeply loyal to tradition
suspects.motive: Facing early retirement and desperate to leave a 'legacy' by funding a new auditorium; planned to repay the money after college fundraising
suspects.alibi: Claims he was attending a Rotary Club meeting in Adyar; has two members who vouch for him
suspects.secret: Has quietly solicited donations for the auditorium project without college approval
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Approved an unusual payment voucher with mismatched signatures weeks before the theft

evidence.description: A PDF of the forged fund transfer request bearing a scanned signature resembling Dr. Nair’s, routed to a shell company called 'EduGrowth Ventures Pvt. Ltd.'
evidence.significance: Appears to implicate Dr. Nair directly; timestamped during her alleged home stay

evidence.description: A crumpled receipt for a Rs. 200 prepaid SIM card purchased under the name 'A. Mehta' at a convenience store near T. Nagar
evidence.location: Waste bin outside Mehta’s hostel room
evidence.significance: Suggests Mehta created an anonymous phone to coordinate financial fraud

evidence.description: Login logs show a session from Vijay Raman’s registered device accessing the finance server at 02:17 AM on the night of the transfer, using Dr. Nair’s credentials
evidence.significance: Strong link between Raman and the breach; used to install keylogger or steal session cookie

evidence.description: A handwritten note in Prakash D’Souza’s handwriting reading: 'Auditorium project—Phase 1. Funds bridge: RGMS. Repay Q1.'
evidence.location: Inside a ledger in his office desk drawer
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditated misuse of scholarship money for infrastructure

evidence.description: Encrypted backup file recovered from a college cloud storage account, titled 'Final Transfer Log'. Contains decrypted records showing the transfer was authorized via an API call from an internal IP masked using a DNS tunnel
evidence.location: Reconstructed from server cache by forensic auditors
evidence.significance: Proves use of technical bypass, not simple credential theft; method known only to IT interns

evidence.description: Security guard reports seeing Dr. Nair’s car leave campus at 9:45 PM on the night of the transfer, though she claims she never came to campus
evidence.significance: Contradicts alibi; suggests direct involvement

evidence.description: Metadata from the forged PDF shows it was created using LaTeX template 'scholarship_form_v3.tex' last modified in Vijay Raman’s personal GitHub repository
evidence.location: Digital forensic analysis of file metadata
evidence.significance: Links Raman directly to creation of fake documentation

timeline: 2023-09-05 18:30: Dr. Nair logs into finance server from home IP to review fund balances.
2023-09-05 21:45: Prakash D’Souza leaves campus; security logs confirm exit.
2023-09-05 22:10: Arun Mehta checks into startup event at T. Nagar (Wi-Fi log and photo tag).
2023-09-05 22:30: Dr. Nair’s official car logged entering campus by gate camera (disputed by her).
2023-09-05 23:58: Suspicious DNS tunnel detected on college network (later linked to Raman’s dorm router).
2023-09-06 02:17: Login to finance server using Dr. Nair’s credentials from IP assigned to Raman’s hostel room.
2023-09-06 02:23: Fund transfer initiated to EduGrowth Ventures via automated payment system.
2023-09-06 08:00: College bank alerts finance team of unauthorized transaction.
2023-09-06 14:00: IT department discovers and deletes suspicious backdoor script on server named 'audit_patch_v2.exe'.
red_herrings: Dr. Nair’s alleged campus visit contradicts her alibi and suggests guilt.
Arun Mehta’s prepaid SIM receipt implies covert communication.
D’Souza’s handwritten note about using scholarship funds suggests embezzlement for auditorium.
Forged document with Dr. Nair’s signature appears to confirm her involvement.

solution.method: Exploited weak authentication on college finance server by planting a backdoor script during routine maintenance. Used a DNS tunnel to mask his IP, then stole Dr. Nair’s session token via a man-in-the-middle attack. Forged the transfer request using a LaTeX template from his own repository and authorized the transaction using elevated privileges granted to IT interns.
solution.motive: Initially intended only to expose the college's outdated cybersecurity by simulating a breach, but accidentally triggered a real automated transfer when testing. Panicked and failed to reverse it before funds were seized by a third-party shell company he couldn't access.
solution.proof: Metadata from the forged PDF ties it to Raman’s GitHub. Server logs confirm his device initiated the DNS tunnel and login. Recovery of the backdoor script from server cache with his digital signature. His reformatted SSD was partially restored, revealing browser searches: 'can a test API call trigger real bank transfer?'
solution.how_to_solve: Detective must cross-reference the PDF metadata with digital footprints, trace the DNS tunnel to Raman’s IP, and reconcile the timing—showing the login occurred from his room while no one else had both technical access and motive. The forged signature and D’Souza’s note are distractions; Mehta’s SIM is unrelated; Dr. Nair’s car was stolen and used to impersonate her. Only Raman had the technical means, opportunity, and digital trail linking all evidence without full intention to steal.

case.title: The Case of the Shadow Syllabus
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Higher Learning (DIHL), Department of Computer Science, Old Campus Block C
case.crime: An underground assignment-selling ring has been operating across multiple departments, using encrypted college Wi-Fi access points and student credentials to distribute paid academic work. The ring has compromised exam papers and manipulated grading patterns.
case.victim: Academic integrity of the institution; several students have been academically disqualified based on falsely flagged plagiarism, while others received undeserved grades.

suspects.name: Aryan Mehta
suspects.motive: Wants to secure a foreign university scholarship by building a false academic record of peer mentorship and research leadership
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at an off-campus hackathon in Gurgaon during the server breach
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his own research paper last semester and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Frequently accessed the department server late at night under a proxy ID; was seen arguing with a professor who later reported a stolen login token

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Wants to discredit the department head to secure a promotion
suspects.alibi: Submitted a draft of her research paper at 1:47 AM on the night of the breach, timestamped from her home IP
suspects.secret: She is in a secret relationship with a university auditor from a rival institution
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She requested increased server access for 'research analytics' two weeks before the breach and accessed student assignment databases without authorization logs

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Introverted, brilliant coder, anxious, socially isolated
suspects.motive: Needs money to support his younger sister’s medical treatment
suspects.alibi: Says he was in the library studying until midnight; library CCTV shows him leaving at 11:58 PM
suspects.secret: He has been anonymously publishing open-source AI tools under a pseudonym and fears academic misuse of his code
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His personal GitHub was linked to an obfuscated script used to automate assignment distribution; he deleted it 12 hours after the investigation began

suspects.name: Neha Desai
suspects.role: Graduate Teaching Assistant and PhD aspirant
suspects.personality: Driven, meticulous, empathetic, resentful of elitism
suspects.motive: Believes the grading system exploits underprivileged students; wants to 'level the field' by redistributing assignments
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading assignments in her room; no digital timestamp confirms activity after 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: She was suspended in her first year for academic misconduct and erased it from her record
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Received multiple unexplained UPI payments from student accounts; her burner phone was seen connecting to a hidden Wi-Fi node in the server room

evidence.description: Encrypted log files from the department server showing repeated access from a spoofed faculty IP between 2:15 AM and 2:45 AM on three exam nights. The logs show data exfiltration masked as routine backups.
evidence.location: Server logs accessed via forensic audit tool
evidence.significance: Indicates insider knowledge of network structure; the spoofed IP belongs to Dr. Nair’s lab

evidence.description: A damaged USB drive found in a campus dustbin near Block C, containing a corrupted script that decrypts to reveal a list of paid assignment transactions and student IDs.
evidence.location: East side waste bin near server room exhaust
evidence.significance: Links Vikram Joshi’s unique encryption signature (recovered from GitHub backups) to the files

evidence.description: A burner Telegram account named 'ShadowSyllabus_Bot' distributing assignment packs; messages show commands issued from a device using Aryan Mehta’s registered MAC address.
evidence.location: Recovered from telecom metadata via college ISP
evidence.significance: Suggests Aryan’s direct involvement in distribution

evidence.description: A handwritten note in the server room maintenance logbook with the phrase 'Cache cleared – Node 7' in a handwriting matching Neha Desai’s.
evidence.location: Server room logbook, last entry timestamped 1 hour before the final exam upload
evidence.significance: Suggests physical access and tampering with network infrastructure

evidence.description: A hidden cron job discovered on the main department server set to auto-upload assignment templates to a cloud locker every Sunday at 3:00 AM. The job was created using elevated privileges and a deprecated admin role.
evidence.significance: Proves long-term, automated access; the admin role was last used by Dr. Nair during system migration

evidence.description: A night janitor reports seeing a student in a hoodie connecting a small device to the server room’s ventilation panel on the night of the breach. He couldn't identify the face but recalls red sneakers.
evidence.significance: Vikram Joshi owns red sneakers; Aryan wears only branded white ones

evidence.description: A deleted email draft from Neha Desai to the Dean, never sent, titled 'Confession on Academic Equity Project' – referencing a failed proposal to allow collaborative assignments.
evidence.location: Recovered from cloud trash after device wipe
evidence.significance: Suggests ideological motive but no direct admission of current crime

timeline: Day -30: Dr. Nair requests extended server access under 'research compliance' protocol
Day -21: Vikram Joshi's GitHub repository with AI assignment generator goes viral in closed student forums
Day -14: Aryan Mehta wins inter-college tech pitch with a 'student success platform' concept
Day -7: First unsolicited Telegram offers of 'guaranteed A-grade assignments' appear in student groups
Day -3: Professor Kapoor reports missing Wi-Fi token; CCTV shows Aryan near his office
Day -1 (Night of breach): Server logs show spoofed access from Dr. Nair’s lab IP at 2:15 AM; cron job activates; 320 assignments exfiltrated
Day 0: Dean discovers anomaly after two students submit identical code with perfect error patterns; investigation launched
red_herrings: Vikram’s deleted GitHub and red sneakers suggest direct involvement, but he only created a tool later weaponized without consent
Aryan’s MAC address on Telegram is due to his device being cloned via phishing link sent by the real culprit
Dr. Nair’s spoofed IP and cron job were possible because her credentials were stolen via keylogger planted during her lab’s shared workstation maintenance
Neha’s burner phone and logbook note indicate sabotage, but she was attempting to expose the ring, not run it

solution.method: Used social engineering to steal Dr. Nair’s login credentials, cloned Vikram’s AI script to auto-generate assignments, and exploited Neha’s activism to frame her. He used a cloned MAC address and phishing to mask his Telegram bot activity. He accessed the server via a hidden Wi-Fi piggyback device installed during the hackathon alibi (which he faked by submitting prerecorded participation videos).
