solution.motive: To create a false narrative of being a 'student innovator' by controlling both supply and exposure of academic fraud, intending to sell his 'anti-cheating AI' to the university
solution.proof: Security footage from a convenience store near Gurgaon shows Aryan never left Delhi on hackathon day; his facial recognition mismatches the event check-in. Additionally, metadata in the cron job’s script editor shows document authorship linked to Aryan’s cloud account, last accessed from his dorm at 2:10 AM during the breach.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference alibis with external CCTV and metadata. The real breakthrough comes from analyzing the cron job’s file creation metadata, not just access logs. The spoofed IP is a distraction—only someone with credential theft and cloning ability could execute it. Aryan is the only suspect with motive tied to profiting from the exposure of the ring, not just running it. His social engineering pattern (phishing, cloning) is confirmed by digital footprint analysis linking the Telegram bot to a virtual machine hosted on his personal router.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Students
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay
case.crime: A systematic fake attendance marking racket uncovered after multiple students with unexplained 100% attendance were found to have never attended classes for weeks
case.victim: Academic integrity of the institution and scholarship allocation process

suspects.name: Arjun Mehta
suspects.motive: Running a paid service to mark attendance for absent students, earning significant income
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been attending all classes, supported by digital attendance logs
suspects.secret: Involved in illegal cryptocurrency trading using college servers
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Frequently seen near professor offices before attendance is marked and owns an unusually expensive lifestyle

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Deshmukh
suspects.motive: Wants to inflate her class attendance metrics to secure a research grant dependent on student engagement
suspects.alibi: Claims to take attendance manually first, then upload to the system, verified by classroom CCTV timestamps
suspects.secret: She falsified parts of her last grant report and fears scrutiny
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Resisted IT audit of her attendance records and deleted some intermediate logs

suspects.name: Rohan Patil
suspects.motive: Blackmailed into helping after being caught plagiarizing a major project
suspects.alibi: Says he was in the library studying during attendance hours
suspects.secret: Suffers from undiagnosed anxiety and takes medication that causes memory lapses
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen cloning RFID student ID cards in the electronics lab late at night

suspects.name: Nalini Kapoor
suspects.personality: efficient, rule-abiding, fiercely loyal to the department
suspects.motive: Personal grudge against absentee students she believes are disrespecting faculty
suspects.alibi: On official leave during two days of suspicious attendance uploads
suspects.secret: Her nephew was expelled for poor attendance last year, and she blames the lax system
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed the attendance server remotely from an unauthorized device

evidence.description: Attendance logs showing 100% attendance for 12 students who were out of state during the week, all marked via the same IP address
evidence.significance: Proves attendance was marked remotely, not in class

evidence.description: Three blank RFID student ID cards with partial fingerprints and a printed list of student IDs and passwords
evidence.significance: Suggests identity duplication attempt

evidence.description: Timestamped CCTV footage showing Dr. Deshmukh scanning a stack of cards at the classroom door RFID reader
evidence.location: Main Block, Room CS-304 security footage
evidence.significance: Appears to show professor marking attendance for absent students

evidence.description: Cafeteria staff reports seeing Arjun Mehta giving cash to Rohan multiple times on Wednesdays
evidence.significance: Suggests a financial transaction between suspects

evidence.description: Encrypted script found in Rohan's personal GitHub repository that automates attendance login using proxy authentication
evidence.significance: Shows technical capability, but script is incomplete and never deployed

evidence.description: Server access logs showing remote login from Nalini's registered device at 2:17 AM on days when attendance was batch-uploaded
evidence.significance: Links Nalini to unauthorized access

evidence.description: Printed attendance confirmation receipts with mismatched timestamps — some show entries before the class officially started
evidence.significance: Indicates attendance was pre-filled, not live-marked

timeline: 2023-11-06 09:00: Dr. Deshmukh begins her Theory of Computation lecture
2023-11-06 09:05: Attendance marked for 58 students, including 7 not on campus
2023-11-06 09:10: CCTV shows Dr. Deshmukh scanning a stack of ID cards at CS-304 door
2023-11-08 02:17: Remote login to attendance server from IP traced to Nalini Kapoor’s home
2023-11-09 14:30: IT department flags anomaly in attendance data for 12 students
2023-11-10 11:00: Blank RFID cards discovered in lab recycling bin
2023-11-10 16:00: Rohan seen arguing with Arjun near the server room
red_herrings: The stack of ID cards scanned by Dr. Deshmukh were test cards used to calibrate the reader — not real student IDs
Rohan’s GitHub script was a class assignment and lacked server access credentials
Blank RFID cards were for a student project on access control systems
Nalini accessed the server remotely to approve urgent grade submissions during her leave

solution.method: Exploited a flaw in the legacy attendance API that allowed bulk submissions if authentication tokens were stolen. He obtained session tokens by phishing students and faculty, then used a script to inject false attendance data during early morning hours, routing through Nalini’s registered device after stealing her credentials via a spoofed login page.
solution.motive: To profit from a paid 'attendance protection' scheme charging ₹1,500 per student per course, which had over 40 active clients
solution.proof: Correlation between phishing email logs (traced to Arjun's dorm IP) and the stolen tokens used in fake submissions; his cryptocurrency wallet shows 67 deposits of ₹1,500 on dates matching attendance uploads
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference the server access logs with phishing activity, confirm device spoofing via browser fingerprinting, and trace financial inflows. The key is realizing that even though Nalini’s device was used, her login behavior (typing speed, mouse patterns) in the logs differs from known samples — indicating credential theft. Arjun’s alibi collapses when CCTV from the cybercafe shows him online during the upload times, not in class.

case.title: The Case of the Buried Past
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, South Campus – Department of Social Sciences
case.crime: A senior student is being blackmailed using decade-old photographs showing a professor in a compromising political protest, falsely implying sedition. The blackmailer threatens to leak the images unless the victim helps sabotage a caste equity committee report.
case.victim: Aanya Malhotra, 21, third-year Sociology major and chair of the college’s Social Equity Committee. She discovered the photos on an anonymous cloud folder sent to her email and has been receiving threatening messages via a spoofed number.

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.personality: Ambitious, socially awkward, deeply insecure, meticulous
suspects.motive: Wants to discredit the equity report to protect his family name—his father is a BJP district president mentioned in the report’s critique of political interference in campus affairs.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the library studying for an economics exam from 7 PM to 11 PM on the night the blackmail began.
suspects.secret: He is secretly dating Aanya's best friend, who is from a lower caste—relationships across caste lines are taboo in his family.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Aanya two days before the blackmail began and accessed the college’s digital archive the same week.

suspects.name: Prof. Arvind Kapoor
suspects.personality: Charismatic, guarded, politically cautious, respected but feared
suspects.motive: The photos show him at a 2010 Kashmir solidarity protest. He fears being labeled anti-national, losing tenure, and damaging his daughter’s career in the civil services.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home grading papers and confirms with his wife. No digital activity on his personal devices that night.
suspects.secret: He helped edit the equity report anonymously to strengthen its findings but didn’t want to be associated with it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Initially denied the photos were him, then admitted it under pressure—behavior that seems evasive.

suspects.name: Priya Deshpande
suspects.personality: Outspoken, activist-minded, impulsive, loyal to causes
suspects.motive: Believes the equity report doesn’t go far enough. May have used blackmail to force Aanya to include stronger recommendations or resign, creating space for a more radical leader.
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a feminist collective meeting until 9 PM, then went home. One friend confirms her presence until 8:45 PM.
suspects.secret: She once leaked internal committee emails to a news portal last year, resulting in a disciplinary warning.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Posted cryptic social media stories the day before the blackmail: 'Sometimes justice needs a shadow.'

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.personality: Quiet, observant, deeply religious, resentful of perceived elite bias
suspects.motive: The equity report recommends phasing out caste-based reservations in college staff hiring—threatening his job security despite being from a Scheduled Caste.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a temple prayer meeting from 6:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Two temple members verify this.
suspects.secret: He has been copying sensitive student data from the admin office for a relative working in a rival political party.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the admin server room on the night of the photo leak, despite not being on duty.

evidence.description: Anonymous cloud folder named 'TruthForAanya' containing three digitized photos of Prof. Kapoor at a 2010 protest holding a sign reading 'Free Kashmir is Not Anti-India'. Metadata shows creation on college server.
evidence.significance: Core of the blackmail; appears to originate from internal network.

evidence.description: IP log from college server showing login from Library Terminal #7 at 8:14 PM on March 4 (the night of the leak). User accessed the legacy archive where the photos were stored.
evidence.significance: Links the leak to a physical location—library. Matches Rohan’s alibi.

evidence.description: Torn page from a calendar found near server room with '8:30–9:00' circled and 'temple' written in Hindi
evidence.significance: Suggests Vikram may have lied about his alibi or returned afterward.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing someone wearing a blue hoodie entering the admin wing at 8:05 PM—matches Priya’s usual style.
evidence.significance: Contradicts Priya’s alibi and places her near sensitive areas.

evidence.description: Recovered browser history from Library Terminal #7 showing login to a fake 'Student Council Portal' that harvested credentials. No access to archive files.
evidence.significance: Reveals terminal was compromised—someone used it to steal login info, not access files directly.

evidence.description: USB drive hidden inside a hollowed-out sociology textbook in Prof. Kapoor’s office shelf. Contains file named 'Backup_KashmirPhotos_Encrypted'.
evidence.significance: Suggests Kapoor knew about the photos and may have staged their leak to control the narrative.

evidence.description: Deleted text messages from Aanya’s phone recovered via forensic analysis. One says: 'I know it was you. You think hiding behind admin access makes you safe? —P.' Sent at 10:17 PM on March 4.
evidence.significance: Indicates Priya may have confronted the blackmailer—proving she wasn’t the culprit.

timeline: March 1, 4:30 PM: Aanya receives final draft of equity report; includes critique of political patronage and staffing policies.
March 2, 11:00 AM: Prof. Kapoor privately meets Aanya, warns her report could 'spark unrest'.
March 3, 7:00 PM: Vikram logs into admin server to download staff policy files.
March 4, 8:00 PM: Library Terminal #7 accessed; fake portal used to steal login credentials.
March 4, 8:28 PM: IP log shows login to archive from admin office desktop (Vikram’s station), using stolen admin credentials.
March 4, 8:32 PM: Photos uploaded to cloud; folder shared with Aanya’s email.
March 4, 8:45 PM: Vikram leaves temple (confirmed by two witnesses).
March 4, 9:15 PM: Aanya receives first blackmail message.
March 5, 10:00 AM: USB found in Prof. Kapoor’s office during search.
red_herrings: Prof. Kapoor’s hidden USB makes him appear guilty of staging the leak.
Rohan accessing the library terminal during the time of the breach—seems like strong evidence.
Priya’s cryptic social media post and janitor’s sighting create suspicion she leaked the photos to radicalize the movement.
The torn calendar suggests Vikram returned to campus after temple—possibly to plant evidence.

solution.method: Used his admin access to monitor network traffic, discovered the existence of the protest photos in the digital archive. Stole an admin’s login credentials by luring them to a phishing page on Library Terminal #7. Used those credentials from his office desktop to access and leak the photos to blackmail Aanya into watering down the equity report’s staffing recommendations.
solution.motive: Feared losing his job if caste-based reservations for staff were removed; wanted to derail the report without being linked to it.
solution.proof: IP log places access to the archive from Vikram’s office desktop at 8:28 PM—only someone with physical access or remote control could do it. His alibi only covers until 8:45 PM, but the act took less than five minutes. The torn calendar in Hindi found near server room matches his handwriting. Forensic data shows no remote access or proxy use.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the timeline: the breach occurred from the admin desktop, not the library terminal. The library terminal was used only to steal credentials—proven by the fake portal in browser history. Rohan was at the library but accessed the phishing site unknowingly. Vikram’s alibi ends at 9:00 PM, but the breach happened at 8:28 PM—within his window if he left temple early. The calendar fragment in Hindi ('temple', '8:30–9:00') was planted to mislead but has Vikram’s handwriting. Priya’s message 'I know it was you' proves she suspected the blackmailer, clearing her. The USB in Kapoor’s office was placed there by Vikram to frame him. Thus, only Vikram had means, opportunity, and a hidden motive tied to staff policies.

case.title: The Case of the Missing Hostel Deposit
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Technology (DIT), North Campus Hostel, New Delhi
case.crime: The hostel deposit money of 15 outgoing third-year students, amounting to ₹2.25 lakh, was never returned despite proper clearance procedures. The funds were confirmed collected and logged but disappeared before disbursement.
case.victim: 15 third-year B.Tech students who paid ₹15,000 each as refundable hostel deposits upon entry and were denied return upon graduation clearance

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.motive: He controlled the initial deposit collection and had access to the refund ledger; rumored to be in massive gambling debt
suspects.alibi: Claims he was attending a coding hackathon in Bangalore from May 10–15, during the refund processing window
suspects.secret: He secretly ran an off-book deposit collection scheme for new students to bypass official channels for faster room allotment
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly defensive when questioned, frequently deleting messages, and pressured juniors not to speak to auditors

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.motive: She authorized the refund process and signed off on the disbursement file; recently denied a promotion and facing financial strain due to ailing father’s medical bills
suspects.alibi: Claims she was on official leave visiting her father in Kochi from May 8–16
suspects.secret: She delayed clearance for two students due to false disciplinary records to settle a personal grudge
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refused to release audit logs, claimed server error, and blocked internal inquiry initially

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.personality: Quiet, meticulous, socially awkward, highly routine-oriented
suspects.motive: Handled physical cash transfers and bank reconciliation; recently denied a housing loan, suggesting financial distress
suspects.alibi: Says he was at his sister’s wedding in Jaipur May 12–14; has no digital proof, only handwritten invitation
suspects.secret: Has a side job tutoring students for cash, undeclared income
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Ledger shows he recorded the refund as 'processed' but no bank record exists; claims 'system error'

suspects.name: Ananya Deshpande
suspects.role: Second-year student, unofficial treasurer of hostel mess committee
suspects.motive: Had unauthorized access to the hostel intranet via her boyfriend in Computer Science; wanted funds to finance a startup pitch competition in Singapore
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in a regional debate competition in Chandigarh May 11–13
suspects.secret: She cloned the login credentials of Dr. Nair using a keylogger planted via a USB drive left in the faculty room
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the admin office late at night two days before the audit; deleted browser history aggressively

evidence.description: Log entry from the hostel management system showing Dr. Nair’s ID approved the refund batch on May 10 at 2:17 AM
evidence.location: Server logs accessed after forensic recovery
evidence.significance: Suggests Dr. Nair was active during her claimed leave, possibly falsifying alibi

evidence.description: A torn receipt from a Jaipur jewelry store dated May 13, found in Vikram’s desk drawer, in his deceased mother’s name
evidence.location: Inside Vikram Singh’s locked desk at the hostel office
evidence.significance: Appears to confirm his presence in Jaipur during the crime window

evidence.description: IP log showing login to the hostel finance portal from Room 317 (Ananya’s room) at 1:48 AM on May 10
evidence.location: Network access logs recovered by college IT
evidence.significance: Direct link between Ananya and system access during refund authorization

evidence.description: Rohan’s boarding pass and hotel receipt from Bangalore hackathon, digitally altered
evidence.significance: Suggests alibi is fake; Rohan may have never left Delhi

evidence.description: Mess cook recalls seeing Vikram depositing a large envelope at State Bank ATM near campus on May 15
evidence.significance: Suggests Vikram handled unrecorded cash

evidence.description: Hidden folder on college server named 'Refund_Backup_Old', containing a duplicate ledger showing deposits were redirected to a 'Maintenance Escrow' account
evidence.location: Recovered via forensic data carving on decommissioned server
evidence.significance: Proves funds were rerouted before deletion; change made via admin override

evidence.description: USB drive labeled 'Dept. Meeting Agenda' in faculty room trash, containing keylogger software
evidence.location: Recovered from waste bin outside faculty lounge
evidence.significance: Used to steal Dr. Nair’s login credentials

timeline: May 1: Final-year students complete exit clearance; deposit refund process initiated
May 5: Vikram Singh prepares refund batch file; submits to Dr. Nair for approval
May 6: Dr. Nair leaves for Kochi; informs office via email she will review approvals remotely
May 10, 1:48 AM: Login from Room 317 (Ananya Deshpande) to finance portal
May 10, 2:17 AM: Refund batch approved using Dr. Nair’s credentials
May 10–12: Funds electronically rerouted from student deposit pool to inactive 'Maintenance Escrow' account via admin override
May 13: Escrow account drained in cash withdrawal by anonymous individual at SBI ATM near hostel
May 15: Students report non-receipt of refunds; hostel office claims 'processing delay'
May 18: Internal audit launched; discrepancies found
red_herrings: Rohan’s fake hackathon alibi suggests he stayed back to orchestrate the theft
Dr. Nair’s login at 2:17 AM appears during her leave, implicating her directly
Vikram’s ATM sighting and jewelry receipt imply guilt and emotional motive
The 'Maintenance Escrow' account is assumed to be a sanctioned college fund, muddying accountability

solution.method: Ananya used a keylogger planted via USB in the faculty room to steal Dr. Nair’s credentials. On May 10, she logged in from her room, approved the refund batch, then exploited a hidden admin override feature to redirect funds to the dormant 'Maintenance Escrow' account. She withdrew the cash using a forged ID at an ATM two days later.
solution.motive: She needed ₹2.5 lakh to register her AI-based edtech startup for a global pitch competition in Singapore, facing a strict deadline. Saw the deposit fund as a 'temporary loan’ she planned to repay anonymously after winning funding.
solution.proof: IP log ties her device to the fraudulent login; USB keylogger matches her fingerprint; forensic server recovery shows the redirect command originated from her IP; bank CCTV (recovered late) shows her face beneath a cap during withdrawal.
solution.how_to_solve: Solver must: 1) Note that only someone with technical skill could use the hidden admin override; 2) Cross-reference IP logs with physical alibis—Ananya’s debate trip lacks digital proof; 3) Realize the 2:17 AM login occurred before Dr. Nair’s plane landed in Kochi, making her alibi valid but credentials compromised; 4) Find the keylogger USB to confirm hacking method; 5) Reconstruct server data to see funds were rerouted, not just unprocessed. Red herrings distract with financial motives, but the real clue is the mismatch between technical capability and access.

case.title: The Case of the Crimson Syllabus
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Advanced Learning (DIAL), a prestigious urban university in New Delhi, during final semester exams in June.
case.crime: Systematic leaking of postgraduate Economics and Computer Science exam papers across multiple departments over three consecutive semesters, culminating in the leak of the high-stakes National Eligibility Entrance Test (NEET) model paper meant for internal assessment.
case.victim: Academic integrity of DIAL; reputational damage; unfair advantage to at least 18 students; loss of accreditation eligibility.

suspects.name: Arnav Malhotra
suspects.personality: Charismatic, academically competitive, socially connected, manipulative
suspects.motive: Wanted to maintain his top-rank status and secure a foreign scholarship; started small but escalated to sell papers for profit.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a late-night study group at the library on the night before each leak.
suspects.secret: He has been using university funds to run an off-campus tutoring racket.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested using 'past papers' that suspiciously resemble leaked ones; was seen arguing with Prof. Desai days before the last leak.

suspects.name: Dr. Meera Desai
suspects.motive: Believes the current academic system favors wealth over merit; wanted to expose flaws in exam security by orchestrating a controlled leak to force administrative reform.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading papers alone in her office during the time of the digital breach.
suspects.secret: She is undergoing treatment for clinical depression and has taken medical leave twice without institutional knowledge.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the only professor to predict the leak would happen; accessed the encrypted exam server 37 minutes before the system logged the breach.

suspects.name: Kabir Ahmed
suspects.personality: Introverted, brilliant coder, socially awkward, morally ambiguous
suspects.motive: Resents the university's plagiarism crackdown after being falsely accused; wanted to prove the system is corrupt by exploiting it.
suspects.alibi: Says he was streaming a coding marathon online the night of the leak, verified by timestamps on a dev forum.
suspects.secret: He built a hidden backdoor in the university's academic portal as a personal project.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His personal drive contains encrypted fragments of exam papers; known for criticizing exam monitoring software.

suspects.name: Rashmi Nair
suspects.motive: Facing possible termination due to budget cuts; sold access to exam files to a private coaching institute to secure a future job there.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was home with her sister, who confirms her presence but admits she fell asleep early.
suspects.secret: She has been falsifying attendance records to cover for her sister, a non-registered student who attends lectures.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made an unusual number of after-hours logins to the exam database; received a large UPI payment from an unknown source the day after the first leak.

evidence.description: Log files show access to the encrypted exam server from Dr. Desai's credentials at 10:37 PM on June 12, 27 minutes before the official breach timestamp. No biometric confirmation (fingerprint) was recorded.
evidence.significance: Suggests either Dr. Desai initiated the breach or her credentials were compromised.

evidence.description: A handwritten draft of the leaked NEET model paper with corrections in red ink, found inside a trash bin near Kabir’s dorm. Contains marginalia with complex code-like notations.
evidence.significance: Appears to link Kabir directly to the content of the leak.

evidence.description: A hidden partition on Kabir’s laptop contains a program called 'ExamShield_Bypass v0.9' and fragments of PDFs matching the leaked papers. Creation timestamp: May 3.
evidence.location: Kabir Ahmed’s personal laptop, seized during investigation
evidence.significance: Strong technical evidence of preparation to access exam files.

evidence.description: Rashmi Nair received ₹42,000 from 'EliteEdge Coaching' via UPI on June 13. Transaction labeled 'Consulting Fee'.
evidence.significance: Direct financial motive and link to an external coaching center known for exploiting leaks.

evidence.description: A night guard reports seeing Arnav Malhotra exiting the admin building at 11:45 PM on June 12, carrying a small USB drive. Arnav denies this.
evidence.significance: Places Arnav at the scene during the breach window with potential storage device.

evidence.description: Email sent from a university ID to 'EliteEdge Coaching' on May 28: 'First packet attached. Full set post-NEET. —R'. No IP trace due to anonymizer.
evidence.significance: Suggests insider cooperation with coaching center; initial suspicion points to Rashmi due to initial 'R'.

evidence.description: A damaged USB drive recovered from a storm drain near the campus perimeter. Data partially recovered: contains a corrupted version of the NEET paper and a temporary file named 'Arnav_Backup_001.temp'.
evidence.significance: Links Arnav directly to possession of the leaked paper; suggests attempt to destroy evidence.

timeline: May 3: Kabir creates 'ExamShield_Bypass' tool on his laptop.
May 28: Anonymous email sent to EliteEdge Coaching with first paper; sent from a spoofed admin email (appears to be Rashmi's).
June 10: Dr. Desai accesses exam server to upload review comments; logs out normally.
June 12, 8:00 PM: Exam papers locked in digital vault; access restricted to 5 officials.
June 12, 9:15 PM: Rashmi logs into exam system to verify upload; logs out.
June 12, 10:37 PM: Server logs show login from Dr. Desai’s credentials.
June 12, 11:00 PM: Actual breach occurs—data exfiltrated via DNS tunneling method.
June 12, 11:45 PM: Night guard sees Arnav leaving admin building.
June 13, 6:00 AM: Leaked papers appear on a Telegram group named 'DIAL TopGrade'.
June 13, 10:00 AM: Rashmi receives ₹42,000 from EliteEdge Coaching.
red_herrings: Dr. Desai’s early server access suggests insider breach, but her credentials were phishing-scraped from a fake university portal.
Kabir’s bypass tool and red-ink draft were part of a white-hat project to report vulnerabilities; he reported it to IT in May but was ignored.
The email from 'R' was forged; 'R' was chosen because it could implicate Rashmi, but the real sender used 'R' to mislead.
Arnav was indeed in the building—but to meet a professor about a scholarship, not to steal papers; the USB was unrelated.

solution.method: Rashmi used a phishing email to steal Dr. Desai's credentials. She accessed the system at 10:37 PM but failed to breach encryption. Later, she physically inserted a malicious USB (pre-loaded with DNS exfiltration malware) into the server room terminal at 10:55 PM using her admin key, triggering the actual data leak at 11:00 PM. She then laundered access logs to make it appear the breach was digital-only.
solution.motive: Facing job insecurity, she conspired with EliteEdge Coaching to sell exam papers for ₹42,000 per leak to secure a future position there.
solution.proof: Security camera footage (initially 'corrupted') was recovered showing Rashmi entering the server room at 10:55 PM on June 12 with a USB drive. The malware on the recovered USB in the storm drain matches the exfiltration signature. The UPI payment confirms transaction.
solution.how_to_solve: The investigator must reconcile the timeline: the 10:37 PM login did not cause the 11:00 PM breach, indicating two events. The physical USB in the drain with Arnav’s name is a plant—he lost it during a tutoring session days earlier. Kabir’s tool was never used in the breach. Dr. Desai’s access was spoofed. Only Rashmi had physical access, motive via financial trail, and opportunity. The fake email used 'R' to misdirect, but the payment and camera proof confirm her guilt.

case.title: The Case of the Forged Futures
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Advanced Learning (DIAL), Department of Computer Science
case.crime: Operation to forge high-level academic recommendation letters for overseas university admissions
case.victim: The integrity of the academic evaluation system; multiple international universities and honest students

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: Failed to get into top universities despite high grades; sought revenge and personal gain by discrediting the system while profiting from selling fake letters
suspects.alibi: Claims he was working on his final thesis in the library from 8 PM to 1 AM on the nights the letters were accessed
suspects.secret: He has been secretly auditing postgraduate cryptography courses and knows advanced digital forgery techniques
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Professor Mehta about a rejected recommendation request weeks before the scandal broke

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Mehta
suspects.role: Associate Professor and Head of Admissions Committee
suspects.motive: Allegedly under pressure to boost the department’s placement statistics; could benefit if more students 'succeeded' abroad
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at home grading exams during all incidents, supported by her husband’s statement
suspects.secret: She is undergoing IVF treatment and has been taking medical leave, which she hides due to stigma
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted several emails from her university account the day before the investigation began; initially withheld access to her office server folder

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.role: third-year undergraduate student and IT lab assistant
suspects.motive: Needed money to pay off gambling debts; discovered a vulnerability in the recommendation system
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a friend’s birthday party both nights; has three friends who confirm his presence
suspects.secret: He has been reselling old lab equipment online and pocketing the money
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed the admissions server remotely on two nights of the breaches using his staff credentials, then wiped the logs

suspects.name: Anjali Patel
suspects.personality: compassionate, anxious, highly ethical, eager to please
suspects.motive: Wanted to help underprivileged students who lacked connections; believed forged letters would 'level the playing field'
suspects.alibi: Claims she was volunteering at a night shelter on both nights; shelter logs confirm her presence but not continuous
suspects.secret: She submitted her own recommendation letter with minor embellishments and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Printed a draft of a suspiciously well-written letter on department printer late at night; was seen retrieving it hastily

evidence.description: Log files show two unauthorized accesses to the recommendation letter database from a faculty terminal at 10:47 PM and 11:13 PM on consecutive Wednesdays. The IP traces back to Dr. Mehta's office computer.
evidence.location: IT server logs, retrieved by the college cyber cell
evidence.significance: Suggests someone used Dr. Mehta’s computer; implies her involvement or compromised credentials

evidence.description: A crumpled piece of paper found in a lab trash bin with a handwritten draft of a recommendation letter for a student not known to any professor. The letter cites research in quantum computing – a subject not taught at DIAL.
evidence.location: IT lab bin, near Rohan's workstation
evidence.significance: Suggests insider knowledge and attempt to draft a fake letter; ties to someone with access to advanced topics

evidence.description: Encrypted USB drive found in Arjun's backpack during a routine security check. Contains a script that can spoof faculty login tokens and generate PDFs with forged digital signatures.
evidence.location: Campus security locker after random check
evidence.significance: Hard evidence of tools capable of committing the crime

evidence.description: Night watchman reports seeing Anjali entering the faculty block at 10:30 PM on one of the breach nights, contradicting her shelter alibi which logs her leaving at 9 PM and returning at 11 PM.
evidence.location: Security logbook, supported by guard testimony
evidence.significance: Places Anjali at the scene during the breach

evidence.description: Metadata analysis of three fake letters shows they were edited using a LaTeX template last modified by Rohan during a lab maintenance project. All letters contain the same unusual font spacing quirk.
evidence.location: Recovered from cloud backups of submitted applications
evidence.significance: Links Rohan’s work environment to the forged documents

evidence.description: A sticky note behind Dr. Mehta’s monitor with a list of login credentials, including her own, written in her handwriting. One username matches the token used in breaches.
evidence.significance: Suggests carelessness or intentional setup

evidence.description: Cross-referenced Wi-Fi logs show Arjun’s phone connected to the 'Faculty_Staff' network — a restricted network — on both breach nights. The connection coincided exactly with the intrusion windows.
evidence.significance: Places Arjun’s device on a network he shouldn’t have access to at the time of the breaches

timeline: June 3, 8:00 PM: Arjun submits thesis draft to university portal.
June 3, 10:47 PM: First unauthorized access to recommendation database from Dr. Mehta's office computer.
June 3, 11:00 PM: Rohan’s friends claim he was at a party (confirmed by video).
June 3, 10:30 PM: Night watchman sees Anjali entering faculty block.
June 4, 7:00 AM: Dr. Mehta arrives at office, uses her computer normally.
June 10, 11:13 PM: Second breach from same IP; Wi-Fi logs show Arjun’s phone on Faculty_Staff network.
June 11, 9:00 AM: Department receives alert from MIT about suspicious recommendation letter.
June 12, 3:00 PM: Encrypted USB found in Arjun's backpack during random security screening.
June 13, 10:00 AM: Investigation begins; all suspects interviewed.
red_herrings: Dr. Mehta’s deleted emails – later found to be personal medical correspondence.
Anjali’s late-night presence – she returned to retrieve a lost phone, confirmed by CCTV stills.
Rohan’s LaTeX template – widely shared among students; used innocently in past projects.
The fake letter draft in the lab – Rohan had left the lab open, and anyone could have used the printer.

solution.method: Used his knowledge of cryptography to spoof Wi-Fi authentication and gain access to the Faculty_Staff network. He remotely accessed Dr. Mehta’s computer via an unpatched remote desktop vulnerability. He used his own script (found on the USB) to generate forged letters with simulated digital signatures, mimicking her writing style using NLP analysis of past letters.
solution.motive: After being rejected by all top universities despite excellent grades, Arjun believed the recommendation system was biased toward well-connected students. He decided to sabotage it by flooding it with fakes, while anonymously selling some to desperate students — not for money, but to prove the system's fragility.
solution.proof: Wi-Fi logs tie Arjun’s device to the Faculty_Staff network during both breaches. His USB contains the exact forging script. Metadata of one fake letter includes a hidden watermark ID that matches a unique compiler version only Arjun had installed from a private repo.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Dismiss Dr. Mehta’s computer access as misleading — her credentials were stolen via the sticky note (planted). 2. Rohan’s LaTeX link is circumstantial — template was public. 3. Anjali’s presence was innocent. 4. Wi-Fi logs are key — only Arjun had both motive, technical skill, and a device logged into the restricted network. 5. The USB is critical — the script contains comments in Arjun’s unique coding style (e.g., 'fix later - AM'). 6. The watermark in the PDF compiler ties the forged documents definitively to Arjun’s private development environment.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Khoj Funds
case.setting: Khoj Literary Club office, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi
case.crime: Over ₹1.2 lakh from the Khoj Literary Club’s annual budget has gone missing just before the national literary fest 'WordPlay'.
case.victim: Khoj Literary Club – a student-run organization responsible for literary events, now unable to fund its flagship fest.

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.motive: Desperately needs money to pay off a secret poker debt to a dangerous off-campus loan shark.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a late-night study group in the library on the night funds disappeared.
suspects.secret: He’s been gambling online and owes ₹1.5 lakh to an illegal loan syndicate.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the club office after hours without permission two days before the theft.

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.personality: Strict, principled, socially distant, deeply private
suspects.motive: Disapproves of the club's 'frivolous spending' and believes the funds should go to academic research grants.
suspects.alibi: Was attending a faculty meeting until 8 PM and then claims to have gone straight home.
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously donating club funds to a rural education NGO without approval.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Access logs show she entered the club office twice in the past week using her faculty key, though she denies visiting.

suspects.name: Zoya Rahman
suspects.motive: Wanted to redirect funds to refugee education workshops the college refused to sponsor.
suspects.alibi: Says she was attending a feminist collective meeting until 9 PM and then went to her dorm.
suspects.secret: She withdrew ₹10,000 from the club account two weeks prior for an unofficial outreach trip and hasn’t logged it.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was overheard arguing with the club treasurer about 'misuse of funds' the day before the theft.

suspects.name: Rajiv Malhotra
suspects.motive: His daughter was recently diagnosed with a rare illness requiring expensive treatment.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was repairing lights in the auditorium from 7 PM to 10 PM.
suspects.secret: He’s been quietly siphoning small amounts from various club budgets for months to fund his daughter’s treatment.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person seen near the club office that night—caught on CCTV closing the door.

evidence.description: A torn receipt for a ₹1,200 cash withdrawal from an ATM near the hostel, dated the night of the disappearance, with partial fingerprints.
evidence.location: Found crumpled in a trash can outside the boys' hostel.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone made a small withdrawal shortly after the theft—possibly a test run or to cover personal expenses with stolen money.

evidence.description: Bank statement shows a ₹1.2 lakh online transfer from the club account to an unknown account under the name 'EduVidya Foundation'.
evidence.location: Extracted from the club's Google Drive financial folder.
evidence.significance: Appears to show an intentional transfer, possibly indicating an inside job by someone with access and motive to redirect funds.

evidence.description: A first-year student claims to have seen Aarav arguing with someone near the club office at 10:30 PM on the night of the theft.
evidence.significance: Places Aarav at the scene despite his alibi.

evidence.description: A keycard access log showing Dr. Nair entered the club office at 6:45 PM and 8:15 PM on the day of the theft.
evidence.significance: Contradicts her claim of going straight home after the faculty meeting.

evidence.description: An encrypted email in Zoya’s draft folder addressed to 'EduVidya Foundation' with subject: 'Funding Arrangement'. It was never sent.
evidence.location: Recovered from club laptop during forensic analysis.
evidence.significance: Suggests she knew of the recipient account and may have planned the transfer.

evidence.description: A sticky note with a handwritten note: 'Transfer complete. Delete logs. – R.M.' found behind the filing cabinet.
evidence.location: Behind a cabinet in the club office.
evidence.significance: Direct confession-like note with initials matching Rajiv Malhotra.

evidence.description: IP log from the college server shows the online transfer was initiated from the staff accounting terminal in the admin building at 8:17 PM, not from the club office. The terminal was logged in under Rajiv Malhotra’s ID.
evidence.significance: Proves the transfer was made remotely using Rajiv’s credentials, but doesn't confirm he was at the terminal.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Faculty meeting ends. Dr. Nair and Rajiv attend.
6:45 PM – Access log shows Dr. Nair enters club office (verified by security cam).
7:00 PM – Rajiv begins 'auditorium repair work' (per work log).
7:30 PM – Zoya leaves feminist collective meeting.
8:15 PM – Security log shows Dr. Nair re-enters club office, exits 5 minutes later.
8:17 PM – Online transfer of ₹1.2 lakh initiated from staff accounting terminal via Rajiv’s login.
8:18 PM – CCTV shows Rajiv walking from auditorium to staff quarters.
9:00 PM – Aarav arrives at library study group (confirmed by 3 students).
10:30 PM – First-year student claims to see Aarav near club office.
11:00 PM – Club president discovers missing funds the next morning after checking account.
red_herrings: The torn ATM receipt suggests a hasty withdrawal by the thief, but it's from a legitimate ₹1,200 club expense Aarav forgot to log.
Zoya’s unsent email to EduVidya implies she planned the transfer, but she was researching NGOs and never intended theft.
The sticky note with 'R.M.' appears to be a confession, but it's a crude forgery by someone trying to frame Rajiv.
Dr. Nair’s double visit to the club office was to drop off graded papers and retrieve a book—unrelated to funds.

solution.method: Used stolen faculty login credentials (copied from Dr. Nair’s unattended laptop during office hours) to access the staff accounting terminal remotely from the library. He initiated the transfer to 'EduVidya Foundation'—an account he created using Zoya’s research notes. He forged the sticky note to implicate Rajiv.
solution.motive: To pay off a ₹1.5 lakh debt to a loan shark who threatened to expose him and ruin his academic future.
solution.proof: IT logs show the transfer’s originating IP matches the library’s public terminal. Browser history on that terminal shows login to the faculty portal using Dr. Nair’s credentials at 8:16 PM. Aarav’s library sign-in timestamp matches, but facial recognition from library CCTV shows he briefly left the study area at 8:15 PM and returned at 8:19 PM—exactly when the transfer was made.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the digital and physical timelines. The transfer was made from the admin terminal under Rajiv’s login, but he was on CCTV near the auditorium at that moment. The library terminal’s logs and facial recognition reveal Aarav’s brief absence. His access to Dr. Nair’s credentials (she left her laptop unlocked during a meeting) and Zoya’s research (found open on the club laptop) gave him the tools. The ATM receipt and sticky note are red herrings. The unsent email and access logs misdirect, but the IP and facial data are irrefutable.

case.title: The Case of the Hushed Hostel
case.setting: Kalinga Institute of Technology, Bhubaneswar — Hostel Block D, Room 307
case.crime: Fatal ragging incident of a first-year student covered up by tampering with evidence and falsifying records
case.victim: Arvind Mehta, a 19-year-old first-year Electrical Engineering student

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Arvind had evidence of Rohan cheating in midterms; silencing him ensured Rohan wouldn't be expelled
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a late-night coding competition in the computer lab, supported by a timestamped login
suspects.secret: He plagiarized his final-year project from an open-source repo
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to clean Arvind’s room post-incident and pressured others to stay silent

suspects.name: Dr. Nalini Iyer
suspects.motive: Fears scandal would tarnish her record and derail her promotion; university administration pressured her to suppress the incident
suspects.alibi: Says she was working from home and submitted grading reports at 2:15 AM
suspects.secret: She falsified her PhD publication record to secure her current position
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Altered the hostel entry log and dismissed the nurse’s initial report as 'exaggerated'

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.motive: Led the ragging session and physically assaulted Arvind; feared criminal charges and rustication
suspects.alibi: Claims he left the hostel by 9:30 PM to visit his girlfriend off-campus
suspects.secret: He’s secretly failing two core subjects and on academic probation
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Destroyed his phone the next morning and gave conflicting accounts of the night

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.role: senior student and student council president
suspects.motive: Wanted to protect the college’s ranking; believed exposure would lead to funding cuts and campus closure rumors
suspects.alibi: Says she was compiling council reports in her room with video call logs to a junior member
suspects.secret: She accepted bribes from a coaching institute to promote their courses to freshers
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Urged witnesses to give 'gentler' versions of events and retracted her own initial police statement

evidence.description: A torn piece of a yellow ragging rule pamphlet with smudged fingerprints and traces of mud, found under Arvind’s bed
evidence.location: Under the victim’s bed in Hostel Room 307
evidence.significance: Suggests ragging occurred; fingerprints eventually link to Vikram, but mud matches grounds near the main gate — misleading because Vikram left early

evidence.description: Rohan’s login timestamp in the computer lab system at 11:48 PM, with a submitted code file at 2:01 AM
evidence.significance: Seems to confirm alibi, but later found to be remotely accessed via an automated script

evidence.description: A damaged wristband with GPS tracker (from a health band) showing last signal at 10:15 PM near Room 307, then sudden discontinuation
evidence.location: Dumped in a drain outside the hostel
evidence.significance: Indicates time of last movement; GPS failure suggests tampering

evidence.description: Dr. Iyer’s submitted grading sheet timestamped at 2:15 AM, but metadata reveals it was created at 5:30 AM
evidence.significance: Proves her alibi is fabricated; she was on campus that night

evidence.description: Night security guard claims he saw Priya enter Hostel D at 11:02 PM, despite female students not permitted after 9 PM
evidence.significance: Places Priya at the scene; contradicts her alibi

evidence.description: A crumpled note in Arvind’s handwriting: 'Rohan knows I have proof. Told Dr. Iyer. Need to submit tomorrow.'
evidence.significance: Suggests both Rohan and Dr. Iyer had motive to silence Arvind; crucial clue

evidence.description: Deleted WhatsApp messages recovered from a backup: Vikram threatening Arvind: 'Shut up or you won’t survive the week.' Sent 2 days before death
evidence.significance: Shows premeditated threat but does not prove murder; used to misdirect toward Vikram as sole perpetrator

timeline: 6:45 PM — Arvind attends ragging session in Room 307 initiated by Vikram
8:10 PM — Arvind leaves bruised but conscious; witnesses see him returning to room
9:30 PM — Vikram exits hostel; confirmed by gate log and girlfriend’s testimony
10:12 PM — Security camera malfunction in Hostel D corridor (suspicious power flicker recorded)
10:15 PM — Arvind’s fitness tracker last sends data inside Room 307
10:45 PM — Dr. Iyer’s car recorded entering campus staff gate (CCTV fragment recovered)
11:02 PM — Security guard claims to see Priya entering Hostel D (later disputed)
11:48 PM — Rohan’s account logs into computer lab remotely
2:01 AM — Code submission from Rohan’s ID
6:30 AM — Arvind found unconscious by roommate; declared dead on arrival
7:15 AM — Dr. Iyer arrives, declares it 'probable cardiac arrest', blocks ambulance report
8:00 AM — Hostel logbook altered to show no entries between 9 PM–6 AM
red_herrings: Vikram’s violent threats and presence during ragging point to him as murderer
Priya seen at hostel late at night suggests involvement in cover-up or crime
Torn ragging pamphlet implies ragging directly caused death
Rohan’s remote login appears solid alibi, masking his digital tampering

solution.method: Dr. Iyer entered Hostel D at 10:45 PM after being alerted by a note Arvind left in her mailbox. She confronted him in Room 307, and during a heated argument, injected him with a potassium chloride solution (obtained from the campus clinic) to induce cardiac arrest. She then staged the scene, disabled cameras, and altered records the next morning.
solution.motive: Arvind had reported Rohan’s cheating to her two days prior and threatened to escalate if no action was taken. She feared exposure of her own academic fraud if an internal probe was triggered by a scandal. The incident threatened her promotion and reputation.
solution.proof: Metadata of the grading sheet shows creation at 5:30 AM, proving she was not at home. A clinic log shows potassium chloride vial unaccounted for that night. Her car’s entry timestamp matches the only window when the backup generator was active, bypassing the main camera grid.
solution.how_to_solve: Solver must notice the contradiction in Dr. Iyer’s alibi via metadata. Combine this with Arvind’s note implicating both Rohan and 'Dr. Iyer' as aware of the evidence. The GPS tracker stops at 10:15 PM, but the security breach at 10:45 PM allows for a second entry. The potassium vial missing from the clinic log ties her to the murder method. Rohan, Vikram, and Priya have motives and suspicious behavior, but only Dr. Iyer had means, access, and a clean cover-up infrastructure. The timeline shows she was on campus, and her actions post-incident (blocking report, altering logs) were too orchestrated for mere damage control — they were concealment of guilt.

case.title: The Case of the Vanished Hypothesis
case.setting: Department of Theoretical Physics, IIT Bombay, Mumbai
case.crime: Sabotage of a doctoral candidate's thesis data and academic reputation through deliberate misinformation and deletion of research
case.victim: Rohan Deshmukh, 23-year-old PhD candidate finalizing his thesis on quantum coherence in superconducting qubits

suspects.name: Dr. Ananya Patil
suspects.motive: Rohan's thesis threatened to disprove her own previously published model, risking her academic standing and upcoming promotion
suspects.alibi: Claims she was attending a virtual conference call with CERN researchers from 8 PM to 10 PM on the night of the data deletion
suspects.secret: She plagiarized part of her 2015 paper from an obscure Japanese journal
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Strongly pushed Rohan to 'reconsider conclusions,' discouraged publication, and deleted his lab access logs from her own computer

suspects.name: Ishaan Mehta
suspects.role: PhD student in same lab, rival researcher
suspects.motive: Rohan's breakthrough would have made Ishaan's similar research obsolete, delaying his graduation and postdoc opportunities
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night gaming session with friends at a cafe in Vashi
suspects.secret: He falsified early experimental results in his own thesis and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Rohan two days before, and accessed the lab server using a shared password

suspects.name: Nandini Rao
suspects.motive: Believed Rohan was cutting corners in simulation validation and felt he didn't deserve credit
suspects.alibi: Claims she was working on her coding assignment in the library until midnight
suspects.secret: She anonymously reported Rohan to the ethics committee weeks earlier
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Downloaded a full backup of Rohan’s simulation scripts a week prior, claiming 'for archival purposes'

suspects.name: Prof. Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: Rohan's thesis implicated flaws in a grant-funded project that Vikram oversaw, risking a ₹12 crore funding audit
suspects.alibi: Says he was home with his family and asleep by 9:30 PM
suspects.secret: Delayed Rohan's equipment request to favor Ishaan’s project, violating impartiality rules
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Urged the university to freeze Rohan’s submission and control internal investigation

evidence.description: Server log showing deletion of Rohan’s final dataset at 9:47 PM on March 12. IP traced to computer in Dr. Patil’s office.
evidence.significance: Places deletion during the CERN call; suggests insider access.

evidence.description: A handwritten note in Ishaan’s handwriting: 'If he submits, we’re both ruined.' Found in a trash bin near the server room.
evidence.location: Crumpled in waste bin outside server room
evidence.significance: Suggests motive and desperation.

evidence.description: Backup USB drive labeled 'Rohan Final Thesis' found in Nandini’s desk drawer. Contains clean, full dataset.
evidence.significance: Appears to be theft or preservation; raises questions.

evidence.description: Janitor reports seeing Prof. Joshi entering the department building after 9 PM on March 12, contradicting alibi.
evidence.significance: Places Joshi on campus during deletion window.

evidence.description: Email from Dr. Patil to journal editor retracting endorsement of Rohan’s preprint, sent minutes after data deletion.
evidence.significance: Shows motive and timing alignment.

evidence.description: Timestamped GitHub commit history showing Rohan’s code was altered to insert a data-corrupting loop on March 10, signed in with his credentials.
evidence.significance: Suggests self-sabotage or credential theft.

evidence.description: Dr. Patil’s office computer had a spoofed Zoom window running during the CERN call—actual activity shows access to server admin panel at 9:45 PM.
evidence.significance: Proves alibi was faked and she performed the deletion.

timeline: March 10, 3:15 PM: Dr. Patil meets Rohan privately, advises 'major revisions'.
March 10, 8:20 PM: GitHub repository altered with corrupted loop (via Rohan’s credentials).
March 11, 11:00 AM: Nandini submits anonymous complaint about Rohan’s methodology.
March 12, 6:00 PM: Ishaan argues with Rohan over lab scheduling.
March 12, 8:00–10:00 PM: Dr. Patil’s claimed CERN conference call.
March 12, 9:47 PM: Server logs show data deletion from Dr. Patil’s office IP.
March 12, 9:50 PM: Janitor sees Prof. Joshi enter building (later revealed to be mistaken identity).
March 12, 9:48 PM: Email from Dr. Patil to journal retracts endorsement.
March 13, 9:00 AM: Rohan discovers data missing and reports sabotage.
red_herrings: The anonymous note implicating Ishaan was actually written by him during a psychology assignment on 'moral dilemmas'—irrelevant context.
Nandini’s backup was made with Rohan’s permission for cross-validation; she kept it to defend against potential false accusations.
GitHub corruption used Rohan’s stored credentials from a lab machine Dr. Patil accessed during office hours.
Janitor misidentified a visiting scholar as Prof. Joshi; confirmed by CCTV stills.
Prof. Joshi delayed equipment but had no access to data systems.

solution.method: Used her administrative server access to delete Rohan’s dataset from the department server. Earlier, she remotely logged into a lab computer using Rohan’s saved credentials (obtained during a 'system check') to insert a malicious script in his GitHub repo, making it appear as if data corrupted organically. She spoofed a Zoom meeting screen to fake her alibi while performing the deletion.
solution.motive: Rohan’s findings directly contradicted her widely cited 2018 model on quantum decoherence. If published, it would discredit her work, jeopardize her National Science Chair nomination, and trigger retraction of her paper.
solution.proof: Forensic analysis of her computer revealed the spoofed Zoom client, active admin panel session at 9:45 PM, and server deletion command logs. The spoofing software left registry traces and mismatched audio timestamps.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must: (1) distrust the alibi due to digital anomalies in the Zoom log; (2) link the server deletion IP to her office; (3) dismiss red herrings by verifying Ishaan’s gaming receipts, Nandini’s chat logs with Rohan about the backup, and CCTVs clearing Joshi; (4) realize only someone with admin rights could permanently purge server data; (5) discover the spoofing via computer forensics showing no real inbound Zoom traffic during the 'call.'

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Vada Pav
case.setting: Jai Bharat College of Commerce and Arts, Mumbai
case.crime: Systematic financial fraud by the canteen contractor involving food subsidy misallocation and inventory falsification over three academic terms
case.victim: The college's student welfare fund and subsidized meal program for economically disadvantaged students

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.role: final-year B.Com student and student council treasurer
suspects.motive: Wanted to divert canteen funds to sponsor a high-profile cultural fest to boost his election campaign for student union president
suspects.alibi: Claims he was attending a debate competition in Pune during the audit verification week
suspects.secret: He falsified his family's income documents to gain access to a need-based scholarship
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Aggressively lobbied to keep the canteen contractor despite student complaints about food quality

suspects.name: Smita Desai
suspects.role: Associate Professor of Accounting and chair of the Student Welfare Committee
suspects.motive: Disagreed with the college's policy of subsidizing junk food; wanted to discredit the canteen to push for a health-food-only policy
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading exams at home on the nights of inventory discrepancies
suspects.secret: She has been quietly funding a free tuition center for slum children using personal savings, making her sensitive to fund misuse
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to escalate the fraud allegations, but refused to share her notes with the audit team

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.role: Canteen contractor and owner of 'Campus Bites Pvt. Ltd.'
suspects.personality: smooth-talking, entrepreneurial, resentful of regulation, financially stretched
suspects.motive: Facing bankruptcy due to a failed restaurant venture; siphoned college subsidies to cover personal debts
suspects.alibi: Says he was in Goa securing a new franchise deal during the period of suspected fraud
suspects.secret: His company is co-owned by his brother, a known figure in a dubious food supply chain raid two years prior
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Submitted forged delivery receipts and altered inventory logs

suspects.name: Ananya Rao
suspects.role: Second-year BMS student and part-time canteen cashier
suspects.motive: Needed money for her sister's medical treatment; may have sold access to the canteen's digital sales system
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at her off-campus hostel studying late on the nights in question
suspects.secret: She's been anonymously running a successful food review blog that criticizes the canteen's hygiene
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen deleting files from the canteen's backup laptop a day before the audit

evidence.description: Canteen POS system logs showing identical daily sales figures for 17 consecutive days, despite fluctuating attendance and weather
evidence.location: Internal audit copy from college IT server
evidence.significance: Suggests manual tampering or system manipulation to simulate consistent sales

evidence.description: A torn invoice from 'Golden Grain Distributors' dated after the company had legally dissolved
evidence.location: Bottom of recycling bin near contractor's office
evidence.significance: Proves Vikram submitted fake supply documentation

evidence.description: A kitchen helper claims Ananya accessed the billing system after hours using a supervisor login
evidence.significance: Implicates Ananya in system tampering

evidence.description: Emails from Smita Desai to the principal threatening to go public with 'canteen malpractices' unless changes were made
evidence.location: Principal's deleted folder, recovered by IT
evidence.significance: Suggests possible sabotage motive

evidence.description: A personal diary belonging to Vikram found hidden in a spice container, listing payments to 'V. More', 'S.D.', and 'R.M.'
evidence.location: Inside canteen storage room during search
evidence.significance: Appears to show bribes paid to suspects, but 'V. More' is actually 'V. More', a transport vendor

evidence.description: A USB drive left in a library return bin containing encrypted sales data differing significantly from official reports
evidence.significance: Represents authentic, unaltered canteen sales data; decryption key found in Ananya's blog metadata

evidence.description: Rohan's debate partner confirms he left the competition early and was unaccounted for during critical audit hours
evidence.location: Statement collected by internal affairs committee
evidence.significance: Weakens Rohan's alibi

timeline: 2023-08-15: Vikram Joshi awarded canteen contract renewal despite lower bid from competitor
2023-09-10: Student Welfare Committee approves increased meal subsidy based on contractor's inflated cost report
2023-11-03: Ananya Rao starts logging irregularities in sales data on personal cloud but does not report
2024-01-17: Smita Desai requests forensic audit after noticing statistical anomalies in monthly reports
2024-02-05: IT discovers duplicate sales entries in POS logs; audit launched
2024-02-12: Torn fake invoice found; contractor claims 'clerical error'
2024-02-14: USB drive with true sales data anonymously deposited in library
2024-02-15: Ananya seen deleting files from backup laptop; kitchen helper reports it
red_herrings: Ananya's access to the billing system and her blog criticizing the canteen
Smita's threatening emails and refusal to cooperate with the audit
Rohan's broken alibi and political ambitions
Vikram's bribe ledger with initials matching other suspects

solution.method: Used duplicate sales entries in the POS system to inflate daily revenue, then under-reported actual sales to claim higher subsidies. Falsified supply invoices to justify inflated cost claims and siphoned the difference.
solution.motive: To cover massive personal debts from a failed restaurant in Bandra, while maintaining the appearance of a profitable canteen contract.
solution.proof: The decrypted USB drive data matches actual kitchen consumption logs and vendor delivery records, proving systematic understatement of sales. Combined with the forged invoice and Vikram's unverifiable Goa trip, it confirms fraud.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must recognize that identical daily sales figures are statistically impossible (e.g., same sales on rainy, exam, and holiday days). The USB data, once decrypted using a password hint from Ananya's blog ('VadaPavTruth2016'), reveals the real numbers. Cross-referencing delivery records with the fake invoice proves fabrication. The initials in the diary are misdirection—'S.D.' refers to 'Sugar Delivery', not Smita Desai. Ultimately, only the contractor had access to both supply documentation and the full POS system, making him the only one who could orchestrate both sides of the fraud.

case.title: The Case of the Silent Syndicate
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Arts and Science, Mumbai
case.crime: Rampant rumors of a high-grade drug network operating within the campus, leading to a student overdose and mental health crisis among students
case.victim: Aakarsh Malhotra (student, 19), who overdosed on a synthetic stimulant (4-FA), and the broader student body affected by panic, false accusations, and institutional mistrust

suspects.name: Riya Sen
suspects.role: final-year psychology student and president of the Student Council
suspects.personality: Charismatic, calculated, highly organized, socially influential
suspects.motive: Wants to expose alleged drug abuse by the college cricket team to sabotage their influence and take control of campus politics
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a student council meeting in Room 304 from 6:00 PM to 8:30 PM on the night Aakarsh overdosed
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing inflammatory campus gossip blogs under the pseudonym 'The Verdict'
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She was seen arguing with Aakarsh two days before his overdose and was the first to spread the rumor about the drugs

suspects.name: Professor Vikram Mehta
suspects.personality: Reclusive, brilliant, socially awkward, deeply private
suspects.motive: Allegedly used to run a research project on synthetic stimulants before it was shut down; may have continued experiments illegally
suspects.alibi: Claims he was grading papers at home on the night of the incident; no digital logs confirm his presence
suspects.secret: He has a terminal illness and has been secretly selling his research data to pharmaceutical startups for money
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen unlocking the chemistry lab late at night multiple times; owns a locked storage cabinet with unlabeled vials

suspects.name: Dheeraj Kapoor
suspects.role: Second-year commerce student and star wicketkeeper of the college cricket team
suspects.motive: Faces disciplinary action for match-fixing allegations; needs money to pay off bookies
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a team party in Hostel B from 7:00 PM onwards
suspects.secret: He is secretly dating Riya Sen, which he hides to maintain his 'lone wolf' image
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was caught on CCTV near the chemistry lab at 10:45 PM on the night Aakarsh overdosed; later deleted his phone logs

suspects.name: Anjali Deshpande
suspects.role: College counselor and part-time lecturer in Behavioral Sciences
suspects.personality: Empathetic, observant, overly cautious, morally rigid
suspects.motive: Believes drugs are corrupting students and wants to force the administration to implement stricter surveillance
suspects.alibi: Claims she was conducting a tele-counseling session from 6:30 PM to 8:45 PM
suspects.secret: She has been self-medicating with prescription anxiolytics due to burnout
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted several files from her office computer after Aakarsh’s hospitalization; was seen meeting Dheeraj secretly

evidence.description: A crumpled napkin found in a campus restroom trash can with a chemical formula (C10H13NO2) and the initials 'V.M.' written in pen
evidence.location: Third-floor boys' restroom near the science block
evidence.significance: Suggests Professor Mehta was involved in drug synthesis; matches the stimulant found in Aakarsh's system

evidence.description: Anonymous blog post titled 'Toxic Games' published 48 hours before Aakarsh's overdose, alleging cricket team involvement in drug trade
evidence.significance: Points to Riya Sen as the source, suggesting she initiated the conspiracy to discredit athletes

evidence.description: Keycard swipe log showing access to Chemistry Lab B at 10:42 PM on the night of the overdose, logged under Dheeraj Kapoor's ID
evidence.significance: Places Dheeraj at the scene; suggests he stole chemicals to make drugs

evidence.description: A small glass vial with white residue found inside a hollowed-out psychology textbook in Riya Sen's dorm room
evidence.location: Under Riya Sen's bed during a voluntary search
evidence.significance: Appears to link Riya directly to drug possession

evidence.description: A janitor claims he saw Anjali Deshpande entering the counseling center’s storage room at 11:20 PM, carrying a small cardboard box, on the night of the overdose
evidence.significance: Suggests she was transporting something illegally

evidence.description: Deleted file recovered from Anjali’s office computer: a spreadsheet titled 'Controlled Intake Monitoring' tracking students prescribed stimulants for ADHD
evidence.location: Forensic data recovery from college IT
evidence.significance: Shows she had access to prescription medications and was monitoring their use

evidence.description: A tamper-proof prescription bottle labeled 'Modafinil 100mg' found in a drainage grate behind the counseling center, registered under Anjali Deshpande’s medical license
evidence.significance: Proves Anjali was diverting prescribed medication for unauthorized use

timeline: May 12, 3:15 PM: Aakarsh Malhotra purchases a 'study aid' pill from an unknown source near the college canteen
May 12, 6:00–8:30 PM: Student Council meeting held (Riya Sen present)
May 12, 7:00–11:00 PM: Cricket team party in Hostel B (Dheeraj Kapoor claims presence)
May 12, 6:30–8:45 PM: Anjali Deshpande’s tele-counseling session (verified by platform log)
May 12, 10:42 PM: Keycard swipe at Chemistry Lab B using Dheeraj Kapoor’s ID
May 12, 10:45 PM: CCTV shows figure resembling Dheeraj near lab (face obscured)
May 12, 11:20 PM: Janitor sees Anjali entering counseling storage room with box
May 13, 2:10 AM: Aakarsh found unconscious in library basement; rushed to hospital
May 13, 9:00 AM: 'The Verdict' blog publishes 'Toxic Games' post implicating cricket team
May 13, 4:00 PM: Professor Mehta reports his lab keycard missing
May 14, 10:00 AM: Vial found in Riya’s room; campus police notified
red_herrings: Riya Sen’s blog post fuels belief in cricket team conspiracy
Napkin with chemical formula and professor’s initials planted in restroom
Dheeraj’s keycard used to access lab (later revealed to be stolen)
Vial in Riya’s room — actually placed there by Dheeraj to frame her after their fight
Professor Mehta’s secret research — unrelated to the drugs, focused on neurodegenerative disease

solution.method: Abused her position as counselor to obtain prescription stimulants (Modafinil) for students with ADHD, then diluted and repackaged them with inert substances to create placebo-like pills, selling them as 'high-grade study drugs' to fund her own mental health treatment and to manipulate campus policy by creating a crisis
solution.motive: To expose what she saw as lax student wellness policies by manufacturing a drug scandal, forcing administrative action, while secretly profiting to afford her own therapy
solution.proof: The prescription bottle with her license number found in the drain, combined with the recovered spreadsheet showing diverted medications and the janitor's testimony placing her at the scene during critical time
solution.how_to_solve: The key is recognizing that no actual illegal drugs were synthesized on campus. The stimulant in Aakarsh’s system was 4-FA, but lab tests show his pill contained only trace stimulants mixed with lactose. The real crime is prescription fraud. The napkin, keycard, and vial are all planted. Only Anjali had consistent access to legitimate stimulants, a motive tied to institutional change, and physical evidence linking her to illicit distribution. Cross-referencing the tele-counseling log with the janitor’s sighting reveals a 35-minute gap — enough time to travel and make a drop. The spreadsheet confirms systematic tracking of medication stocks. She orchestrated the chaos to appear as a whistleblower while being the source.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Variance
case.setting: Department of Advanced Statistics, IIT Bombay
case.crime: Accusation of research data fabrication in a high-stakes AI optimization paper submitted to NeurIPS
case.victim: Dr. Ananya Deshmukh, associate professor whose academic reputation is at risk

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.personality: Ambitious, perfectionist, socially anxious, highly competitive
suspects.motive: Wants first-author credit on the NeurIPS paper; resents Dr. Deshmukh for delaying his graduation
suspects.alibi: Claims he was working alone in the data lab from 8 PM to 11 PM on the night the data was allegedly altered
suspects.secret: He has been secretly submitting work to a rival lab at IISc under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen deleting files from a shared server the day after the data discrepancy was noticed

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Wants to take over the research group; stood to gain first authorship if Dr. Deshmukh were discredited
suspects.alibi: Says she attended an off-campus research seminar in Pune and has a signed attendance sheet
suspects.secret: She plagiarized part of her own PhD thesis from an unpublished Japanese paper
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Initiated the formal accusation of data fabrication and pushed for an internal inquiry

suspects.name: Arvind Patel
suspects.personality: Naïve, eager to please, technically gifted, insecure
suspects.motive: Fears being expelled for poor grades; Dr. Deshmukh threatened to withdraw his research privileges
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a hostel LAN party from 7:30 PM to 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: He accessed the lab server using Rohan's login after forgetting his own password
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Nervously changed his story about when he last accessed the lab computer

suspects.name: Prof. Vikram Joshi
suspects.role: Senior faculty member, head of department
suspects.motive: Jealous of Dr. Deshmukh’s rising international profile; wants her position as department chair
suspects.alibi: Was at a formal dinner with university trustees at the faculty club until 9:45 PM
suspects.secret: He approved a fake grant claim two years ago and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accelerated the ethics investigation and blocked Dr. Deshmukh from accessing her research files

evidence.description: Log entry showing data file 'neurips_final_data_v3.csv' was modified at 10:17 PM on August 12 via remote access from IP address 10.45.2.168
evidence.significance: Proves data was altered after final submission draft was locked

evidence.description: A sticky note with a handwritten formula: 'σ² = Σ(xi - μ)² / (n - k)', found crumpled in the lab trash
evidence.significance: Suggests someone manually recalculated variance to fabricate consistency

evidence.description: Git commit history showing Rohan Mehta pushed a data-correction script at 9:48 PM on August 12
evidence.location: GitHub repository for the research project
evidence.significance: Makes it seem like Rohan was actively modifying data

evidence.description: Hostel warden reports seeing Arvind Patel leave the building at 7:15 PM and return at 10:40 PM
evidence.significance: Partially confirms his alibi but leaves a 30-minute gap

evidence.description: Email from Priya Nair to the ethics committee dated August 13, 8:02 AM, accusing Dr. Deshmukh of fraud before the investigation began
evidence.significance: Suggests prior knowledge or orchestration

evidence.description: Wi-Fi access log showing device with MAC address XX:YY:ZZ:AB:12:34 (linked to Prof. Joshi’s university-issued tablet) connected to campus network from Room 214 (data lab) at 10:05 PM on August 12
evidence.significance: Places Joshi's device in the lab during the alteration window

evidence.description: Printed draft of the paper with handwritten marginalia criticizing data 'too clean', attributed to Prof. Joshi
evidence.significance: Suggests Joshi had early doubts, possibly motive to sabotage

timeline: August 10, 3:00 PM: Final draft of paper approved by Dr. Deshmukh; GitHub repo locked.
August 12, 7:30 PM: Arvind Patel leaves hostel for LAN party.
August 12, 8:00 PM: Rohan Mehta logs into data lab; camera shows him at workstation.
August 12, 8:15 PM: Priya Nair arrives at seminar in Pune (attendance sheet signed).
August 12, 8:30 PM: Prof. Joshi arrives at faculty dinner (guest list confirmed).
August 12, 10:05 PM: Prof. Joshi’s tablet connects to Wi-Fi in data lab (per logs).
August 12, 10:17 PM: Data file modified remotely from internal IP.
August 12, 10:40 PM: Arvind Patel returns to hostel.
August 12, 11:00 PM: Rohan Mehta logs out of lab system.
August 13, 8:02 AM: Priya Nair files formal accusation.
August 13, 9:15 AM: Dr. Deshmukh discovers data anomalies during final check.
red_herrings: Rohan's Git commit appears to show data tampering, but it was a metadata script for visualization, not data manipulation.
The handwritten formula suggests manual fraud, but it's a student's discarded homework on statistics.
The critical notes in the printed draft were written by Dr. Deshmukh herself during peer review prep.

solution.method: Used a stolen lab keycard to enter the data lab after returning early from the seminar; used Prof. Joshi’s tablet (which she borrowed under false pretenses) to connect to the network and remotely access the server via a pre-installed backdoor she created weeks earlier to alter the data
solution.motive: To eliminate Dr. Deshmukh as competition for a prestigious international research fellowship that requires an unblemished academic record
