solution.proof: CCTV footage (recovered from backup) shows a figure matching Priya’s height and gait entering the lab at 10:02 PM; her alibi collapses when the seminar organizer confirms she left early; digital forensics trace the remote session to Joshi’s tablet but with a keystroke pattern matching Priya’s typing rhythm, stored in her previous lab reports
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Cross-reference the server modification time with Wi-Fi logs: Joshi’s device was in the lab, but he couldn’t physically be there. 2. Realize only someone with high-level access could install a backdoor. 3. Note that Priya had both motive and opportunity: she could’ve returned early. 4. The accusation came too fast—only someone who knew the data was altered would file a report before the victim. 5. The backdoor was linked to a typo in a script only Priya used. 6. Keystroke dynamics in the remote log match her writing style. Conclusion: she used Joshi’s device to mask her digital trail, framing both him and Rohan.

case.title: The Case of the Crimson Frame
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Technical Studies (DITS), New Delhi – Department of Computer Science, girls’ hostel corridor, and college server room
case.crime: A series of anonymous threats involving deepfake revenge porn videos targeting female students, circulated via a private Telegram group. The videos are not yet released publicly but victims receive direct messages threatening exposure unless they comply with anonymous demands.
case.victim: Three female students: Priya Malhotra, Shreya Iyer, and Neha Chatterjee, all third-year Computer Science majors. They received threatening messages with doctored video clips splicing their faces onto adult content with forged college ID overlays.

suspects.name: Arjun Mehta
suspects.personality: Tech genius, socially awkward, introverted, deeply resentful of social cliques
suspects.motive: Was rejected by Priya during a college fest; has a history of being mocked for his lack of social skills
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the server room debugging the college ERP system from 10 PM to 2 AM on the night the first threat was sent
suspects.secret: Runs an anonymous meme page that mocks faculty, which could get him expelled
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen entering the server room late at night multiple times. Found searching for 'deepfake detection bypass' on college Wi-Fi logs

suspects.name: Tanvi Rao
suspects.role: third-year Mass Communication student and campus journalist
suspects.motive: Shreya exposed her plagiarized article in the college magazine; Tanvi lost her editor position as a result
suspects.alibi: Attended a late-night film screening at campus cultural center; several witnesses confirm her presence until 11:30 PM
suspects.secret: Secretly dating a professor, which violates college policy
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had access to victims’ social media via a fake ‘survey’ project; her laptop had encrypted Telegram backups

suspects.name: Dr. Anil Joshi
suspects.personality: Authoritative, traditional, defensive of reputation, patriarchal views
suspects.motive: Strongly disapproves of female students using social media; Priya publicly challenged his outdated syllabus in class
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home grading papers; wife confirms but was asleep by 11 PM
suspects.secret: Misused research funds for personal travel; feared exposure if audited
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for immediate disciplinary action against the 'alleged victims', calling it a 'moral breakdown'

suspects.name: Kabir Dalal
suspects.role: Masters student in Cybersecurity, part-time IT staff
suspects.motive: Was rejected by Neha after a brief relationship; overheard arguing with her about 'ruining his image'
suspects.alibi: Says he was on a video call with a friend in Canada from 9 PM to 1 AM
suspects.secret: Sold college Wi-Fi access credentials to outsiders for cryptocurrency
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had admin-level access to college server logs; deleted cache files from the IT backup drive the day after threats began

evidence.description: Telegram group admin ID traced to a burner account 'ShadowDITS', created using a proxy server based in Mumbai. Messages were sent during late-night hours (12–2 AM).
evidence.significance: Suggests insider knowledge due to accurate use of student IDs and internal college jargon.

evidence.description: A coffee-stained notebook found in the server room with Python scripts related to face-swapping algorithms and Telegram bot automation.
evidence.location: Under a server rack in the basement server room
evidence.significance: Contains syntax consistent with Arjun’s coding style; timestamps match logins to his account.

evidence.description: Encrypted Telegram session file recovered from Tanvi Rao’s old laptop during a random hostel raid (unrelated to case). Decryption revealed drafts of threatening messages.
evidence.location: Confiscated laptop in college security office
evidence.significance: Appears to link Tanvi directly to the threats.

evidence.description: Hostel warden reports seeing Kabir near the girls’ hostel Wi-Fi booster at 1:15 AM on the night of the second threat, claiming he was 'fixing signal issues'.
evidence.significance: Raises suspicion due to timing and location.

evidence.description: Server log shows abnormal access from Dr. Joshi’s registered device at 1:07 AM on the night the first threat was sent, though he denies being awake.
evidence.significance: Indicates possible remote access from his IP.

evidence.description: Metadata from the deepfake video shows it was rendered using a GPU cluster not available on campus. The rendering time was 3.2 hours, between 8:45 PM and 12:05 AM.
evidence.location: Forensic analysis by Delhi Cyber Police
evidence.significance: Rules out most student laptops; points to off-campus high-performance computing.

evidence.description: A forgotten USB drive in the college printing lab, labeled 'Final Project – A. Mehta'. Contains a corrupted deepfake model and logs showing test runs with non-victim faces.
evidence.significance: Suggests Arjun was experimenting but not with the actual victims.

timeline: Day 1, 6:30 PM: Priya Malhotra receives a Telegram message with a deepfake video threat.
Day 1, 10:00 PM: Arjun logs into college server room; security camera shows him entering with laptop.
Day 1, 10:45 PM: Kabir connects remotely to college Wi-Fi from IT office; logs show data export.
Day 1, 11:30 PM: Tanvi leaves film screening; no witnesses until 1:00 AM.
Day 1, 1:07 AM: Login from Dr. Joshi’s IP to server, access to student database.
Day 1, 1:15 AM: Kabir seen on hostel rooftop by warden.
Day 2, 8:00 AM: College administration alerted; Cyber Cell called in.
Day 2, 10:00 AM: USB drive found in printing lab.
Day 2, 6:00 PM: Second threat sent to Shreya Iyer.
Day 3, 9:00 AM: Encrypted Telegram backup found on Tanvi’s laptop.
Day 3, 2:00 PM: Rendering metadata analysis completed, revealing off-campus GPU use.
red_herrings: Arjun’s notebook in the server room with relevant code.
Tanvi’s encrypted Telegram drafts containing threatening language.
Dr. Joshi’s late-night login from his home IP.
Kabir’s presence near the girls’ hostel at night.

solution.method: Used his IT privileges to extract victim photos from college cloud backups, then used a rented GPU cloud service (via cryptocurrency) to render deepfakes. Sent threats via a Telegram bot running on a virtual private server masked through Mumbai proxies. Used Arjun’s server room access pattern to plant the notebook, framing him.
solution.motive: Revenge after Neha ended their relationship and called him 'emotionally abusive' in a group chat, damaging his reputation among peers.
solution.proof: Cyber Police traced the GPU rental invoice to Kabir’s cryptocurrency wallet via a campus Bitcoin mining group he secretly administers. The payment used a college lab computer logged under his ID on Day 0.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. The rendering time (8:45 PM–12:05 AM) rules out Arjun, who entered the server room at 10 PM—too late to have rendered the video there. 2. The GPU cluster is off-campus, so only someone with crypto access could afford it. 3. Kabir’s Bitcoin group activity links him to the wallet. 4. His 'fixing Wi-Fi' story contradicts the warden’s report that the booster was offline that night. 5. His remote login at 10:45 PM matches the data extraction timestamp. 6. The planted notebook has a timestamp created *after* the video was sent—proving it was placed later. Only Kabir had the access and motive to frame Arjun.

case.title: The Case of the Counterfeit Campus
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, South Campus – Merchandise Store and Economics Department
case.crime: Large-scale counterfeiting and distribution of unauthorized college-branded merchandise funded through manipulated student society funds
case.victim: Delhi Metropolitan College’s official merchandise store and student union treasury

suspects.name: Rohan Mehta
suspects.role: final-year economics student and treasurer of the Economics Society
suspects.personality: analytical, reserved, highly organized, socially awkward
suspects.motive: Desire to pay off massive personal debts from family medical bills by siphoning society funds through fake invoices
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been working on a thesis in the library from 7 PM to 11 PM on the night audit discrepancies were discovered
suspects.secret: He falsified his semester GPA to retain his scholarship; fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly defensive during questioning, erased browser history on society laptop

suspects.name: Ananya Desai
suspects.role: fashion design student and president of the Arts & Culture Club
suspects.motive: Wanted to launch her own fashion brand using the college’s brand recognition without permission
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a late-night fashion workshop in the arts studio with three classmates
suspects.secret: She plagiarized her final year project from an international designer
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her recent Instagram posts feature students wearing authentic-looking college hoodies she supposedly 'designed for a contest'

suspects.name: Prof. Arvind Malhotra
suspects.role: Associate Professor of Commerce and faculty advisor to multiple student societies
suspects.personality: authoritative, frugal, socially distant, morally rigid
suspects.motive: Disapproves of the commercialization of college culture; may have sabotaged the official store to discredit administration
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been grading exams at home; wife confirms but was asleep by 9 PM
suspects.secret: He has been quietly funneling college grant money into a rural education NGO without approval
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for the audit that uncovered the fraud, yet resists further investigation

suspects.name: Karan Patel
suspects.role: second-year business student and part-time store assistant at the official merchandise outlet
suspects.personality: smooth-talker, entrepreneurial, impulsive, loyal to friends
suspects.motive: Running a side hustle, saw opportunity to profit from knockoff demand during college fest season
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a cricket match with teammates until 8:30 PM, then went home
suspects.secret: He used store inventory logs to cover theft of actual merchandise for resale
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near a warehouse district late at night; owns a new phone he couldn’t afford

evidence.description: Altered society fund transfer records showing ₹2.1 lakh paid to 'Campus Threads Pvt. Ltd.' for 'event merchandise' – a company that doesn’t exist
evidence.significance: Indicates financial fraud involving fake vendor; linked to Rohan as treasurer

evidence.description: Swatch of fabric with incorrect GSM and misaligned college logo stitching, recovered from a trash bin behind Karan’s apartment
evidence.significance: Matches quality of counterfeit hoodies sold near campus

evidence.description: A student claims to have seen Ananya arguing with the store manager two days before the audit
evidence.significance: Suggests possible grudge or motive against official store

evidence.description: Printed email draft on the society printer from Rohan’s account requesting quote from a garment factory in Noida for 500 college-branded hoodies
evidence.significance: Suggests direct involvement in unauthorized production

evidence.description: USB drive hidden in a hollowed-out economics textbook in Prof. Malhotra’s office containing encrypted files and a ledger showing transfers to a shell company
evidence.significance: Appears to link him to financial manipulation

evidence.description: Server logs from the college domain showing repeated access to the official logo vector files from Ananya’s student account at 2:17 AM on three separate weekends
evidence.significance: Confirms unauthorized use of college IP for design purposes

evidence.description: Microfiber label from a counterfeit hoodie found in the arts studio trash with a partial fingerprint and a tiny thread of indigo blue silk unique to Ananya’s personal sewing kit
evidence.location: Arts & Culture Club studio waste bin
evidence.significance: Direct physical link between Ananya and the counterfeit production

timeline: October 3, 7:00 PM: Official merchandise store closes; inventory count appears normal
October 3, 9:15 PM: College security logs show Ananya’s ID card used to access the arts studio
October 3, 9:45 PM: Karan Patel leaves cricket match; no verified sighting until 11:30 PM
October 3, 10:20 PM: IP log shows access to college logo files from Ananya’s account
October 4, 8:00 AM: Store assistant Karan reports 'inventory glitch' – 75 hoodies missing
October 4, 12:30 PM: Students begin selling suspiciously cheap 'authentic' college hoodies near metro station
October 5, 10:00 AM: Audit initiated after official store reports financial discrepancy
October 6, 3:00 PM: Fake vendor 'Campus Threads Pvt. Ltd.' traced to fake address in Ghaziabad
red_herrings: Rohan’s fake invoice suggests he stole funds directly, but the money was laundered through a third party
The USB in Prof. Malhotra’s office was planted to frame him; encryption keys don’t match his devices
Karan’s theft of real hoodies distracts from the larger counterfeit operation
Ananya’s argument with the store manager was about a design submission, not sabotage

solution.method: Used her design access to replicate official college merchandise, produced knockoffs through an unauthorized factory, and sold them during fest season. Used student society sponsorship funds routed through a fake vendor created by Rohan (unwittingly) to finance production.
solution.motive: To fund her underground fashion label and gain recognition by associating with the college brand without official approval
solution.proof: The microfiber label with indigo silk thread matching her personal kit, combined with server logs proving unauthorized logo access, and witness confirmation of her presence in the studio the night of the theft
solution.how_to_solve: Detective must cross-reference the server logs with the physical evidence from the studio. The fake invoice implicates Rohan, but he only authorized payment—never handled goods. The planted USB and Karan’s theft are distractions. Only Ananya had design capability, physical access, and digital footprint. The silk thread is the definitive link proving she handled counterfeit materials.

case.title: The Case of the Compromised Professor
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College - Department of Political Science, New Delhi
case.crime: A confidential email detailing an inappropriate relationship between a professor and a student is anonymously leaked to the college administration and media, triggering disciplinary proceedings and public scandal. The email is later proven to be fabricated, but the damage is done. The investigation reveals a conspiracy to frame an innocent professor.
case.victim: Dr. Arvind Mehta, 38, Assistant Professor of Political Science – professionally and personally destroyed by the false accusation

suspects.name: Neha Malhotra
suspects.personality: Ambitious, socially adept, emotionally guarded, highly observant
suspects.motive: Dr. Mehta rejected her romantic advances and gave her a low grade on a paper she believed was excellent. She wanted revenge and to gain favor with another professor.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying from 7:00 PM to 10:30 PM on the night the email was sent
suspects.secret: She is secretly dating Professor Ramesh, the department head, who is married
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Dr. Mehta a week before the leak and was the first student to circulate rumors about the relationship

suspects.name: Professor Vikram Ramesh
suspects.motive: Wanted to remove Dr. Mehta, a rising academic star whose research exposed flaws in Ramesh’s own published work and threatened his promotion to Dean
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a faculty dinner with the Dean from 6:30 PM to 9:00 PM
suspects.secret: Engaged in a secret relationship with student Neha Malhotra and has been accepting bribes to admit unqualified students
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed aggressively for swift disciplinary action against Dr. Mehta and blocked the IT investigation initially

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: Introverted, tech-savvy, socially anxious, deeply loyal to Dr. Mehta
suspects.motive: None – actively trying to clear Dr. Mehta’s name. But his skills make him a suspect.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was working alone in the department server room from 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM on the night of the leak
suspects.secret: He has been diagnosed with clinical depression and was taking medication that causes memory fog
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the admin office late at night; has admin-level access to the college email server

suspects.name: Priya Iyer
suspects.personality: Efficient, by-the-book, observant, quietly resentful of faculty privileges
suspects.motive: Harbors a grudge against Dr. Mehta for reporting her for forging attendance records. Wants to see him punished
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at home watching a live-streamed religious ceremony from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM
suspects.secret: She has been diverting department funds into a personal account for years
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to receive the anonymous email and immediately forwarded it to the Dean without logging it through proper channels

evidence.description: The leaked email, dated October 12, 2023, timestamped 8:47 PM, from Dr. Mehta’s official account to a generic student email, using suggestive language and making veiled references to meetings in his office after hours.
evidence.location: College email server logs and forwarded chain in Dean’s inbox
evidence.significance: Appears to be the smoking gun. However, digital forensics reveal it was sent via a spoofed IP using a script that mimicked Mehta’s login session.

evidence.description: A handwritten note found crumpled in a campus trash can near the admin block. It reads: 'They’ll believe it. He deserves it. Time to fall.' In neat cursive handwriting.
evidence.location: Bin near Admin Block, found October 14
evidence.significance: Matches Neha Malhotra’s handwriting from class assignments. However, later proven to be written after the leak – possibly planted.

evidence.description: Server logs show a login to Dr. Mehta’s email from IP address 10.45.221.13 at 8:45 PM on October 12. The IP belongs to a lab computer in Room 214, which has CCTV coverage.
evidence.significance: The CCTV from Room 214 shows no one used the computer that night. The IP was spoofed. The actual access came from a remote session routed through the department head’s office router.

evidence.description: A keycard swipe record shows Neha Malhotra entered the admin building at 7:58 PM on October 12. Building is usually locked after 7:30 PM.
evidence.significance: Places Neha at the scene. But further checks show her card was cloned – she reported it lost two days prior, but failed to deactivate it.

evidence.description: A hidden script in the college’s internal messaging system that allows email spoofing, discovered in the server backups. The script was uploaded 10 days before the leak and last accessed from an account with elevated privileges.
evidence.significance: Only Professor Ramesh and the IT head had such access. IT head confirms he did not upload it. The script is tied to Ramesh’s login.

evidence.description: A coffee-stained draft of the leaked email found in the recycling bin of Professor Ramesh’s office during a covert search. Contains multiple edits and references to 'removing the obstacle'.
evidence.significance: Handwriting analysis confirms it’s Ramesh’s. The draft predates the leak and shows intent.

evidence.description: A night janitor reports seeing someone resembling Rohan Desai carrying a laptop near the server room on October 12. The janitor is near-sighted and was 30 meters away.
evidence.location: Campus grounds, near server access point
evidence.significance: Initially points to Rohan, but contradicted by server logs showing the spoofing script was not active until 8:45 PM, when Rohan was already logged in under his own name.

timeline: October 2, 2023: Dr. Mehta submits peer review criticizing Ramesh’s latest publication.
October 5: Neha Malhotra receives a B+ on her term paper from Dr. Mehta and confronts him angrily.
October 8: Neha reports her keycard lost. IT logs show it was never deactivated.
October 9: A hidden email spoofing script is uploaded to the college server from Ramesh’s office during a staff meeting (server log timestamp).
October 12, 7:30 PM: Faculty dinner begins. Ramesh is seen there until 9:00 PM.
October 12, 7:58 PM: Neha’s cloned keycard used to enter admin building.
October 12, 8:45 PM: Spoofed email sent from 'Dr. Mehta’s' account using the hidden script.
October 12, 8:50 PM: Ramesh logs into college server from his office to verify the email was sent.
October 13, 9:00 AM: Priya Iyer receives the email and forwards it to the Dean.
October 13, 11:00 AM: Dr. Mehta suspended pending inquiry.
October 14: Handwritten note found; Rohan seen near admin office; investigation begins.
red_herrings: Neha’s keycard access and handwriting on the note
Rohan’s server room alibi and tech skills
Priya’s grudge and early involvement in the leak
The CCTV showing no one in the lab despite the IP trace

solution.method: Used his administrative access to upload a hidden email spoofing script to the college server. On October 12, he remotely triggered the script from his phone during the faculty dinner to send the fake email from Dr. Mehta’s account. He used Neha’s un-deactivated keycard (which he had secretly cloned earlier) to create a false trail.
solution.motive: To eliminate professional competition and protect his reputation and ambitions by framing Dr. Mehta, whose research threatened his academic credibility.
solution.proof: The coffee-stained draft in Ramesh’s recycling bin with his handwriting and incriminating edits, combined with server logs showing the spoofing script was uploaded from his office and last accessed under his credentials shortly after the email was sent.
solution.how_to_solve: The investigator must: 1) Question the reliability of digital evidence by identifying IP spoofing; 2) Trace the origin of the spoofing script to an account with elevated access; 3) Dismiss red herrings by verifying alibis (e.g., Neha’s library CCTV, Rohan’s login logs); 4) Discover the physical draft in Ramesh’s office; 5) Connect motive through Mehta’s critical review and Ramesh’s stalled promotion. The clincher is the draft – it could not have been planted by anyone else and predates the leak.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Valedictorian
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Advanced Studies, Mumbai
case.crime: Forgery of a final-year B.Sc. (Hons) Mathematics degree certificate for fraudulent job placement at a multinational bank
case.victim: The college's academic integrity and reputation; the legitimate student who was denied the job

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.personality: Ambitious, socially aloof, perfectionist, intensely private
suspects.motive: Failed final viva by 2 marks; needed degree to fulfill family expectations and secure a corporate job
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been alone in the library studying from 6 PM to 10 PM on the night of the breach
suspects.secret: Suffers from undiagnosed anxiety disorder; had been secretly submitting assignments late with faculty favors
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too eager to prove his innocence; frequently visited the admin office before the results

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.personality: Strict, principled, socially distant, deeply empathetic beneath surface
suspects.motive: Had approved Arjun's re-evaluation request, which was later overturned by the Dean; feared professional scrutiny
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at home grading papers; no digital activity on college systems that night
suspects.secret: Formerly involved in a minor plagiarism controversy in her PhD days, covered up by her mentor
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Strongly defended Arjun's academic capability despite his failure, even lobbying the placement cell

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Held a grudge against the administration for rejecting his internship recommendation letter
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night movie with friends
suspects.secret: Ran an underground side-business printing fake ID cards and recommendation letters for underclassmen
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the admin server room the night of the incident; owns software capable of replicating official seals

suspects.name: Shalini Kapoor
suspects.motive: Under investigation for financial irregularities in exam fee collections; feared exposure if audit intensified
suspects.alibi: Claims to have attended a virtual PTA meeting from 7 PM to 9 PM
suspects.secret: Diverted ₹1.2 lakh in late exam fees to personal account over two semesters
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Delayed reporting the breach by 36 hours; claimed the digital backup logs were corrupted

evidence.description: A timestamped log shows admin server access at 8:47 PM from IP 10.4.16.205 — linked to a terminal in the computer lab.
evidence.significance: Places someone in the system during the forgery window

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'MathSoc2023' found in the library return bin. Contains a near-perfect replica of the forged certificate and a template generator.
evidence.significance: Suggests insider technical knowledge; contains metadata linking to Rohan's personal laptop

evidence.description: An email draft in Dr. Nair’s college account addressed to the Dean, stating: 'I cannot let Arjun's future collapse due to a technicality.'
evidence.location: Drafts folder of Dr. Nair’s email
evidence.significance: Implies intent to intervene in Arjun’s result

evidence.description: A signed but unofficial transcript showing Arjun with passing marks in viva, found in Dr. Nair’s desk drawer during inspection.
evidence.significance: Suggests possible early forgery or tampering

evidence.description: Library security guard states Arjun left at 7:15 PM, not 10 PM as claimed, contradicting alibi.
evidence.significance: Undermines Arjun’s alibi

evidence.description: Biometric log from admin building shows Shalini Kapoor swiped in at 8:30 PM on the night of the breach, but she claims to have been at home.
evidence.significance: Direct contradiction to alibi

evidence.description: A water-stained copy of the forged certificate recovered from the college drainage near the admin block, partially burned.
evidence.significance: Indicates attempt to destroy evidence; forensic analysis reveals toner from Shalini’s office printer

timeline: June 10, 4:00 PM: Final results declared. Arjun Malhotra fails viva by 2 marks.
June 10, 5:30 PM: Arjun submits re-evaluation request, approved by Dr. Nair.
June 10, 6:00 PM: Dean overturns approval, citing policy violation.
June 10, 7:15 PM: Arjun seen leaving library by security guard.
June 10, 7:30 PM: PTA meeting begins (virtual); Shalini logs in briefly, then disconnects.
June 10, 8:30 PM: Shalini’s biometric card used at admin block entrance.
June 10, 8:47 PM: Unauthorized access to degree certificate generation module from computer lab terminal.
June 10, 9:15 PM: Server logs show certificate file exported and printed.
June 11, 10:00 AM: Forged certificate submitted to ICICI Bank placement panel.
June 11, 4:00 PM: Bank verifies certificate via college portal; college system flags discrepancy.
June 12, 9:00 AM: Dean reports anomaly to campus investigators.
red_herrings: The USB drive planted in the library to implicate Rohan Desai.
Dr. Nair’s email draft and unofficial transcript, suggesting she altered records.
Arjun’s broken alibi makes him appear guilty despite lacking technical access.
Rohan’s side business makes him seem the most likely forger.

solution.method: Used her administrative access to disable logging temporarily, generated the forged certificate from the lab terminal (IP 10.4.16.205), printed it using her office printer, and submitted it online posing as Arjun through a spoofed email. Later attempted to destroy evidence by burning a copy.
solution.motive: Feared that a deep audit triggered by the forgery scandal could expose her embezzlement of exam fees. By creating a high-profile academic forgery case, she aimed to redirect attention toward students and faculty, shielding her financial crime.
solution.proof: Biometric entry log placing her in admin block during the breach, combined with toner analysis matching the burned certificate to her office printer. Server logs (recovered from offline backup) show her account initiated the certificate export.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must reconcile the timeline: Shalini claimed to be in a virtual meeting but disconnected early. The biometric entry at 8:30 PM contradicts her alibi. While the USB and Dr. Nair’s draft suggest faculty involvement, only Shalini had both unrestricted access and a motive tied to internal audits. The toner match is irrefutable physical proof linking her printer to the forged document’s destruction. Rohan’s software was used, but the metadata was planted—the real generator was the internal admin tool, accessible only to staff like Shalini.

case.title: The Case of the Hollow Hostel Funds
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Engineering, Hostel Block D, Chennai
case.crime: Embezzlement of ₹2.8 crore allocated for student hostel renovation through a kickback scheme involving fake invoices and inflated contracts
case.victim: The college's development fund and student welfare; students continue to live in dilapidated conditions despite renovation being declared complete

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Wants to secure funding for his pet initiative—a student startup incubator—by redirecting unused renovation funds
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been leading a student protest at the municipal office on 14th March, supported by social media posts and rally photos
suspects.secret: Secretly indebted to a loan shark due to gambling; fears exposure would ruin his political future
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed aggressively for a specific contractor to win the bid, despite higher quotes

suspects.name: Dr. Anjali Nair
suspects.personality: Calculating, reserved, highly efficient, emotionally detached
suspects.motive: Facing financial strain due to her son's expensive medical treatment abroad
suspects.alibi: Claims she was attending a national education conference in Hyderabad from 10th–16th March; has an official badge and hotel receipt
suspects.secret: Her son is not ill—she fabricated the story to justify large withdrawals to support her sister in an illegal real estate scam
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Approved all renovation invoices without cross-verification and dismissed student complaints about poor workmanship

suspects.name: Vikram Mehta
suspects.personality: Egotistical, traditionalist, fiercely loyal to alumni network, dismissive of student concerns
suspects.motive: Received equity stake in a construction firm owned by his cousin
suspects.alibi: Says he was grading final-year project reports at home on 14th March; no witnesses
suspects.secret: Academic misconduct—he plagiarized parts of his PhD thesis, which is under quiet investigation
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Recommended the winning contractor despite lack of ISO certification and a history of substandard work

suspects.name: Sanya Patel
suspects.role: Third-year Architecture Student and Intern in College Planning Office
suspects.personality: Observant, quiet, ethically strict, socially anxious
suspects.motive: Disillusioned with corruption; possibly leaked documents to media anonymously
suspects.alibi: Was supposedly at a late-night study group in the library on 14th March; two friends confirm, but leave at 10 PM
suspects.secret: Is the anonymous whistleblower behind a blog exposing college corruption; fears retribution
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed digital renovation files after hours and downloaded blueprints days before audit

evidence.description: Email trail between Dr. Nair and contractor 'Shree Ram Constructions' showing approval of invoices 30% above market rate, with a note: 'Final disbursement clears the obligation.'
evidence.location: College server, recovered from Dr. Nair’s deleted folder
evidence.significance: Suggests financial collusion with contractor

evidence.description: A torn receipt for ₹5 lakh in cash withdrawn from Dr. Nair’s personal account on 12th March, found in a campus dumpster near staff quarters
evidence.significance: Indicates unexplained cash movement

evidence.description: GPS location data from the college’s security portal shows Vikram Mehta’s ID card accessed the civil engineering server room at 1:17 AM on 15th March
evidence.significance: Suggests unauthorized access to renovation project files late at night

evidence.description: A fake wall panel discovered behind the new warden’s office in Hostel D—inside, mismatched tiles and water-damaged wiring indicate incomplete work
evidence.significance: Proof that renovation was faked in key areas to pass inspection

evidence.description: Night watchman Raju claims he saw Rohan Desai arguing with a man in a construction uniform near the generator room on 14th March at 8:45 PM
evidence.significance: Places Rohan near a renovation site during critical time

evidence.description: Cloud backup of original blueprints showing structural changes (e.g., additional drainage) never implemented, compared with as-built reports signed by Vikram Mehta
evidence.location: Architecture department server, accessed by Sanya Patel 5 days before audit
evidence.significance: Proves falsification of completion reports

evidence.description: Bank statement fragment found printed and burned in hostel incinerator—shows a ₹7 lakh transfer from Shree Ram Constructions to a shell company 'Urban Spaces LLP' incorporated in Vikram Mehta’s cousin’s name
evidence.significance: Direct link to kickback scheme

timeline: 1st March: College announces completion of Hostel D renovation. Students complain about poor quality.
5th March: Anonymous blog 'Campus Truth' publishes allegations of corruption in renovation contract.
10th–16th March: Dr. Nair 'attends' education conference in Hyderabad.
12th March: Dr. Nair withdraws ₹5 lakh in cash from personal account.
14th March, 8:30 PM: Rohan Desai leads protest at municipal office (verified by news footage).
14th March, 8:45 PM: Watchman sees 'Rohan' arguing with construction worker (later disputed).
15th March, 1:17 AM: Vikram Mehta’s ID card logs into server room.
15th March: Sanya Patel downloads blueprints and inspection reports.
16th March: Internal audit scheduled; files go missing temporarily.
17th March: Fake wall panel discovered during routine inspection.
red_herrings: Dr. Nair’s large cash withdrawal—seemingly suspicious but used to fund sister’s real estate scam, unrelated to hostel funds.
Rohan Desai’s protest alibi contradicted by watchman’s sighting—watchman later admits poor eyesight and confusion with a lookalike worker.
Email trail between Dr. Nair and contractor—later revealed to be forged by Vikram using admin access to frame her.
Sanya’s late-night file access—motivated by whistleblowing, not theft.

solution.method: Used his authority to rig the contractor bidding process in favor of Shree Ram Constructions (owned by his cousin). Submitted falsified completion reports with forged signatures, approved inflated invoices, and siphoned off kickbacks through a shell company. Used admin access to plant fake evidence implicating Dr. Nair.
solution.motive: To fund his cousin's struggling construction business and secure a future financial partnership, while leveraging the project to boost his department’s budget.
solution.proof: The burned bank statement fragment linking the shell company to the contractor, combined with server log showing Vikram’s unauthorized access to file systems at 1:17 AM on 15th March—after the contractor’s final invoice was uploaded and before the audit. Digital forensics confirm the fake email was created from his workstation.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must: (1) Note discrepancies between blueprints and actual construction; (2) Cross-reference server logs with suspect alibis—Vikram has no alibi and accessed systems at a suspicious time; (3) Dismiss Dr. Nair’s cash withdrawal as unrelated after tracing funds to real estate; (4) Recognize the email trail was digitally forged (metadata shows creation after 15th); (5) Connect the shell company to Vikram via property records and phone metadata showing repeated calls to his cousin. The GPS data and burned bank evidence provide irrefutable financial and technical proof.

case.title: The Case of the Silent Alarm
case.setting: Vivekananda College of Science and Technology, Delhi — Engineering Wing, third floor
case.crime: A student fell from the third-floor balcony during a late-night electrical blackout. Official reports claim it was an accident, but evidence suggests foul play and a cover-up involving multiple campus authorities.
case.victim: Arjun Mehra, 21, second-year computer science student — died from fall injuries; no suicide note found

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Arjun had discovered she plagiarized her thesis and threatened to report her, jeopardizing her scholarship.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying until 11:30 PM — supported by library CCTV entry log, but no footage inside stacks after 9:45 PM.
suspects.secret: Secretly dating the head of security, Rajan Dube, which violates college policy.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for the 'accident' verdict and discouraged other students from discussing the incident.

suspects.name: Professor Vikram Oberoi
suspects.motive: Arjun was investigating irregularities in the college's electrical retrofit contract, which Oberoi approved and personally benefited from via kickbacks.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home grading papers — supported by a timestamped email sent at 9:17 PM, but no other witnesses.
suspects.secret: Has been falsifying energy audit reports to hide embezzlement.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Insisted the blackout was due to city grid failure, despite campus generators being functional.

suspects.name: Rajan Dube
suspects.personality: Disciplined, loyal to administration, emotionally guarded, manipulative
suspects.motive: Oberoi promised him a promotion if he helped suppress evidence of electrical negligence.
suspects.alibi: On duty in security control room — claims he reviewed footage but found nothing unusual.
suspects.secret: Romantic relationship with Priya, which he concealed to avoid scrutiny of her activities.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted backup camera footage from the third-floor hallway hours after the incident.

suspects.name: Neha Reddy
suspects.motive: None — but has been feeding misinformation to throw off investigators to protect a source.
suspects.alibi: Claimed she was interviewing a professor for an article — no confirmation from the professor.
suspects.secret: Possesses anonymous documents linking Oberoi to corruption but fears retaliation.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Told conflicting stories about what she saw near the balcony that night.

evidence.description: A torn piece of a yellow maintenance tag found under the balcony, partially burned, with serial number fragment 'E-78...'.
evidence.location: Beneath the balcony where Arjun fell
evidence.significance: Links to faulty circuit breaker E-782, which was part of Oberoi's retrofit project and had been improperly installed.

evidence.description: Security camera log shows a 12-minute gap in the third-floor hallway footage at 9:03–9:15 PM — timestamp anomaly suggests manual deletion.
evidence.significance: Proves deliberate tampering — Rajan Dube accessed the system remotely at 10:41 PM.

evidence.description: A pair of prescription reading glasses with a cracked left lens, engraved 'P.M.'
evidence.location: Near the fire extinguisher on the third floor
evidence.significance: Belongs to Priya Malhotra — but she claims she lost them weeks ago. Planted to mislead?

evidence.description: Arjun’s encrypted cloud draft: 'Project Voltage: Proof that Oberoi’s retrofit is a scam. Meeting with Neha tonight. If I disappear—'
evidence.location: Recovered from Arjun’s old phone by his roommate
evidence.significance: Reveals motive for murder and Arjun’s intent to expose corruption.

evidence.description: Night canteen vendor claims he saw Neha running from the engineering wing at 9:20 PM, looking pale.
evidence.significance: Places Neha near scene — but she says she was fleeing after discovering the body.

evidence.description: Email from Oberoi to city power department dated two days before: 'Confirm we are NOT on city grid — using independent generator during retrofits.'
evidence.location: Recovered from Oberoi’s deleted items after forensic scan
evidence.significance: Proves Oberoi lied — blackout was not due to city failure but campus system sabotage.

evidence.description: Burn marks on circuit breaker E-782 with traces of accelerant (lighter fluid).
evidence.significance: Indicates arson to cause blackout — method used to create opportunity for push.

timeline: 7:10 PM: Arjun texts friend, 'I’m meeting Neha at 9. Have proof on Oberoi.'
8:55 PM: Campus-wide blackout — generators fail to activate.
9:03–9:15 PM: Security camera footage deleted from third-floor hallway.
9:12 PM: Arjun falls from third-floor balcony — no witnesses immediately report it.
9:20 PM: Canteen vendor sees Neha exit engineering building.
9:30 PM: Rajan Dube logs into security system remotely from his phone.
9:45 PM: Priya enters library (CCTV log) — no footage shows her inside.
10:17 PM: Oberoi sends email from home about grading — IP traced to college server proxy.
10:41 PM: Rajan accesses and deletes backup camera logs.
red_herrings: Priya’s glasses at the scene suggest she was present, but she lost them earlier and someone planted them.
Neha seen fleeing the building — she was actually first to find the body and panicked.
Arjun’s draft implies he trusted Neha, but she didn’t attend the meeting — he was misled.
Claim that city power failed, contradicted by Oberoi’s own email.

solution.method: Sabotaged circuit breaker E-782 with accelerant to trigger blackout, then lured Arjun to the third-floor balcony under false pretense of a meeting. Pushed him during darkness and used security ally Rajan Dube to erase evidence.
solution.motive: Arjun was about to expose Oberoi’s corruption in the electrical retrofit scam, which would have led to legal and professional ruin.
solution.proof: Oberoi’s email admitting independent power, combined with burn traces containing his fingerprints and DNA on the lighter used — found hidden in his office desk drawer. Also, timeline shows he faked being at home by routing emails through college servers.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Cross-reference blackout cause with Oberoi’s email. 2. Link maintenance tag to E-782 and burner residue. 3. Notice that Oberoi’s 'at home' email came through college proxy, not home IP. 4. Confirm Rajan’s deletion of footage was on Oberoi’s orders via call logs recovered from cloud backup. 5. Realize only Oberoi had technical expertise and access to sabotage the breaker. Priya’s and Neha’s clues are misdirections created by the cover-up.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Scholars
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Advanced Studies (DIAS), Department of Computational Sciences
case.crime: International student visa fraud involving the enrollment of non-existent students using forged documents and academic records
case.victim: The Indian Ministry of Education and the college's international accreditation status; several legitimate international students were displaced due to filled quotas

suspects.name: Arnav Mehta
suspects.personality: Tech-savvy, introverted, socially awkward, highly intelligent
suspects.motive: Wanted to fund his startup idea and pay for his sister's medical treatment
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been coding in the campus hackerspace from 8 PM to 2 AM on the night of the server breach
suspects.secret: He has been selling old exam papers to foreign students online under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the registrar’s server via a backdoor script during a routine network audit

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.role: Associate Professor and International Admissions Coordinator
suspects.motive: Under pressure to increase international enrollment numbers to secure research funding and a promotion
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been attending an online faculty development workshop from home on the night the fake applications were submitted
suspects.secret: She falsified her own research publication count in her last promotion application
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Approved seven international applications without required visa interviews or document verification

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.role: International student from Mauritius, M.Sc. Data Analytics
suspects.motive: Wanted to create a black-market visa brokerage using college credentials
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night cricket match at the hostel grounds with friends
suspects.secret: His own student visa was nearly expired, and he was at risk of deportation
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had unusual access to the college’s document notarization stamp and was seen printing multiple acceptance letters with blank names

suspects.name: Prof. Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: Secretly receiving kickbacks from a foreign education consultancy in Dubai
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a formal dinner with university vice-chancellor and donors on campus
suspects.secret: He has been plagiarizing research from visiting scholars for years
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Blocked an internal audit of international admissions despite repeated warnings from the finance office

evidence.description: Log files showing a script named 'VisaAutoFill.py' ran from the campus network at 1:17 AM on October 12, uploading 14 fake student profiles with identical IP headers
evidence.significance: Indicates automated forgery of applications; the script used student login credentials belonging to Arnav Mehta

evidence.description: A printed list of fake student names, passport numbers, and DIAS application IDs found torn in a hostel room trash can
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan was directly involved in creating fraudulent applications

evidence.description: Email trail between 'admissions@dias-consultants.ae' (a fake UAE-based consultancy) and Prof. Joshi, discussing 'processing fees' per 'placed student'
evidence.location: Recovery from deleted emails in Joshi’s college account via forensic software
evidence.significance: Strong indication of financial motive and external collusion

evidence.description: Security guard statement that Dr. Nair exited her office at 12:45 AM on October 12, 15 minutes after the fake applications were submitted
evidence.location: Campus gate logbook and CCTV metadata
evidence.significance: Contradicts her alibi of being at home during the attack

evidence.description: USB drive hidden in a hollowed-out textbook ('Advanced Cryptography') in Arnav’s bookshelf, containing encrypted files and a keylogger log
evidence.location: Arnav Mehta’s room during dorm inspection
evidence.significance: Contains keystrokes showing login to Dr. Nair’s account and execution of the upload script

evidence.description: Metadata from a submitted fake transcript showing 'Author: p.nair@dias.edu.in' but edited using a proxy IP traced to a café in Dubai
evidence.significance: Proves Dr. Nair’s credentials were used, but from abroad—indicating impersonation

evidence.description: Lab technician statement: Saw Prof. Joshi meet with Rohan Desai in the admin annex at 11:30 PM on October 11, shortly before server breach
evidence.significance: Indicates a possible conspiracy between faculty and student

timeline: October 11, 6:00 PM: Prof. Joshi attends donor dinner on campus (verified by guest list and photos)
October 11, 11:30 PM: Security camera logs show Prof. Joshi and Rohan Desai meeting briefly in admin annex storage room
October 12, 12:03 AM: Dr. Nair logs into the admissions portal from campus Wi-Fi
October 12, 1:17 AM: Automated script uploads 14 fraudulent applications from IP address linked to Arnav Mehta’s dorm
October 12, 12:45 AM: Dr. Nair seen leaving campus by gate guard
October 12, 8:00 AM: Registrar discovers anomalies in new international applications during routine check
October 13, 2:00 PM: College IT begins forensic analysis after reporting to UGC and Ministry of Home Affairs
red_herrings: Arnav Mehta’s script and login credentials used in the breach
The list of fake students found in Rohan’s room
Dr. Nair’s late-night presence on campus contradicting her alibi
Metadata showing her email as author of forged documents

solution.method: Used his authority to obtain Dr. Nair’s login details through a phishing email he sent disguised as an IT security update. He then remotely accessed her account via a Dubai-based proxy and used a script (written by Arnav Mehta but stolen by Rohan and sold to Joshi) to upload fake applications. He coordinated with Rohan Desai to provide real-looking documents and used a fake consultancy front to collect payments from families.
solution.motive: To earn kickbacks from a Dubai consultancy for every fraudulent student 'placed,' with plans to emigrate and retire abroad
solution.proof: Encrypted emails recovered from the USB drive in Arnav’s room (though Arnav was not the conspirator) contained decryption keys that revealed the full transaction history between Joshi and the Dubai consultancy. Combined with the lab technician's testimony and the Dubai IP’s access to Dr. Nair’s account, Joshi’s guilt was confirmed.
solution.how_to_solve: The detective must realize that multiple red herrings point to Arnav, Dr. Nair, and Rohan—but only Prof. Joshi had the authority to block audits, the motive involving external finance, and the opportunity through his late meeting with Rohan. The key is reconciling the Dubai IP with the phishing log: Joshi tricked Dr. Nair into revealing her password. Arnav’s script was stolen—his USB contained logs from when he monitored unauthorized use of his code. The real 'author' metadata was spoofed. Only Joshi had consistent access, motive, and control over the entire admissions pipeline.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Spectrometer
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Technology and Applied Sciences (DITAS), Central Research Laboratory, Basement of the Science Block
case.crime: Theft and illegal sale of a high-value FTIR spectrometer used for environmental chemistry research, replaced with a non-functional dummy unit. The theft was disguised as equipment malfunction.
case.victim: Dr. Meera Patel, Associate Professor of Analytical Chemistry, and the Department of Chemical Sciences which lost critical research funding due to compromised data.

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.personality: Ambitious, socially competitive, financially insecure, intense under pressure
suspects.motive: Desperately needs money to pay for a private job preparation course abroad; his family recently faced financial ruin after a failed business
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library studying for a competitive exam from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM on the night of the theft
suspects.secret: He cheated on a mid-term exam and fears expulsion if discovered
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Actively questioned lab access logs, showed unusual interest in equipment valuation online

suspects.name: Prof. Vinod Rajan
suspects.role: Associate Dean of Research and former mentor of Dr. Patel
suspects.personality: Charismatic, bureaucratic, secretive, appears calm under scrutiny
suspects.motive: Facing internal audit for misappropriation of research grants; needed to cover losses by selling university equipment
suspects.alibi: Says he was attending a virtual conference call with collaborators in Germany from 7:00 PM to 9:30 PM
suspects.secret: He has been running a private consultancy using university resources without approval
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for the lab to report the equipment as 'malfunctioning' instead of stolen, delaying police involvement

suspects.name: Simran Kaur
suspects.role: second-year MSc Chemistry student and lab assistant
suspects.personality: Quiet, observant, anxious, deeply loyal to Dr. Patel
suspects.motive: None apparent; financially stable and academically strong
suspects.alibi: States she was at her off-campus hostel, alone, watching a web series
suspects.secret: She is secretly in a romantic relationship with Arjun, which is against hostel rules
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person seen entering the lab before lockdown and initially gave conflicting statements about her access time

suspects.name: Rajiv Mehta
suspects.role: Senior Lab Technician and equipment custodian
suspects.personality: Meticulous, resentful of academic staff, pragmatic, has a gambling habit
suspects.motive: Owes ₹3 lakhs to an illegal betting syndicate and was threatened with violence
suspects.alibi: Claims he left campus at 5:30 PM to visit his ailing mother in Noida
suspects.secret: He has been siphoning small chemicals for side sales to private labs
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Tampered with the lab's access log timestamps and failed to file a maintenance report for the dummy spectrometer

evidence.description: A non-functional replica of the FTIR spectrometer installed in the lab. Serial number plate is forged with incorrect font style and lacks a holographic security seal.
evidence.significance: Indicates premeditated theft and replacement, not a random break-in. Requires insider knowledge.

evidence.description: Deleted browser history on a lab computer showing searches for 'second-hand FTIR spectrometer buyers India' and 'how to fake equipment malfunction report'. Recovered via forensic tools.
evidence.location: Lab desktop computer, IP logged to Simran Kaur's user profile
evidence.significance: Suggests Simran planned the theft, but timestamp shows activity at 4:15 AM — when she claims to be asleep.

evidence.description: A receipt for a locker rental at the Inter-State Bus Terminal (ISBT) dated two days after the theft, purchased in cash. Found in a trash bin near the science block. Partially burned.
evidence.location: Campus waste bin behind Science Block
evidence.significance: Suggests stolen equipment was stored temporarily off-campus. Matches timeline of equipment resale.

evidence.description: Prof. Rajan’s virtual conference call logs show a 45-minute gap between 8:05 PM and 8:50 PM, during which his video feed froze and audio dropped. No official record of discussion in that interval.
evidence.significance: Breaks his alibi. Suggests he may have left the call to coordinate or execute the theft.

evidence.description: Night security guard reports seeing Rajiv Mehta arguing with an unknown man near the service gate at 6:45 PM on the night of the theft, carrying a large tool crate.
evidence.location: Service gate, west side of campus
evidence.significance: Places Rajiv on campus after claimed departure time. Crate matches spectrometer dimensions.

evidence.description: Anonymous listing on a scientific equipment resale portal (LabBay.in) for a 'refurbished FTIR model 7800', withdrawn 12 hours after posting. IP traced to an internet cafe in Lajpat Nagar.
evidence.significance: Proves attempted sale. IP trace leads to physical location near Rajiv's home.

evidence.description: A university ID card belonging to Arjun Malhotra found in the lab after the theft, though he claims he didn’t visit that day.
evidence.location: Under a lab bench near the spectrometer
evidence.significance: Suggests presence at the crime scene, but could have been dropped earlier.

timeline: June 12, 4:00 PM: Rajiv Mehta clocks out officially but is seen near the service gate at 6:45 PM.
June 12, 5:30 PM: Prof. Rajan joins virtual conference call (verified for first 35 minutes).
June 12, 6:15 PM: Simran Kaur swipes into the lab using her access card. No exit swipe recorded.
June 12, 7:00 PM: Security patrol confirms lights on in the lab.
June 12, 8:05–8:50 PM: Gap in Prof. Rajan's virtual call. No logs of activity.
June 12, 9:00 PM: Lab power briefly cut for 7 minutes due to 'circuit overload' (logged by maintenance).
June 12, 9:15 PM: Final security round passes lab — door locked, no anomalies reported.
June 13, 8:00 AM: Dr. Patel discovers the dummy spectrometer and reports malfunction.
June 13, 10:00 AM: Anonymous LabBay listing posted.
June 13, 10:00 PM: Locker at ISBT rented under fake name (surveillance footage shows man resembling Rajiv).
June 14, 11:00 AM: Listing withdrawn; equipment presumed sold to private buyer.
red_herrings: Simran’s browser history suggests she planned the theft, but it was planted remotely via malware.
Arjun’s ID card in the lab implies presence, but he lost it days earlier and Rajiv found it.
Prof. Rajan’s alibi gap makes him seem guilty, but he was briefly attending to a medical emergency (undiagnosed arrhythmia).

solution.method: Used his custodial access to disable alarms, removed the spectrometer during a scheduled power cut, replaced it with a dummy he built over weeks. Used Arjun’s lost ID to clone a swipe card for alibi confusion. Sold the equipment via dark web middleman after storing it in an ISBT locker.
solution.motive: To repay debts from a cricket betting ring that threatened his family.
solution.proof: Forensic analysis of the dummy spectrometer reveals epoxy residue matching glue used exclusively in the technician’s workshop. Additionally, partial fingerprint on the ISBT receipt matches Rajiv’s left thumb.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is recognizing that only someone with technical and physical access could build and install the dummy. The power cut at 9:00 PM aligns with the only time security systems were offline. Simran’s browser history was accessed remotely — possible only with a login hijack, which Rajiv could do as system maintainer. Prof. Rajan’s alibi gap is medical, not criminal. Arjun’s card was found by Rajiv during cleaning. The ISBT locker rental and equipment listing timeline point to Rajiv. Final proof is the epoxy match and fingerprint, irrefutable under forensic standards.

case.title: The Case of the Silenced Quill
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College, Department of Journalism and Mass Communication
case.crime: Systematic censorship and sabotage of the college newspaper 'The Campus Chronicle' before its annual 'Freedom Edition'
case.victim: The Campus Chronicle newspaper and its editorial independence

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.role: final-year student, Editor-in-Chief of The Campus Chronicle
suspects.motive: Wanted to manufacture a censorship controversy to gain media attention and national awards for the paper
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library researching until 10 PM on the night of the sabotage
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a major article in last year's edition and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Publicly outraged but deleted browser history from the newsroom computer the next day

suspects.name: Dr. Nalini Deshpande
suspects.role: Associate Professor of Journalism, Faculty Advisor
suspects.personality: Authoritative, pragmatic, politically connected, emotionally reserved
suspects.motive: Worried that an exposé in the newspaper would reveal her past ties to a discredited media conglomerate accused of propaganda
suspects.alibi: Says she was at home grading papers; her husband confirms but was asleep at the time
suspects.secret: She falsified her academic credentials during her initial job application
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested deleting the controversial article about campus corruption and abruptly cancelled the newspaper's funding review meeting

suspects.name: Riya Malhotra
suspects.role: second-year student, Tech Head of The Campus Chronicle
suspects.personality: Tech-savvy, anxious, socially awkward, highly principled
suspects.motive: Believes the newspaper was becoming sensationalist and feared backlash that might get students expelled
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her hostel room streaming a coding tutorial
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously running a whistleblower blog criticizing student union corruption
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the newspaper's server admin panel two hours after everyone else left

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.role: student council president and third-year political science student
suspects.motive: The upcoming 'Freedom Edition' included a damaging article about his misuse of student funds for political campaigns
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a late-night council strategy meeting with two friends, both loyal allies
suspects.secret: He is being blackmailed by an off-campus political group for past electoral fraud
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Urged the faculty to 'temporarily suspend' publication and was seen arguing with Aarav the day before the sabotage

evidence.description: Server logs show the article titled 'Power Behind the Union: Follow the Money' was deleted at 10:47 PM on April 12. The IP address traces to a laptop logged in under 'Riya Malhotra'.
evidence.significance: Points to Riya as the person who deleted the article

evidence.description: Burnt fragments of paper found in a basement dumpster. Partial text reads: '...Joshi diverted ₹1.2 lakhs...' and '...Deshpande's role in MT News...'
evidence.location: Basement waste chute, near old printing lab
evidence.significance: Suggests a physical copy of the censored article was destroyed, implicating someone who wanted to erase all traces

evidence.description: A hidden folder on the newsroom computer contains a draft article titled 'Manufacturing Censorship: A Staged Rebellion' authored by Aarav, dated two weeks prior.
evidence.location: Newsroom desktop, recovered via forensic wipe
evidence.significance: Indicates Aarav planned to fake a censorship event

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing Dr. Deshpande near the basement lab at 10:30 PM on April 12, carrying a paper folder.
evidence.significance: Places Dr. Deshpande near the site where burnt remnants were found

evidence.description: USB drive labeled 'Backup – DO NOT ERASE' found taped under the newsroom desk. Contains a full copy of the censored article and encrypted logs of file access.
evidence.significance: Proves the article was preserved and suggests someone anticipated the sabotage

evidence.description: Riya’s login to the server was at 10:45 PM, but forensic analysis shows the delete command originated from a spoofed session using a script that mimics her credentials.
evidence.location: Deep server audit logs (requires admin access)
evidence.significance: Reveals that Riya was framed—someone with advanced technical knowledge and access spoofed her login

evidence.description: A first-year student saw Vikram arguing with Aarav near the admin block at 8:15 PM. Overheard: 'If that article runs, I’ll bury you.'
evidence.significance: Suggests Vikram had motive and threatened Aarav

timeline: April 10, 6:00 PM: The editorial board finalizes the 'Freedom Edition', including exposés on student union finances and historical media corruption.
April 11, 9:30 AM: Vikram Joshi demands an emergency meeting to 'review ethics' of the article on student funds.
April 11, 2:00 PM: Dr. Deshpande cancels the scheduled funding approval meeting for the newspaper.
April 12, 7:00 PM: Entire article database is accessible; final proofing begins.
April 12, 8:15 PM: Vikram and Aarav seen arguing near admin block.
April 12, 9:00 PM: Riya logs into server to update website plugins.
April 12, 10:30 PM: Janitor sees Dr. Deshpande near basement lab.
April 12, 10:47 PM: Server logs show deletion of the censored article via Riya’s credentials.
April 13, 8:00 AM: Aarav discovers the article missing, raises alarm.
April 13, 10:00 AM: Burnt paper fragments discovered in basement dumpster.
April 13, 3:00 PM: USB drive found under newsroom desk.
red_herrings: Riya’s server access and IP trace to the deletion
Dr. Deshpande’s presence in the basement, linking her to the burnt pages
Vikram’s public threats and political motive
Aarav’s hidden draft about staging censorship

solution.method: Used her faculty admin access to spoof Riya’s login with a server-side script, deleted the article at 10:47 PM, then printed a copy to burn in the basement to simulate a panicked cover-up by a student. She timed it after Riya’s routine login to exploit her credentials.
solution.motive: The censored article mentioned 'Deshpande's role in MT News' – a reference to her undisclosed past with a propaganda media group. Exposure would end her career and lead to institutional investigation.
solution.proof: The encrypted logs on the USB drive (which only someone with foresight would create) show a second, invisible deletion command from a privileged admin account at 10:46:58 PM – two seconds before the spoofed user deletion. This timestamp matches no legitimate action by Riya. Only Dr. Deshpande had that level of access.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must recognize that the USB drive was a 'canary trap' – only someone expecting sabotage would make such a hidden backup. Riya, though tech-savvy, wouldn’t leave spoofing logs behind. Aarav’s plan was theatrical, not technical. Vikram lacked IT access. The key is correlating the spoofing script (evidence 6) with the burnt document (evidence 2) – only someone with both administrative access and knowledge of the article’s contents would destroy a physical copy. The janitor’s testimony places her at the scene, and the real proof lies in the two-tiered server logs on the USB, which reveal a dual deletion: first by admin, then by spoofed user to mislead.

case.title: The Case of the Graded Shadows
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi (IIT-D)
case.crime: Systematic manipulation of final exam grades through bribery and backdoor academic favoritism orchestrated by a faculty member in exchange for financial and social benefits.
case.victim: Academic integrity of the department and multiple high-achieving students denied fair evaluation

suspects.name: Dr. Arvind Mehta
suspects.personality: Authoritative, meticulous, politically ambitious, socially calculating
suspects.motive: Wants to secure research grants and higher administrative promotions by showcasing 'exceptional' student outcomes under his mentorship
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a closed-door Academic Senate meeting during the grade tampering window
suspects.secret: He falsified his own publication metrics in a recent promotion review
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suddenly upgraded personal car and made large deposits at a local credit union; also pressured TAs to avoid auditing his grading logs

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wants top rank to secure a Rhodes Scholarship; knows she barely missed top position in previous semesters due to strict grading
suspects.alibi: Says she was studying in the library’s 24-hour zone with recorded Wi-Fi login
suspects.secret: She has been ghostwriting research papers for foreign students for money
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen meeting Dr. Mehta late at night three times before results; her grades improved suspiciously in courses he influenced

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.role: Second-year undergraduate, student council tech officer
suspects.personality: Introverted, brilliant coder, socially awkward, rule-follower
suspects.motive: None directly, but he had full access to the internal academic portal and could have altered grades for revenge — his sister was unfairly failed last year
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been debugging the department website from his dorm
suspects.secret: He suffers from untreated anxiety and had been accessing university counseling records without authorization
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Logged into the grade database from an admin account during the blackout period — though he claims it was for maintenance

suspects.name: Nalini Iyer
suspects.personality: Efficient, observant, underappreciated, quietly resentful of faculty
suspects.motive: Resents professors who exploit students; may have altered records to expose corruption or balance the scales
suspects.alibi: Says she was home with her daughter who had fever; no verifiable proof
suspects.secret: She has been leaking internal memos to a journalist about faculty misconduct
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Printed multiple blank grade change forms the week before the incident; seen shredding documents after hours

evidence.description: Access logs showing admin-level login to the academic database at 02:14 AM on May 17, originating from the department server room. IP traced to a terminal manually powered on remotely.
evidence.significance: Grade changes occurred at 02:10–02:25 AM; this login matches the timeframe. Terminal had no camera coverage.

evidence.description: Torn corner of a blank grade change form found in Dr. Mehta’s trash can. Matches a batch issued to Nalini Iyer.
evidence.significance: Suggests Mehta may have used unauthorized forms to push through alterations.

evidence.description: Encrypted email draft on Priya Malhotra’s laptop addressed to Dr. Mehta with subject 'Final Arrangement'. Never sent.
evidence.location: Priya's cloud storage, recovered via digital forensics
evidence.significance: Implies a financial transaction: 'As discussed, the amount will be transferred upon confirmation of grade update.'

evidence.description: A handwritten ledger seized from Nalini Iyer’s desk drawer listing student names, amounts (₹20,000–₹50,000), and codes like 'CS401-F' and 'CS405-P'.
evidence.significance: Appears to be a bribery record. However, codes later identified as 'F' = Failed, 'P' = Passed — part of her unofficial tracking of grading bias.

evidence.description: A Python script on Rohan Deshpande’s personal GitHub marked private, titled 'auto_grader_update.py'. Uses real API keys from the university portal.
evidence.location: GitHub repository, accessed via forensic subpoena
evidence.significance: Capable of mass grade updates. Modified on May 16 — the day before the breach.

evidence.description: Night security guard reports seeing someone in a department hoodie entering the server room at 1:50 AM. Describes medium build, wearing glasses.
evidence.significance: Corroborates unauthorized physical access. Hoodie common among students and staff.

evidence.description: Hidden backup log in the database system showing a grade override for 17 students, authorized under proxy authentication using Dr. Mehta’s credentials — but routed through a virtual private server in Singapore.
evidence.significance: Proves credentials were stolen and used remotely. Digital fingerprint matches login pattern from Priya's laptop when she accessed the portal from a café in Goa during spring break.

timeline: May 15, 6:00 PM: Final exams conclude; answer sheets submitted.
May 16, 9:00 AM: Preliminary grades uploaded by faculty; inconsistencies noted by TA.
May 16, 6:30 PM: Dr. Mehta holds meeting with selected students, including Priya Malhotra.
May 16, 10:00 PM: Rohan Deshpande logs into university server for 'website update' — verified by timestamp.
May 17, 1:50 AM: Security guard sees figure in hoodie enter server room.
May 17, 2:10–2:25 AM: Unauthorized grade modifications made via admin terminal.
May 17, 8:45 AM: Official results released; uproar begins when top ranks shift unexpectedly.
May 17, 10:00 AM: Internal audit initiated by Dean after student complaints.
red_herrings: The torn grade form in Dr. Mehta’s trash implies direct involvement.
Priya’s unsent email draft suggests an active bribery deal.
Rohan’s GitHub script makes him appear technically capable and potentially vengeful.
Nalini’s ledger falsely appears to document bribe payments.
Dr. Mehta’s sudden wealth suggests personal gain from corruption.

solution.method: Stole Dr. Mehta’s authentication token during a guided portal session by installing a keylogger on his department-issued tablet. Used it to remotely access the admin terminal via a virtual machine routed through Singapore to mask location. Physically sent a colleague (a friend in Facilities) to turn on the server room terminal remotely via IoT smart plug she had installed weeks earlier.
solution.motive: Desperate to secure first-rank for international scholarship; believed she was being held back by Mehta’s bias toward research students over academics.
solution.proof: Digital fingerprint from Singapore VPS matches login artifacts on Priya’s personal laptop; IoT smart plug registered to a fake name but purchased with a college discount using her ID; Facilities worker confesses under interrogation.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Rule out Rohan: His GitHub script never executed; logs show no API calls from his IP. 2. Dismiss Nalini’s ledger: Cross-check with official grades — codes match her personal ethics project on bias. 3. Discredit Mehta: Senate meeting confirmed by 5 witnesses; financial deposits linked to inheritance. 4. Focus on digital trace from Singapore — only student with international travel (Goa) and technical skill to use token hijacking. 5. Corroborate with security: Hoodie wearer was Facilities worker; alibi fails when phone GPS shows proximity to server room. 6. Keylogger malware found in tablet recovery logs, last accessed by Priya.

case.title: The Case of the Rigged Placements
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, Jai Bharat Institute of Technology, Bengaluru
case.crime: Systematic corruption in the campus placement cell that favored certain students in exchange for money, undermining fair recruitment processes
case.victim: The integrity of the placement process; several meritorious students lost job opportunities

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.motive: Desperate to secure a high-paying job despite poor academic performance; family under financial pressure
suspects.alibi: Claims to be attending a hackathon in Mysuru during the crucial week of placement data tampering
suspects.secret: Has an undeclared sibling with a congenital illness requiring expensive treatment
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suddenly placed in a top-tier company despite being near-bottom of class; was seen accessing the placement server room late at night the week before results

suspects.name: Dr. Shalini Iyer
suspects.personality: Strict, efficient, authoritative, secretive about her personal life
suspects.motive: Facing foreclosure on her home; recent large bank deposits unexplained
suspects.alibi: Claims to be on medical leave due to severe migraines during the alleged data manipulation period
suspects.secret: Her brother is involved in illegal real estate dealings; she’s been laundering small amounts through college events
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Has administrative access to placement records and bypassed audit logs during the incident window

suspects.name: Karan Patel
suspects.motive: Resents the placement bias toward rich students; believes meritocracy is dead
suspects.alibi: Says he was home with his parents in Vadodara during the critical week
suspects.secret: He runs an anonymous college blog criticizing college administration anonymously
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was caught by a lab monitor downloading a network spoofing tool weeks before placement week; IP logs tie an unauthorized access to his dorm router

suspects.name: Prof. Ramesh Nair
suspects.motive: Has a side consulting business and funneled underperforming students to companies in exchange for kickbacks
suspects.alibi: Attended a national education summit in Delhi during the placement week
suspects.secret: Uses college research funds to pay for his son’s overseas education illegally
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Several students he privately coached mysteriously had their placement profiles upgraded without documentation

evidence.description: Log files from the placement server show an admin login at 2:17 AM on May 12 using Dr. Iyer’s credentials, modifying shortlisted candidates for three companies. The session lasted 43 minutes and bypassed two-factor authentication via a backdoor script.
evidence.significance: Proves administrative access was abused during off-hours

evidence.description: A handwritten note found in Aarav Mehta’s desk with company names, candidate IDs, and amounts like '₹1.2L' and 'Confirmed with S.I.'
evidence.location: Inside a torn notebook in Aarav’s hostel room
evidence.significance: Suggests Aarav was involved in a bribery scheme with someone named S.I. (possibly Dr. Shalini Iyer)

evidence.description: IP address 192.168.3.42 accessed the placement portal's candidate database on May 11 at 11:03 PM. The IP is registered to Karan Patel’s room router.
evidence.location: Network traffic logs from college IT
evidence.significance: Links Karan to unauthorized access

evidence.description: Email from Prof. Nair to a placement coordinator: 'Make sure Tanvi and Arjun are 'discovered' by Zentex. Friends of the family.' Sent May 8.
evidence.location: Deleted but recovered from backup email server
evidence.significance: Shows Nair influencing placements for personal reasons

evidence.description: A USB drive found in the server room trash can contains a script that disables log tracking for specific admin accounts and modifies candidate rankings based on external inputs.
evidence.location: Wastebasket in the placement server room
evidence.significance: Proof of malicious software used to alter records without detection

evidence.description: A third-year student claims to have seen Aarav Mehta arguing with Dr. Iyer near the server room on May 11 night. Says Dr. Iyer said, 'You’ll get what you paid for, but don’t push me.'
evidence.location: Hostel corridor adjacent to admin block
evidence.significance: Suggests direct involvement between Aarav and Dr. Iyer in a corrupt exchange
