evidence.description: Bank records show Dr. Iyer deposited ₹4.5 lakhs in cash across multiple branches in April–May, with no documented source. Her salary is ₹1.2L/month.
evidence.significance: Financial motive linked to Dr. Iyer

timeline: May 8: Prof. Nair emails placement coordinator to 'discover' two students for Zentex.
May 10: Dr. Iyer submits official leave application citing migraines.
May 11, 9:45 PM: Karan Patel’s IP accesses placement database (unauthorized).
May 11, 11:30 PM: Aarav Mehta seen near server room arguing with Dr. Iyer (witness account).
May 12, 2:17 AM: Admin login using Dr. Iyer’s credentials alters 14 student records.
May 12, 10:00 AM: Dr. Iyer calls in from her home, reports 'technical issues' with the portal.
May 13: Placement results announced; anomalies noticed by students.
May 15: Anonymous tip sent to dean about placement tampering.
May 16: Server room USB drive discovered by IT staff during audit.
red_herrings: Aarav’s notebook with monetary figures suggests he paid for placement; in reality, it was his personal ledger tracking medical fund donations.
Karan’s IP address was spoofed; his router was hacked using a known vulnerability.
The argument witnessed between Aarav and Dr. Iyer was about Aarav demanding transparency, not a payoff.
Prof. Nair’s email shows unethical conduct but is unrelated to the actual data breach.

solution.method: Used her admin access to install a backdoor script (found on USB) that disabled logging and allowed her to alter candidate rankings. She accessed the server remotely using a virtual private network (VPN) from her home but spoofed the location to appear as if she were on campus. She laundered bribes through cash deposits over weeks.
solution.motive: Facing home foreclosure, she created a corrupt system where students or their families paid her ₹1–2.5 lakhs to be pushed into shortlists. She targeted desperate but wealthy students, altering rankings while covering her tracks.
solution.proof: The backdoor script on the USB drive uses a unique coding signature matching personal scripts Dr. Iyer wrote in a past training workshop (confirmed by forensic analysis). Additionally, a hidden log fragment recovered shows the actual attack originated from her home IP, not the college network.
solution.how_to_solve: The investigator must: 1) Dismiss the IP evidence against Karan by noting the absence of keystroke logs from his device; 2) Realize Aarav’s notebook doesn’t match actual bribe amounts; 3) See that Prof. Nair’s actions were unethical but not technical; 4) Notice that Dr. Iyer’s 'medical leave' coincides exactly with the attack window; 5) Correlate the script’s coding style with her digital footprint; 6) Cross-check the bank deposits with placement anomalies—14 altered records, 14 cash deposits, same intervals. The clincher is the forensic match of code syntax and variable naming ('temp_flush_arr' and 'bypass_2fa_magic') used only by Dr. Iyer in prior public projects.

case.title: The Case of the Silent Watchman
case.setting: Delhi Metropolitan College – Electrical Engineering Department building and surrounding campus area
case.crime: Systematic misuse of campus security access logs and unauthorized entry into restricted faculty offices, accompanied by digital sabotage and theft of internal examination data
case.victim: The institution's academic integrity and examination board; specifically, the head examiner's office was compromised, leading to a delayed semester-end evaluation and investigation into exam leaks

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.personality: intense, highly competitive, socially isolated, perfectionist
suspects.motive: Believes he was unfairly denied a scholarship due to biased faculty; wants to discredit the examination system
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been studying in the library computer lab between 10:00 PM and 1:00 AM on the night of the breach
suspects.secret: He has been accessing restricted college forums using a hacked faculty login for months to monitor administrative decisions about him
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the head examiner two days before the incident and was caught near the server room the previous week by security

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Wants to expose corruption in the examination process; believes the current faculty is manipulating grades for political donors' children
suspects.alibi: Says she was at home, working remotely; her smart home logs show activity on her work laptop
suspects.secret: She’s been anonymously publishing articles on an education reform blog that criticizes the college dean
suspects.suspicious_behavior: She requested enhanced access permissions for the server room two weeks prior, citing 'research on digital security'.

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.personality: authoritarian, loyal to administration, gruff, protective of his reputation
suspects.motive: Wants to cover up his negligence and falsified patrol logs; may have allowed unauthorized access to someone in exchange for favors
suspects.alibi: Claims to have completed his rounds between 9:00 PM and 1:30 AM, as per log entries he personally filed
suspects.secret: He has been sleeping during late-night shifts for months and falsifying patrol records
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His security logs show entries at precise 30-minute intervals, even during power fluctuations when electronic logging should have failed

suspects.name: Aarav Patel
suspects.motive: Believes there's a cover-up involving faculty and wants to uncover it for his campus magazine; might have gone too far
suspects.alibi: Says he was interviewing a professor for a story until 9:30 PM, then went home
suspects.secret: He snuck into the admin wing two weeks ago to photograph suspicious financial documents but was never caught
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was spotted by a cleaner near the faculty elevator at 10:45 PM on the night of the breach—contradicting his alibi

evidence.description: Server access log showing login from a faculty account at 11:17 PM on May 12. IP traced to a first-floor network port near the electrical room.
evidence.significance: Proves unauthorized access during night hours; timestamp overlaps with security patrol window

evidence.description: A rusted keychain with the initials 'V.S.' and a broken flashlight found behind a ventilation unit near the server closet.
evidence.location: Behind HVAC unit on first floor, west wing
evidence.significance: Links to Vikram Singh; suggests possible presence or negligence

evidence.description: Saved draft email on Aarav Patel’s cloud account titled 'Proof of Corruption' containing screenshots of financial records from the admin database.
evidence.location: Google Drive backup accessed via forensic recovery
evidence.significance: Suggests motive and capability to breach systems

evidence.description: Fingerprint on the server room door lock identified as belonging to Rohan Malhotra.
evidence.significance: Direct physical link to a suspect at the crime scene

evidence.description: Anomalous biometric swipe record from the head examiner’s office: the security system registered Vikram Singh’s ID badge at 11:48 PM, but facial recognition failed due to 'low light'.
evidence.significance: Suggests either Vikram was present or his badge was used

evidence.description: Night canteen worker claims to have seen Aarav Patel leaving the admin building at 10:50 PM on May 12.
evidence.significance: Contradicts Aarav’s alibi

evidence.description: Timestamped CCTV footage from the east stairwell showing a figure in a security uniform at 11:30 PM bypassing the server floor using a keycard. Face obscured, but gait analysis later suggests shorter stature than Vikram.
evidence.significance: Proves someone impersonated a guard; timing matches server breach

timeline: May 12, 8:45 PM – Aarav Patel leaves the professor’s office after an interview.
May 12, 9:30 PM – Rohan Malhotra logs into library computer; digital activity recorded.
May 12, 9:45 PM – Vikram Singh begins night shift; signs in at main gate kiosk.
May 12, 10:45 PM – Cleaner reports seeing someone resembling Aarav near faculty elevator.
May 12, 10:50 PM – Canteen worker sees Aarav exiting admin building.
May 12, 11:17 PM – Faculty account logs into server via port near electrical room.
May 12, 11:30 PM – CCTV shows security-uniformed figure accessing server floor.
May 12, 11:48 PM – Vikram Singh’s ID badge used to enter head examiner’s office.
May 12, 1:15 AM – Vikram files digital patrol report claiming full rounds completed.
May 13, 7:00 AM – Faculty discovers tampered files and missing exam drafts.
red_herrings: Rohan’s fingerprints on the server door – he accessed it legally two days prior for a tech project.
Aarav’s draft article and past break-in – suggests he was involved, but unrelated to this breach.
Vikram’s faulty patrol logs – appear suspicious but mask his negligence, not his guilt.
The keychain and flashlight – planted to mislead investigators toward Vikram.

solution.method: Used her approved access request to obtain a duplicate keycard. Hacked into the security system using a zero-day exploit to disable facial recognition and cloned Vikram’s badge ID for the access logs. Entered the server room disguised in a borrowed security uniform at 11:30 PM, then used a faculty login (obtained earlier) to access exam data and plant false evidence implicating others.
solution.motive: She discovered that the dean had manipulated exam results to benefit a politician’s son and planned to leak the data to the press. To protect her identity, she staged it as a student-driven breach to draw suspicion away from faculty.
solution.proof: The CCTV gait analysis did not match Vikram but matched Priya’s height and walk when compared to archived footage. Additionally, a hidden Wi-Fi packet logger placed near the server port captured a device MAC address linked to Priya’s personal router. The server access used a keystroke pattern identical to her registered lab computer.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Cross-reference the CCTV figure’s height and gait with known individuals. 2. Analyze the biometric failure event—why facial recognition failed only when Vikram’s badge was used. 3. Trace the MAC address from the packet capture to Priya’s home network. 4. Realize that only someone with faculty-level access and technical knowledge could bypass both physical and digital safeguards. 5. Confirm that the keystroke dynamics from the server login match Priya’s typing rhythm, stored in university research databases. The evidence converges on her despite her airtight alibi, which was falsified using pre-recorded laptop activity.

case.title: The Case of the Triple Heist at Kala Samudra College
case.setting: Kala Samudra College of Arts and Applied Sciences, Chennai
case.crime: Three interconnected thefts: (1) The stolen final-year sculpture 'Agni Rekha' from the Art Department's secured gallery, (2) The theft of sensitive research data on traditional Tamil herbal medicine from a password-protected server in the Biotechnology lab, and (3) The disappearance of the original manuscript of a late professor's unpublished novel from the college archives.
case.victim: The college community, including faculty, students, and the legacy of the late Professor Arunachalam

suspects.name: Meera Iyengar
suspects.motive: Her father, a renowned sculptor, had a bitter rivalry with the deceased professor whose work inspired the stolen sculpture.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been alone in her studio working on her final project from 9:00 PM to 1:00 AM.
suspects.secret: She is secretly in love with Professor Thakur and has been leaving anonymous love notes in his mailbox.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with the gallery curator the day before the theft, demanding access to the sculpture after hours.

suspects.name: Rahul Varma
suspects.motive: His family owns a pharmaceutical startup that could profit from the herbal research data.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at an off-campus pub with friends until midnight and then went straight to his dorm.
suspects.secret: He hacked into the college grading system two months ago to change a failing mark.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Used a college network proxy at 2:17 AM on the night of the theft to access a dark web forum.

suspects.name: Dr. Nalini Thakur
suspects.personality: Elegant, authoritative, secretive, fiercely protective of academic legacy
suspects.motive: She was the last known person to see Professor Arunachalam alive and is rumored to have co-authored the unpublished novel, which could threaten her reputation if released.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been grading papers at home and was logged into the college LMS from 7:00 PM to 10:30 PM.
suspects.secret: She forged the authentication of a grant application using the dean's digital signature last semester.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Requested unusual access logs to the archives system two days after the theft, claiming 'review for security'.

suspects.name: Karthik Balaji
suspects.motive: His mother was wrongfully dismissed by Professor Arunachalam years ago and died shortly after, leaving a grudge.
suspects.alibi: States he was monitoring the server room from 8:00 PM onward and slept on the cot there.
suspects.secret: He has been quietly digitizing and selling rare college manuscripts on the black market for years to support his sick sister.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was found deleting cache files from the archive's access terminal the morning after the theft.

evidence.description: A single drop of blue clay, specific to the Art Department's premium modeling clay, found under the Biotechnology server rack.
evidence.location: Biotech Lab B3, near server Rack 2
evidence.significance: Suggests someone involved in the art theft also accessed the server room, or that items were moved between buildings.

evidence.description: A corrupted data fragment recovered from the Biotech server showing a partial upload to an external IP hosted in Malaysia, timestamped 1:43 AM. File name: 'Project_Agni.zip'.
evidence.significance: Links the art theft ('Agni') with the data theft; suggests the thief bundled both items digitally.

evidence.description: A torn piece of a college ID badge with 'Nalin...' visible, found near the archive's ventilation shaft.
evidence.location: Basement corridor adjacent to the archives
evidence.significance: Points directly to Dr. Thakur, but could be planted.

evidence.description: A night watchman reports seeing Meera Iyengar exiting the arts building at 10:30 PM, but notes she was carrying a large cloth bundle.
evidence.significance: Places Meera near the scene with possible stolen goods.

evidence.description: Security camera footage (time-lapsed) shows Karthik Balaji accessing the archive’s master control terminal at 12:08 AM, though no file access is logged.
evidence.significance: Suggests he was present during the theft but did nothing—or manipulated the system.

evidence.description: A USB drive hidden in a hollowed-out textbook in Rahul’s dorm, containing encrypted files and a network decryption tool.
evidence.location: Under 'Molecular Genetics' textbook in Rahul’s room
evidence.significance: Indicates capability and intent, but no direct link to the stolen data.

evidence.description: A faint thermal imprint on the archive’s manuscript safe interior, shaped like a smartphone with a cracked screen, matching Karthik’s known device.
evidence.location: Inside the safe, detected via forensic thermography
evidence.significance: Proves someone placed a phone inside the safe—likely to record combination or bypass lock via thermal exploit.

timeline: 6:45 PM: Meera Iyengar enters the Arts Building; seen by security.
7:00 PM: Dr. Thakur logs into college LMS from home; IP confirmed.
8:00 PM: Karthik Balaji clocks in for night shift; signs server room log.
9:00 PM: Meera claims to be working in Studio 4; no witnesses.
9:30 PM: Rahul Varma and friends leave for pub; confirmed by CCTV and receipts.
10:30 PM: Watchman sees Meera leaving Arts Building with bundle; she waves and says 'finished casting'.
11:15 PM: Biotech lab motion sensor triggered briefly; dismissed as a glitch.
12:08 AM: Karthik accesses archive terminal for 'system check'; no file retrieval logged.
1:43 AM: Data exfiltration from Biotech server to Malaysian IP.
2:17 AM: Rahul’s device uses college proxy to access dark web forum.
6:00 AM: Archivist discovers manuscript missing. Gallery curator reports sculpture gone. Biotech professor notices server anomaly.
red_herrings: Meera’s argument with the curator and her father's rivalry makes her a prime suspect.
The torn ID badge with 'Nalin...' appears to implicate Dr. Thakur.
Rahul’s hacking history and USB drive suggest he stole the research data.
Meera’s midnight exit with a bundle seems to confirm the art theft.

solution.method: Used his access to stage a multi-phase theft: (1) He 3D-printed a dummy sculpture days prior and swapped it with the original during a 'system calibration' visit. (2) Used a thermal-recording phone placed in the archive safe during a prior maintenance check to capture the heat imprint of the combination dial and later reproduce the code. (3) Accessed the Biotech server via a backdoor he installed months earlier, exfiltrating data during the archive theft to create a diversion.
solution.motive: Revenge for his mother's dismissal by Professor Arunachalam, and a desire to erase the professor’s legacy by destroying the unpublished novel and discrediting his academic work.
solution.proof: The thermal phone imprint in the safe matches Karthik’s device. The blue clay on the server rack came from the dummy sculpture’s base, which he stored briefly in the server room to avoid detection. The 'system check' at 12:08 AM was used to disable archive alarms temporarily.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is connecting the blue clay in the server room with Karthik's access log and the thermal phone evidence. The Malaysian data upload was a smokescreen—he never sent the full file. Meera’s bundle was a legitimate casting; the watchman misidentified it. The ID badge was planted by Karthik to frame Dr. Thakur. Only someone with continuous access, like Karthik, could coordinate all three thefts without appearing on any building's main access log at the critical time. The timeline proves Meera left before the Biotech breach, Rahul was off-campus, and Dr. Thakur was logged in remotely. Only Karthik was physically present and had the technical means.

crime_type: coded messages left at crime scenes

case.title: The Case of the Ciphered Chaprasi
case.setting: St. Aravind's College of Arts and Technology, Delhi – Department of Computer Science building, specifically the server room and adjacent library
case.crime: A series of threatening coded messages appear overnight in locked academic spaces, culminating in the sabotage of the college's internal exam server system. No physical violence, but psychological tension and academic sabotage.
case.victim: The integrity of the final examination system and the reputation of the Computer Science department; Professor Ila Menon, Head of Department, is directly targeted in the final message.

suspects.name: Kabir Malhotra
suspects.personality: brilliant but arrogant, socially isolated, competitive, perfectionist
suspects.motive: Failed a critical project under Professor Menon; believes she unfairly sabotaged his academic future
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been coding alone in his dorm room, supported by late-night GitHub commits
suspects.secret: He has been selling exam answer keys illegally through a dark web proxy
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Overly defensive when questioned about server access, argues he wouldn’t risk coding near the server

suspects.name: Tanvi Reddy
suspects.personality: quiet, observant, highly intuitive, emotionally guarded, deeply ethical
suspects.motive: Her sister was expelled last year over cheating allegations tied to Professor Menon’s disciplinary committee
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a late-night study group in the library; two friends partially confirm but admit she left for 30 minutes
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing cybersecurity articles under a male pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing an admin terminal 15 minutes after the second message appeared, claiming she 'saw a glitch'

suspects.name: Professor Rajiv Nair
suspects.personality: charming, eccentric, theatrical, deeply intellectual, flirtatious with students
suspects.motive: Passed over for Department Head in favor of Professor Menon; resents her leadership
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a faculty dinner until 9 PM, then grading at home; wife confirms but admits he left for 'smoke break'
suspects.secret: He has been plagiarizing research from international journals
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Wrote a blog post about 'the beauty of unsolvable ciphers' the day after the first message

suspects.name: Anu Patel
suspects.personality: meticulous, no-nonsense, loyal to institution, socially awkward, highly discreet
suspects.motive: Professor Menon initiated a review of her performance after a minor network outage she blamed on 'unauthorized access'
suspects.alibi: Security logs show her ID badge accessed server room at 2:15 AM, but she claims it was a remote login from home for routine check
suspects.secret: She is secretly developing an AI-based network monitor and fears exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her badge was used in the server room during the window of tampering; she cannot prove it wasn’t her

evidence.description: A handwritten cipher written in red ink on a sticky note stuck to the server room door: 'Qebob fp x cxfirob, xka f fp pefmmva'. Found at 7:00 AM. Pencil smudges suggest it was written in haste.
evidence.location: Server room door (inside the locked room, visible through glass)
evidence.significance: Simple Caesar cipher (shift +23) decodes to: 'There is a failure, and i am shipped'. Grammatical oddity suggests non-native speaker or deliberate misdirection. 'Shipped' likely refers to academic expulsion or exile.

evidence.description: A timestamped log entry showing a login to the admin server at 1:48 AM from Anu Patel’s credentials. The session accessed the exam scheduler and modified lockdown protocols.
evidence.significance: Suggests insider access. Anu insists the login was spoofed via stolen session token.

evidence.description: A crumpled piece of paper in the library trash bin with scribbled numbers: '16,9,20,8,15,14 → 17,10,21,9,16,15'. Arrows drawn in blue pen.
evidence.significance: Shift +1 cipher on alphabet positions. Letters spell 'PYTHON → QZUIPO'. But 'Python' refers to the programming language, not a person. Clue is part of a larger cipher key.

evidence.description: A hidden text file named 'exam_bkup.log' found in a cache folder: contains Base64-encoded text. Decoding reveals a message: 'Menon must fall. The past resets at midnight.'
evidence.location: Recovered from temporary files on library computer #7
evidence.significance: Points to direct threat. Metadata shows it was created at 2:03 AM by a guest account. Connected to Tanvi's study group.

evidence.description: A torn corner of a sticky label with part of a barcode and 'SRV-23' visible. Found near ventilation grate under library staircase.
evidence.significance: Matches inventory tags used on server room hardware. Suggests physical transfer or concealment of equipment. Only staff or authorized students would have access.

evidence.description: A deleted email draft found in Professor Nair’s trash (recovered from college server backup): 'The Vigenère is perfect—no one remembers the key is KABIR. Too easy.' Sent 2 days before first message.
evidence.significance: Suggests he knows about the ciphers and possibly framed Kabir. But why would he leave such a clue?

evidence.description: Library security guard reports seeing a student in a hoodie enter the restricted archive room at 1:55 AM. Height matches Tanvi. No badge scan recorded, but side door was propped with a book.
evidence.significance: Contradicts Tanvi’s alibi. Archive room houses old department records, including disciplinary files.

timeline: 6:30 PM – Faculty dinner attended by Professor Nair and others
7:45 PM – Kabir uploads final project revision to GitHub (timestamped)
8:20 PM – Tanvi joins study group in library
8:50 PM – Tanvi steps out 'for tea'; unaccounted for until 9:20 PM
1:48 AM – Anu Patel’s credentials used to access server admin panel
1:55 AM – Security guard sees hooded figure enter archive room
2:03 AM – Mysterious file created on library computer #7
2:15 AM – Server room door badge swipe logged under Anu Patel’s ID
2:30 AM – Motion sensor in server room triggers briefly
7:00 AM – First cipher discovered on server room door
9:15 AM – Exam system lockdown detected; Professor Menon receives final message via internal mail: 'You were the first. The cycle ends.'
red_herrings: The Caesar cipher pointing to 'failure' and 'shipped' suggests student retaliation.
Anu Patel’s credentials being used implies her involvement.
Professor Nair’s email draft appears to frame Kabir intentionally.
The Base64 message on the library computer links to Tanvi’s presence.

solution.method: Used a combination of social engineering and hardware tampering. She cloned Anu Patel’s RFID badge using a portable skimmer during a routine helpdesk visit. Used it to access server room at 2:15 AM. Planted a Raspberry Pi into the server rack (hidden behind SRV-23 unit) to send commands via encrypted Wi-Fi. Used the library computer to remotely trigger messages and system changes. The cipher messages used a Vigenère cipher with key 'PYTHON', derived from the programming language she believed Professor Menon undervalued. She accessed the archive room to retrieve her sister’s old file as emotional justification.
solution.motive: To expose Professor Menon’s bias in disciplinary actions and force a review of past expulsions, especially her sister’s. She believed the only way to make the college listen was through an unignorable digital provocation.
solution.proof: The torn label 'SRV-23' matches the only unit with dust disturbance. The Raspberry Pi is found hidden behind it, still transmitting. Its Wi-Fi MAC address matches a logged connection from library computer #7 at 2:03 AM. Tanvi’s laptop contains a script that generates the exact ciphers using key 'PYTHON'. Her browser history shows searches for 'Vigenère cipher Python implementation' and 'RFID cloning techniques'.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Decode the number sequence (PYTHON → +1) to realize 'PYTHON' is a cipher key. 2. Apply Vigenère cipher with key 'PYTHON' to the first message: 'Qebob fp x cxfirob...' becomes 'Server is compromised, and I am sorry' — emotional and personal. 3. The real server log shows Anu’s login was remote, but the badge swipe at 2:15 AM is physical. Only someone with a clone could do that. 4. The hooded figure entering the archive ties Tanvi to unauthorized access. 5. Her secret publication record proves her advanced knowledge of encryption. 6. The Raspberry Pi with Python-based payload confirms method and key. 7. Her sister’s file in her bag seals motive.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Countdown
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay – Main Lab, 3rd Floor, Nirali Building
case.crime: A complex, time-sensitive bomb threat is discovered during the annual TechFusion hackathon, triggering campus lockdown. The bomb is later revealed to be a sophisticated, non-functional replica, but its design and placement caused mass panic and nearly disrupted emergency response logistics.
case.victim: Campus security and student morale; near-miss with evacuation injuries due to stampede

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.personality: Brilliant, socially aloof, perfectionist, emotionally detached
suspects.motive: Frustrated with institutional neglect of cybersecurity flaws he reported months prior
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been coding in the library basement server room from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM
suspects.secret: Secretly developed an AI-based facial recognition exploit using campus CCTV
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with security two days prior about access permissions

suspects.name: Professor Kavita Reddy
suspects.personality: Authoritative, meticulous, publicly supportive of students, privately insecure about relevance
suspects.motive: Wanted to demonstrate the necessity of increased funding for her department by staging a believable cyber-physical threat
suspects.alibi: Attended a virtual conference call with IISc from 6:30 PM to 8:45 PM
suspects.secret: Submitted a research grant proposal that depends on proving campus vulnerability
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Suggested the bomb squad use a protocol only her lab had recently developed

suspects.name: Zara Khan
suspects.role: second-year robotics enthusiast and hackathon participant
suspects.personality: Innovative, impulsive, activist-minded, confrontational toward authority
suspects.motive: Protesting the college’s sponsorship by a defense contractor involved in surveillance tech
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the women’s restroom from 7:10 PM to 7:25 PM, then back at her team’s station
suspects.secret: Built a drone capable of indoor navigation and object delivery
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her hackathon project involved remote-controlled mechanical arms resembling bomb-disposal tools

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.role: college security systems intern and part-time janitor
suspects.personality: Charming, observant, financially struggling, deeply loyal to campus staff
suspects.motive: Wanted to expose gaps in security to secure a full-time job post-graduation
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been restocking cleaning supplies in the east wing from 6:45 PM to 7:40 PM
suspects.secret: Has been selling access logs to a local tech blogger for side income
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to report the 'bomb' but gave inconsistent details in initial statements

evidence.description: A 3D-printed device with blinking LEDs, labeled wires, and a digital countdown timer set to 00:07:12 when found. Contains no explosives. Includes a fake pressure plate and dummy capacitor array.
evidence.location: Underneath the central server rack in the CS main lab
evidence.significance: Designed to mimic a military-grade IED but lacks actual detonators or power source for one. Timer uses a Raspberry Pi with custom code.

evidence.description: Log file extract from lab door access system showing a swipe by 'K. Reddy' at 6:58 PM. However, timestamp overlaps with her verified video call.
evidence.significance: Suggests Professor Reddy entered the lab during her alibi window, but the badge system was spoofed using cloned RFID data from earlier in the week.

evidence.description: A micro-SD card hidden inside a fake power adapter near the 'bomb', containing encrypted files and a corrupted audio clip of someone humming the college anthem.
evidence.location: Inside power strip near server rack
evidence.significance: Encryption key derived from Zara’s public GitHub repository. Files reveal blueprints of a drone payload system, but no bomb schematics.

evidence.description: A timestamped Python script found on a public Git mirror, titled 'CountdownSimulator_v2.py', authored under a pseudonym 'NullByte_99'. Simulates realistic bomb UI and sound effects.
evidence.significance: Code matches the interface on the fake timer. Author’s coding style matches Aarav’s prior projects.

evidence.description: A first-year student reports seeing someone in a janitor’s uniform placing a black backpack near the lab’s service entrance at 6:50 PM, but couldn't identify the face.
evidence.significance: Matches Rohan’s work route, but the 'janitor' was wearing a uniform too large—suggesting disguise.

evidence.description: A crumpled sticky note in the men’s restroom wastebasket with scribbled resistor color codes: 'Brown-Black-Red-Gold'.
evidence.significance: Translates to 1kΩ resistor—used in basic timer circuits. Handwriting matches Aarav’s, but he frequents that restroom.

evidence.description: Thermal camera data from lab HVAC system shows a brief heat spike near the server rack at 7:02 PM, inconsistent with normal equipment output.
evidence.significance: Indicates recent placement of a powered device. Corroborates bomb placement between 6:55 PM and 7:05 PM.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Hackathon officially begins. Lab access logs show normal student entries.
6:30 PM: Professor Reddy joins virtual conference (verified by IISc logs).
6:45 PM: Rohan logs into east wing supply room (security cam footage).
6:50 PM: Janitor-like figure seen with backpack near service entrance (witness).
6:58 PM: Fake badge swipe under Professor Reddy’s name at CS lab door (spoofed RFID).
7:02 PM: Thermal anomaly detected at server rack location.
7:05 PM: Zara enters restroom (cam at corridor end).
7:10 PM: Zara exits restroom, returns to hackathon station.
7:12 PM: Aarav pings campus Wi-Fi from library basement (verified).
7:15 PM: 'Bomb' discovered by Rohan, who alerts security.
7:17 PM: Campus lockdown initiated. Bomb squad en route.
7:45 PM: Device confirmed as non-functional replica. Crisis defused.
red_herrings: Professor Reddy’s spoofed badge entry
Zara’s drone payload blueprints on the SD card
Aarav’s resistor note and coding style match
Rohan’s inconsistent initial statement about how he found the device

solution.method: Used her autonomous drone to deliver the fake bomb during a gap in CCTV coverage. The drone flew from the service roof access, through an open vent, and deposited the device under the rack at 7:02 PM. She spoofed Reddy’s badge using an RFID cloner she built for her project, timed to 6:58 PM to mislead logs. The countdown was powered by her Raspberry Pi script.
solution.motive: To expose the administration’s prioritization of corporate sponsorships over student-led ethical tech initiatives. She believed a dramatic demonstration was necessary.
solution.proof: Thermal anomaly timestamp (7:02 PM) coincides with drone-sized heat signature. Drone’s flight path confirmed via residual GPS logs recovered from SD card’s corrupted files. Humming audio on the card is her voice—verified by music teacher who heard her sing the anthem earlier that day. The RFID cloner was hidden in her hackathon toolkit.
solution.how_to_solve: Cross-reference thermal data with digital alibis: Aarav was online elsewhere, Reddy on video call, Rohan in supply room. The spoofed badge entry lacks video confirmation—proving digital tampering. Zara’s 15-minute restroom break is unaccounted for on camera. The drone blueprint isn’t proof of a bomb, but it proves capability. The humming matches her voice. Only Zara had access to both RFID cloning tech and indoor drone control. The timing of the heat spike matches drone deployment, not human entry.

case.title: The Case of the Phantom Prankster of Jyoti Engineering College
case.setting: Jyoti Engineering College, Pune – primarily the Central Academic Block and Hostel D
case.crime: A series of increasingly complex and technically sophisticated pranks targeting faculty and administration, culminating in a near-fatal 'accident' during the college fest
case.victim: Multiple faculty members and the college administration; the final incident nearly kills Professor Meenakshi Rao during the cultural fest launch

suspects.name: Arnav Deshpande
suspects.personality: Brilliant but aloof, socially awkward, perfectionist, intensely private
suspects.motive: Harbors resentment toward the administration for denying him a research grant he believed he earned
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been coding alone in his room during all incidents
suspects.secret: Secretly runs an anonymous cybersecurity blog that critiques college IT policies
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the server room late at night before the digital pranks began

suspects.name: Kavya Malhotra
suspects.role: second-year Electrical Engineering student and fest committee head
suspects.personality: Charismatic, manipulative, highly ambitious, thrives on attention
suspects.motive: Wants to prove her crisis management skills by 'saving' the college during pranks, boosting her reputation
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at rehearsal with drama club during the main incidents
suspects.secret: She plagiarized her fest proposal from a foreign university's event plan
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Seems oddly prepared for each prank, always appears first on scene

suspects.name: Professor Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Strict, traditional, bitter about lack of promotions, deeply suspicious of students
suspects.motive: Believes the pranks are a student conspiracy to undermine faculty; may be staging them to justify harsher discipline
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been grading papers at home during incidents
suspects.secret: Alcohol dependency; hides late-night drinking sessions
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was overheard arguing with the dean about student indiscipline the day before first prank

suspects.name: Nandini Patel
suspects.personality: Quiet, observant, artistically gifted, emotionally sensitive
suspects.motive: Her older brother was expelled last year over a prank gone wrong; seeks symbolic justice
suspects.alibi: Says she was sketching in the garden during the first few pranks, later claims insomnia and night walks
suspects.secret: Maintains a hidden journal filled with elaborate mechanical drawings of prank devices
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her sketches include a blueprint of the trap that nearly hit Professor Rao

evidence.description: A sequence of encrypted logs found in the college’s smart lighting system showing unauthorized access from an internal IP 192.168.4.108 during each prank. The pattern matches a Fibonacci-based timing algorithm.
evidence.significance: Indicates pranks were remotely triggered via the IoT network using a predictable but hidden pattern. The Fibonacci sequence suggests the perpetrator has mathematical sophistication.

evidence.description: A torn piece of paper with the words 'Karma Circuit' and a partial circuit diagram involving relays and delay triggers, stained with green tea.
evidence.location: Under a bench in the faculty lounge garden
evidence.significance: Suggests a technical mind with a flair for drama; green tea matches brand only sold at the Architecture canteen.

evidence.description: A sketchbook found hidden under floorboards in Nandini’s hostel room containing detailed designs of prank mechanisms, including the collapsing projector mount used in the final incident.
evidence.significance: Appears to directly implicate Nandini as the planner.

evidence.description: An anonymous post on the college’s secret Discord server at 02:17 AM the night before each prank, quoting a line from R.D. Laing: 'The condition of alienation... is the condition of late bourgeois society.'
evidence.significance: Timestamps align with pranks; the quote appears in Arnav’s published blog.

evidence.description: A night watchman reports seeing a figure in a hoodie entering the Academic Block on the night of the final prank. Describes the person as medium height, carrying a rectangular case like a laptop, wearing red-and-white sneakers.
evidence.significance: Arnav owns red-and-white sneakers; Kavya was seen wearing a similar hoodie that week.

evidence.description: A micro-SD card hidden inside a hollowed-out physics textbook in the library return bin. Contains video files of all pranks from elevated angles, recorded in advance, with timestamps.
evidence.significance: Proves the pranks were premeditated and recorded in advance. The camera angles match the vantage point of the air conditioning vents.

evidence.description: A deleted Python script recovered from the smart lighting server that automates the Fibonacci timing sequence. Metadata shows it was last edited using a virtual machine hosted on a machine with MAC address 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E.
evidence.significance: Ties the digital trigger to a specific device. This MAC address belongs to Professor Joshi’s personal laptop.

timeline: 2023-09-12 07:00: Professor's podium emits loud playback of a goat meme during morning lecture.
2023-09-19 14:30: Dean's office toilet flushes every 30 seconds for 3 hours due to IoT tampering.
2023-10-03 11:15: All digital notice boards display inverted college logo with 'Justice Delayed' tagline.
2023-10-17 20:45: During cultural fest inauguration, Professor Rao narrowly avoids being hit by a falling stage prop (projector mount collapses).
2023-10-18 06:00: Micro-SD card discovered in library.
2023-10-18 10:00: IT recovers lighting logs and Python script.
2023-10-18 15:00: Sketchbook found in Nandini’s room.
red_herrings: The 'Karma Circuit' note with green tea stain points to Architecture students, implicating Nandini.
Arnav’s blog uses the same R.D. Laing quote as the Discord posts.
Professor Joshi’s laptop MAC address appears in the server logs.
Kavya’s presence at every incident scene makes her appear orchestrator.
Nandini’s sketchbook seems to contain blueprints of the pranks.

solution.method: Kavya used Professor Joshi’s unlocked laptop (which she accessed during a faculty meeting she attended as fest coordinator) to run a virtual machine from a USB drive. She programmed the Python script with the Fibonacci sequence to control the IoT lights, which triggered synchronized mechanical traps she pre-installed. The traps were built using her brother’s old engineering notes and assembled during fest setup. The SD card was planted to simulate foresight.
solution.motive: To engineer a crisis she could heroically resolve, thereby gaining recognition for a national student leadership award she secretly applied for.
solution.proof: The Python script was run in a VM not native to Joshi’s OS. Forensic analysis shows USB insertion logs on his laptop at 14:32 on 2023-10-16, matching Kavya’s swipe card entry to the faculty wing. Additionally, the SD card has Kavya’s fingerprints and was formatted using a phone model she owns.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the digital and physical timelines. The Fibonacci pattern in the lighting logs must align with the actual prank triggers. The SD card shows recordings made *before* the pranks, meaning the footage was faked and planted. Only someone with access to faculty areas (like Kavya) could have planted it. The MAC address is a red herring—Joshi’s laptop was compromised. The witness description of red-and-white sneakers matches Arnav, but the hoodie and case point to Kavya (seen carrying a laptop case that night). The final proof is the USB log and phone format metadata on the SD card, linking it to Kavya.

case.title: The Case of the Buried Cipher
case.setting: IIT Bombay's Heritage Campus Quad, during the annual cultural fest 'Festronix 2023'
case.crime: A treasure hunt competition turns deadly when a student collapses after drinking a bottled water, later confirmed as poisoning. The real treasure—a lost colonial-era manuscript rumored to reveal a hidden library—vanishes.
case.victim: Arnav Mehta, 22, second-year engineering student and treasure hunt favorite

suspects.name: Kiara Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Ambitious, highly analytical, competitive, socially reserved
suspects.motive: Believed Arnav stole her cipher-solving algorithm used in the hunt’s first round, jeopardizing her win and scholarship chances
suspects.alibi: Claims she was solving the fourth clue near the old library between 16:30 and 17:15
suspects.secret: She hacked into the fest’s server to modify clue order, fearing unfair advantage
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the water cooler 10 minutes before Arnav drank; refuses to disclose her alibi’s witness

suspects.name: Professor Varun Iyengar
suspects.motive: Wanted to retrieve the manuscript for himself to publish and gain academic fame
suspects.alibi: Was giving a lecture in Lecture Hall B from 16:00 to 17:00
suspects.secret: His grandfather was a British colonial archivist who hid the manuscript; family legend says it holds proof of stolen Indian artifacts
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Knew the treasure’s true nature before the hunt began; was seen arguing with Arnav the night before

suspects.name: Rohan Kapoor
suspects.motive: Desperately needed money to pay off gambling debts; planned to steal and sell the manuscript
suspects.alibi: Says he was at the music stage watching a band from 16:00 to 17:30
suspects.secret: He forged his father’s signature on college loan forms
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His backpack had traces of soil matching excavation site; changed alibi twice

suspects.name: Dr. Neha Malhotra
suspects.personality: Strict, emotionally detached, perfectionist, protective of college image
suspects.motive: Feared the treasure hunt would expose a secret underground archive beneath the quad, violating heritage laws
suspects.alibi: Was in her office handling student complaints from 15:45 to 17:20
suspects.secret: She authorized unauthorized renovations that damaged part of the archive, covering it up
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Ordered security to restrict access to the dig site after the incident; deleted CCTV footage

evidence.description: A half-empty water bottle with traces of Aconitum toxin (monkshood). Label shows it was taken from the official fest cooler near the quad.
evidence.location: Beside Arnav’s body near the sundial
evidence.significance: Cause of death was poisoning. Bottle had no fingerprints due to gloves or wiping.

evidence.description: A torn piece of paper with a partial cipher: 'ROT13(FTUEZ JNFGYR) → ...'
evidence.significance: Indicates he was close to solving the final clue. 'Jnfgyr' decodes to 'Wasteland'—a campus nickname for the abandoned greenhouse.

evidence.description: Server logs showing a login from Kiara’s IP at 02:17 AM modifying clue sequence. Also, a deleted file named 'final_key.txt' accessed by Professor Iyengar’s account.
evidence.significance: Kiara tampered with clues; Iyengar accessed the solution key, but logs show it was merely viewed, not altered.

evidence.description: A student ID card belonging to Rohan found near the greenhouse shed
evidence.location: Under a pile of bricks in the greenhouse
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan was at the final location, possibly stealing the manuscript.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing Dr. Malhotra burying a small metal box near the sundial at 15:30, before the hunt began.
evidence.location: Witnessed from the third-floor window of humanities block
evidence.significance: Places the dean at the crime scene before the event; implies prior knowledge.

evidence.description: A soil sample from the excavation pit: contains traces of neem wood and 19th-century ink. Matches a hidden compartment in a statue in the library.
evidence.significance: Confirms the manuscript was moved from the statue compartment to the pit, then stolen after the poisoning.

evidence.description: Dr. Malhotra’s calendar backup showing a meeting labeled 'Heritage Compliance' scheduled at 15:00 on the day of the incident—but the room was empty.
evidence.significance: She forged an alibi; was not in her office as claimed.

timeline: 15:00 – Treasure hunt begins; 10 teams given first clue.
15:30 – Janitor sees Dr. Malhotra burying a metal box near the sundial.
15:45 – Dr. Malhotra claims to be in office; calendar shows fake meeting.
16:15 – Arnav solves third clue, accesses greenhouse area.
16:20 – Kiara seen near water cooler; claims to be heading to library.
16:25 – Rohan seen near music stage; band confirms he arrived late.
16:45 – Arnav drinks water at sundial, collapses within minutes.
16:50 – Professor Iyengar exits lecture hall, seen walking toward quad.
17:05 – Security finds ID card under greenhouse bricks.
17:10 – Dean orders area sealed, deletes CCTV footage from cameras facing the sundial.
17:20 – Forensic team discovers empty poison bottle.
red_herrings: Kiara’s server hack suggests she sabotaged the hunt to win.
Rohan’s ID card in the greenhouse implicates him in theft.
Professor Iyengar’s access to the solution key implies he manipulated the game.
The poison bottle’s lack of fingerprints points to a professional killer.

solution.method: She poisoned the water bottle before the hunt began, knowing Arnav—always thirsty—would be drawn to the cooler near the final clue. She planted the manuscript in the pit after secretly moving it from the library statue to frame the hunt as the discovery. After Arnav’s death, she retrieved the manuscript from the pit during the chaos.
solution.motive: To prevent exposure of her illegal renovation and the existence of the underground archive, which could end her career and lead to criminal charges.
solution.proof: Janitor’s testimony places her at the sundial at 15:30 burying the box (which contained the manuscript). Soil from the statue matches the pit. Her calendar shows a fake meeting, disproving her alibi. Deleted CCTV confirms intent to hide actions.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Decode 'Wasteland' clue to locate greenhouse. 2. Use soil evidence to link pit to library statue—meaning manuscript was moved before hunt. 3. Janitor’s sighting proves dean was burying it. 4. Her order to seal the area wasn’t precaution—it was to retrieve the manuscript after Arnav’s death. 5. She poisoned the water because only someone with prior knowledge of Arnav’s habits and the hunt route could have done it at that location. Kiara, Iyengar, and Rohan had motives but no opportunity or physical proof linking them to the burial or cover-up.

crime_type: multiple false confessions to same crime

case.title: The Case of the Stolen Merit List
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay
case.crime: The tampering and theft of the final-year B.Tech merit list before grades were officially released
case.victim: The academic integrity of the examination board and the students' future placements

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.personality: Brilliant but arrogant, highly competitive, socially isolated
suspects.motive: He was ranked third but believed he deserved first; wanted to erase the list to force a re-evaluation
suspects.alibi: Claims he was coding in the library until midnight
suspects.secret: He plagiarized a minor project and fears exposure if his academic record is scrutinized
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to help investigate the breach, showing unusual familiarity with the database structure

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.personality: Idealistic, principled, fiercely protective of students
suspects.motive: Disagreed with how the merit list prioritized coding skills over research; wanted to expose flaws in the system
suspects.alibi: Says she was attending a virtual conference call with MIT collaborators from 8 PM to 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: She leaked a research paper to a rival institution months ago and is under internal investigation
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the first to suggest the breach was an inside job, subtly directing suspicion toward students

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.personality: Anxious, tech-savvy, eager to impress, prone to panic
suspects.motive: His sister is on the list at rank 12; feared she'd lose a scholarship if not in top 10
suspects.alibi: Claims he was gaming online with friends from 7:30 PM onward
suspects.secret: He hacked into the college portal last year to change a grade and has been blackmailed since
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made a public post days earlier criticizing the merit system, calling it 'rigged'

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Cynical, overworked, resentful of faculty, loyal to routine
suspects.motive: Felt disrespected when his proposal to upgrade the database was rejected; wanted to prove a point
suspects.alibi: Says he was at home watching a cricket match alone
suspects.secret: He has been selling access to archived student data on the dark web for side income
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Delayed reporting the breach by 12 hours, citing a 'system glitch'

evidence.description: Log file shows login to the academic server from IP 192.168.7.21 at 9:17 PM using Dr. Nair's credentials. Session lasted 18 minutes.
evidence.significance: Suggests Dr. Nair accessed the system during her supposed conference call

evidence.description: A Python script named 'scrub_merit.py' found in Aarav’s public GitHub, last updated 3 days before the breach. It can wipe and randomize database entries.
evidence.significance: Indicates Aarav had the tools to commit the crime

evidence.description: A crumpled note in Rohan’s hostel bin with database login hints: 'dean_pass = Feb2024!', 'port = 3306'
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan attempted unauthorized access

evidence.description: DNS logs show a hidden DNS tunneling request from the college network at 9:20 PM to an external IP associated with a data exfiltration tool.
evidence.significance: Indicates data was extracted using covert channel, requiring admin-level access

evidence.description: A sticky note under Vikram’s keyboard with handwritten credentials: 'root / iitbomb@y2k'
evidence.significance: Proof of poor security practices; root access was easily obtainable by anyone who entered his office

evidence.description: Night watchman reports seeing Rohan near the admin block at 9:05 PM, though Rohan insists he was in his room.
evidence.significance: Contradicts Rohan’s alibi

evidence.description: Camera footage from hallway outside server room shows Vikram entering at 8:45 PM and leaving at 8:50 PM. No one else entered.
evidence.significance: Places Vikram at the scene, though he claims he only checked the AC unit

timeline: 6:30 PM - Dr. Nair joins virtual conference call (verified by Zoom logs)
7:15 PM - Rohan joins online game server (verified by Steam and Discord logs)
8:45 PM - Vikram enters server room (security footage)
8:50 PM - Vikram exits server room
9:17 PM - Login to academic server using Dr. Nair’s credentials from IP 192.168.7.21
9:20 PM - DNS tunneling detected on college network
9:35 PM - Server logs show merit table deleted and overwritten with random data
9:40 PM - Aarav logs into library Wi-Fi (verified by network logs)
10:30 PM - Dr. Nair ends conference call
10:45 PM - Rohan logs off game server
2:00 PM next day - Breach discovered by clerk preparing placement reports
red_herrings: Dr. Nair's credentials used in the breach
Aarav's Python script on GitHub
Rohan's note with login hints
Rohan seen near admin block
Aarav's early interest in database forensics

solution.method: Used his physical access to install a rogue Raspberry Pi inside the server closet at 8:45 PM. The device spoofed Dr. Nair's credentials via MAC address impersonation and executed the deletion and data exfiltration remotely via DNS tunneling at 9:20 PM while he was at home watching cricket.
solution.motive: To demonstrate the vulnerability of the system after his upgrade proposal was rejected, thereby forcing administration to recognize his expertise and approve funding.
solution.proof: The Raspberry Pi was found hidden behind a UPS unit, still connected. It contained logs of the spoofed session, DNS tunnel commands, and a draft email to the Dean titled 'Proof of Vulnerability'.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Note that the login from Dr. Nair's credentials occurred at 9:17 PM, but Vikram was the only one physically near the server at 8:45 PM. 2. DNS tunneling at 9:20 PM requires a device already on the internal network. 3. No external breach was detected, so the attack originated inside. 4. Only Vikram had both physical access and knowledge to set up a rogue device. 5. The GitHub script and Rohan's note are too crude for the sophisticated DNS exfiltration used. 6. Dr. Nair’s credentials were spoofed: the IP 192.168.7.21 is not her office device. 7. The Raspberry Pi proves premeditation and execution, placing Vikram as the only one with means, access, and motive tied to system security.
