case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Witness
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay, Mumbai
case.crime: Murder of a student found in the locked server room during exam week
case.victim: Ananya Patel, 21, second-year Computer Science student and whistleblower

suspects.name: Dr. Arvind Mehta
suspects.motive: Ananya discovered his unauthorized use of college servers for cryptocurrency mining and threatened to expose him
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been live-streaming an online faculty meeting from 8:00 PM to 10:30 PM, verified by IT logs
suspects.secret: He is undergoing treatment for early-stage Parkinson’s and fears losing tenure if discovered
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to secure the server room after the body was found, potentially contaminating evidence

suspects.name: Rohan Desai
suspects.motive: Ananya rejected his romantic advances and threatened to expose his use of AI to forge research papers
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night study group in the library from 7:30 PM to 11:00 PM; confirmed by three friends
suspects.secret: He is plagiarizing his final thesis from a foreign university database
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Deleted his WhatsApp chat logs with Ananya the morning after the murder

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Ananya discovered Priya was leaking exam papers to a coaching institute for money
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in her dorm asleep by 8:00 PM; no one saw her until morning
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously writing a blog criticizing college administration, using a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the server room at 7:45 PM by a night guard but denies it

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.motive: Ananya discovered he had backdoored the exam grading system to help failing students—for a fee
suspects.alibi: Says he was working remotely from his personal laptop in his on-campus apartment from 7:00 PM onward; system logs show remote login
suspects.secret: He is in a secret relationship with a junior faculty member, against college policy
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Modified server access logs two hours after the body was discovered

evidence.description: A rubber-grip screwdriver with traces of blood and dark blue paint, found behind a false panel in the server rack
evidence.location: Behind Server Rack B, Server Room
evidence.significance: Matches bruising pattern on Ananya’s skull; blue paint matches paint from the lab assistant’s toolkit

evidence.description: Server access log showing Dr. Mehta’s ID accessed the server room’s lock system at 8:17 PM
evidence.significance: Suggests Dr. Mehta unlocked the room remotely; timestamp matches estimated time of death

evidence.description: A blurred CCTV still showing a figure in a hoodie entering the server room corridor at 8:10 PM; height matches Rohan
evidence.significance: Places a suspect near the crime scene

evidence.description: A torn piece of exam paper with the words 'final warning' written in red ink, clutched in Ananya’s hand
evidence.significance: Indicates motive related to academic corruption

evidence.description: A scheduled task log on Vikram’s personal laptop showing an automated script that logged into the server at 8:00 PM and ran until 9:00 PM
evidence.significance: Appears to confirm his alibi, but the script could have been set in advance

evidence.description: A keycard with Rohan’s name but Dr. Mehta’s photo, found in a dustbin near the server room
evidence.significance: Suggests identity fraud or card cloning

evidence.description: A night janitor reports seeing Priya near the server room at 7:45 PM but cannot confirm it was her due to poor lighting
evidence.significance: Weakly places Priya at the scene

timeline: 6:30 PM – Ananya sends final email to college ethics committee with evidence of academic corruption
7:00 PM – Vikram logs into server remotely from his apartment
7:30 PM – Rohan joins study group in library (confirmed by librarian sign-in log)
7:45 PM – Janitor reports seeing a hooded figure (possibly Priya) near server room
8:00 PM – Automated script on Vikram’s laptop begins server session
8:05 PM – Dr. Mehta’s ID used to unlock server room door (via remote command)
8:10 PM – Blurry CCTV footage shows hooded figure entering server room corridor
8:15 PM – Estimated time of death (blunt force trauma to head)
8:17 PM – Bloodied screwdriver placed behind false panel
9:00 PM – Server room door locked automatically
10:30 PM – Night security patrol finds door ajar, discovers body at 10:32 PM
10:35 PM – College security called, scene secured
red_herrings: The screwdriver with Rohan’s fingerprints and blue paint (he lent it to Vikram weeks prior)
Dr. Mehta’s remote unlock command (his credentials were stolen via phishing)
The hooded figure on CCTV (Rohan’s hoodie, but worn by someone else)
Priya’s presence near server room (she was retrieving a lost phone, not committing murder)

solution.method: Used a cloned keycard (created using Rohan’s card as template) and Dr. Mehta’s stolen credentials to remotely unlock the server room. Wore a hooded jacket stolen from Rohan’s locker. Killed Ananya with a server maintenance tool, then reset the door lock via console to make it appear locked from inside. Later planted Rohan’s screwdriver to frame him.
solution.motive: Ananya discovered his pay-to-pass grading scheme and refused his bribe. He feared expulsion and criminal charges.
solution.proof: Digital forensic analysis reveals Vikram’s personal laptop accessed Dr. Mehta’s phishing email containing stolen credentials at 7:48 PM. Also, the automated script log was faked; actual server logs show no remote session from 8:00–9:00 PM—only the unlock command was sent. The keycard found in the bin has Vikram’s fingerprints and microscopic residue from a card printer in his apartment.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Cross-reference server access logs with actual login sessions—showing no remote session despite script claim. 2. Analyze the unlock command: only someone with access to both Mehta’s credentials and internal network (like Vikram) could have sent it. 3. The keycard with mixed IDs indicates cloning; only a network admin has tools and knowledge. 4. The screwdriver was wiped but had Vikram’s partial print under the grip. 5. The torn exam paper in Ananya’s hand had Vikram’s handwriting in the margins of a previous draft she recovered. 6. The timing: Vikram’s alibi relies on the script, but no actual data was transferred—proving it was staged.

case.title: The Case of the Midnight Circuit
case.setting: Electrical Engineering Department, IIT Bombay – Power Systems Lab
case.crime: Sabotage of a national power grid simulation during a live demonstration, resulting in critical data loss and a near-electrocution incident
case.victim: Professor Aniket Rao, lead researcher, and the National Energy Security Initiative project

suspects.name: Kavya Mehra
suspects.motive: Professor Rao had rejected her groundbreaking algorithm for the simulation, calling it 'unstable'. She believed it would have prevented the crash.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the library studying circuit diagrams alone from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
suspects.secret: She had secretly implemented her algorithm on a backup server without authorization.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the lab’s admin panel two days prior with elevated privileges. Acts overly defensive when questioned about her code.

suspects.name: Rohan Deshmukh
suspects.motive: Failed Rao's course and was barred from the project. Rumored to have applied for a rival private energy startup.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night cricket match on campus from 6:30 PM to 9:00 PM, confirmed by three friends.
suspects.secret: He was dating Kavya in secret and knew about her unauthorized code.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the lab’s electrical substation 15 minutes before the outage by a janitor. Denied knowing why he was there.

suspects.name: Dr. Nalini Iyer
suspects.motive: Rao's project success would have earned him a national award and possibly the Director position she is eyeing. Her own research funding depends on departmental prestige.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in a Zoom call with a funding committee from 7:45 PM to 9:30 PM. Call was recorded.
suspects.secret: She had quietly lobbied the administration to reduce Rao’s project budget weeks earlier.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed for an internal investigation to be dropped within hours of the incident. Overly eager to blame 'student error'.

suspects.name: Vikram Patel
suspects.personality: Quiet, meticulous, resentful, loyal to routines
suspects.motive: Rao publicly reprimanded him a week earlier for a minor wiring mistake, threatening to report him to HR.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at his cousin's birthday dinner off-campus from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM. No one remembers seeing him there.
suspects.secret: He has been stealing scrap copper wiring from the lab for months to sell.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His access card was used to enter the lab at 7:58 PM—the only physical entry during the outage. He claims his card was stolen.

evidence.description: A charred fragment of a custom resistor with micro-engraved serial 'KV-9X', not listed in the lab inventory
evidence.location: Found fused inside the main circuit breaker panel
evidence.significance: Deliberate insertion of an unstable resistor that overheated during peak load, triggering the cascade failure

evidence.description: Log file showing a remote login to the simulation server at 8:03 PM from Kavya’s student account, running a script labeled 'ALPHA_OVERRIDE'
evidence.significance: Appears to show Kavya tampering with the system during the outage

evidence.description: A pair of engineering gloves with traces of copper dust and a small oil stain near the thumb
evidence.location: Trash bin in the lab restroom
evidence.significance: Matches Vikram's uniform issue gloves. Oil stain matches lubricant used in the substation switches

evidence.description: A hidden partition on Kavya’s laptop with a compiled version of her rejected algorithm, timestamped 7:45 PM
evidence.significance: Suggests she was preparing to activate her code during the demo

evidence.description: The night watchman reports seeing a figure in a lab coat enter the substation room at 7:56 PM. Described as 'tall, with curly hair'
evidence.significance: Rohan has curly hair. Kavya and Vikram have straight hair. Dr. Iyer has short, straight hair.

evidence.description: A USB drive disguised as a power plug, containing a keystroke logger and a script that can spoof login credentials
evidence.significance: Used to capture passwords and remotely mimic a user’s login—explains Kavya's 'remote access'

evidence.description: Dr. Iyer’s Zoom call recording shows a 90-second gap in audio at 8:02 PM, with video frozen on a static slide
evidence.significance: Indicates the call was pre-recorded or looped; she was not online during the critical window

timeline: 6:30 PM – Live demo setup begins. Power grid simulation at 30% load.
7:00 PM – Kavya leaves lab for 'library'. Rohan arrives at cricket field.
7:45 PM – Dr. Iyer joins Zoom call. Vikram clocks out digitally.
7:56 PM – Watchman sees figure enter substation room.
7:58 PM – Vikram’s access card used to enter lab (CCTV shows no face due to outage prep).
8:00 PM – Power outage begins. Lights, security, and backup generators fail for 4 minutes.
8:03 PM – Kavya’s account logs into simulation server (via spoofed credentials).
8:04 PM – Simulation crashes. Main breaker blows with visible spark. Rao suffers minor shock.
8:05 PM – Emergency lights activate. Backup systems come online.
9:30 PM – Dr. Iyer ends Zoom call. Rohan returns from cricket.
red_herrings: Kavya’s unauthorized algorithm suggests she sabotaged to prove her point.
Rohan seen near substation with motive and opportunity.
Vikram’s access card and gloves place him at the scene.
Kavya’s remote login during the crash.

solution.method: Used a keystroke logger (planted earlier) to steal Kavya’s credentials. During the 90-second gap in her Zoom call, she physically entered the lab using Vikram’s stolen access card (copied weeks earlier). Inserted the custom resistor into the breaker panel, then remotely triggered Kavya’s script via spoofed login to create a false trail. The resistor was designed to fail only under full simulation load, which occurred at 8:03 PM.
solution.motive: To sabotage Rao’s project and eliminate him as a rival for the Institute Director position, ensuring her own promotion and increased funding for her department.
solution.proof: The 90-second audio gap in Dr. Iyer’s Zoom call proves she was not online during the attack. The keystroke logger matches her administrative access. The resistor’s serial 'KV-9X' is a red herring — 'KV' stands for 'kilo-volt', and '9X' is a prototype code she used in her own early research, found in her personal notebooks.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. The remote login from Kavya’s account is impossible during the power outage unless the attacker had remote access — only faculty had that. 2. The watchman’s description points to Rohan, but the outage began at 8:00, and the login was at 8:03 — cameras were down, so no facial confirmation. 3. Vikram’s card was used, but his gloves in the bin suggest someone else used them. 4. The keystroke logger reveals a device capable of spoofing logins, accessible only to someone with admin rights. 5. Only Dr. Iyer had the technical knowledge to build the resistor, the authority to install the logger, and the motive to eliminate Rao. The 'KV-9X' serial in her old research notes ties her to the resistor. Her Zoom gap proves she was not where she claimed during the attack.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Catalyst
case.setting: Chemistry Research Lab, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi
case.crime: A rare and highly sensitive catalytic compound essential for cancer research went missing under locked-room conditions during a 15-minute blackout caused by a campus-wide power surge.
case.victim: Dr. Arvind Mehta, lead researcher, whose 7-year project was set back by the sabotage and theft of 'Cat-7X', a proprietary catalyst stored in a dual-locked, tamper-proof vault inside the lab.

suspects.name: Ishita Malhotra
suspects.personality: Ambitious, perfectionist, emotionally guarded, intensely competitive
suspects.motive: She was about to be removed from the research team due to ethical violations in data reporting; stealing Cat-7X could allow her to continue the research independently.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the campus library accessing digital archives during the blackout.
suspects.secret: She falsified results in two earlier experiments to impress Dr. Mehta.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen arguing with Dr. Mehta two days prior; her student ID was found near the vault door.

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.personality: Quiet, tech-savvy, socially anxious, deeply loyal to Dr. Mehta
suspects.motive: None obvious—was well-liked and had no known grievances.
suspects.alibi: Says he was fixing a fume hood in Lab B during the incident.
suspects.secret: He has been secretly dating Ishita, which violates lab conduct rules.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His access log shows he entered the secure lab 10 minutes before the blackout, but he denies it.

suspects.name: Prof. Nalini Sethi
suspects.role: Senior chemistry professor and department head
suspects.personality: Charismatic, politically astute, protective of institutional reputation, secretly envious of Dr. Mehta’s grant funding
suspects.motive: Wanted to discredit Dr. Mehta's lab to redirect future funding to her own nanomaterials project.
suspects.alibi: Was chairing a Zoom faculty meeting during the blackout; has 6 colleagues as witnesses.
suspects.secret: She plagiarized portions of her last grant proposal from Dr. Mehta’s unpublished work.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Pushed hard for an internal inquiry immediately after the theft, bypassing campus security protocol.

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Brilliant but reckless, thrill-seeking, prone to hacking challenges
suspects.motive: Wanted to prove he could bypass the lab’s security system as a personal challenge; didn’t realize Cat-7X was irreplaceable.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a cricket match in the evening; 4 friends confirm.
suspects.secret: He previously hacked the lab’s temperature control system as a prank.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His personal laptop contains encrypted files labeled 'LabVault_Project'.

evidence.description: A student ID card bearing Ishita Malhotra’s name, found 2 meters from the vault door, slightly bent as if dropped in haste.
evidence.significance: Suggests Ishita was near the vault at or near the time of the theft.

evidence.description: Security access logs show Rohan Deshpande's ID scanned at the lab’s inner door at 18:40, 5 minutes before the blackout at 18:45.
evidence.significance: Indicates Rohan entered just before the theft, contradicting his alibi.

evidence.description: A small piece of black rubber tubing (3 cm) found inside the vault ventilation duct; chemically inert and heat-resistant.
evidence.location: Inside ventilation shaft of the sealed vault
evidence.significance: Used to create a siphon mechanism to extract the liquid catalyst without opening the vault.

evidence.description: Timestamped video from Lab B’s camera shows Rohan working on the fume hood at 18:42, just before the blackout.
evidence.significance: Supports Rohan’s alibi and contradicts the access log—suggests a system breach.

evidence.description: A faint smudge of UV-reactive grease on the vault’s secondary lock cylinder; matches grease used in the maintenance of electronic access panels.
evidence.location: On the lock of the dual-key vault
evidence.significance: Indicates tampering with the lock’s internal mechanism using a tool inserted through the keyhole.

evidence.description: Encrypted file named 'VaultSim.exe' recovered from Vikram’s laptop; simulation software modeling the lab’s power backup delay and lock override timing.
evidence.location: Vikram Joshi’s personal laptop (seized with consent)
evidence.significance: Shows Vikram planned a timing-based intrusion exploiting the 15-second gap between main power loss and backup activation.

evidence.description: A coffee-stained research proposal draft with Prof. Sethi’s handwriting, referencing 'Cat-7X synthesis protocol' with annotated deviations.
evidence.location: In a recycling bin outside Prof. Sethi’s office
evidence.significance: Suggests she attempted to reverse-engineer the catalyst—motive for theft.

timeline: 18:00 – Dr. Mehta confirms Cat-7X is in the vault and locks it with dual key + biometric scan.
18:30 – Power grid fluctuation detected across campus; backup systems initiate protocol.
18:40 – Security log shows Rohan’s ID scanned at inner lab door.
18:42 – Lab B camera shows Rohan repairing fume hood.
18:45:00 – Main power fails; backup activates after 15-second delay.
18:45:03 – During the 3-second window when both locks disengage due to power transition, vault is remotely manipulated.
18:46 – Lights restore; Dr. Mehta returns to lab at 18:50, discovers vault open and Cat-7X missing.
19:00 – Campus security notified; crime scene sealed.
red_herrings: Ishita’s ID card found near the vault—planted to mislead.
Prof. Sethi’s coffee-stained proposal implies attempted replication, but she never accessed the lab that day.
Rohan’s access log entry is a spoofed RFID signal, not his actual presence.

solution.method: Vikram used a pre-programmed microcontroller hidden in the lab’s power relay box weeks earlier. During the 15-second power transition, the device sent a spoofed release signal to the vault’s electromagnetic lock, synchronized with a vacuum siphon made from the rubber tube inserted into the ventilation shaft. The catalyst was drawn out silently before the backup power fully engaged and re-locked the vault.
solution.motive: To prove he could bypass the 'unhackable' system; he intended to return the catalyst after炫耀 his exploit but panicked when Dr. Mehta announced its irreplaceability.
solution.proof: The microcontroller was found behind the relay panel with Vikram’s fingerprint; the 'VaultSim.exe' file matches the exact timing sequence of the power failure and lock disengagement. The siphon tube matches lab maintenance tubing Vikram had access to as an intern.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Reconcile the contradiction between Rohan's alibi video and access log—digital spoofing occurred. 2. Note the 3-second dual-lock vulnerability during power shift—only someone with system knowledge would exploit this. 3. The siphon tube indicates physical theft without vault entry. 4. Vikram’s simulation file proves foreknowledge of the exploit window. 5. His prank history and hacking skills align with the method. 6. The planted ID and forged log were distractions by Vikram to implicate others.

case.title: The Case of the Silent Examination
case.setting: St. Xavier's College of Engineering, Mumbai - Department of Computer Science, Central Server Room
case.crime: Sabotage of the university's final semester examination database 48 hours before scheduled digital exams, resulting in complete data corruption and system lockdown. No ransom, no announcement, no apparent gain.
case.victim: Institute's academic integrity and 850 students' exam schedules; the Examination Controller, Dr. Meenal Patel, suffered a stress-induced cardiac episode upon discovering the breach.

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.personality: Brilliant but arrogant, socially isolated, competitive, perfectionist
suspects.motive: Was disqualified from the Dean's Honors List due to a disputed plagiarism case; wanted to disrupt the system that 'unfairly' judged him.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was streaming a 12-hour coding marathon on Twitch from 8 PM to 8 AM.
suspects.secret: Secretly dating the victim's daughter, who is unaware of his disqualification.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the server room two nights before the incident arguing with Dr. Patel.

suspects.name: Dr. Kavita Nair
suspects.motive: Opposed the new digital examination system on security grounds; warned administration repeatedly.
suspects.alibi: Attended a virtual faculty meeting from 7 PM to 10 PM; logged in from her official university account.
suspects.secret: Her brother is serving time for cybercrime, which she has hidden from colleagues.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Accessed server logs post-incident without authorization, claiming 'forensic curiosity.'

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.role: second-year computer science student and campus janitor (part-time night cleaner)
suspects.personality: Quiet, observant, financially struggling, highly resourceful
suspects.motive: His sister failed last year's digital exam due to technical glitches; blames the system.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was cleaning the third floor from 10 PM to 1 AM.
suspects.secret: Has been reverse-engineering university network access using old credentials from a discarded IT internship form.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was caught on camera entering the server room at 11:47 PM with a flash drive.

suspects.name: Priya Agarwal
suspects.role: Graduate Teaching Assistant and Ph.D. aspirant
suspects.personality: Ambitious, empathetic, manipulative when cornered, politically savvy
suspects.motive: Stands to gain a permanent faculty position if the current system fails and a 'reform committee' is formed.
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a late-night study group in the library with three friends.
suspects.secret: Submitted a research paper with falsified data that was to be reviewed after exams.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Asked Dr. Patel detailed questions about server backup protocols the day before the breach.

evidence.description: A USB flash drive labeled 'CS_BACKUP_2024' found plugged into Server Rack 3. Contains corrupted data and a fragmented log showing a script execution at 11:52 PM.
evidence.significance: Physical access required; indicates insider knowledge of server naming conventions.

evidence.description: Twitch stream logs confirm Arjun was live from 8 PM to 8 AM, but metadata shows the stream was pre-recorded. Actual login IP traced to a proxy server in Singapore.
evidence.location: Digital footprint analysis via university cyber lab
evidence.significance: Arjun's alibi is faked; he had opportunity.

evidence.description: A pair of latex gloves found in a trash can outside the server room, smeared with machine grease and dust consistent with the janitor’s cleaning cart.
evidence.location: East corridor trash can, second floor
evidence.significance: Suggests attempt to avoid fingerprints; links to janitorial staff.

evidence.description: Server access logs show a login from Dr. Nair's ID at 11:30 PM, but her biometric scan was not recorded. The system allowed fallback authentication due to a recent update.
evidence.significance: Her credentials were used, but not necessarily by her.

evidence.description: A night security guard reports seeing Rohan with a flash drive at 11:45 PM, but admits poor vision and no direct view of the server room door.
evidence.significance: Places Rohan near the scene with incriminating item.

evidence.description: A hidden partition on the central server contained an encrypted script that activates only when the main exam database is corrupted. It logs all post-breach access attempts — including Dr. Nair’s and Priya’s.
evidence.location: Forensic disk image of main server
evidence.significance: Script was planted weeks earlier; designed to frame investigators by exposing their unauthorized access.

evidence.description: A torn corner of a library seating chart found in the server room ventilation grate, with 'P.A.' and '10:45' written in pencil.
evidence.significance: Links Priya to the server room; she was not in the library at that time.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Regular server maintenance completed by IT staff.
7:00 PM: Virtual faculty meeting begins; Dr. Nair logs in from her office IP.
8:00 PM: Arjun 'begins' Twitch stream (later revealed as pre-recorded).
8:30 PM: Priya seen entering the library with study group.
10:00 PM: Rohan begins night cleaning shift; signs in at security desk.
10:45 PM: Library seating chart updated; Priya’s name logged at Table 7.
11:30 PM: Server logs show login using Dr. Nair's credentials (no biometrics).
11:47 PM: Security camera shows figure resembling Rohan entering server room with flash drive.
11:52 PM: Corrupted script executed; database begins overwriting.
11:55 PM: Emergency alarms trigger; system isolates server.
12:15 AM: Dr. Patel arrives after alert; discovers breach; collapses.
1:00 AM: Rohan clocks out; no flash drive visible.
8:00 AM: Arjun appears on campus, claims to have just ended stream.
red_herrings: Arjun's fake stream suggests premeditated cybercrime.
Rohan's flash drive and janitor access imply he had means and motive.
Dr. Nair’s unauthorized post-incident access makes her appear guilty of covering tracks.
Latex gloves and grease point to janitorial involvement.
Server login under Dr. Nair’s name suggests insider betrayal.

solution.method: Used her teaching assistant privileges to plant a hidden script on the server two weeks prior. On the night of the crime, she bypassed library security by slipping out through a service exit, entered the server room using a stolen biometric override code (obtained by shoulder-surfing the IT head), and triggered the corruption script via a remote command from a burner laptop. She left the fake USB drive to implicate Arjun, knowing he had both motive and capability.
solution.motive: She needed the system to fail spectacularly so that the administration would dismantle the current digital exam framework, creating a vacancy for a 'cyber-reform' coordinator — a role she had already lobbied for and was poised to win.
solution.proof: The torn library seating chart with her initials (P.A.) and timestamp, found in the ventilation grate — she discarded it while hiding in the server room post-activation. Additionally, the hidden script includes a digital fingerprint matching her personal coding style (use of nested XOR encryption and comment syntax in Marathi), which forensic linguists matched to her past submissions.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must notice that multiple suspects have alibis broken by digital evidence (Arjun's stream, Dr. Nair's login), but only Priya’s alibi is broken by physical evidence. The library chart proves she wasn't where she claimed. The script’s coding style is the technical confirmation. The gloves, USB, and login trace are red herrings designed to misdirect toward Arjun, Rohan, and Dr. Nair. The true clue is the *location* of the torn chart — only someone who entered the server room could have dropped it in the vent. The motive is revealed by cross-referencing administration emails (available in evidence logs) about the pending reform committee.

case.title: The Case of the Perfect Alibi
case.setting: Lakshmi Narayan College of Technology, Pune – Central Library, 3rd Floor – Digital Archives Wing
case.crime: Sabotage of the National Robotics Championship prototype and theft of its AI core, resulting in disqualification of the college team
case.victim: Project AETHER: a prototype autonomous robot developed by the college's robotics team for a national competition

suspects.name: Arnav Khatri
suspects.role: final-year engineering student and team leader of Project AETHER
suspects.motive: He stood to lose his national recognition and scholarship renewal if the project failed; secretly resentful of the AI core’s original designer
suspects.alibi: Was live-streaming a coding tutorial on YouTube from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM on the night of the sabotage; the stream shows him at his desk the entire time
suspects.secret: He plagiarized part of the robot's pathfinding algorithm from an international journal
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Acted overly devastated, aggressively blamed internal leaks, and pushed for immediate accusation of juniors

suspects.name: Ishani Mehta
suspects.role: second-year computer science student, AI specialist on Project AETHER
suspects.personality: brilliant, introverted, socially anxious, deeply proud of her work
suspects.motive: She was the sole developer of the stolen AI core and believed Arnav would take full credit; recent argument over authorship
suspects.alibi: Was attending an online therapy session via encrypted platform 'MindScape' from 7:30 PM to 8:30 PM; the session was confirmed by the therapist
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing advanced AI papers under a pseudonym, feared exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Refused to provide password to her personal GitHub where the AI core backup supposedly existed; claimed it was lost

suspects.name: Professor Damini Rajan
suspects.role: Head of Computer Science Department and faculty advisor for Project AETHER
suspects.motive: The failure of AETHER clears the way for her pet project—'Project LOKI'—to receive next year’s innovation grant
suspects.alibi: Attended the college cultural festival’s judging panel from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM; confirmed by 12 witnesses and CCTV at the open-air amphitheater
suspects.secret: She falsified research data in a previous grant application that could be exposed if AETHER succeeded and invited scrutiny
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Expressed relief disguised as disappointment; pushed administration to 'move on' too quickly

suspects.name: Zubin Dastoor
suspects.role: third-year mechanical engineering student and lab technician’s assistant
suspects.motive: He was offered ₹2 lakh by a rival college to steal the AI core
suspects.alibi: Was allegedly playing mobile PUBG with three friends in the hostel common room from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM; all three friends confirm
suspects.secret: He used college funds to buy cryptocurrency and is being blackmailed
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Changed his phone right after the incident and deleted his game account

evidence.description: YouTube live stream footage of Arnav Khatri coding between 7:00 PM and 10:00 PM. The feed shows only his upper body at a desk with a laptop and a blinking Wi-Fi router.
evidence.significance: Appears to be solid alibi; timestamped and publicly verifiable.

evidence.description: A single partial thumbprint on the inside of the window latch of the library’s emergency exit—clean except for this print, suggesting entry or exit.
evidence.location: Digital Archives Wing, west-side emergency window
evidence.significance: Matches Ishani Mehta’s fingerprint from her lab access file.

evidence.description: Encrypted session log from MindScape therapy platform confirming Ishani’s login and 60-minute active session from 7:30–8:30 PM.
evidence.location: Email inbox of college counselor (obtained via permission)
evidence.significance: Appears to confirm Ishani's alibi during the core sabotage window.

evidence.description: A micro-SD card hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of 'Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach' on shelf 4B. Contains a backup of the AI core code and a hidden script that logs keystrokes.
evidence.location: Library shelf in Digital Archives Wing
evidence.significance: Proves the AI core was copied before theft; the keystroke logger suggests espionage was planned.

evidence.description: CCTV log from amphitheater entrance shows Professor Rajan entering at 6:05 PM and exiting at 9:35 PM. Also shows her briefly stepping out at 8:17 PM to 'take a call'.
evidence.significance: Her absence at 8:17 PM is unaccounted for—only 3 minutes missing, but enough time if she used the underground service tunnel.

evidence.description: Game server logs from PUBG showing Zubin’s device was connected from the hostel IP from 7:00–10:00 PM, but with no actual gameplay actions between 8:15–8:25 PM.
evidence.location: ISP logs obtained via college IT
evidence.significance: Suggests Zubin may have logged in remotely or used an automated proxy; his device was online but inactive during critical window.

evidence.description: A corroded copper grounding wire from the library’s old electrical system found near the server cabinet. One end is twisted with a custom hexagonal crimp—matching only Professor Rajan’s personal toolkit.
evidence.location: Behind server rack in Digital Archives
evidence.significance: Used to bypass the tamper-proof alarm on the server cabinet by creating a dummy ground loop. Only someone with engineering knowledge and access to tools could do this.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Professor Rajan arrives at cultural festival amphitheater.
6:30 PM – AETHER team locks prototype in server cabinet; alarm activated.
7:00 PM – Arnav begins YouTube stream; Zubin joins PUBG session.
7:15 PM – Library security system logs normal status.
7:30 PM – Ishani logs into therapy session.
8:00 PM – Lights flicker briefly in Digital Archives Wing (power surge logged).
8:17 PM – Professor Rajan steps out of amphitheater for 'phone call'.
8:18 PM – Library alarm system records 90-second anomaly in grounding loop; logs auto-reset.
8:20 PM – Security camera outside library shows no entry, but internal motion sensor triggered in Wing 3.
8:25 PM – Ishani’s therapy session ends; she logs out.
8:30 PM – Zubin’s gameplay stops momentarily, then resumes.
9:30 PM – Arnav ends YouTube stream.
9:35 PM – Professor Rajan returns to amphitheater.
10:00 PM – Night guard discovers broken server cabinet and missing AI core.
red_herrings: Ishani’s fingerprint on the window—she accessed it days earlier during a solo debugging session.
Zubin’s inactive game period—caused by a lag spike, not absence.
Arnav’s YouTube stream—pre-recorded and looped after 7:45 PM using a script.
Ishani’s encrypted therapy log—verified but does not prove she was present; session can be pre-answered via AI bot (discovered in platform breach report).

solution.method: Used her knowledge of the library’s outdated electrical system to create a dummy grounding loop with a modified copper wire, bypassing the alarm. Entered via the underground maintenance tunnel connected to the engineering block, which is unmonitored. Disassembled the server cabinet, removed the AI core, and exited before 8:20 PM. Returned to amphitheater by 8:20 PM, claiming she was on a call.
solution.motive: AETHER’s success would trigger an external audit of all department projects, exposing her falsified data in a previous grant and costing her career and funding.
solution.proof: The copper wire with the hexagonal crimp uniquely matches her personal toolkit, which was checked out that day. The grounding anomaly at 8:18 PM coincides with her unaccounted 3-minute absence. Tunnel access log shows a manual override at 8:16 PM—only she has the master key.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the 3-minute alibi gap with a feasible method. The electrical bypass is the only way to silently disable the alarm. The wire is physical proof of her involvement. The YouTube, game, and therapy alibis can all be faked with tech knowledge, but hers is the only one with both means (engineering expertise), access (master key), and a hidden motive tied to institutional consequences. Cross-referencing the power surge, grounding anomaly, and tunnel override confirms the timeline. The other suspects’ alibis, while suspicious, lack a physically possible method within the time window.

case.title: The Case of the Cracked Cipher and the Vanished Vault Key
case.setting: Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur – Department of Computer Science and Engineering, during the annual tech fest 'Kshitij'
case.crime: Double-cross between two students who conspired to steal the prototype AI encryption module from the college's Secure Research Vault, but one betrayed the other, resulting in one being framed and the other disappearing with the device.
case.victim: Arjun Mehta, a third-year computer science student, is falsely accused of stealing the AI module and suffers academic suspension and public disgrace. The actual prototype AI encryption module 'AURA-7' is also the victim of theft.

suspects.name: Vedika Rao
suspects.personality: Brilliant coder, emotionally detached, fiercely ambitious, meticulous planner
suspects.motive: Wants to sell AURA-7 to a foreign tech firm to fund her startup and escape academic expectations.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was giving a guest lecture at the Entrepreneurship Cell from 8:00 PM to 9:30 PM on the night of the theft.
suspects.secret: She has been secretly applying for political asylum in Germany due to family persecution, using college funds to pay a lawyer.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her alibi is corroborated by a recorded video, but the timestamp shows she left the lecture 15 minutes early without being noticed.

suspects.name: Rohan Kapoor
suspects.personality: Charismatic, impulsive, loyal to friends, skilled in social engineering
suspects.motive: Originally partnered with Arjun, but switched sides after being offered triple the money by a rival bidder who contacted him anonymously.
suspects.alibi: Says he was at the fest's DJ night in the open amphitheater from 7:30 PM to 11:00 PM, seen by many people.
suspects.secret: He has an undeclared romantic relationship with Vedika, which he hides to avoid rumors affecting his popularity.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Multiple witnesses saw him near the CS department building around 8:45 PM, contradicting his alibi.

suspects.name: Dr. Anil Deshpande
suspects.role: Professor and head of the Secure Research Lab
suspects.personality: Strict, paranoid about security, emotionally distant, obsessed with legacy
suspects.motive: Suspected of wanting to sabotage AURA-7 to prevent it from being commercialized, as he believes it could be weaponized.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been reviewing papers at home; supported by metadata from his academic submissions logged at 8:15 PM and 9:40 PM.
suspects.secret: He falsified a grant report last year and is under investigation by the college audit committee.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: The vault’s security logs show his biometric was used at 8:32 PM, but he claims his credentials were stolen.

suspects.name: Priya Malhotra
suspects.personality: Inquisitive, bold, tech-savvy, manipulative when pursuing a story
suspects.motive: Wants to expose the theft for a Pulitzer-level campus exposé and national publication deal.
suspects.alibi: Says she was editing her article in the campus media lab from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
suspects.secret: She hacked into the college's grade server last semester to change a friend’s marks and is terrified of exposure.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her laptop contains a partial copy of the vault’s access algorithm, downloaded 3 days before the theft.

evidence.description: Security log from the Secure Research Vault showing two biometric scans: one at 8:32 PM (Dr. Deshpande) and one at 8:33 PM (Arjun Mehta). The log also shows a 3-second gap in CCTV footage between 8:32:15 and 8:32:18.
evidence.location: Department server backup, recovered by IT team after system purge attempt.
evidence.significance: Appears to show Arjun entering after Dr. Deshpande, implicating him directly.

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'Project Kite' found in a trash bin near the amphitheater. Contains a corrupted file named 'AURA_BACKUP_FINAL.enc' and a text file with the message: 'R—Don’t trust A. Meet at Old Gate at 9. –V.'
evidence.location: Behind a bench in the amphitheater lawn
evidence.significance: Suggests Vedika and Rohan conspired and planned a handoff, implicating both.

evidence.description: Call log from Arjun’s phone showing an outgoing call to an unknown number at 8:30 PM that lasted 11 seconds. The number is unregistered but traced to a burner SIM used near the campus boundary.
evidence.location: Arjun’s phone records (obtained with permission after accusation)
evidence.significance: Appears to be Arjun contacting a co-conspirator during the heist.

evidence.description: A laminated campus ID card with Arjun’s photo but altered magnetic strip. Found taped under the lab desk.
evidence.significance: Used to clone Arjun’s biometric data via spoofing. Proves someone framed Arjun using his credentials.

evidence.description: Metadata from Vedika’s guest lecture video: the file creation timestamp is 8:00 PM, but camera power logs show the recording device was turned off at 8:12 PM and restarted at 8:27 PM. The 'continuity' was faked using editing software.
evidence.location: Camera system logs from Entrepreneurship Cell
evidence.significance: Proves Vedika was not at the lecture during the critical window and had time to access the lab.

evidence.description: Encrypted message fragment recovered from the Secure Research Vault server: '...trust V. She’ll reroute the log. Use D’s scan first...'
evidence.location: Cached in temporary memory of the vault’s authentication server
evidence.significance: Implies collaboration between Arjun and someone else (Rohan) to use Dr. Deshpande’s credentials, but suggests Vedika was the mastermind.

evidence.description: A night security guard reports seeing a student matching Rohan’s description entering the CS building via the basement service door at 8:43 PM, using a fake cleaning staff ID.
evidence.location: Security checkpoint log and verbal testimony
evidence.significance: Places Rohan at the scene, breaking his DJ night alibi.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Tech fest events begin across campus.
7:30 PM – Rohan is seen entering the amphitheater DJ night.
7:55 PM – Vedika begins her guest lecture at Entrepreneurship Cell.
8:00 PM – Vedika’s lecture officially starts (video timestamp).
8:12 PM – Camera at lecture hall powers off (logged in system).
8:30 PM – Arjun makes a brief call to a burner number.
8:32 PM – Dr. Deshpande’s biometric scan recorded at vault (later proved spoofed).
8:32:15–8:32:18 – CCTV footage gap in vault corridor.
8:33 PM – Arjun’s biometric scan appears in logs (entirely fabricated).
8:43 PM – Rohan seen entering CS building basement via service door.
8:45 PM – USB drive dropped near amphitheater (estimated from trash pickup logs).
9:00 PM – Vedika’s lecture video resumes (camcorder logs show restart).
9:30 PM – Vedika ends lecture and returns to dorm.
10:15 PM – AURA-7 reported missing during routine check.
red_herrings: The corrupted USB with the message from V to R suggests Vedika and Rohan double-crossed Arjun together.
Arjun’s call to a burner phone implies he was coordinating the theft.
Dr. Deshpande’s biometric scan makes him appear complicit or negligent.
Priya’s possession of the access algorithm hints at her involvement in the hack.

solution.method: Vedika used a spoofing device to mimic Dr. Deshpande’s biometric signature at 8:32 PM. During the 3-second CCTV gap, she entered the vault, removed AURA-7, and planted Arjun’s cloned ID under Deshpande’s desk. She then used a pre-recorded video loop to fake her lecture between 8:12 and 8:27, giving her a window to return. She tricked Rohan into showing up at 8:43 PM to retrieve a decoy, making him appear guilty, while she already had the real device hidden in a hollowed-out textbook.
solution.motive: She planned to sell AURA-7 to an overseas contact but needed to eliminate both Arjun and Rohan as loose ends. She used their partnership against them by feeding false information.
solution.proof: The camera power logs from the lecture hall contradict the video timestamp, proving she was absent during the heist. Combined with the cloned ID under Deshpande’s desk and the CCTV gap, only someone with high-level technical skills (like Vedika) could have orchestrated the spoofing and editing.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must notice the discrepancy in Vedika’s lecture timeline (camera off vs. video continuity). Then, cross-reference the 3-second CCTV gap with the spoofing capability mentioned in a forgotten lab manual. Realize the biometric log is forged because real systems don't allow back-to-back scans in 1 second. The USB is a red herring planted by Vedika to implicate Rohan. Arjun’s call was actually to report suspicion to authorities, cut short when he was drugged. Only Vedika had motive, means, opportunity, and the technical skill to execute the spoof-and-frame.

crime_type: crime that happened in the past being investigated now

case.title: The Case of the Buried Manuscript
case.setting: Delhi College of Engineering, Department of Humanities & Social Sciences (DHSS) basement archive
case.crime: Intellectual theft and sabotage involving a stolen unpublished manuscript from 20 years ago that resurfaces with damning alterations
case.victim: Dr. Arvind Mehta (deceased professor), posthumously discredited by a forged academic manuscript that invalidates his life's research

suspects.name: Isha Malhotra
suspects.personality: Intense, meticulous, socially awkward, fiercely loyal to academic integrity
suspects.motive: Her late father was Dr. Mehta’s protégé and was expelled due to the scandal; she seeks to restore his reputation
suspects.alibi: Was attending a late-night feminist theory webinar on Zoom; claims she never left her dorm
suspects.secret: She has been secretly rewriting her father’s banned thesis to resubmit under her name
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen breaking into the archive two nights before the manuscript was found, but claims she was just retrieving old notes

suspects.name: Professor Rajiv Khanna

suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a faculty banquet until 10:30 PM and then went straight home
suspects.secret: He plagiarized Mehta’s research for his first book, which launched his career

suspects.name: Nakul Desai
suspects.role: Third-year Computer Science student, part-time IT assistant for DHSS
suspects.personality: Quiet, tech-savvy, introverted, deeply interested in digital forensics
suspects.motive: His grandfather was Dr. Mehta’s lab assistant and lost his job unfairly; Nakul collects digital relics of academic injustices
suspects.alibi: Says he was fixing the server logs in the IT closet from 8 PM to 12 AM
suspects.secret: He has a hidden archive of digitized college cover-ups, including a corrupted copy of the original manuscript
