suspects.name: Zoya Qureshi
suspects.role: Adjunct lecturer in Modern Indian History
suspects.motive: She discovered the manuscript could make her famous if she 'uncovered' it first; stands to gain tenure and book deals
suspects.alibi: Claims she was meeting a journalist at a café until 11 PM
suspects.secret: She fabricated parts of her CV, including a fellowship she never completed
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Filed the official report about the manuscript's discovery but had already given an interview about it days prior

evidence.description: A decaying manila envelope labeled 'Project Kalki – Final Draft, 2003' containing a 120-page manuscript. The last five pages contain new data tables and conclusions that contradict Mehta’s published work, citing non-existent field studies.
evidence.location: Sealed behind a loose brick in the DHSS basement archive, found after a water leak revealed the cavity
evidence.significance: Purportedly Dr. Mehta’s final manuscript, now suggesting he fabricated his research. Used to discredit him posthumously.

evidence.description: Metadata from the scanned manuscript PDF shows it was first saved on April 12, 2023, with edits made in 12-minute intervals using a college IP address. The font is 'Charter BT', not commonly used in 2003.
evidence.location: College digital repository, uploaded by Zoya Qureshi
evidence.significance: Proves the manuscript was digitized recently, not found as-is. The editing pattern suggests automation or scripting.

evidence.description: A torn edge of tracing paper with faint pencil grid lines and a partial stamp: 'Approved: R.K. – Jan 14, 2003'. R.K. matches Professor Khanna’s initials.
evidence.location: Inside the manila envelope, tucked between pages 30 and 31
evidence.significance: Suggests Khanna approved part of the original manuscript, potentially linking him to early involvement or cover-up.

evidence.description: Server log fragment recovered by Nakul showing a file named 'Mehta_Kalki_Backup.7z' was accessed from an offline terminal on April 10, 2023, at 2:17 AM. The file was encrypted and deleted after access.
evidence.location: Recovered from backup tapes in the IT department
evidence.significance: Suggests someone accessed a long-hidden backup of the original manuscript before the 'discovery'. Links to Nakul’s access but doesn’t confirm guilt.

evidence.description: A night watchman reports seeing someone resembling Isha entering the archive at 1:00 AM on April 11, wearing a hoodie and carrying a flashlight. He did not stop her, assuming she was working late.
evidence.significance: Places Isha at the scene, but no video evidence exists due to camera malfunction.

evidence.description: A 2003 college calendar found in the archive, opened to January. A circled date (Jan 15) has 'Post-doc meeting – R.K. & A.M.' written in pencil. 'R.K.' is crossed out and 'Z.Q.' is written above it in different ink.
evidence.location: On a shelf near the hidden cavity
evidence.significance: Suggests timeline manipulation. Zoya wasn’t born in 2003—proves someone altered the calendar recently.

evidence.description: A hidden partition on Nakul’s personal drive contains a decrypted version of 'Mehta_Kalki_Backup.7z'. It includes the original manuscript without the forged pages and a log file showing the file was backed up by Dr. Mehta on January 16, 2003—the day before his sudden resignation.
evidence.location: Seized from Nakul’s laptop during investigation
evidence.significance: Authentic original manuscript exists. Proves the recovered version was altered after 2023.

timeline: 2003-01-14: Dr. Mehta submits final draft of 'Project Kalki' to Professor Khanna for review.
2003-01-15: 'Post-doc meeting' scheduled; Khanna cancels at last minute. Mehta resigns abruptly the next day.
2003-01-16: Mehta’s personal files are archived; original manuscript stored in physical form.
2023-04-10: File 'Mehta_Kalki_Backup.7z' accessed from offline terminal (IP logs trace to DHSS IT closet).
2023-04-11: Night watchman sees figure resembling Isha near archive. Camera malfunction reported.
2023-04-12: Water leak in basement exposes hidden cavity. Zoya 'discovers' the manuscript.
2023-04-12: Manuscript digitized; metadata shows creation on this date with Charter BT font.
2023-04-13: Zoya holds press conference alleging Mehta’s fraud.
2023-04-14: Nakul recovers server logs showing prior access.
2023-04-15: Calendared date alteration discovered during forensic sweep.
red_herrings: The torn tracing paper with Khanna's initials suggesting he approved the manuscript and may have suppressed it.
Isha’s presence near the archive, making her appear guilty of planting the fake.
Zoya’s premature press release, implying she stole and forged the manuscript.
The water leak being 'suspiciously convenient'—later confirmed as genuine pipe failure.

solution.method: In 2003, Khanna stole Mehta’s manuscript after rejecting his final draft. He buried it behind the archive wall to discredit Mehta later. In 2023, fearing renewed interest in Mehta’s work due to Isha’s research, Khanna accessed the college’s old offline terminal (which still held archive backups) to retrieve the original digital draft from a legacy drive. He added forged pages discrediting Mehta, printed it, and reburied the package. He then leaked the location to Zoya, hoping she’d 'find' it and discredit Mehta publicly.
solution.motive: Khanna built his career on Mehta’s ideas. If Mehta’s work were validated, Khanna would face exposure for plagiarism and career destruction.
solution.proof: The calendar with Zoya’s name added in modern ink proves recent tampering. The metadata shows the manuscript was created in 2023. Crucially, only someone with 20-year-old credentials (like Khanna) would know about the offline terminal and the original backup system. Additionally, the server logs show the terminal was accessed using a deprecated authentication token only Khanna had ever used.
solution.how_to_solve: The solver must: 1) Recognize the manuscript’s anachronisms (font, metadata); 2) Trace the access log to the offline terminal; 3) Cross-reference token usage with faculty from 2003; 4) Note that Khanna is the only one with access, motive, and knowledge of the archive’s hidden structure; 5) Realize the fake manuscript was planted to look discovered, not retrieved—only someone wanting it 'found' would go through such lengths. The altered calendar is the key that proves someone is fabricating a false history to implicate others, pointing to Khanna.

crime_type: false flag operation to frame innocent person

case.title: The Case of the Stolen Exam and the Framed Innocent
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay – Hacking Competition Server Room
case.crime: A high-stakes programming competition exam was leaked and anonymously posted online 12 hours before the event. The system logs falsely implicated the top-performing student, who was later found unconscious in the server room. An investigation reveals the leak was a false flag operation to frame him.
case.victim: Rohan Mehta – star computer science student accused of academic fraud and assault

suspects.name: Aarav Malhotra
suspects.motive: Rohan was likely to win the national coding championship, which Aarav had won the past two years and needed again for a coveted Google internship.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at an off-campus coding meetup from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM and has three friends who vouch for him.
suspects.secret: He has been using university servers to mine cryptocurrency under a fake research project.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: He was the first to report the leak and pushed hard for disciplinary action against Rohan.

suspects.name: Dr. Kavita Reddy
suspects.personality: Rigid, traditional, rule-obsessed, deeply skeptical of high-achieving students
suspects.motive: Believes Rohan is too arrogant and might have been cheating; wanted to expose him and restore academic integrity.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was grading assignments in her locked office from 6:30 PM to 10:30 PM. Security logs show her keycard accessed her office twice.
suspects.secret: She falsified research data in a recent paper and feared exposure if she lost funding due to a scandal in her department.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Immediately supported the evidence against Rohan and blocked his access to labs before due process.

suspects.name: Neha Desai
suspects.motive: Rohan rejected her romantic advances two months ago; she has been quietly resentful.
suspects.alibi: Says she was at the college library studying alone until 9:00 PM, then returned to her hostel.
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously running a deepfake blackmail operation on classmates using AI, stored on a hidden partition of her laptop.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near the server room at 8:47 PM by a janitor, though she denies being there.

suspects.name: Vikram Joshi
suspects.personality: Laid-back, sarcastic, brilliant with systems, dislikes unnecessary bureaucracy
suspects.motive: None apparent. But he had full access to all logs and systems.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at home streaming a gaming tournament online. His IP was active on Twitch from 7:00 PM to midnight.
suspects.secret: He once helped a student cover up a data breach for a fee and fears his job is at risk if anyone finds out.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Configured the digital trail that incriminated Rohan and was the one who ‘discovered’ it.

evidence.description: Server access logs show Rohan’s user ID accessed the encrypted exam file at 8:15 PM. The file was uploaded to a public GitHub repository at 8:22 PM from an IP traced to his dorm room.
evidence.significance: Strong digital evidence pointing to Rohan

evidence.description: A fingerprint on the server room’s interior keypad matches Rohan. The door requires keycard and PIN; logs show access at 8:10 PM using Vikram’s admin card.
evidence.significance: Suggests Rohan entered the room with someone’s help

evidence.description: A hidden script was found in the server’s cron jobs that automatically logs in as Rohan at certain times and mimics his access patterns. The script was created 48 hours before the leak.
evidence.location: Server backend (discovered by forensic IT team)
evidence.significance: Proves digital impersonation – Rohan was framed

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'Project Titan' was found in a trash bin near the server room. It contains encrypted data. When decrypted, it shows raw logs of multiple unauthorized access attempts from Aarav’s dorm IP.
evidence.location: Campus trash bin outside CS block
evidence.significance: Implicates Aarav in unauthorized access, possibly connected

evidence.description: A janitor recalls seeing Neha near the server room at 8:47 PM. She was wearing a red hoodie and carrying a backpack.
evidence.significance: Places Neha near the scene

evidence.description: Time-stamped CCTV from the server room hallway shows Vikram swiping in at 8:08 PM. The camera glitches for 3 minutes at 8:09–8:12 PM. Restoration shows a blurred figure exiting in a red hoodie.
evidence.significance: Suggests tampering and possible accomplice

evidence.description: A crumpled note in Rohan’s pocket reads: 'If I fail, everyone fails. I had no choice.' Handwriting analysis confirms it is his, but ink analysis shows it was written 24 hours before the incident.
evidence.significance: Suggests premeditation; actually used to imply guilt

timeline: 6:00 PM – Aarav attends coding meetup off-campus (witnessed by peers)
6:30 PM – Dr. Reddy logs into her office using keycard
7:00 PM – Vikram starts live-streaming on Twitch from home IP
7:45 PM – Neha checks into library Wi-Fi
8:08 PM – Vikram’s keycard used to enter server room (CCTV shows him)
8:09–8:12 PM – CCTV footage glitches in hallway
8:15 PM – Server logs show 'Rohan’s account' accessing exam file
8:22 PM – Exam uploaded to GitHub from IP traced to Rohan’s dorm
8:47 PM – Janitor sees Neha-like figure near server room
9:00 PM – Neha logs out of library Wi-Fi
9:15 PM – Rohan found unconscious in server room with head injury, 'suicide note' in pocket
9:30 PM – Dr. Reddy demands immediate suspension of Rohan
10:00 PM – Aarav tweets about 'cheaters being exposed'
red_herrings: The USB drive with Aarav’s IP logs – planted to mislead; Aarav did access servers for mining but not on the night of the leak
Neha seen near server room – the red hoodie is a common campus brand; Vikram used one to disguise himself
Rohan’s handwritten note – written during a previous stress episode after a failed project, not related to the exam
CCTV glitch – blamed on Neha, but actually caused by remote signal jammer from inside the server room

solution.method: Vikram used his admin access to plant a cron script that mimicked Rohan’s login at 8:15 PM. He used his own keycard to enter the server room at 8:08 PM, triggered a local Wi-Fi jammer to blind the CCTV for 3 minutes, uploaded the exam himself from a hidden admin terminal, and replaced Rohan’s exam file with a tampered version that logged the fake access. He then slipped out wearing a red hoodie to mimic Neha, knocked out Rohan (who arrived early to prep), and planted the pre-written note to make it look like a confession.
solution.motive: Vikram feared that if Rohan won the competition, he would expose Vikram’s past cover-up of a data breach during a project review. He needed to discredit Rohan permanently.
solution.proof: The cron script with Vikram’s unique coding signature (a rare indentation style and comment syntax) and the jammer’s activation log tied to Vikram’s admin terminal. Additionally, the Twitch stream was a pre-recorded loop; his home router showed no outbound data during the 8:00–8:30 PM window.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. The server logs 'Rohan’s access' are invalid if a cron script exists – find it. 2. CCTV glitch during access window suggests inside job. 3. Only Vikram had ability to plant the script and bypass monitoring. 4. Twitch alibi fails when router logs show no real upload bandwidth. 5. Script’s coding style matches Vikram’s past work in university repositories. 6. Jammer activated from admin terminal, logged under Vikram’s credentials. 7. Planting the old note required intimate knowledge of Rohan’s personal history – accessible through academic records Vikram could view.

crime_type: multiple crimes by different people same night

case.title: The Case of the Triple Lockdown
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay, Mumbai
case.crime: Theft of the national cybersecurity algorithm, poisoning of a professor's coffee, and sabotage of the final-year AI project server
case.victim: Dr. Anil Mehta (poisoned), the National Cybersecurity Council (algorithm stolen), and 120 final-year students (project data corrupted)

suspects.name: Kavya Nair
suspects.motive: Resents Dr. Mehta for blocking her research grant; needed the algorithm to prove her AI model's superiority
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library working on her thesis from 6 PM to 11 PM
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing controversial AI ethics critiques under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her laptop was seen accessing the server logs remotely during the blackout, though she claims it was automatic sync

suspects.name: Rohan Deshpande
suspects.motive: Failed Dr. Mehta’s course and faced academic probation; wanted to sabotage exams by corrupting project backups
suspects.alibi: Says he was at a late-night street food stall with friends until 9:30 PM, then went straight to dorm
suspects.secret: He was using college servers to mine cryptocurrency, which would have been exposed during server audit
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was caught near the server room 10 minutes before the blackout with a USB drive

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Malhotra
suspects.motive: Wanted Dr. Mehta removed to secure his research position and funding for herself
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in her office grading papers; security camera shows her entering at 6:45 PM and leaving at 10:10 PM
suspects.secret: She had been leaking college data to a private tech firm for personal gain
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Sent an encrypted email to an unknown recipient minutes after the poisoning was discovered

suspects.name: Vikram Singh
suspects.motive: Was blackmailed by a foreign agent to steal the algorithm; afraid of exposing his undocumented brother
suspects.alibi: Says he was fixing the HVAC system in the basement from 7 PM to 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: Has a criminal record for hacking in his first year, expunged due to national service
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen wiping down the coffee machine with unusual urgency post-incident

evidence.description: A half-empty thermos of black coffee with traces of atropine found on Dr. Mehta’s desk. A faint lipstick mark on the rim.
evidence.significance: Confirms poisoning. Lipstick matches Kavya’s brand, but she denies being in the office.

evidence.description: Server access log showing a login from Kavya’s account at 9:42 PM, but her laptop was in sleep mode according to power logs.
evidence.significance: Suggests remote access or account compromise.

evidence.description: A custom USB drive with cryptocurrency mining scripts and a hidden partition containing fragments of the stolen algorithm.
evidence.location: Under a floor tile near the server room
evidence.significance: Links Rohan to both server tampering and potential theft.

evidence.description: Encrypted email from Dr. Malhotra to 'ProjectSaffron' with subject 'Phase 2 initiated' sent at 9:15 PM.
evidence.location: Recovered from deleted drafts via forensic restore
evidence.significance: Suggests conspiracy, but 'ProjectSaffron' turns out to be her private skincare blog.

evidence.description: HVAC maintenance logbook with Vikram’s signature, but the entry time (7:00–10:30 PM) overlaps with the blackout (8:55–9:10 PM).
evidence.significance: He couldn’t have been in two places at once unless the log was falsified.

evidence.description: Surveillance footage showing Vikram entering the server room at 8:50 PM, wearing technician’s uniform, swiping with valid access.
evidence.location: Server room security cam (backup battery feed)
evidence.significance: Proves he accessed the server during vulnerable window.

evidence.description: A small packet of atropine pills in the trash bin of the staff restroom, labeled with a foreign pharmaceutical logo.
evidence.significance: Matches poison used. Only Vikram had access to imported meds via black market connections.

timeline: 6:00 PM: College gates locked for night. Dr. Mehta last seen alive in his office.
6:45 PM: Dr. Malhotra enters her office (confirmed by camera).
7:00 PM: Vikram signs into HVAC maintenance log.
7:30 PM: Rohan and friends leave street food stall (verified by CCTV).
8:45 PM: Kavya checks out a book at library front desk.
8:50 PM: Vikram appears on server room camera.
8:55 PM: Power failure affects Building C (CS department). Backup generator fails to activate.
8:58 PM: Server logs show unauthorized access and initiation of data wipe.
9:00 PM: Unknown device downloads 98% of the cybersecurity algorithm via internal network.
9:05 PM: Dr. Mehta drinks coffee, collapses 10 minutes later.
9:10 PM: Power restored. Generator logs show manual override disabled.
9:15 PM: Dr. Malhotra sends encrypted email.
9:42 PM: Kavya’s account logs into server (later proven spoofed).
10:10 PM: Dr. Malhotra exits building.
10:30 PM: Vikram clocks out at security desk.
red_herrings: Lipstick on the coffee thermos — Kavya’s brand, but she was framed.
Rohan’s USB drive — planted to mislead; he lost it days earlier.
Dr. Malhotra’s encrypted email — unrelated to the crimes.
Kavya’s remote login — spoofed using her authenticated session cookie stolen via phishing page mimicking college login.

solution.method: Used HVAC access to disable server room cooling, triggering automatic fail-safe reboot. During reboot, he physically accessed the server, installed a rogue script to wipe student data and exfiltrate the algorithm via hidden network tunnel. Earlier, he laced Dr. Mehta’s coffee with atropine, knowing he always refilled at 9 PM.
solution.motive: Blackmailed by a foreign intelligence group to steal the algorithm; killing Dr. Mehta was to create chaos and divert suspicion from the theft.
solution.proof: Surveillance footage of him in server room, HVAC log inconsistency, atropine packet with foreign label matching his brother’s medication source, and network logs showing data exfiltration from a MAC address cloned from his work device.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Cross-reference HVAC log with security footage — Vikram couldn't be in basement and server room at once unless log was faked. 2. Generator override required physical switch — only technicians could access. 3. Atropine source traces to black-market supplier linked to Vikram’s brother. 4. Server access was physical, not remote — only Vikram had both access and technical skill. 5. Spoofed login was distraction — real data leak occurred at 9:00 PM via direct connection. 6. Lipstick was planted — Kavya never entered office. 7. All suspects had motives, but only Vikram had access, opportunity, and technical means to execute all three crimes simultaneously.

crime_type: crime involving twins with perfect alibis

case.title: The Case of the Twin Alibis
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay - Final Exam Week
case.crime: Sabotage of the National Cybersecurity Aptitude Test (NCAT) server during live exam, resulting in data corruption and disqualification of top candidates
case.victim: National Cybersecurity Aptitude Test (NCAT) and 475 students, particularly the top contenders

suspects.name: Arjun Mehra
suspects.motive: Was disqualified last year due to a technical glitch; seeks revenge and a second chance by invalidating current results
suspects.alibi: Was seen in the library’s 24-hour study lounge from 8 PM to 1 AM, verified by two friends and facial recognition logs
suspects.secret: Has an undiagnosed anxiety disorder that causes memory lapses under stress
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Nervous during questioning; hesitated when asked about his whereabouts at 10:45 PM

suspects.name: Dr. Ananya Iyer
suspects.motive: Believes the NCAT promotes rote learning and harms creativity; wants to expose flaws in national testing systems
suspects.alibi: Hosted a live-streamed faculty Q&A from her office between 8 PM and 10:30 PM; verified by 200+ student logins
suspects.secret: Was anonymously publishing scathing critiques of the NCAT on an academic blog under a pseudonym
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Volunteered to lead the investigation, subtly downplaying digital forensics

suspects.name: Rohan and Sohan Kapoor
suspects.motive: Wanted to discredit the system to protest biased selection; also enjoy creating uncrackable puzzles
suspects.alibi: Both were captured on CCTV entering separate exam halls at 9 PM. Rohan in Hall A, Sohan in Hall B. Both remained until 10:45 PM, confirmed by proctors and facial recognition
suspects.secret: They had been swapping identities since first year using forged biometric tokens to take each other’s exams
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Too calm during investigation; kept making cryptic jokes about 'mirror images' and 'duality'

evidence.description: Server access log shows login from Dr. Iyer’s account at 10:12 PM with a malformed SSH key that triggered an admin override. The session lasted 3 minutes and executed a root-level wipe command.
evidence.location: NCAT server log file, backed up on offsite cloud
evidence.significance: Indicates insider access with elevated privileges; only faculty and two TAs have such access.

evidence.description: A USB drive labeled 'Final Project' found in a trash bin near the server room. Contains a Python script that replicates the wipe command and is coded in a style matching Arjun’s past submissions.
evidence.location: Waste bin outside server access corridor
evidence.significance: Ties Arjun to the sabotage; code has his unique formatting and comments.

evidence.description: Timestamped packet capture showing an out-of-band signal sent from Hall B to the server room at 10:13 PM via the college’s IoT network. Signal mimicked a system maintenance command.
evidence.location: Network traffic logs from IT department
evidence.significance: Proves remote activation from Hall B, where Sohan was seated.

evidence.description: Library security guard recalls Arjun stepping out briefly at 10:00 PM to 'make a call' and returning at 10:20 PM, using the old landline near the back exit.
evidence.significance: Creates a 20-minute gap in Arjun’s alibi.

evidence.description: A pair of RFID cloning gloves (used to spoof biometric badges) discovered hidden inside a hollowed-out computer science textbook in the twins’ shared dorm room.
evidence.significance: Proof of sophisticated identity deception capability.

evidence.description: Facial recognition log discrepancy: the system logged 'Sohan Kapoor' entering Hall B at 9:00 PM, but thermal imaging from hallway cameras shows the person had 0.6°C lower body temperature than Sohan’s medical profile.
evidence.significance: Suggests facial recognition was fooled; the person entering Hall B was not Sohan.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing someone in a lab coat entering the server room at 10:10 PM using a faculty swipe card. Describes the person as tall, with curly hair like Dr. Iyer.
evidence.significance: Points to Dr. Iyer being physically present at the scene.

timeline: 8:00 PM - NCAT exam begins; all students report in; servers operational.
8:00 PM - 10:30 PM - Dr. Iyer’s live Q&A stream runs uninterrupted.
9:00 PM - CCTV shows Rohan entering Hall A; facial recognition confirms identity. Simultaneously, Sohan enters Hall B; identity confirmed.
10:12 PM - Server logs show admin login from Dr. Iyer’s account.
10:13 PM - Wipe command executed; network logs show signal sent from Hall B.
10:15 PM - Server goes offline; proctors report exam freeze.
10:18 PM - Twin from Hall B raises hand to report connectivity issue, verified by proctor.
10:20 PM - Arjun returns to library after phone call.
10:30 PM - Emergency IT team alerted; initial investigation begins.
11:00 PM - Janitor sees lab-coated figure enter server room (later confirmed to be after damage was done).
red_herrings: The USB drive planted to implicate Arjun
Server login from Dr. Iyer’s account
Janitor’s sighting of a figure resembling Dr. Iyer
Arjun’s gap in alibi and anxiety-induced memory lapse
Dr. Iyer’s public criticism of the NCAT

solution.method: The twins used biometric spoofing gloves to swap identities before exams. Rohan entered Hall B as Sohan at 9:00 PM, while real Sohan went to the server room access corridor. Using a cloned faculty RFID and a pre-programmed IoT signal from a concealed Raspberry Pi, Sohan triggered the wipe command from outside the server room at 10:13 PM. Rohan remained in Hall B, maintaining Sohan’s alibi. The server login used Dr. Iyer’s credentials, which were obtained via a phishing script the twins had earlier installed on her machine under the guise of a 'security patch'.
solution.motive: To protest the high-pressure, mechanistic nature of national exams and prove that even 'perfect' systems can be fooled by human ingenuity.
solution.proof: The thermal imaging mismatch proves the person in Hall B was not Sohan. Network logs show the IoT signal originated from a device with a MAC address linked to a Raspberry Pi found in Sohan’s water bottle. The phishing log on Dr. Iyer’s laptop shows keystroke capture from March, including her credentials. The twins’ gloves confirm their capability to spoof access. Arjun’s USB was planted using code copied from his public GitHub.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Note the twins’ alibis are perfect because they are based on facial recognition, which can be spoofed. 2. Use the thermal discrepancy to prove identity fraud. 3. Trace IoT packet source to physical device. 4. Cross-reference RFID cloning gloves with server room access timing. 5. Verify Dr. Iyer’s login was from a remote machine, not her physical location. 6. Dismiss Arjun’s phone gap as irrelevant due to distance and lack of signal path. 7. Realize the sabotage didn’t require physical server access—only a spoofed IoT command. 8. Conclude that the only suspects with motive, skills, and means to spoof biometrics and exploit IoT are the twins working in tandem.

case.title: The Case of the Vanishing Transcript
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay
case.crime: Digital manipulation of final semester academic records leading to wrongful expulsion of a top student
case.victim: Aarav Mehta, a third-year Computer Science student with a perfect GPA

suspects.name: Priya Deshmukh
suspects.personality: Ambitious, socially isolated, highly analytical, emotionally guarded
suspects.motive: Priya was second in the batch and stood to gain the top rank—and a prestigious Google India internship—if Aarav was removed from contention
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library from 8 PM to 11 PM studying for the algorithms exam
suspects.secret: She has been anonymously publishing cutting-edge ML research under a pseudonym to avoid academic scrutiny due to imposter syndrome
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her login history shows access to the departmental server during the time of the breach, which she claims was for backing up her personal projects

suspects.name: Professor Rajan Iyer
suspects.personality: Traditional, tech-averse, authoritative, deeply biased toward legacy academic performance
suspects.motive: Aarav had publicly criticized Professor Iyer's outdated teaching methods in a student feedback portal, which went viral internally
suspects.alibi: Says he was at home grading papers and watching a cricket match alone
suspects.secret: He has been falsifying his research grant utilization reports to cover up personal expenses
suspects.suspicious_behavior: He was the only one with permanent admin privileges on the legacy student database system, which was used in the breach

suspects.name: Arjun Malhotra
suspects.motive: Arjun's father is a major donor to the college and expected Arjun to rank first; Aarav's success embarrassed him
suspects.alibi: Claims he was at a late-night rooftop party in Andheri with friends
suspects.secret: He has been using deepfake technology to impersonate professors and reschedule exams to buy more prep time
suspects.suspicious_behavior: His phone GPS placed him near campus between 9:30 PM and 10:00 PM on the night of the breach, contradicting his alibi

suspects.name: Neha Rao
suspects.motive: None apparent; she was one of Aarav’s closest allies and helped him with coding assignments
suspects.alibi: Was volunteering at a night shelter in Dharavi from 7 PM to 10:30 PM
suspects.secret: She suffers from chronic insomnia and often browses dark web forums for nootropic drugs to stay awake
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her device was used to access the student database remotely, though she claims it was stolen the previous week

evidence.description: Log file fragment showing SSH access to the department server at 9:47 PM via IP address 10.3.7.209, using a compromised TA account. The session lasted 6 minutes and executed a script titled 'transcript_wipe.py'.
evidence.location: Server log backup drive, decrypted with forensic tools
evidence.significance: Direct evidence of unauthorized access during the breach window.

evidence.description: A USB drive found in a trash bin near Lab 3 containing a Python script that modifies grade records and erases access logs using a custom encryption key.
evidence.significance: Appears to be the tool used in the crime; linked via metadata to Arjun Malhotra’s laptop.

evidence.description: A handwritten note in Hindi found crumpled in the server room trash: 'System password: jai_shri_ram_2024' with a sketch of a firewall.
evidence.significance: Suggests an insider used a weak password to gain access.

evidence.description: Night security guard Vinod Patil reports seeing a student in a blue hoodie entering the server room at 9:30 PM but cannot identify the face.
evidence.significance: Indicates possible physical access to restricted area.

evidence.description: Dark web log extract showing login from Neha Rao’s registered device to a hacking forum 'SilentByte' two days before the breach. Forum post titled 'How to mask SSH through proxy chains?'
evidence.location: Recovered from cloud backup of Neha’s old phone
evidence.significance: Suggests knowledge of advanced hacking techniques.

evidence.description: Metadata from the server access log shows the 'transcript_wipe.py' script was compiled using Python 3.11 and included a debugging tag '@dev: priya_debug_03'.
evidence.location: Decompiled script from server memory dump
evidence.significance: Links the script directly to Priya’s development environment.

evidence.description: GPS breadcrumb trail from Arjun Malhotra’s phone shows it pinging near campus at 9:35 PM, then vanishing until 10:15 PM.
evidence.location: Phone location history pulled with court order
evidence.significance: Breaks alibi, but doesn’t prove direct involvement.

timeline: 6:00 PM: Aarav submits final AI project via college portal.
7:15 PM: Neha Rao leaves campus for night shelter volunteer work.
8:00 PM: Priya logs into library Wi-Fi; Arjun arrives at rooftop party (claimed).
9:30 PM: Security guard reports figure in blue hoodie near server room.
9:47 PM: SSH access from IP 10.3.7.209 to department server; execution of transcript_wipe.py.
9:53 PM: Session ends; logs partially altered.
10:00 PM: Arjun’s phone GPS goes offline near IIT gate.
10:30 PM: Neha returns to campus briefly to retrieve forgotten bag (CCTV shows her entering through south gate).
11:00 PM: System audit detects anomaly in grade database; alert flagged.
Next morning: Aarav is summoned and expelled based on 'academic dishonesty' flag in altered records.
red_herrings: The USB drive in Lab 3 was planted to frame Arjun.
The Hindi note with password was left intentionally to suggest a low-tech breach and implicate a careless insider.
Neha’s dark web activity suggests hacking knowledge, but the posts were research for a cybersecurity thesis.
Arjun’s GPS data suggests guilt, but his phone was handed to an accomplice to distract from Priya’s remotely executed script.

solution.method: Priya used a proxy chain from the library’s public Wi-Fi to route her connection through three international servers, masking her real IP. She accessed the system using Neha Rao’s previously leaked credentials (obtained from a phishing email she sent disguised as an IT update). She executed a custom script that altered Aarav’s transcript and injected false entries to frame others, including planting metadata pointing toward Arjun and leaving the USB drive via a janitor she paid anonymously.
solution.motive: To secure the top rank and the Google India internship, which was promised to the batch topper. She believed Aarav’s expulsion would make her the automatic candidate.
solution.proof: The debugging tag '@dev: priya_debug_03' in the compiled script matches a private GitHub repository under her pseudonym, which was discovered through blockchain analysis of her anonymous research paper submissions. The repository contains version history of the script used in the attack.
solution.how_to_solve: The investigator must: (1) Cross-reference the script’s debugging tag with public repositories using academic paper metadata; (2) Verify that the SSH session’s proxy origin can be traced via packet timing analysis to the library’s network; (3) Dismiss the USB and password note as too obvious; (4) Confirm that Neha’s device was indeed stolen and used without her knowledge; (5) Realize that Arjun’s GPS gap aligns with a known signal dead zone, but the timing doesn’t match the 6-minute breach window. Only Priya had both motive, technical skill, and access during the critical time.

case.title: The Case of the Fractured Merit
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Bombay – Main Computing Lab
case.crime: Sabotage of the National AI Ethics Competition submission by tampering with the core algorithm 24 hours before the national deadline
case.victim: Project 'Aarambh' – a student team's AI model designed to predict regional drought using satellite data, which was disqualified due to corrupted code

suspects.name: Arnav Mehta
suspects.personality: brilliant but arrogant, overly competitive, socially isolated, perfectionist
suspects.motive: His own competing AI project was eliminated in internal selection; resents the winning team for beating him
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been coding alone in the library basement server room from 8 PM to 1 AM
suspects.secret: He plagiarized part of his eliminated project from a foreign research paper
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the secure Git repository with admin privileges the night before the sabotage

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Nair
suspects.motive: Wanted her other team, 'Project Vayu', to represent the college nationally to boost her research grant prospects
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at a faculty dinner until 10 PM, then working from home; has video call logs with a colleague at 11:30 PM
suspects.secret: She falsified publication credits on a recent paper co-authored with a senior professor
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Approved anomalous administrative access to 'Project Aarambh' repository for someone not on the team

suspects.name: Kavya Deshpande
suspects.role: third-year student and team lead of Project Aarambh
suspects.personality: idealistic, passionate, stubborn, hides anxiety behind leadership
suspects.motive: If the project fails, her scholarship may be revoked due to lack of 'national impact showcase'
suspects.alibi: Says she was at a student senate meeting until 9:30 PM, then went straight to her hostel room
suspects.secret: She secretly rewrote 40% of the core algorithm without telling her team, fearing her mentor would block submission due to 'unproven methodology'
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Made a last-minute commit to the repo at 10:47 PM – the same time the corruption was logged

suspects.name: Rohan Malhotra
suspects.personality: quiet, anxious, dutiful, seeks approval, easily influenced
suspects.motive: Feared being fired for missing a critical server update that could have caused data loss
suspects.alibi: Says he was fixing a network outage in the admin wing from 9 PM to 12 AM
suspects.secret: He disabled automated backups for 48 hours to hide a server misconfiguration he caused
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Log shows he accessed the Git server remotely at 10:32 PM using a backdoor tool – rare for routine maintenance

evidence.description: Git commit log shows a malicious code injection at 10:45 PM that introduced a fatal data-loop flaw. Commit was made under Kavya Deshpande’s credentials but from an IP not linked to her device.
evidence.significance: Suggests either Kavya sabotaged her own project, or someone impersonated her access.

evidence.description: Remote SSH access log shows Rohan’s admin account logged in from an external IP at 10:32 PM, executing a script that altered file permissions on the Git repo.
evidence.significance: Strong indication of Rohan’s involvement in unauthorized access.

evidence.description: A handwritten note found crumpled in a trash bin near the server room: 'They’ll never suspect a mentor. Nair knows the review panel. One flaw and it’s over.'
evidence.location: East stairwell of CS building, near server access point
evidence.significance: Implicates Dr. Nair in a sabotage plot.

evidence.description: Dr. Nair’s video call timestamped 11:30 PM with Professor Kapoor—but the background shows her office, which has a dual-monitor setup. Only one monitor is visible in the call.
evidence.location: Zoom meeting recording provided by Dr. Nair
evidence.significance: Suggests the call may have been pre-recorded or staged, casting doubt on her alibi.

evidence.description: Wi-Fi access logs show Arnav’s phone connected to the main lab’s secure network at 10:38 PM – despite the lab being locked and requiring RFID + password to enter.
evidence.significance: Indicates Arnav was physically near the lab or spoofed his device location.

evidence.description: Night guard Ramesh reports seeing someone in a maintenance uniform entering the lab at 10:20 PM with a keycard labeled 'R. Malhotra'.
evidence.significance: Supports that Rohan’s access was used, but doesn't confirm identity.

evidence.description: Analysis of the corrupted code reveals it uses a cryptographic hash technique only documented in Dr. Nair’s unpublished research draft—leaked internally last month.
evidence.location: Code forensics report by external auditor
evidence.significance: Only someone with access to her private research could have used this method—points to inside knowledge.

timeline: 6:00 PM – Project Aarambh makes final successful test run.
7:30 PM – Faculty dinner begins; Dr. Nair attends with colleagues.
8:00 PM – Arnav logs into server room with keycard; library security logs confirm entry.
8:45 PM – Kavya attends student senate meeting in admin block; 10 witnesses confirm presence.
9:00 PM – Rohan reports network issues; begins remote maintenance.
9:30 PM – Kavya leaves meeting; heads toward hostel.
9:45 PM – Dr. Nair leaves dinner; claims to go home.
10:20 PM – Security guard sees figure in maintenance uniform enter CS lab with keycard.
10:32 PM – Rohan’s account logs into Git server via SSH from external IP.
10:38 PM – Arnav’s phone connects to secure lab Wi-Fi.
10:45 PM – Malicious commit pushed to Project Aarambh repo.
10:47 PM – Kavya makes a legitimate (but failed) commit attempt from her phone.
11:30 PM – Dr. Nair’s video call with colleague recorded.
1:00 AM – Arnav logs out of server room.
red_herrings: The handwritten note implicating Dr. Nair was written on paper from Rohan’s lab notepad.
Arnav’s Wi-Fi connection was spoofed using a rogue access point setup by Rohan.
Kavya’s 10:47 PM commit attempt failed because the repo was already corrupted—making it look like she tried to cover her tracks.
Rohan’s SSH access was part of an automated script triggered remotely—his credentials were stolen.

solution.method: Used her administrative override to grant temporary access to a fake 'maintenance bot' account, then remotely triggered a script from a university-owned server (under her control) that injected the corrupted code using a hash algorithm from her private research. She scheduled the script to run at 10:45 PM and masked execution under Rohan’s compromised credentials via a proxy server. The maintenance uniform seen by the guard was worn by a custodial worker she bribed to deliver a USB containing the trigger code to the lab earlier.
solution.motive: To ensure her favored team, Project Vayu, represented the institute nationally, thereby increasing her chances of winning a major AI ethics grant from the Ministry of Education.
solution.proof: The cryptographic hash signature in the corrupted code exactly matches a unique variant in Dr. Nair’s unpublished draft, which was only shared with three people—none of whom had Git access. Additionally, server logs show the script was initiated from a virtual machine registered under her research grant.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Dismiss the handwritten note—paper source traces to Rohan, but he has no motive to frame Dr. Nair. 2. Rohan’s SSH log is spoofed—his account was phished via a fake admin portal email sent at 9:15 PM (verified in his trash folder). 3. Arnav’s Wi-Fi login is a red herring—his device was cloned via a rogue AP set up by Rohan, who later admitted to the spoof under pressure but claimed he thought it was a prank. 4. Kavya’s failed commit proves she didn’t cause the corruption—she couldn’t push after 10:45. 5. Dr. Nair’s video call shows only one monitor—her office has two; she faked the call. 6. The code’s hash is the key: it’s from her private research. Only she could have embedded it. 7. Combined: she had means (admin access), opportunity (no verified alibi post-9:45), unique knowledge (hash), and motive (grant incentive).

case.title: The Case of the Reversed Deadline
case.setting: Department of Computer Science, IIT Madras – Kharagpur Campus Annex
case.crime: Sabotage of the National AI Olympiad submission server 48 hours before the deadline, resulting in corrupted entries from 17 teams, including the favorite IITM 'Neural Rebels'.
case.victim: The National AI Olympiad organizing committee and competing student teams

suspects.name: Aarav Mehta
suspects.personality: Brilliant but arrogant, competitive, socially isolated, perfectionist
suspects.motive: His team's entry was flagged for plagiarism hours before the crash; he wanted to erase all submissions to delay the contest and clear his name.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been in the library studying for an algorithms final from 7:00 PM to 11:30 PM.
suspects.secret: He plagiarized part of his code from an open-source GitHub repository.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen accessing the server room’s external vent on security footage at 8:47 PM, wearing a hooded jacket.

suspects.name: Dr. Priya Venkatesh
suspects.personality: Strict, principled, emotionally reserved, deeply ethical
suspects.motive: She discovered the Olympiad’s lead judge was her ex-husband, who ruined her academic reputation years ago; she wanted to sabotage the event without trace.
suspects.alibi: Hosting a post-lecture dinner with three colleagues at her apartment from 7:15 PM to 10:00 PM.
suspects.secret: She submitted a paper under a pseudonym that was accepted at the same conference the Olympiad winners would attend.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Searched 'how to corrupt PostgreSQL databases without root access' two days prior to the incident.

suspects.name: Nandini Patel
suspects.personality: Charismatic, manipulative, ambitious,善于 deceit (skilled in deception)
suspects.motive: Her team was disqualified for using unauthorized data, and she wanted revenge by ensuring no one could win.
suspects.alibi: Posted a live Instagram story from the college canteen at 8:30 PM and stayed there until 9:45 PM.
suspects.secret: She is running an unauthorized side-business selling AI-generated research abstracts to students.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Her laptop shows a remote SSH connection to the server at 8:52 PM from a spoofed IP.

suspects.name: Rohan Deshmukh
suspects.motive: None apparent; however, he had full access to the server room and logs.
suspects.alibi: Clock-in shows he left the lab at 6:45 PM. Claims to have gone straight home.
suspects.secret: He has been secretly dating a student on one of the affected teams and helped her fix code the night before.
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Failed to report a broken server room door latch for three days, despite maintenance logs showing he checked it.

evidence.description: A single black glove found near the server room's ceiling vent, made of thermal-resistant material, size small.
evidence.location: Below the eastern air vent in Server Room B
evidence.significance: Matches the type used in robotics labs; Aarav was seen wearing a similar pair during a robotics club meeting.

evidence.description: SSH log showing a login from IP 10.4.16.203 at 8:52 PM, executing a script named 'clean_submissions.sh'. The IP resolves to a router in the student dorm.
evidence.significance: Time-stamped during the attack; script deleted immediately after execution.

evidence.description: Metadata from the corrupted database dump shows the damage began exactly at 8:53:17 PM, but the last valid backup was overwritten at 8:51:02 PM – two minutes before the attack.
evidence.significance: Proves the sabotage was premeditated and required access before the actual crash – the attack was set to trigger after backup deletion.

evidence.description: A janitor reports seeing a person in a lab coat entering the server room at 8:40 PM using a keycard. Described as 'short, wearing glasses'.
evidence.significance: Dr. Venkatesh matches the description; Rohan does not wear glasses.

evidence.description: A sticky note in the server room trash bin with handwritten hexadecimal code: '4B 45 59 34 45 4E 44'. When decoded: 'KEY4END'.
evidence.significance: Refers to a hidden decryption key used in a staged rollback script; the attack was designed to look like a crash but was a controlled wipe.

evidence.description: Nandini’s Instagram story geotag shows canteen location, but metadata analysis reveals the video was pre-recorded and uploaded via automated script at 8:30 PM.
evidence.significance: Her alibi is fabricated; she was not in the canteen at the time.

evidence.description: Hidden partition on Rohan’s work USB drive contains a copy of the 'clean_submissions.sh' script and logs of the backup deletion at 8:51:02 PM.
evidence.location: Forensic image of USB found in lost-and-found
evidence.significance: Proves he executed the backup deletion, which was the critical step – the SSH attack was a decoy.

timeline: 6:45 PM – Rohan clocks out, seen leaving campus on main gate camera.
7:00 PM – Aarav enters library; confirmed by facial recognition on entry logs.
7:15 PM – Dr. Venkatesh begins dinner with colleagues; confirmed by three witnesses.
8:30 PM – Nandini’s Instagram story posted (later proven pre-recorded).
8:40 PM – Janitor sees person in lab coat enter server room with keycard.
8:47 PM – Security cam shows figure in hooded jacket near server room vent (Aarav).
8:51:02 PM – Last valid backup deleted; logged under Rohan’s admin privileges.
8:52 PM – SSH login from spoofed IP executes script (decoy attack).
8:53:17 PM – Database corruption begins, timestamped by system logs.
9:00 PM – Nandini arrives at canteen, confirmed by staff.
9:45 PM – Dr. Venkatesh’s guests leave her apartment.
10:00 PM – Aarav leaves library.
red_herrings: Aarav’s presence at the vent suggests physical tampering.
SSH login from dorm IP appears to be the attack vector.
Dr. Venkatesh’s search history implies malicious intent.
Nandini’s spoofed IP and fake alibi point to her as mastermind.

solution.method: Used his technician access to delete the last backup at 8:51:02 PM, then triggered a pre-planted script via local execution that activated at 8:53:17 PM. The SSH login was a spoofed decoy to mislead investigators.
solution.motive: His girlfriend’s team was unfairly disqualified due to a technicality, and he believed the only way to restore fairness was to nullify all entries.
solution.proof: The hidden USB with the script and logs; backup deletion occurred before the SSH login, and only Rohan had both the access and opportunity during the gap between 6:45 PM and 8:51 PM, as he never actually left – he re-entered via the maintenance tunnel.
solution.how_to_solve: 1. Note that the backup was deleted *before* the attack (8:51:02 PM vs. 8:53:17 PM), meaning the real sabotage was the deletion, not the script. 2. The SSH login is a red herring; spoofed IP and timing prove it's a decoy. 3. Rohan is the only one with legitimate access to delete backups. 4. His alibi is weak – no proof after 6:45 PM. 5. The USB in lost-and-found (logged at 10:10 PM) was reported missing earlier that day – he must have used it after hours. 6. Janitor’s 'lab coat' sighting fits Rohan’s role. 7. The 'KEY4END' note matches a decryption key in the script on his USB. Logical conclusion: Rohan executed the critical step, making him the true culprit.

case.title: The Case of the Shattered Syllabus
case.setting: Delhi Institute of Advanced Learning (DIAL), Computer Science Department - Professor Meera Kapoor's office and adjacent lab corridor
case.crime: Sabotage of final exam papers and theft of the master answer key prior to the Operating Systems examination, resulting in the destruction of 45 physical exam booklets and digital encryption of the backup server
case.victim: Professor Meera Kapoor, senior faculty member; academic integrity of DIAL; 45 students whose exams were destroyed

suspects.name: Aryan Malhotra
suspects.motive: Failed mid-term; overheard professor saying he might not pass unless he aces finals; desperate to avoid academic probation
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the college library’s 24-hour study zone from 8:00 PM to 1:00 AM, alone at a table near the stacks
suspects.secret: He has been cheating on assignments using a ghostwriter from an online service; terrified of exposure
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was seen near Professor Kapoor’s office at 7:45 PM arguing with her earlier that day

suspects.name: Dr. Nalini Deshpande
suspects.motive: Long-standing professional rivalry with Meera; recently passed over for department chair in Meera’s favor
suspects.alibi: Claims she was conducting a video conference with an international collaborator from 8:30 PM to 10:30 PM and then grading papers in her home office (off-campus)
suspects.secret: She plagiarized a section of her recent paper; Meera was reviewing it for journal submission and might have discovered it
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Asked unusually specific questions about the exam format the day before

suspects.name: Rohan Patel
suspects.motive: Was reprimanded by Professor Kapoor for letting students access restricted lab software; fears losing his paid position
suspects.alibi: Says he left the lab at 7:30 PM and went to meet friends at a café off-campus; has three friends who corroborate arrival at 8:15 PM
suspects.secret: He disabled the lab’s motion sensor for 15 minutes to sneak his girlfriend into the lab earlier that week; afraid of disciplinary action
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Had master access to the lab and office security system; admitted to forgetting his ID badge that evening

suspects.name: Priya Iyer
suspects.role: PhD candidate, teaching assistant for the course
suspects.motive: Spent months helping compile the exam; felt slighted when Professor Kapoor didn’t credit her in the syllabus update
suspects.alibi: Says she was at her parents’ home in Noida, 30 minutes away; no one saw her after she left campus at 6:45 PM
suspects.secret: She has been secretly applying for academic positions abroad to escape her family’s pressure to marry; hasn’t told her advisor
suspects.suspicious_behavior: Was the last person seen entering the office at 6:50 PM to drop off paperwork

evidence.description: Torn corner of an exam booklet found in the office wastebasket with the partial watermark: '...yan M... ID: 2021...'. The rest is burned.
evidence.significance: Suggests Aryan Malhotra was in the office; possible evidence of document tampering

evidence.description: Server log showing a login from Dr. Deshpande’s authenticated account at 9:12 PM to access and encrypt the exam backup folder. IP trace leads to her home router.
evidence.significance: Implicates Dr. Deshpande in the digital sabotage

evidence.description: A single fingerprint on the office door’s internal lock mechanism (which requires physical presence to unlock from inside). Matches Rohan Patel.
evidence.location: Interior side of the office door lock
evidence.significance: Suggests someone locked the office from the inside after entering—requires access and intent

evidence.description: Security camera footage from the lab corridor (cameras 2 and 3) shows a 7-minute gap between 8:58 PM and 9:05 PM. Cameras restart with no visible disturbance.
evidence.significance: Indicates someone with admin-level access paused the recording

evidence.description: Café cashier recalls serving Rohan Patel and friends at 8:20 PM and remembers him wearing a blue hoodie with the college logo.
evidence.significance: Supports Rohan’s alibi

evidence.description: A USB drive hidden in a potted plant outside the lab, containing a decoy answer key with obvious errors and a corrupted encryption script.
evidence.significance: Appears to be a failed attempt to plant evidence; too obvious to be genuine

evidence.description: Professor Kapoor’s personal calendar shows a meeting scheduled with 'P. Iyer' at 7:00 PM on the day of the sabotage, but the entry was created at 6:48 PM—the same minute it was supposedly scheduled.
evidence.significance: Suggests someone forged a meeting entry to establish Priya’s presence on campus after she left

timeline: 6:45 PM: Priya Iyer leaves campus, according to gate security log.
6:48 PM: A meeting with 'P. Iyer' is created in Professor Kapoor’s calendar.
6:50 PM: Security camera shows Priya Iyer entering Professor’s office (verified). She exits at 6:53 PM.
7:30 PM: Rohan Patel clocks out of lab; claims he leaves campus.
7:45 PM: Aryan Malhotra is seen arguing with Professor Kapoor outside her office.
8:00 PM: Aryan claims he arrives at library; no timestamped check-in or CCTV of entry.
8:30 PM: Dr. Deshpande begins video conference; confirmed by collaborator.
8:58 PM: Security camera feed in lab corridor stops.
9:05 PM: Cameras resume; no visible disturbance.
9:12 PM: Login to exam server from Dr. Deshpande’s account with her credentials.
9:15 PM: Rohan Patel arrives at café with friends; timestamped photo from group chat.
10:30 PM: Dr. Deshpande ends video call.
11:00 PM: Night guard makes first round; sees office door locked, no signs of break-in.
6:00 AM next day: Professor discovers exam booklets shredded in office, server encrypted.
red_herrings: Torn exam booklet with Aryan’s name fragment
USB drive with fake answer key planted near lab
Server login from Dr. Deshpande’s IP and account
Rohan’s fingerprint on interior lock and missing badge

solution.method: Priya never left campus at 6:45 PM. She faked her exit on the gate log by asking a friend to swipe out with her ID (a known loophole). She returned to the office at 8:55 PM using her access key. She paused the security cameras by exploiting a scripted admin function (known to TAs for maintenance), entered the office, shredded the exams, encrypted the server using a backdoor password she knew from creating the exam, then locked the door from the inside. She forged the calendar entry at 6:48 PM to give herself an alibi. The USB decoy was planted to implicate someone tech-savvy like Rohan.
solution.motive: She discovered Professor Kapoor had promised her exam credit in return for her work but then reneged, calling it 'expected duty'. She snapped after feeling exploited and invisible, wanting to delay the exam to buy time to apply for jobs abroad without academic failure on record.
solution.proof: Analysis of the calendar metadata reveals the meeting was created at 6:48 PM from an IP address logged in the campus Wi-Fi network—not from her home. The Wi-Fi logs show her device connected continuously from 6:40 PM to 9:20 PM. The gate log shows duplicate swipe for her ID at 6:45 PM—impossible without proxy swiping.
solution.how_to_solve: The key is reconciling the timeline with digital footprints. The calendar entry timestamp (6:48 PM) contradicts her alibi. The Wi-Fi log proves her device was on campus during the sabotage. The interior fingerprint on the lock means someone locked the office from inside—only possible if they were already in the building after hours. The server login from Dr. Deshpande’s IP was spoofed using a proxy script found in Priya’s personal laptop (recovered later). Rohan’s alibi is solid (photo timestamp and café receipt), and the torn exam paper was planted—Aryan never accessed the office. The culprit is the one who manipulated time, access, and perception: Priya.
